chapters.title: Chapter 801
paragraphs: “We’re leaving soon. Get ready.”
At that one remark, tossed out when I came back without warning, Yamamoto Genji surprisingly nodded obediently.
“Understood.”
For a guy who’d been going on about Chōsenjin when he first woke up, he was being about as polite as possible.
If Heo Jun had witnessed this astonishing change, he might have written this on the first line of the *Donguibogam*:
A beating is the best medicine.
Bodily wounds called for potions. A rotten mind called for fists.
Yamamoto Genji scrambled out of bed and snapped to attention like a recruit.
“I’m ready.”
“Already?”
“Yes, sir.”
“You planning to fight in that?”
“Huh?”
Yamamoto Genji blinked. From that innocent look, he clearly hadn’t understood what I meant. Or maybe he hadn’t heard me properly.
So I kindly repeated myself.
“You planning to fight in your hospital gown?”
A brief silence.
At last, he realized what I meant by *leaving*. His voice trembled.
“W-we’re going to the battlefield?”
“Where did you think we were going?”
“I’m still a patient, so I naturally assumed I’d be sent back to the main camp...”
“Sent back?”
“Y-yes, sir.”
“Hmm. Right. You’re still a patient. A patient.”
Good grief. I’d forgotten something important.
Muttering to myself, I kicked open the firmly shut door.
“Hey! Anyone out there?”
A healer from the medical unit came running before the words had left my mouth.
“Yes, sir.”
“Uh, the transport vehicle going back to the main camp hasn’t left yet, right?”
“No, sir. It’s still waiting.”
“Good. Contact the team leader right away and tell him to load one more body. I’ll take care of the cleanup, so all they have to do is come pick him up.”
“I’ll pass that along.”
“...Wait.”
Yamamoto Genji had been listening. Now he looked distinctly uneasy.
“One more body? Cleanup? What does that mean?”
“Nothing. Don’t worry about it.”
“It sounds like something I should worry about. Hey, you. Put down the phone. Who are you calling?”
The healer answered flatly, “Team Leader Jones, as the boss instructed.”
“Who’s Team Leader Jones?”
“He’s in charge of recovering the dead. He transports the fallen back to the main camp.”
Yamamoto Genji looked from me to the healer and back. Then his expression turned resolute.
“On my honor as a samurai, I’ll give my life in battle.”
“What honor? I looked you up online. Your nickname’s ‘Swift No-Show.’”
“Quit talking bullshit. Gear up and get out here.”
“Yes, sir. But, by any chance...”
“What?”
“I’m still not feeling well. Is there really no way you could send me to the rear...”
*Whack!*
“Ugh!”
Even now, all he could think about was running away. A bastard like this needed a beating.
I sighed and watched him stagger to his feet.
I’d have loved to beat the hell out of him, but the fact that I needed even a piece of shit like him left a bad taste in my mouth.
“Hey.”
“W-why? What is it?”
“I’m not going to hit you, so relax. I just want to check one more time.”
My voice dropped.
“What you said he told you back then. Are you sure?”
Before Yamamoto Genji could answer, the words I’d already heard several times replayed in my ears.
“Rub’ al Khali. Come find me in the land where the black jewel sleeps, before it’s too late.”
The trailing hem of The Prophet’s long robe seemed close enough to grab.
The Arabian Desert covers most of the Middle East, stretching from Yemen through Oman and the Persian Gulf to Jordan and Iraq.
More than 2.3 million square kilometers. Korea’s official area, as submitted to the UN, was just over 200,000 square kilometers. By comparison, the desert was absurdly vast.
*No wonder the estimated search time was so long. We were planning to comb through all this.*
But we’d had no other choice.

Mana readings rose by the day, and the concentration had grown so dense that even the most advanced equipment couldn’t function properly. Covering that much ground meant sending a hundred thousand Hunters out on foot.
Then The Prophet, who’d been hiding somewhere in that vast desert, named a place himself. Whether that was good news or bad, I couldn’t say.
The Rub’ al Khali Desert.
If the Arabian Desert was the broad term for the desert regions of the Middle East, the Rub’ al Khali was the vast desert at its center, spread across the southern Arabian Peninsula.
It was the second-largest desert in the world, after the Sahara in Africa. Even so, narrowing down the area The Prophet meant wasn’t difficult.
At least, not for Team Leader Choi.
“The Empty Quarter.”
“What’s that?”
“Rub’ al Khali means ‘Empty Quarter’ in Arabic. A land where no one can live. Nothing but blazing sun and sand. That’s probably how it got such a desolate name.”
“Then the black jewel...”
“There are oil fields there. Supposedly, they were once the largest in the world. Judging by his message, that’s our likeliest destination.”
Searching was the hard part. Getting there wasn’t. Once we had a destination, we advanced at astonishing speed.
The thousand Hunters chosen for the expedition were among the best deployed to the Middle East. We took the shortest route across the Arabian Desert and reached the Rub’ al Khali.
And we immediately understood why the people of the ancient Middle East had called this place the Empty Quarter.
Desert and wilderness stretched to the horizon like a vast sea, with small villages scattered through it like reefs.
Machinery and abandoned industrial complexes stood among them. The place was so desolate that it was hard to believe the world’s largest oil field had once been here.
Even the Skeleton King blinked in confusion.
“What? Humans live here? This isn’t a Gate?”
Team Leader Choi had said *once* for a reason.
This land had been abandoned twice.
Once, long ago, when its inhabitants named it the Rub’ al Khali. Then again during the Great Cataclysm.
And a place didn’t get abandoned without reason.
“Spectacular.”
I wished Magic Johnson, who’d come with us, had said that. Unfortunately, it was the Skeleton King. I could feel what he meant, though.
Maybe we all did.
*The concentration of magical power... It’s too dense.*
At some point, the air had grown heavy. It wasn’t just the sun beating down on us.
*Clunk. Psssh.*
An engine died abruptly. The vehicles carrying our thousand Hunters all ground to a halt, and Magic Johnson murmured, “Here we go.”
A simple mechanical failure was out of the question.
Yamamoto Genji had been through something similar before. His face was already deathly pale.
“He’s here. He’s here. He’s here...”
The Skeleton King watched him mutter without pause, then turned to me.
“Can I kill that human?”
“No. Unfortunately, you can’t.”
“Why not? Didn’t we bring him along to put his body to use? If I have to keep looking at him like that, I might as well turn him into an undead.”
“Oh.”
Was this bastard a genius?
I barely stopped myself from nodding at his surprisingly logical argument. Then I gave Yamamoto Genji a hard kick and got out of the vehicle.
*What do you mean, he’s here already?*
We were still a considerable distance from the oil fields The Prophet had hinted at. Apart from the rising concentration of magical power, I hadn’t sensed anything unusual.
This was only a sign.
An ominous but unmistakable sign that something we hadn’t encountered yet was out there in the vast desert.
Then the specialist checking the magical-power distribution at regular intervals gave his report, turning my suspicion into certainty.
“We can’t get a reading. Our equipment can’t determine an accurate value.”
Not even with several precious A-rank Magic Gems fitted into the measuring device.
I licked my dry lips.
“He told us to come find him. Guess he wasn’t just talking bullshit.”
Team Leader Choi stepped quietly up beside me.
“Should we pull back and request reinforcements while we still can?”
A cautious suggestion, just like him. I shook my head without hesitation.
“No. We keep going.”
“We don’t know what kind of trap may be waiting.”
“Of course there could be a trap. We know what that bastard Prophet is like.”
“Then why...”
“Trap or not, we have to break through. We don’t have time. And...”
I lowered my voice.
“If luring us here is his goal in itself, that’s all the more reason not to call for reinforcements.”
We didn’t know the limits of The Prophet’s abilities or One God’s fighting strength. Calling S-rank Hunters here—the core of our forces—would put everyone left behind in danger.
In this desert, The Prophet was practically a pope with countless fanatics at his command.
*It’d be a problem if we brought in reinforcements only to leave the rear wide open to a raid.*
That didn’t mean I planned to fight recklessly.

Normally, I would’ve gone alone. The reason I’d brought a thousand Hunters was that I knew I wasn’t invincible, no matter how strong I was. Nothing was more dangerous than an enemy you didn’t understand.
And the force we had now was neither too small nor too large.

Even without me, we had two dependable powerhouses in Magic Johnson and the Skeleton King. Add the cowardly Yamamoto Genji and Team Leader Choi, and I was sure we could smash our way through whatever came.
*Bring in more forces, though, and he might run.*
We held the front, while Chuck Hagel, Faye Chen, Prince Felix, and several other S-rank Hunters guarded the encirclement with a considerable force to our rear.
If we added or removed even a little from either side, the balance of power would shift—and our chance to eliminate The Prophet would slip that much farther away.
“No beast attacks something that looks stronger than itself. Especially not a fox like The Prophet. Right, Jin?”
“That’s right.”
I nodded at Magic Johnson, watching the heat haze rise over the distant desert.
“Still, that’s a relief. Looks like that quick-witted fox hasn’t gotten scared and run off.”
“What do you mean—!”
His face went rigid in an instant.
Realizing what I meant, Magic Johnson hurriedly swallowed the rest of his words and shouted, pouring his mighty mana into his voice.
“Prepare for battle!”
Right.
They were coming.

chapters.title: Chapter 802
paragraphs: *Slide.*
Sand slipped slowly down the hillside. The day was sweltering, without a breath of wind. Beneath the blazing sun, the shadows of flying beasts passed over everyone’s heads.
*Kreeeaaak!*
A dozen or so eagles glided through the sky, their cries almost like screams.
Their enormous wings, spanning several meters, were nothing but bare white bones. The eyes gazing down from far above were not made of flesh and blood. They burned with a vivid blue light.
The gaze of something returned from the edge of death.
Something caught between life and death.
“Undead...”
The word escaped someone’s lips like a sigh.
Yet none of the people watching the eagles fly overhead and on toward the horizon looked afraid. They already knew the undead monsters weren’t their enemies.
More precisely, they knew the creatures’ master was on their side.
And at least one of them thought of him as more than an ally. He was a friend.
“Hey.”
“What? Don’t talk to me. I’m concentrating.”
“How’s it going?”
“I said don’t talk to me. I’m sharing my vision.”
“Still? You’re damn slow.”
“Fuck it. I’m done.”
“Sorry.”
“Then shut your mouth, you lunatic. Do you think this is some cheap Familiar like the ones humans use?”
His voice was curt. The human and the monster spoke as casually as old friends while staring into the heat haze shimmering over the desert.
Beneath them, vibrations slowly crumbled the sand dunes.
“Anything yet?”
“No. Actually, I finished a little while ago.”
“What? Why didn’t you say so?”
“To build suspense.”
“You’re a nutcase.”
“I’m kidding. I didn’t say anything because I wasn’t sure how to tell you.”
“...There are that many?”
“Yes.”
“How many?”
“At least ten thousand. After that, there were too many, so I gave up counting.”
At the Skeleton King’s answer, Jin Taekyung fell silent.
Ten thousand.
An enormous army.
And that was only how many the Skeleton King had confirmed. The true number might be far higher.
“Fuck. They really went all out.”
“They had a reason for drawing us all the way here.”
“What about him?”
The Skeleton King knew who Jin meant by *him*. He shook his head.
“I still don’t know. From above, there are about three that look like serious threats, but whether one of them is The Prophet... Hmm.”
The Skeleton King let out a low groan. His expression stiffened as he continued.
“There was one in the air, too.”
“All S-rank?”
“Probably. My servants were taken out before they could do a thing.”
Three on the ground. One in the air.

The news that four S-rank monsters had led an army of tens of thousands right to their doorstep shook the nearly one thousand Hunters. However carefully selected and battle-hardened they were, they couldn’t simply stop fearing death.
*Thud. Rumble, rumble.*
The vibrations grew stronger. The Hunters’ gazes trembled as they watched the sand shift beneath their feet.
They could almost see the countless monsters about to surge toward them like a wave.
And amid the monsters’ roars and the fierce fighting, they could see their comrades—or themselves—dying in sprays of blood.
Then a calm voice reached them.
“So, want to retreat now?”
One by one, those who’d been staring at the ground raised their heads. Jin Taekyung stood on the hill, watching them with a steady, solemn gaze.
“No. I guess we should call it running away, not retreating. Right?”
“Honestly, whether you call it a strategic retreat or running away, I can’t blame you. Everyone wants to survive. Everyone has a reason to keep living, even if they have to run like hell to do it.”
That was true of everyone.
People had family bound to them by blood, and friends who were family in all but blood. Even those who had neither still had reasons to go on living.
But...
“I don’t know where it came from, but there’s a saying: There’s no paradise at the end of the road when you run away.”
It was strange.
The sun overhead was hot enough to set them on fire, yet the moment they heard Jin Taekyung’s voice, a chill went through them as though they’d been doused in cold water.
He was right.
There was no paradise at the end of the road when you ran away. They lived in a time like that.
“Run, and run, and keep running... Then one day, after doing everything you can to stay alive, you look around. Will there be anything left for you to protect?”
It had been some thirty years.
Humanity had rebuilt bigger, grander cities on the ruins left by the Great Cataclysm. The disaster’s traces remained only in records and scars.
Those who survived the war, or were born after peace arrived, didn’t know what war was like.
But Jin Taekyung was different.
“Once you start backing down, it’s over.”
A battle was not a war. A Gate was not the real world.
In the Gates they’d faced until now, they could retreat to avoid a fight. But the place where they stood now was the world where they’d been born and raised.
A world with something they had to protect.
A world they had to protect, no matter what.
Jin Taekyung had known that since the day he survived alone, leaving behind someone who’d been like an older brother. He knew it still, now that he’d come to know another world.
“If there’s something you want to protect, put your life on the line and fight. That’s why you’re here, isn’t it?”
Everyone wondered, but no one knew why the cursed monsters had invaded this world—or how humans had come to possess such incredible power.
But they all had some inkling.
The power that had come to them one day like a stroke of luck had been given to them to protect this world from monsters.
“And for that one reason...”
*Whoosh.*
Sand whipped around Jin Taekyung. A hot wind blew in from somewhere and swept over the people.
It thawed their hands and feet, frozen despite the scorching sun, and set the red blood in their veins boiling—blood unlike that of the monsters now emerging in the distance through a vast sandstorm.
“That’s why people—why this world—calls us Hunters.”
*Fwoosh!*
An immense wave of qi jolted everyone alert. Heat haze rose around Jin Taekyung as he slowly turned.
The heat was so intense that the space around him seemed to warp.
His spearhead caught the sunlight and blazed like a blue-white sun.
“Get into formation.”
*Clang, clang, clang!*
Countless weapons came free at once, as if on cue.
Magic Johnson raised his staff, and dozens of transport vehicles, each weighing several metric tons, moved across their front to form a barricade.
Behind them, nearly a hundred tanks drove tower shields larger than their own bodies deep into the sand.
*Boom. Rumble!*
A wall of steel took shape amid heavy thuds.
And then...
*Rumble...*
A wave of monsters raced across the boundless desert, throwing up a vast cloud of sand.
Jin Taekyung watched them come. His next words were so matter-of-fact that they took everyone by surprise.
“Fuck. Hang in there, everyone. Killing all those bastards is going to be a real pain in the ass.”
Someone burst out laughing. A Hunter who’d been staring at the comrade beside him as if he’d gone mad let out a short laugh, too. Soon everyone’s shoulders were shaking.
*Kill them all? Every last one of those monsters?*
Ordinarily, they’d have thought it was ridiculous nonsense.
If anyone else had said it, no matter how great a Hunter they were, they’d have cursed them under their breath.
But that startlingly young Asian man was Jin Taekyung, the new Alliance Leader of the World Hunter Federation.
A hero who had proven himself.
The only person writing a new legend after Cheon Taemin.
They couldn’t help believing in him. Jin Taekyung had always fought at the very front, harder than anyone else.
That alone was reason enough to fight.
*Boom. Rumble, rumble!*
*Graaaar!*
Even as the rumbling and roars swelled until their eardrums throbbed, the Hunters couldn’t stop laughing.
From the sand dune, where he stood as solid as a mountain, Jin Taekyung swung his spear.
*Crunch!*
Blood shot up like a fountain and evaporated before it touched the ground. Torn bodies and entrails scattered in every direction.
It was the opening moment of the great battle that would later be called the Desert Storm.
Chuck Hagel stared silently at the cigar in his hand.
The cigar he’d taken—or rather, acquired—from the French President not long ago was still burning down.
He’d since heard it had been a gift from Michael Silbert himself. Given where it came from, it was obviously worth a fortune.
Cuban cigars made before the Great Cataclysm were impossible to find now, no matter how much money you had.
Why?
Simple. Cuba had been destroyed.
The Monster Wave that began in the center of Cuba’s capital had grown beyond control. It ended only after sinking three island nations in the Cayman Islands deep beneath the sea.
Perhaps that was when it started.
When a certain middle-aged man who’d never touched tobacco began smoking cigars out of habit.
His mother had been in Cuba.
*Crackle.*
Ash that had been burning for a long time dropped with a soft *tap*.
After watching it in silence for a long while, Chuck Hagel abruptly spoke.
“Any request for backup?”
His aide waved away the thick cigar smoke before answering.
“Not yet.”
“Goddamn it.”
“You don’t need to worry so much, boss.”
“Worry? About that punk?”
*He’s too strong to call a punk. And he’s your superior, too.*
The aide barely kept the words from slipping out. He clicked his tongue instead.
“We’re fully prepared and standing by. We have the rear of the Rub’ al Khali Desert covered.”
“Damn it. That’s all well and good, but that goddamn satellite surveillance still doesn’t work. Why are the drones down? Did some defense contractor take a kickback?”

sentences.text: *Slide.*
Sand slipped slowly down the hillside.
The day was sweltering, without a breath of wind.
Beneath the blazing sun, the shadows of flying beasts passed over everyone’s heads.
*Kreeeaaak!*
A dozen or so eagles glided through the sky, their cries almost like screams.
Their enormous wings, spanning several meters, were nothing but bare white bones.
The eyes gazing down from far above were not made of flesh and blood.
They burned with a vivid blue light.
The gaze of something returned from the edge of death.
Something caught between life and death.
“Undead...”
The word escaped someone’s lips like a sigh.
Yet none of the people watching the eagles fly overhead and on toward the horizon looked afraid.
They already knew the undead monsters weren’t their enemies.
More precisely, they knew the creatures’ master was on their side.
And at least one of them thought of him as more than an ally.
He was a friend.
“Hey.”
“What?
Don’t talk to me.
I’m concentrating.”
“How’s it going?”
“I said don’t talk to me.
I’m sharing my vision.”
“Still?
You’re damn slow.”
“Fuck it.
I’m done.”
“Sorry.”
“Then shut your mouth, you lunatic.
Do you think this is some cheap Familiar like the ones humans use?”
His voice was curt.
The human and the monster spoke as casually as old friends while staring into the heat haze shimmering over the desert.
Beneath them, vibrations slowly crumbled the sand dunes.
“Anything yet?”
“No.
Actually, I finished a little while ago.”
“What?
Why didn’t you say so?”
“To build suspense.”
“You’re a nutcase.”
“I’m kidding.
I didn’t say anything because I wasn’t sure how to tell you.”
“...There are that many?”
“Yes.”
“How many?”
“At least ten thousand.
After that, there were too many, so I gave up counting.”
At the Skeleton King’s answer, Jin Taekyung fell silent.
Ten thousand.
An enormous army.
And that was only how many the Skeleton King had confirmed.
The true number might be far higher.
“Fuck.
They really went all out.”
“They had a reason for drawing us all the way here.”
“What about him?”
The Skeleton King knew who Jin meant by *him*.
He shook his head.
“I still don’t know.
From above, there are about three that look like serious threats, but whether one of them is The Prophet...
Hmm.”
The Skeleton King let out a low groan.
His expression stiffened as he continued.
“There was one in the air, too.”
“All S-rank?”
“Probably.
My servants were taken out before they could do a thing.”
Three on the ground.
One in the air.
The news that four S-rank monsters had led an army of tens of thousands right to their doorstep shook the nearly one thousand Hunters.
However carefully selected and battle-hardened they were, they couldn’t simply stop fearing death.
*Thud.
Rumble, rumble.*
The vibrations grew stronger.
The Hunters’ gazes trembled as they watched the sand shift beneath their feet.
They could almost see the countless monsters about to surge toward them like a wave.
And amid the monsters’ roars and the fierce fighting, they could see their comrades—or themselves—dying in sprays of blood.
Then a calm voice reached them.
“So, want to retreat now?”
One by one, those who’d been staring at the ground raised their heads.
Jin Taekyung stood on the hill, watching them with a steady, solemn gaze.
“No.
I guess we should call it running away, not retreating.
Right?”
“Honestly, whether you call it a strategic retreat or running away, I can’t blame you.
Everyone wants to survive.
Everyone has a reason to keep living, even if they have to run like hell to do it.”
That was true of everyone.
People had family bound to them by blood, and friends who were family in all but blood.
Even those who had neither still had reasons to go on living.
But...
“I don’t know where it came from, but there’s a saying: There’s no paradise at the end of the road when you run away.”
It was strange.
The sun overhead was hot enough to set them on fire, yet the moment they heard Jin Taekyung’s voice, a chill went through them as though they’d been doused in cold water.
He was right.
There was no paradise at the end of the road when you ran away.
They lived in a time like that.
“Run, and run, and keep running...
Then one day, after doing everything you can to stay alive, you look around.
Will there be anything left for you to protect?”
It had been some thirty years.
Humanity had rebuilt bigger, grander cities on the ruins left by the Great Cataclysm.
The disaster’s traces remained only in records and scars.
Those who survived the war, or were born after peace arrived, didn’t know what war was like.
But Jin Taekyung was different.
“Once you start backing down, it’s over.”
A battle was not a war.
A Gate was not the real world.
In the Gates they’d faced until now, they could retreat to avoid a fight.
But the place where they stood now was the world where they’d been born and raised.
A world with something they had to protect.
A world they had to protect, no matter what.
Jin Taekyung had known that since the day he survived alone, leaving behind someone who’d been like an older brother.
He knew it still, now that he’d come to know another world.
“If there’s something you want to protect, put your life on the line and fight.
That’s why you’re here, isn’t it?”
Everyone wondered, but no one knew why the cursed monsters had invaded this world—or how humans had come to possess such incredible power.
But they all had some inkling.
The power that had come to them one day like a stroke of luck had been given to them to protect this world from monsters.
“And for that one reason...”
*Whoosh.*
Sand whipped around Jin Taekyung.
A hot wind blew in from somewhere and swept over the people.
It thawed their hands and feet, frozen despite the scorching sun, and set the red blood in their veins boiling—blood unlike that of the monsters now emerging in the distance through a vast sandstorm.
“That’s why people—why this world—calls us Hunters.”
*Fwoosh!*
An immense wave of qi jolted everyone alert.
Heat haze rose around Jin Taekyung as he slowly turned.
The heat was so intense that the space around him seemed to warp.
His spearhead caught the sunlight and blazed like a blue-white sun.
“Get into formation.”
*Clang, clang, clang!*
Countless weapons came free at once, as if on cue.
Magic Johnson raised his staff, and dozens of transport vehicles, each weighing several metric tons, moved across their front to form a barricade.
Behind them, nearly a hundred tanks drove tower shields larger than their own bodies deep into the sand.
*Boom.
Rumble!*
A wall of steel took shape amid heavy thuds.
And then...
*Rumble...*
A wave of monsters raced across the boundless desert, throwing up a vast cloud of sand.
Jin Taekyung watched them come.
His next words were so matter-of-fact that they took everyone by surprise.
“Fuck.
Hang in there, everyone.
Killing all those bastards is going to be a real pain in the ass.”
Someone burst out laughing.
A Hunter who’d been staring at the comrade beside him as if he’d gone mad let out a short laugh, too.
Soon everyone’s shoulders were shaking.
*Kill them all?
Every last one of those monsters?*
Ordinarily, they’d have thought it was ridiculous nonsense.
If anyone else had said it, no matter how great a Hunter they were, they’d have cursed them under their breath.
But that startlingly young Asian man was Jin Taekyung, the new Alliance Leader of the World Hunter Federation.
A hero who had proven himself.
The only person writing a new legend after Cheon Taemin.
They couldn’t help believing in him.
Jin Taekyung had always fought at the very front, harder than anyone else.
That alone was reason enough to fight.
*Boom.
Rumble, rumble!*
*Graaaar!*
Even as the rumbling and roars swelled until their eardrums throbbed, the Hunters couldn’t stop laughing.
From the sand dune, where he stood as solid as a mountain, Jin Taekyung swung his spear.
*Crunch!*
Blood shot up like a fountain and evaporated before it touched the ground.
Torn bodies and entrails scattered in every direction.
It was the opening moment of the great battle that would later be called the Desert Storm.

He’d since heard it had been a gift from Michael Silbert himself.
Given where it came from, it was obviously worth a fortune.
Cuban cigars made before the Great Cataclysm were impossible to find now, no matter how much money you had.
Why?
Simple.
Cuba had been destroyed.
The Monster Wave that began in the center of Cuba’s capital had grown beyond control.
It ended only after sinking three island nations in the Cayman Islands deep beneath the sea.
Perhaps that was when it started.
When a certain middle-aged man who’d never touched tobacco began smoking cigars out of habit.
His mother had been in Cuba.
*Crackle.*
Ash that had been burning for a long time dropped with a soft *tap*.

His aide waved away the thick cigar smoke before answering.
“Not yet.”
“Goddamn it.”
“You don’t need to worry so much, boss.”
“Worry?
About that punk?”
*He’s too strong to call a punk.
And he’s your superior, too.*
The aide barely kept the words from slipping out.
He clicked his tongue instead.

chapters.title: Chapter 803
paragraphs: Human beings possess almost limitless potential.
With minds more capable than those of any other living thing on Earth, they built systems of their own and developed civilization.
From the primitive prehistoric age to the present, what humans had achieved was dazzling—especially the history and culture they had built over the past several thousand years.
Progress, progress, and more progress.
Humans never stopped discovering new things. With each discovery, they moved forward.
Until gunfire filled battlefields where swords and spears had once clashed. Until car horns replaced the whinny of horses on streets lit by neon signs.
Until they crossed five seas and six continents and finally ventured into space.
“Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed.”

On the day that grand plan, named after an ancient sun god, succeeded, what did the god watching from somewhere think? A human had set foot on the moon for the first time and called that historic moment “one small step, one giant leap for mankind.”
No one could know the will of God. But an old man with the rather long name Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Ali was certain.
God must have been enraged.
Otherwise, He would not have unleashed a great flood called the Great Cataclysm.
Sending the great Prophet down to this land and commanding him to punish them surely meant that he was to punish humanity’s arrogance on God’s behalf.
“Do you not think so too, sinful infidel?”
The middle-aged man trembled at the old man’s calm voice.
Drenched in blood, he stood amid his many subordinates. Only moments ago, they had been alive and breathing. Now they lay strewn across the ground.
He had nothing left but the sword in his hand and the mana boiling through his body, his fighting spirit still undiminished.
“Atone through death. Like those who went before you.”
“Go... fuck yourself!”
With a shout like a scream, the middle-aged man drew on every ounce of his strength and charged the old fanatic.
*Whoooosh!*
A strike that would likely be his last.
His sword flew faster than ever before, its blade blazing with aura.
*Shhk!*
A flash came out of nowhere, cleaving both the aura-wreathed sword and its wielder in two.
*Splatter!*
Blood gushed like a fountain.
As the headless corpse crumpled, something glinting fell at the old man’s feet.
A necklace. It was a necklace.
The old man stared at the crucifix necklace half-buried in the hot sand, then spoke.
“Any survivors?”
“None. That infidel was the last.”
The young man who had cut down the middle-aged A-rank Hunter as easily as breathing continued, “Amir, there are more infidels not far from here. If you let me go...”
“Their main force will have heard from them over the radio this time. We’ve dealt with them easily so far, but it won’t be that simple from now on.”
“No matter how strong the infidels’ forces are, we can defeat them!”
“You’re right, Hamid, son of Hassan. But have you forgotten what the Prophet said?”
Hamid flinched at the old man’s piercing gaze. A moment later, he realized what Amir meant, and his eyes widened.
“What the Prophet said... Could it be?”
“Yes. The time has finally come. The time promised by the Prophet and almighty Allah is upon us.”
Surprise turned to joy. Joy to fervor.
The old man smiled as he watched Hamid’s expression change. Then he looked over the warriors of God surrounding them and murmured, “Inshallah. The Prophet will lead us to the promised land!”
“Inshallah!”
“Allah hu akbar!”
Their voices rose together in a mighty shout. The countless fanatics who had lain dormant deep in the desert for decades began their advance.
Toward the promised land they had awaited for so long.
Toward the place overflowing with God’s grace.
*Rumble, rumble, rumble!*
A vast cloud of sand swept across the desert.
If this world were a chessboard, what would my role be?
A pawn that could only move forward?
A knight that could go farther than a pawn?
A bishop crossing the board diagonally?
Maybe a rook moving in straight lines, a queen with the combined reach of a bishop and a rook, or the king—ironically, the most important piece and yet weaker than the queen.
Honestly, I didn’t know.
Even now, as the Alliance Leader of the World Hunter Federation, even with everyone in the world knowing who I was, I still didn’t know exactly where I stood.
What I could do on this chessboard, or how far I could go.
But one thing I could say for sure.
If that chessboard was a battlefield rather than the world, I could dominate it.
I could push forward like a pawn, leap over my enemies’ heads like a knight, then range across the board like a bishop, rook, or queen and swallow everything in my path.
Just like right now.
*Baaang!*
Flesh and bone burst apart before the spearhead even touched them. A Troll with its upper half blown away toppled like a rotten log, and someone shouted behind me.
“Damn it! How many times do I have to tell you? Kill them like that and I can barely use them as undead!”
Instead of answering, I twisted my body.
*Whoom. Boom!*
Three flails flying in from different directions tangled together.
—Kwo?
The ogres blinked stupidly, a beat too late to understand what had happened.
White Flame’s spearhead had already swept past their necks.
*Shhk!*
Three heads flew free of their massive bodies.
I sprang off an ogre’s lifeless corpse and plunged toward the monsters packed around me.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear, Form Two.
Heavenly Strike.
*Krrrunch!*
Blood sprayed. Flesh split.
*Ding. Ding, ding.*
System alerts rang in my ears without pause as I leaped into the thick cloud of dust.
*Open Inventory.*
One weapon stored, another summoned at the same instant.
*Pop.*
White Flame vanished from my hand like an illusion. In its place, two short daggers settled firmly into my hands.
In a fight at this close range, they were faster and more efficient than any divine weapon.
I’d watched someone wield a dagger like this up close. With a single blade, he had earned the name Slaughter Saint.
*And I watched him do it from right beside him.*
For one brief moment, I steadied my breathing.
I calmed the internal energy pounding as though it would burst out of me. Light on my toes. Shoulders loose.
Remembering the Slaughter Saint’s advice, I copied the movements I’d seen him perform right in front of me dozens of times.
Then I took a step.
*Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step.*
*Swish.*
The wind that had always struck me head-on now slipped gently past.
I felt as though I were floating through the air in zero gravity.
Of course, I couldn’t claim I’d perfectly copied the Slaughter Saint’s personal martial art just by doing this much. But for dealing with these bastards right now, this much was enough.
*Shhk, shhk, shhk!*
The sound of slicing reached my ears only after flesh and bone had been cut.
Sound wasn’t slow.
I was fast enough to leave it behind. So were the daggers in my hands.
*Thud, thud, thud!*
I slipped among the monsters like mist, my daggers stabbing and slashing in flashes. Dozens fell, spraying blood.
No—they fell and rose again at the same moment.
—In the king’s name, I command you: answer the call.
*Whoooooosh.*
A voice seemed to ring inside my head rather than reach my ears, and a chilling cold swept across the battlefield.
It raised the monsters that had fallen moments ago and those falling even now.
—Krr. Grrrk.
Slow, rasping cries.
An eerie light glimmered deep in their eyes.
Reborn as new beings at the edge of death, the undead army obeyed their king’s command. Without hesitation, they charged the monsters pouring in from every direction.
—Kraaaaaa!
—Grr. Uh. Uh. Uh!
*Thud. Kraaang!*
The cries of living and undead monsters tangled together. Weapons swung hard into bodies on both sides.
But the living monsters felt pain. The undead had forgotten it when they died.
—Graaah.
*Crunch! Splatter!*
Outnumbered? It didn’t matter.
Even when weapons took their limbs or pierced their chests, they kept moving to the very end.
The Skeleton King had given them only one goal: before the magical power he had bestowed on them ran out, before they died a second death, they were to create another soldier.
*Crack!*
—Kyaaaah!
A monster screamed as its throat was torn out.
The undead that had done it, already missing an arm and a leg, was ripped to shreds by enraged monsters. That didn’t matter either.
Thanks to that, I—
No, we—had bought a little more time.
“Fire!”
“Fire Wall!”
“Lightning Spear!”
*Fwoooosh.*
Countless bolts of lightning and tongues of flame streaked through the air.

Behind the enormous transport vehicle blocking the way like a barricade, the monsters packed in so tightly there wasn’t a gap—like the first day of an E-Mart Black Friday sale—had no choice but to take the sudden barrage of attacks head-on.
*Crackle. KRAAAASH!*
—Kraaaaaa!
—Kgh! Grrrk!
Screams filled the air.
Lightning seared scales and flesh. Flames slipped through the gaps and burned bone and organs.
Many of the hundreds of monsters writhing in pain unlike anything they had ever felt even swung their weapons at their own allies.
—Kwoooooo!
Seized by their own savage instincts, the monsters charged one another.
But I didn’t let my guard down for a second.
“Hold formation! Don’t move a single step!”
I drove internal energy into the command. The Hunters who had begun advancing, swept up in the heat of battle and the thrill of gaining the upper hand, stopped in their tracks.
Battle was flow. Battle was momentum.
But there was a time to ride that momentum.
Against a force of well over ten thousand, taking out a mere thousand monsters wouldn’t win us the battle all at once.
Slowly. Carefully.
We had to win while keeping our losses to a minimum.
Besides...
*I still can’t see him.*
The bastard who had yet to show himself.
The Prophet.
And the S-rank monsters waiting for their moment among that sea of beasts—or somewhere in the sky above.
Until we took them down, neither this battle nor the war would end.
*This fight... is only just beginning.*
And at that moment, just as I muttered those words deep in my heart—
*Thud. Thud. Thuuum.*
An immense magical power surged from far away, making the desert tremble.

Without hesitation, they charged the monsters pouring in from every direction.
—Kraaaaaa!
—Grr.
Uh.
Uh.
Uh!
*Thud.
Kraaang!*
The cries of living and undead monsters tangled together.
Weapons swung hard into bodies on both sides.
But the living monsters felt pain.
The undead had forgotten it when they died.
—Graaah.
*Crunch!
Splatter!*
Outnumbered?
It didn’t matter.
Even when weapons took their limbs or pierced their chests, they kept moving to the very end.
The Skeleton King had given them only one goal: before the magical power he had bestowed on them ran out, before they died a second death, they were to create another soldier.
*Crack!*
—Kyaaaah!
A monster screamed as its throat was torn out.
The undead that had done it, already missing an arm and a leg, was ripped to shreds by enraged monsters.
That didn’t matter either.
Thanks to that, I—
No, we—had bought a little more time.
“Fire!”
“Fire Wall!”
“Lightning Spear!”
*Fwoooosh.*
Countless bolts of lightning and tongues of flame streaked through the air.

Behind the enormous transport vehicle blocking the way like a barricade, the monsters packed in so tightly there wasn’t a gap—like the first day of an E-Mart Black Friday sale—had no choice but to take the sudden barrage of attacks head-on.
*Crackle.
KRAAAASH!*
—Kraaaaaa!
—Kgh!
Grrrk!
Screams filled the air.
Lightning seared scales and flesh.
Flames slipped through the gaps and burned bone and organs.
Many of the hundreds of monsters writhing in pain unlike anything they had ever felt even swung their weapons at their own allies.
—Kwoooooo!
Seized by their own savage instincts, the monsters charged one another.
But I didn’t let my guard down for a second.
“Hold formation!
Don’t move a single step!”
I drove internal energy into the command.
The Hunters who had begun advancing, swept up in the heat of battle and the thrill of gaining the upper hand, stopped in their tracks.
Battle was flow.
Battle was momentum.
But there was a time to ride that momentum.
Against a force of well over ten thousand, taking out a mere thousand monsters wouldn’t win us the battle all at once.
Slowly.
Carefully.
We had to win while keeping our losses to a minimum.
Besides...
*I still can’t see him.*
The bastard who had yet to show himself.
The Prophet.
And the S-rank monsters waiting for their moment among that sea of beasts—or somewhere in the sky above.
Until we took them down, neither this battle nor the war would end.
*This fight... is only just beginning.*
And at that moment, just as I muttered those words deep in my heart—
*Thud.
Thud.
Thuuum.*
An immense magical power surged from far away, making the desert tremble.

chapters.title: Chapter 804
paragraphs: Even when a thick fog hides the sea, anyone can tell there’s an ocean beyond it. They can hear the faint cries of gulls and feel the salt in the wind.
A battlefield is the same.
Screams and blood fly in every direction. Countless blades clash, throwing off sparks. And yet, something with a special power can change the air of a battlefield simply by existing.
Just like now.
*Rrrrmmm.*
The air trembled.
A deep rumble rolling in from far away shook the desert.
The monsters that had been charging over the bodies of their own kind came to a halt as if on cue. People stiffened with a start.
What were they feeling at that moment?
A chill creeping down their spines? Or fear they’d briefly forgotten?
I didn’t know exactly what it was, but I wasn’t feeling either one.
What you saw depended on where you stood.
Unlike them, I stood on a peak. From there, I could see farther and sense more.
And I wasn’t the only one.
“This is...”
The Skeleton King, who’d come up beside me at some point, murmured as if groaning.

Magic Johnson, who’d been saving his strength by focusing on defense in the rear, looked grim. So did Yamamoto Genji, an S-rank Hunter at least in name, and Team Leader Choi, whose Qi Sense was nearly as sharp as his.
“Fuck.”
“Chikushō. This is insane. I have to get out of here.”
“So the leaders are finally making their move.”
*Whack!*
There’s always a reason when some bastard gets hit.
I kicked Yamamoto Genji in the shin for spouting nonsense at a time like this. As I turned away, I stirred my internal energy and stamped down with a quake step.
*Boom!*
The ground shuddered around me, and a wall of sand surged upward.
Through the countless grains falling back down, I saw the Hunters’ faces. They looked as if they’d just been doused in cold water.
“What are you all scared of? You that eager to die?”
“B-but this is...”
“However you rank them, they’re still monsters. And we’re all still Hunters. So quit freezing up like you’re about to die and...”
*Thud!*
I drove a dagger into the head of an ogre still writhing and clinging stubbornly to life, then finished my sentence.
“Fight. Like Hunters.”
*Ding.*

**System** Defeated Lv. 95 Ogre! Gained a tiny amount of EXP! The effect of the Title **One Against a Thousand** activates! **Intimidation** has greatly increased! Enemies are rapidly losing confidence due to your **Intimidation**! The status effect **Fear**, which had been applied to numerous allies, has been removed! Ally morale has greatly increased. Those who follow your leadership will share a strong bond and perform even better! Certain stats increase when facing numerous enemies!
One Against a Thousand was the Title I’d earned while fighting the Arch Lich’s army in Sichuan Province. For a reward earned through such a rare feat, it certainly delivered.
“GRAAAAAH!”
A few Hunters who’d been swallowing nervously until now roared, their eyes bloodshot. A tremendous cheer followed, heating the air around us.
Of course, there were always exceptions.
“No, even so, that was a bit much...”

I clicked my tongue softly at the sight of Yamamoto Genji rubbing his shin where I’d kicked it, watching me warily. Then I turned my eyes toward the monster army stretching endlessly across the vast desert.
*Clack. Clack-clack.*
Their movements were orderly now, unlike before.
A force of well over ten thousand marched with measured precision, parting to the left and right. Three paths opened, and at last, the beings radiating an overwhelming presence appeared.
*The S-rank monsters.*
Some were huge and grotesque. Others were so small compared to the monsters around them that they barely stood out.
But the demonic qi and Fear pouring from them were as overwhelming as all those countless monsters put together.
Enough to frighten even Yamamoto Genji. Cowardly and less capable though he was, he was still an S-rank Hunter.
“So those are the commanders leading this monster army,” the Skeleton King murmured.
“But the most important one is still missing,” I said.
“...The Prophet.”
“Right. The Prophet’s the head. Those guys are the hands and feet.”
“But is he here now? It pains me to admit it, but... I haven’t seen or sensed anyone I’d take to be The Prophet.”
To be honest, neither had I.
But there was one thing I was sure of.
The Prophet was somewhere on this battlefield.
Given how meticulous the bastard was, he was probably watching everything unfold from some distance away.
*If he came close, I’d sense him right away.*
The enemies were too numerous, and the battlefield too vast, for me to get a clear read with Qi Sense.
On top of that, the monster army’s momentum had changed with the arrival of its S-rank commanders. It was nothing like before.
“Jin.”
Magic Johnson’s low voice reached my ears. His eyes had sunk deep, as if he could already guess what the battle about to begin again would cost us.
He was worried about me, too—the one who would have to bear it all.
“If you’ll let me, I’d like to take command instead.”
I stared silently at Magic Johnson for a moment, then shook my head.
“No. I’m in command.”
Of course, Magic Johnson had the skill and the qualifications. He was a veteran of the Great Cataclysm and a fine commander who’d led his forces to victory in more than ten major battles.
But...
“If there’s something I have to bear, I won’t push it onto someone else.”
“That’s one of the reasons I’m here, isn’t it?”
Magic Johnson looked at me with wide eyes, then gave a small nod.
When he spoke, I heard firm trust and the faintest trace of a smile.
“All right, young friend. Give us our orders.”
I took a deep breath and looked around at everyone.
A thousand Hunters in all. I didn’t know every name or every face.
But if someone fell here and never got back up, I’d remember everything about them for the rest of my life.
Yeah. That was enough.
If I died, they’d do the same for me.
“I’m dropping the formalities now, Magic Johnson.”
“Yes, young boss.”
“Keep the enemies in the air in check and focus on protecting our allies. The Hunters under you are to follow your orders until I say otherwise.”
“Yes, sir!”
Magic Johnson shouted his answer and rose into the air.
The Grand Mage’s eyes, alight with a keen edge, followed hundreds of specks slowly crossing the cloudless sky—and the eagle beating its wings at their head.
More precisely, he was watching a monster with enormous wings tens of meters across and a lion’s lower body: a Griffon.
“Choi Minwoo.”
“Yes.”
“Take a hundred troops and hold the front line. If the tanks break formation, hand in your sword and retire.”
Team Leader Choi raised the Hero’s Sword, its blade shining with transparent light, and answered.
“That won’t happen.”
Team Leader Choi was the great hero Cheon Taemin’s only blood descendant and the master of the Ares Guild, yet he’d never once slacked off.
Sometimes I thought that if a new S-rank Hunter emerged anytime soon, it would be him.
I let out a quiet laugh at his calm confidence, then turned to the others still waiting.
“Skeleton King. Yamamoto Genji. You two...”
“No need to waste time saying it. There are three S-rank monsters on the ground, so we can each take one.”
“M-me too?”
I silenced Yamamoto Genji with a hard stare, then corrected the Skeleton King.
“You and him take one each. I’ll take two.”
“What?”
“Huh?”
The two of them questioned me at the same time. I turned away and muttered inwardly.
*Open Inventory. Summon.*
The two daggers that had served me so well in close combat disappeared. The cool, solid feel of a spear shaft filled my hand, which had been empty for an instant.
A flame warped the space around it.
*Fwoosh.*
Force formed around the transparent spearhead, wrapping it in a clear sheen.
In an instant too brief to measure, I gripped the spear in reverse and drove it down like a streak of light.
At an unseen enemy that had approached from deep in the desert without anyone noticing.
*Shhk. KRAAAAAASH!*
The heat-soaked ground split like tofu.
Hard sand and earth beneath my feet shot high into the air. In the ground, gouged out like a vast crater, countless writhing creatures came into view.
Among them was the largest of all, a monster gleaming red.
*That’s...*
A warning light flashed in my mind.
At the same time, the blue circle of Qi Sense spread out alongside my spearhead and reached the monster’s hard body.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
**System** Your **Qi Sense** is currently at the eighth stage. You have detected targets within range using **Qi Sense**! Lv. 87 Soldier Scorpion Lv. 76 Worker Scorpion Lv. 99 Elite Scorpion
Countless details reached me through my eyes and ears.
But my attention was fixed on only one of them.
**System** Lv. 140 Scorpion King
Countless scorpions as large as grown men—and one scorpion larger than dozens of them put together.
*The Scorpion King.*
That was the enemy I had to take down first.
*KRAAAAAASH! Crunch!*
Superheated flames scorched the monsters’ lair, deep beneath the ground.
Their hard carapaces, sharp pincers, even the venomous stingers on their tails—all of it melted away.
*Kiiiiieeet!*
The scorpions—or rather, the monsters—screamed in agony. Their dying cries spilled out of the pit and into the world.
Humans and monsters.
Monsters and humans.
Everyone could hear their screams, and everyone reacted.
“Kill. The. Humans!”
The Demon Realm language erupted like a roar from an S-rank monster, and a massive tremor swept in every direction.
*Rumble, rumble, rumble!*
Their numbers weren’t the problem.
Their momentum, and the quantity and quality of the demonic qi they emitted, were beyond comparison with what we’d faced before.
The elite monsters waiting in the rear charged after their S-rank commanders. More than ten thousand monsters surged behind them like a wave.
*KRAAAAAH!*
On the ground came an enormous force led by three S-rank monsters. Over everyone’s heads, hundreds of flying monsters shrieked, led by the Griffon spreading its unusually large wings.
*Kiaaaak!*
The attack began across both sky and ground.
But I neither feared nor hesitated.
*Kiaaaat!*
The Scorpion King screamed as it burst out of the pit. I drove one decisive strike into it.
*Crunch! Fwoooooosh!*
Its acidic blood melted away in the flames.
*Ding.*
With the System alert I’d been waiting for, I charged like a beast toward the S-rank monsters.
*KRAAAAAASH!*

chapters.title: Chapter 805
paragraphs: A beast.
That was what Jin Taekyung looked like to everyone watching: fierce as a hungry tiger, majestic as a lion, swift as a leopard.
*KRAAAAAASH!*
Sand and earth swirled up around him. His figure seemed to ripple out of sight where he stood, then shot forward at terrifying speed.
Flamefire Path.
A single streak of flame crossed the space between them. He was faster than when he’d simply charged in headlong before, his movements incomparably more controlled.
Jin Taekyung felt he was beginning to understand, if only a little, the enlightenment the Fire King and the Slaughter Saint had reached over their lifetimes.
And how to bring down the enemies drawing closer by the second.
**System** Lv. 130 Lycanthrope Champion Lv. 140 Death Knight Legion Commander Lv. 148 Manticore Lord
As the concentration of magical power had risen, so had these S-rank monsters’ levels.
But Level wasn’t an absolute measure of strength. An enemy with a lower Level might possess far greater qi, while one with a higher Level could be physically weaker.
Once opponents reached this tier, it ultimately came down to timing and matchup. Jin Taekyung had just turned the Level 140 Scorpion King into a roast with a surprise attack.
And there was only one way to size up an opponent’s strength and find out how well you matched up.
Fight them.
*Whoosh.*
Several dozen meters vanished in an instant.
As Jin Taekyung charged straight at them, keeping his center of gravity low, three streaks of light fell toward him.
*Shraaah!*
The Death Knight’s sword. The Lycanthrope’s axe. And, last of all, the Manticore’s claws.
Dark crimson magical power, so dense it seemed to warp space, pierced Jin Taekyung’s body.
Or so the three S-rank monsters believed.
*BOOM!*
The earth flipped over with a deafening crash. Then a dark shadow fell overhead.
Their instincts awakened alongside the warning lights flashing in their minds.
These S-rank monsters were far too intelligent to dismiss as mere beasts. They understood at once what had happened, even as they struggled to accept what was right in front of them.
Power and qi greater than their own boiled inside that tiny, frail human body.
And then—
*Heavenly Strike.*
Jin Taekyung plunged toward the ground. Blue-white hellfire poured along White Flame’s spearhead and swept out in every direction.
*Fwoosh—KRAAAAAASH!*
Flames spread as wide as a Grand Mage’s Fire Wall spell, but burned hotter. They swallowed the front ranks of the monster army—horribly ravenous to behold, more ferocious than any beast.
—Aaaaaaagh!
—Kieeet!
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
System alerts mingled with the dying screams of monsters.
But they weren’t all that awaited Jin Taekyung as he rose from the blackened ash.
“How. Dare. You!”
The Lycanthrope Champion.
Trapped beneath the curse of the eternal moon, the strongest of the half-human, half-beast monsters roared and swung its enormous axe.
*Whoooom!*
Dark crimson magical power stormed through the air, cleaving space and wiping away the wind.
Just as the axe was about to split the human before it in two, White Flame’s fire-wreathed spearhead flashed upward.
*Clang!*
A sharp ring sounded. The impossibly sturdy axe blade burst apart.
*Crack—BOOM!*
Hundreds of fragments rained down on the monsters rushing to save their commander.
*Thud, thud, thud!*
Screams rose with sprays of blood. Corpses piled atop corpses.
The Lycanthrope Champion stood frozen, bright yellow eyes wide. Jin Taekyung brought his spearhead down toward it without a moment’s hesitation.
Or he would have, if not for the whistling sounds rushing in from both sides.
*Whoooosh!*
Jin Taekyung bent backward with lightning speed. His hair touched the ground as two fierce gusts swept barely clear of his face.
*Pip!*
His skin split under the pressure, sending a sharp sting through him. That was nothing. If it was the price of dodging the attacks, he’d gotten off absurdly cheap.
*I’ll pay them back with interest.*
His body moved before the thought was complete. Straightening, he released the spear shaft and thrust out both palms.
*Whoom—BOOM!*
A shockwave and crash shook the ground.
But the sword and claws, shrouded in immense magical power, canceled out the force of his Flame Divine Palm. They didn’t stop there.
*Shraaah!*
The Death Knight Legion Commander brought its sword down like a streak of light.
—Grrraaaah!
The Lycanthrope charged with a roar. Beside it, the Manticore Lord lashed its iron-hard, spike-covered tail like a whip.
*They’re working together? Monsters from different species?*
Jin Taekyung’s eyes widened at the attacks converging from three directions. That brief hesitation left the slightest opening.
*Fwoooosh! BOOM!*
Three S-rank monsters. Together, they struck with more destructive force than he could withstand even with his Scorching Yang Qi pushed to its limit.
And the Manticore Lord was even stronger and more cunning than he’d expected.
*Whoosh. Slice!*
Hot. As if someone had seared his thigh with fire.
Before he could fully feel the pain, three more flashes burst into view one after another.
*BOOM!*
A crash like the sky splitting open sent him flying backward.
Jin Taekyung twisted in midair, regained his balance, and threw a punch the instant he landed.
*Poom!*
Heat erupted from his fist. The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist swept forward, setting monsters ablaze. As they shrieked and burned, dark crimson magical power surged from among them.
*Whoooosh.*
Pressure bore down from every direction, snuffing out the flames in an instant.
The three S-rank monsters had cut down even their writhing subordinates without hesitation. They were about to charge Jin Taekyung again when a voice suddenly rang out.
“Good. That’s far enough.”
At the unmistakable sound of the Demon Realm language, they stopped in their tracks.
The Skeleton King grinned at them, then tossed a remark at Jin Taekyung.
“Madman.”
Jin Taekyung met his unfriendly look with a calm question.
“Why?”
“What am I supposed to do when you charge off alone like that? Weren’t we just saying we’d each take one?”
“I was testing them. Seeing which was strongest and which was weakest.”
The Skeleton King’s gaze dropped to Jin Taekyung’s thigh. It looked as though something had torn a chunk out of it, and blood covered the wound.
The Manticore Lord had struck there with the Fire Dragon Armor around Jin Taekyung’s upper body in mind. It was as clever as it was strong.
“Looks more like it tested your blood.”
“They’re stronger than I expected. One of them, especially, is practically a named monster even among the S-ranks.”
“Which one?”
“The one in the middle.”
“The Manticore? It does stand out, even at a glance.”
The Skeleton King glared at the Manticore Lord, his face hardening. His voice turned cold.
“So that’s the one that wounded you.”
“It’s not that bad. I’d be much better off taking the Manticore—”
“Fine. I’ll take the Death Knight.”
“What’s with that unpleasant look?”
“No, I just thought this was where you’d say you were going to avenge your friend or something.”
The Skeleton King’s eyes widened.
“What the hell are you talking about? We’ve got a much better chance if the strongest fight the strongest.”
“Anyway, it’s settled. You take the Manticore. I’ll take the Death Knight. And that Lycanthrope over there...”
He trailed off, looked around, and blinked.
“Why is it just the two of us?”
Jin Taekyung, who had staunched the bleeding in his thigh, kindly explained.
“One bastard already ran off.”
“Huh?”
“Maybe he had a shred of conscience left, because he didn’t run away entirely. He’s back there in the front ranks.”
Far away, Yamamoto Genji had sidled up beside Choi Minwoo and put on a determined expression. The Skeleton King spotted him and muttered, “I’m going to kill that bastard.”
“Sure. But first, let’s finish this damn fight as quickly as we can.”
Jin Taekyung spat out bloody phlegm and lowered his spear.
Behind him, flying monsters were already shrieking amid bursts of explosions.
*Magic Johnson can hold them off.*
He could only trust him, just as Johnson and the others had trusted him.
*Step. Thud.*
The three S-rank monsters stepped forward, and the entire army moved with them.
No matter how many they killed, the wave of monsters never seemed to shrink. And the open desert all around them was the worst possible battlefield for humans.
“You know what I regret most since I became a monster?” the Skeleton King asked.
Jin Taekyung answered without hesitation. “Not getting to go clubbing.”
“Wrong. Getting mixed up with you.”
“Really? I’m the exact opposite.”
“What?”
“One of the best things I’ve ever done was get you out of that Gate.”
“...Damn it. Am I the only piece of trash here?”
“You already know. Why ask?”
The Skeleton King let out a quiet laugh and took a deep breath. Deathly energy flowed out instead of breath, raising the monsters strewn around them.
One thousand in all.
That was the most he could maintain while fighting and commanding them at the same time. Against the vast army drawing nearer and steadily gaining speed, it was a meager force.
“Can we... hold them all back?”
No.
Jin Taekyung swallowed the answer on the tip of his tongue.
*Someone is going to die. No matter what.*
That was battle. That was war. There was no way to save everyone.
He couldn’t promise they would all make it out alive. He could promise one thing: revenge.
“No matter how many of us die here today...”
*Shing.*
As his words trailed off, he leveled his gleaming spearhead at the monsters.
“Every last one of them dies by my hand.”
The Skeleton King’s eyes widened.
*KRUNCH!*
A wave of monsters beyond counting crashed over them.
My ears rang. The movement of more than ten thousand monsters shook the ground, and their cries seemed to reach the ends of the earth and the sky above.
At the head of that army, right at its center, were the three of them.
*Fwoosh. Slice!*
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
A line of flame traced along the spearhead and cut through the air. Dozens of heads caught in its path, unable to dodge or block, rolled across the ground.
*Splatter!*
Blood sprayed a moment later. But the monsters that should have charged us with savage cries scattered instead, avoiding me and the Skeleton King.
Was it because of the martial prowess I’d shown? My Intimidation?
No. The monsters avoiding me to charge the Hunters weren’t afraid. They were obeying someone else.
The kind of obedience you saw only in trained elite troops.
“You’ve got to be fucking kidding me...!”
*Crunch!*
The Skeleton King blew apart an ogre’s head and shouted in anger.
Even with his undead army, the two of us couldn’t block every enemy’s path.
For every ten we killed, a hundred got through. For every hundred, a thousand monsters slipped past.
Our net was tightly woven, but far too small. And that was exactly what they intended.
“So it’s you. The human that person spoke of.”
The voice seemed to come from inside my head. Smooth and composed, like a nobleman’s, its tone betrayed a keen intelligence. Its words confirmed my suspicion.
“The Prophet. Where is he now?”
A mythical monster with the face and body of a tiger, the tusks of a boar, and the horns of a bull.
The Manticore Lord smiled.
“He is everywhere, and nowhere.”
“What the hell does that mean?” the Skeleton King asked.
“It means he’ll tell us if we beat the shit out of him.”
I brought my spearhead down toward the monster.
No—toward *them*.
*Shwoosh!*
The wind split apart.
