paragraphs: There’s an old saying that’s been passed down in the Murim for ages.

*A Third Rate swordsman gets beaten to death by street thugs. A Peak master dies fighting a master like himself. But the only things that can kill a Supreme Peak master are his own arrogance and carelessness.*
That was how martial artists saw Supreme Peak masters.
Beings to be marveled at and feared.
While everyone else wandered Murim’s treacherous mountains, they stood on the highest peaks and looked down on them all.
But there was no such thing as *invincible* in this world.
Even among those who reach the chosen realm, there are clear differences in strength.
People looking up from below couldn’t tell. Those who stood on peaks of their own could see and feel someone else beyond the thick fog—standing higher or lower than they were.
I was no different.
*Shwaa!*
A sharp gust burst from the spearhead as I slashed down at an angle.
It tore apart the limbs of monsters unlucky enough to cross its path and shot toward its target, only to die away amid a tremendous roar.
—Kyaaaaa!
The shockwave imbued with magical power faded along with the wind.
I stared at the monster that had canceled out my spear strike with a single roar.
*Strong.*
Magical power boiled all around me, prickling my skin. The air tasted bitter and stale with every breath.
*Manticore Lord.*
A monster straight out of myth. A leader strong enough to be called a *Lord* even among its own kind.
*Step.*
The moment its lion-like forepaw touched the blood-soaked sand, it vanished from where it stood and tore through space.
*Boom!*
As fast as the wind. Faster, even.
In some ways, it was far more troublesome than Leviathan, the last named monster I’d taken down.

Leviathan had possessed far more magical power. But the strength I’d felt from this thing earlier, together with the speed it was showing now and the size of its body, made it better suited to one-on-one combat than mass slaughter.
*And there’s the Lycanthrope Champion, too.*
I couldn’t afford to let my guard down.
I watched the two S-rank monsters and kicked off the ground at just the right moment, sending a Sound Transmission to the Skeleton King.
—Don’t lose and embarrass yourself.
No answer came.
The Death Knight Legion Commander had summoned a Nightmare—a ghost horse that was an A-rank monster in its own right—and was leaping high into the air to come crashing down on the Skeleton King.
*BOOM!*
A thunderous crash erupted behind me, already far off in the distance. The Skeleton King’s voice rang across the battlefield.
“A mere legion commander dares challenge me? Kneel before your king!”
It would have been ideal if the Death Knight Legion Commander had knelt and sworn allegiance. But reality wasn’t so accommodating.
They already served another master, and right now a tail and claws brimming with magical power were bearing down on me.
*BANG!*
The spearhead of White Flame shuddered as I held it upright to block the attack.
But unlike our earlier clash, this time *they* were the ones who had to back off.
*Whoosh! Slice!*
I brought the spearhead down without hesitation. It sliced through the half-man, half-beast Lycanthrope Champion’s huge, hook-like claw as easily as tofu.
*Not a difficult opponent.*
If it were the only one.
—Grr?

The Lycanthrope Champion let out a startled growl and stumbled backward. I was about to cut it in two when the Manticore Lord’s tail—knocked aside by my spear—writhed like a snake and lunged for my face.
*Whoom!*
The wind pressure brushing past my neck felt as heavy as a block of iron.
But I’d already seen that move once.
If I’d been facing all three of them alone, I would have been in real trouble. Now, things were different.
*One at a time.*
*Fwoosh.*
The Lycanthrope Champion saw the flames gathering in my hand and twisted away, but it was half a beat too late.
No. I was faster.
*BOOM!*
The Flame Divine Palm struck it dead-on and sent it sliding backward. It clutched its blackened arm and let out a roar that sounded almost like a scream.
—GRAAAAAH!
Too bad.
It was the weakest of the three, but an S-rank monster was still an S-rank monster. My strike had missed its intended target—its chest—by a hair.
*One strike. One more will finish it.*
But the Manticore Lord was every bit as cunning as it was strong.
Just as I moved to swing my spear and finish off the Lycanthrope, it came for my back faster than it had moved at any point so far.
*BOOM!*
I blocked the claw that crashed down like lightning.
The spear shaft shook under the tremendous pressure, and my legs—usually free to move even in the desert—sank deep into the sand.
That, too, was part of its plan.
*Shwaa! Thud!*
Its tail slammed into my side with more weight and force than a battering ram.
The stinger on its tip couldn’t pierce all the way through my Fire Dragon Armor, but I had to bear the full force of the tremendous impact it delivered.
My vision went hazy. Something hot surged up through my chest.
I swallowed the blood rising in my throat and reached out through the blur.
*Open Inventory. Summon.*
As one hand left the spear shaft, the pressure on it grew heavier. I drew a dagger from my Inventory and swung it in a flash.
*Shhk, slice!*
There was only one sound of cutting, but three thin lines appeared across the iron-hard tail.
The Manticore Lord’s eyes widened as it tried to crush me beneath its two massive forepaws.
*FWOOSH!*
Blood belatedly sprayed from the faint lines like a fountain.
Its jaws gaped wide in pain, releasing the stench of countless deaths.
—GRAAAAAAAH!
The lion-like roar it unleashed right in my face left my ears ringing.
No. My eardrums had to have burst.
*You son of a bitch.*
I clenched my teeth, feeling hot blood run from my ears.
As the force bearing down on me briefly eased, I drove the dagger still in my hand into its ribs.
*Thud!*
The Force on the dagger came from Scorching Yang Qi.
Its lava-like heat cut through tough hide and flesh, broke bone, and burned through what lay inside.
*Sssss!*
—GRAAAAH!
—Kyaaaaa!
The Manticore Lord’s cry seemed to come twice, the sounds overlapping like audio from broken earbuds. Maybe it was because my eardrums had burst.
But my instincts told me I wasn’t imagining it.
*This...*
They were different cries. I hadn’t misheard.
The first was a scream of pain. The second was a roar of rage.
And my bad feelings were never wrong.
*Lycanthrope Champion.*
As its name came to mind, the half-man, half-beast monster I’d briefly forgotten lunged at me from behind.
*Shwaa!*
Its speed was dazzling—every bit worthy of an S-rank monster.
One arm swung at its side as though it might crumble to ash at any moment. The other was still sound, and when it swept that arm toward me, its hooked claws flashed.
*Too late to pull out the dagger and swing it.*
Countless movements and possible futures flashed through my mind in that instant.
In the end, only one choice remained.
As the world seemed to slow around me, I let go of the dagger lodged in the Manticore Lord’s ribs and thrust out my palm.
*Fwoosh—crack!*
The internal energy I’d hurriedly drawn up scattered. Flames burst apart.
Dizzying pain shot through my hand. I stared at the silver claw that had pierced my palm and emerged from the back of it.
*...Fuck.*
It had stopped just short of my face. I couldn’t help swearing.
But that wasn’t the end of the pain waiting for me.
*Crack. Crunch!*
Bones shifted, and a neck stretched out like a turtle’s.
With my life hanging in the balance, the Manticore Lord finally used the ability it had cunningly kept hidden. Its neck shot over the spear shaft between us, bringing its jaws straight at me.
—GRAAH!
Its mouth gaped all the way to its ears like a ghost from a horror story, reeking of rotting corpses. At the sight of its huge, saw-toothed teeth, every hair on my body seemed to stand on end.
A chill ran down my spine.
If those jaws closed on me, I was dead.
I twisted with all my strength. The teeth that had been about to swallow my head whole brushed my hair and sank into my collarbone.
Or rather, into the red armor covering it.
*CRUNCH!*
*Beep. Beep-beep!*

**System** Part of your **Fire Dragon Armor** has been damaged! The durability of your **Fire Dragon Armor** has dropped significantly! **Danger! Danger!** If you are exposed to another attack like that, your **Fire Dragon Armor** may be automatically returned to your Inventory! **Manticore Lord’s Venom** has entered through a gap in the damaged armor! Status abnormality **Poisoned** has been applied! Detoxify as soon as possible! If you do not detoxify within the time limit, your condition may worsen!
*Damn it. What the hell is this now?*
I’d thought my collarbone felt a little prickly. Now, out of nowhere, it was venom?
All I’d been born with was a pair of balls. This bastard was named-monster level, and it had more damn abilities than I could count.
“...Human!”
Even in the middle of his own fight, the Skeleton King had somehow seen what happened. His urgent shout came from far behind me.
But despite his worry, I had no intention of dying here. Not even the slightest.
If anything, I was almost glad that being **Poisoned** had dulled my senses.
At least now I wouldn’t feel much pain from what I was about to do.
“Thanks for the help, you son of a bitch.”
At my barely audible whisper, the Manticore Lord’s eyes widened.
I dropped White Flame from my free hand and slammed that hand into what I guessed was its throat.
*Thwack!*
A heavy blow.
The Manticore Lord caught its breath, malice filling its eyes.
*Thud!*
Its teeth drove in harder than before, prying open the gap in my Fire Dragon Armor and sinking deep into my collarbone.
*Beep. Beep-beep.* The warnings rang in my ears, but the pain had faded even further. I could move my hand without a care, though its palm was little more than raw flesh caught on a hook.
*Crack.*
The Lycanthrope Champion’s claw was still lodged through my palm. It bared its teeth at me in a sneer.
Pure contempt.
The sneer lasted only an instant.
—Grr?
Its face filled with surprise. No matter how hard it strained, it couldn’t make me budge. As it blinked at me, I spoke calmly.
“You think I can’t beat *you*, you little shit, just because I’m in bad shape?”
On Strength stats alone, I had seniority over an ogre’s dad.
Even with all my stats drastically reduced by the special debuff, my physical abilities were still comparable to—or better than—those of most S-rank monsters.
And the Lycanthrope Champion was built for Agility, not Strength. I could slam it into the ground with one hand.
“Now, you little punk... Attention!”
*Whack! Crunch!*
I kicked its knee joint, shattering it in an instant.
As the strongest of the half-man, half-beast warriors let out a mournful cry, I kept a firm grip on its claw and slammed the monster into the ground.
*Whoom—BANG!*
The impact raised a cloud of dust. At the same time, blood spurted from my palm as the claw tore free.
But only one thing mattered.
At last, I had a free hand.
*Open Inventory. Summon.*
A sharp dagger flashed. Above it, blazing hellfire surged and flew toward the Manticore Lord’s head.
The Lycanthrope Champion realized my plan and threw itself forward.
Too late.
*Thud—KRAAAAAASH!*
The blade cut through hide and shattered flesh and bone. Flames exploded.
*Ding.*
Just as the clear chime I’d been waiting for rang in my ears, a flash of light suddenly swept in from somewhere and cut through the Lycanthrope Champion’s neck as it charged at me.
*Slice!*
“I’m here, Jin Sama!”
This son of a bitch stole my kill.

sentences.text: There’s an old saying that’s been passed down in the Murim for ages.
*A Third Rate swordsman gets beaten to death by street thugs.
A Peak master dies fighting a master like himself.
But the only things that can kill a Supreme Peak master are his own arrogance and carelessness.*
That was how martial artists saw Supreme Peak masters.
Beings to be marveled at and feared.
While everyone else wandered Murim’s treacherous mountains, they stood on the highest peaks and looked down on them all.
But there was no such thing as *invincible* in this world.
Even among those who reach the chosen realm, there are clear differences in strength.
People looking up from below couldn’t tell.
Those who stood on peaks of their own could see and feel someone else beyond the thick fog—standing higher or lower than they were.
I was no different.
*Shwaa!*
A sharp gust burst from the spearhead as I slashed down at an angle.
It tore apart the limbs of monsters unlucky enough to cross its path and shot toward its target, only to die away amid a tremendous roar.
—Kyaaaaa!
The shockwave imbued with magical power faded along with the wind.
I stared at the monster that had canceled out my spear strike with a single roar.
*Strong.*
Magical power boiled all around me, prickling my skin.
The air tasted bitter and stale with every breath.
*Manticore Lord.*
A monster straight out of myth.
A leader strong enough to be called a *Lord* even among its own kind.
*Step.*
The moment its lion-like forepaw touched the blood-soaked sand, it vanished from where it stood and tore through space.
*Boom!*
As fast as the wind.
Faster, even.
In some ways, it was far more troublesome than Leviathan, the last named monster I’d taken down.
Leviathan had possessed far more magical power.
But the strength I’d felt from this thing earlier, together with the speed it was showing now and the size of its body, made it better suited to one-on-one combat than mass slaughter.
*And there’s the Lycanthrope Champion, too.*
I couldn’t afford to let my guard down.
I watched the two S-rank monsters and kicked off the ground at just the right moment, sending a Sound Transmission to the Skeleton King.
—Don’t lose and embarrass yourself.
No answer came.
The Death Knight Legion Commander had summoned a Nightmare—a ghost horse that was an A-rank monster in its own right—and was leaping high into the air to come crashing down on the Skeleton King.
*BOOM!*
A thunderous crash erupted behind me, already far off in the distance.
The Skeleton King’s voice rang across the battlefield.
“A mere legion commander dares challenge me?
Kneel before your king!”
It would have been ideal if the Death Knight Legion Commander had knelt and sworn allegiance.
But reality wasn’t so accommodating.
They already served another master, and right now a tail and claws brimming with magical power were bearing down on me.
*BANG!*
The spearhead of White Flame shuddered as I held it upright to block the attack.
But unlike our earlier clash, this time *they* were the ones who had to back off.
*Whoosh!
Slice!*
I brought the spearhead down without hesitation.
It sliced through the half-man, half-beast Lycanthrope Champion’s huge, hook-like claw as easily as tofu.
*Not a difficult opponent.*
If it were the only one.
—Grr?
The Lycanthrope Champion let out a startled growl and stumbled backward.
I was about to cut it in two when the Manticore Lord’s tail—knocked aside by my spear—writhed like a snake and lunged for my face.
*Whoom!*
The wind pressure brushing past my neck felt as heavy as a block of iron.
But I’d already seen that move once.
If I’d been facing all three of them alone, I would have been in real trouble.
Now, things were different.
*One at a time.*
*Fwoosh.*
The Lycanthrope Champion saw the flames gathering in my hand and twisted away, but it was half a beat too late.
No.
I was faster.
*BOOM!*
The Flame Divine Palm struck it dead-on and sent it sliding backward.
It clutched its blackened arm and let out a roar that sounded almost like a scream.
—GRAAAAAH!
Too bad.
It was the weakest of the three, but an S-rank monster was still an S-rank monster.
My strike had missed its intended target—its chest—by a hair.
*One strike.
One more will finish it.*
But the Manticore Lord was every bit as cunning as it was strong.
Just as I moved to swing my spear and finish off the Lycanthrope, it came for my back faster than it had moved at any point so far.
*BOOM!*
I blocked the claw that crashed down like lightning.
The spear shaft shook under the tremendous pressure, and my legs—usually free to move even in the desert—sank deep into the sand.
That, too, was part of its plan.
*Shwaa!
Thud!*
Its tail slammed into my side with more weight and force than a battering ram.
The stinger on its tip couldn’t pierce all the way through my Fire Dragon Armor, but I had to bear the full force of the tremendous impact it delivered.
My vision went hazy.
Something hot surged up through my chest.
I swallowed the blood rising in my throat and reached out through the blur.
*Open Inventory.
Summon.*
As one hand left the spear shaft, the pressure on it grew heavier.
I drew a dagger from my Inventory and swung it in a flash.
*Shhk, slice!*
There was only one sound of cutting, but three thin lines appeared across the iron-hard tail.
The Manticore Lord’s eyes widened as it tried to crush me beneath its two massive forepaws.
*FWOOSH!*
Blood belatedly sprayed from the faint lines like a fountain.
Its jaws gaped wide in pain, releasing the stench of countless deaths.
—GRAAAAAAAH!
The lion-like roar it unleashed right in my face left my ears ringing.
No.
My eardrums had to have burst.
*You son of a bitch.*
I clenched my teeth, feeling hot blood run from my ears.
As the force bearing down on me briefly eased, I drove the dagger still in my hand into its ribs.
*Thud!*
The Force on the dagger came from Scorching Yang Qi.
Its lava-like heat cut through tough hide and flesh, broke bone, and burned through what lay inside.
*Sssss!*
—GRAAAAH!
—Kyaaaaa!
The Manticore Lord’s cry seemed to come twice, the sounds overlapping like audio from broken earbuds.
Maybe it was because my eardrums had burst.
But my instincts told me I wasn’t imagining it.
*This...*
They were different cries.
I hadn’t misheard.
The first was a scream of pain.
The second was a roar of rage.
And my bad feelings were never wrong.
*Lycanthrope Champion.*
As its name came to mind, the half-man, half-beast monster I’d briefly forgotten lunged at me from behind.
*Shwaa!*
Its speed was dazzling—every bit worthy of an S-rank monster.
One arm swung at its side as though it might crumble to ash at any moment.
The other was still sound, and when it swept that arm toward me, its hooked claws flashed.
*Too late to pull out the dagger and swing it.*
Countless movements and possible futures flashed through my mind in that instant.
In the end, only one choice remained.
As the world seemed to slow around me, I let go of the dagger lodged in the Manticore Lord’s ribs and thrust out my palm.
*Fwoosh—crack!*
The internal energy I’d hurriedly drawn up scattered.
Flames burst apart.
Dizzying pain shot through my hand.
I stared at the silver claw that had pierced my palm and emerged from the back of it.
*...Fuck.*
It had stopped just short of my face.
I couldn’t help swearing.
But that wasn’t the end of the pain waiting for me.
*Crack.
Crunch!*
Bones shifted, and a neck stretched out like a turtle’s.
With my life hanging in the balance, the Manticore Lord finally used the ability it had cunningly kept hidden.
Its neck shot over the spear shaft between us, bringing its jaws straight at me.
—GRAAH!
Its mouth gaped all the way to its ears like a ghost from a horror story, reeking of rotting corpses.
At the sight of its huge, saw-toothed teeth, every hair on my body seemed to stand on end.
A chill ran down my spine.
If those jaws closed on me, I was dead.
I twisted with all my strength.
The teeth that had been about to swallow my head whole brushed my hair and sank into my collarbone.
Or rather, into the red armor covering it.
*CRUNCH!*
*Beep.
Beep-beep!*
**System** Part of your **Fire Dragon Armor** has been damaged!
The durability of your **Fire Dragon Armor** has dropped significantly! **Danger!

Danger!** If you are exposed to another attack like that, your **Fire Dragon Armor** may be automatically returned to your Inventory! **Manticore Lord’s Venom** has entered through a gap in the damaged armor!
Status abnormality **Poisoned** has been applied!
Detoxify as soon as possible!
If you do not detoxify within the time limit, your condition may worsen!
*Damn it.
What the hell is this now?*
I’d thought my collarbone felt a little prickly.
Now, out of nowhere, it was venom?
All I’d been born with was a pair of balls.
This bastard was named-monster level, and it had more damn abilities than I could count.
“...Human!”
Even in the middle of his own fight, the Skeleton King had somehow seen what happened.
His urgent shout came from far behind me.
But despite his worry, I had no intention of dying here.
Not even the slightest.
If anything, I was almost glad that being **Poisoned** had dulled my senses.
At least now I wouldn’t feel much pain from what I was about to do.
“Thanks for the help, you son of a bitch.”
At my barely audible whisper, the Manticore Lord’s eyes widened.
I dropped White Flame from my free hand and slammed that hand into what I guessed was its throat.
*Thwack!*
A heavy blow.
The Manticore Lord caught its breath, malice filling its eyes.
*Thud!*
Its teeth drove in harder than before, prying open the gap in my Fire Dragon Armor and sinking deep into my collarbone.
*Beep.
Beep-beep.* The warnings rang in my ears, but the pain had faded even further.
I could move my hand without a care, though its palm was little more than raw flesh caught on a hook.
*Crack.*
The Lycanthrope Champion’s claw was still lodged through my palm.
It bared its teeth at me in a sneer.
Pure contempt.
The sneer lasted only an instant.
—Grr?
Its face filled with surprise.
No matter how hard it strained, it couldn’t make me budge.
As it blinked at me, I spoke calmly.
“You think I can’t beat *you*, you little shit, just because I’m in bad shape?”
On Strength stats alone, I had seniority over an ogre’s dad.
Even with all my stats drastically reduced by the special debuff, my physical abilities were still comparable to—or better than—those of most S-rank monsters.
And the Lycanthrope Champion was built for Agility, not Strength.
I could slam it into the ground with one hand.
“Now, you little punk...
Attention!”
*Whack!
Crunch!*
I kicked its knee joint, shattering it in an instant.
As the strongest of the half-man, half-beast warriors let out a mournful cry, I kept a firm grip on its claw and slammed the monster into the ground.
*Whoom—BANG!*
The impact raised a cloud of dust.
At the same time, blood spurted from my palm as the claw tore free.
But only one thing mattered.
At last, I had a free hand.
*Open Inventory.
Summon.*
A sharp dagger flashed.
Above it, blazing hellfire surged and flew toward the Manticore Lord’s head.
The Lycanthrope Champion realized my plan and threw itself forward.
Too late.
*Thud—KRAAAAAASH!*
The blade cut through hide and shattered flesh and bone.
Flames exploded.
*Ding.*
Just as the clear chime I’d been waiting for rang in my ears, a flash of light suddenly swept in from somewhere and cut through the Lycanthrope Champion’s neck as it charged at me.
*Slice!*
“I’m here, Jin Sama!”
This son of a bitch stole my kill.

chapters.title: Chapter 807
paragraphs: Even a Supreme Peak master will go down if he gets kicked in the balls. No matter how strange or powerful a monster is, its weaknesses are much like a human’s.
Blow its head off, or burst its heart.
Of course, there are exceptions to everything.
Some Trolls can put even a shattered head back together. Golems won’t fall until you destroy the core hidden somewhere inside them.
A Lich, both undead and a skilled black wizard, might store part of its soul in a Life Force Vessel.
But as far as I knew, there wasn’t a Lycanthrope anywhere that could survive having its head cut off.
Not even an S-rank monster that had earned the title of Champion as the strongest warrior of its kind.
“I’m here, Jin Sama!”
I looked back and forth between Yamamoto Genji, who was chattering so loudly he was spitting, and the headless body of the EXP... No, the Lycanthrope Champion.
*No, fuck...*
What kind of bullshit was this?
It had been the perfect time to level up. The meal was already laid out in front of me, and some bastard had swooped in and gobbled it all up.
I was so furious my hands and feet felt ready to shake.
*Beep.*
**System** Status abnormality **Convulsions** has been applied! Status abnormality **Poisoned** is worsening! **Manticore Lord’s Venom** must be removed from your body as soon as possible!
Right. No wonder my hands were shaking so much.
I was already in bad shape, and the anger made my vision blur for a moment.
If things had gone as I’d calculated, I’d have leveled up by now and recovered completely. Since that hadn’t happened, I had no choice but to use another method.
“Uh? Jin Sama, is something wrong?”
“Do I look like I’m all right, you fucking idiot?”
“Ah. Oh...”
That shut Yamamoto Genji up. I gave the command in my head.
*Open Inventory. Summon.*
The System manifested in response to the command.
*Shk.*
The moment my trembling fingers touched something cold, a clear chime rang out, different from the earlier ones.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*

**System** Equipped **Myriad-Poison Ring**. An unknown energy washes over your entire body! The **Myriad-Poison Ring** has absorbed **Manticore Lord’s Venom**! Status abnormality **Poisoned** has been removed! Status abnormality **Convulsions** has been removed!
As the chimes rang one after another, my vision cleared and the convulsions stopped.
The Myriad-Poison Ring had drawn in the poison spreading from my collarbone through the rest of my body. It gleamed with its familiar black light.
*I didn’t level up, but thank God I had the Myriad-Poison Ring.*
It was a good thing I’d ended the fight quickly. The venom the Manticore Lord had carried was truly terrifying.

With Scorching Yang Qi, which was the natural enemy of poison, and a top-grade potion, I could have been cured without much difficulty. But a potion ultimately worked by paying in advance with the body’s energy and vitality to maximize its recovery.
With so many enemies still out there, a risk-free level-up would have been a hundred times better.
Of course...
“A-are you all right?”
Some bastard had been hanging back, watching for an opening, then rushed in and stole the last hit from me.
“Forget it. Don’t worry about it.”
But what could I do?
The bus had already left, and I didn’t have time to stand at an empty bus stop waiting for the next one and slap Yamamoto Genji across the face.
The one bit of good news amid all the bad was that the Skeleton King was the kind of excellent monster who knew how to finish his assigned job on time.
*Crack-crunch!*
We’d gotten quite far apart while fighting our respective opponents, but I could clearly see—and hear—the Death Knight, well over two meters tall, crumple along with his armor.
I heard its final scream, too.
—GRAAAAAAH!
*Fwoosh!*
That was the end.

Black mist flowed out from beneath the helmet pulled low over its face. The Skeleton King absorbed the Death Knight’s soul as it escaped just before Erasure, as though sucking it in. Then he grinned at me as I approached using qinggong.
“You monster.”
He spotted Yamamoto Genji tucked under my arm like a piece of luggage and added, “That fucking bastard.”
I agreed. If that little shit had held up the Lycanthrope Champion for even a moment, everything would’ve ended much more smoothly.

But kicking Yamamoto Genji in the joints in the middle of a battle involving thousands—tens of thousands—of fighters would be something only a lunatic would do. If I had time for that, I needed to use it to save one more person.
“Let’s go.”
With that brief word, I shot forward. My limbs creaked, proof of the fierce battle that had just taken place, and my internal energy was considerably depleted.
Even so, I had to go. I had to fight.
*Shweee—BOOM!*
The spearhead of White Flame, sent flying with tremendous force, swept through the rear of the monster army swarming like ants.
A muffled boom swallowed their screams, and flames burst out, burning the living monsters’ limbs.
*One more.*
I kept running without slowing down.
I pulled another spear from my Inventory, gripped it in a reverse hold, and hurled it.
*Boom!*
A thunderous crack split the desert.
The spear didn’t carry as much internal energy as the first, but the sheer force and speed behind its spearhead were enough to pierce dozens of monsters.
*Crack-crunch!*
—GRAAAH!
Even a glancing blow burst heads like watermelons and sent severed limbs flying.
The monster army, which had seemed as though it would never shrink no matter how many I killed, began to falter.
*Boom!*
—Grrk, gaaah!
The screams drew closer by the moment. The stench grew stronger.
By the time I hurled a third spear, hundreds had already fallen. I kicked off the air and soared upward, flung Yamamoto Genji from under my arm toward the ground, and reached out.
*Come.*
*Shweee! Snap!*
White Flame answered my call through the Middle Dantian and flew into my hand.
Its grip had become so familiar that I could recognize it without looking.
As soon as I reclaimed it, I poured in Scorching Yang Qi. The transparent spearhead took on a reddish glow.
*Fwoosh.*
Flames. Wind. A world moving slowly.
And... the eyes staring blankly at me as I soared through the air, with the entire battlefield laid out below.
*Whoosh.*
The wind brushed across my body. Time, which had stopped, gradually returned to its usual pace.
I saw opposite emotions appear in countless wide eyes.
There was joy in some. In others, despair was slowly sinking into reality.
Humans and monsters. Monsters and humans.
No one there needed to be told which side felt which.
*Fire Dragon Divine Spear. This form.*
I drew in a breath.
My body descended slowly, keeping pace with time as I perceived it, while the flame-filled spearhead rose high, as if to pierce the sky.
*Fwoosh.*
At that moment, when the space around me warped under the extreme heat, a massive shadow that had been circling over the Hunters surrounded by monsters shot toward me.
—Screee!
A piercing cry rang in my ears.
I didn’t have to look to sense its approach. Unlike the other monsters, it flew toward me like a streak of light. The gale raised by a single flap of its wings carried immense magical power.
*The leader of the Griffins.*
Yeah. It had to be.
As a flying monster that ranged through the sky as if it owned it, it was one of the most troublesome opponents in its own way.
But...
*It doesn’t matter.*
Ignoring the Griffins rushing at me with a gale of magical power, I brought the spearhead down.
Heavenly Strike.
*Whoooooom!*
Flames poured over the spearhead of White Flame, wiping out the gale of magical power rushing toward me and cleaving through space.
A fierce, razor-sharp slash like a dragon’s claw descended on the center of the tightly packed monster army.
*Fwoosh!*
The heat and flash were so intense they seemed capable of melting everything before they even touched it.
Hellfire engulfed hundreds—perhaps a thousand—monsters and exploded.
*BOOM! Rumble-rumble!*
A rain of fire poured down. Screams and death flowed like lava.
Neither the hides of the upper-level monsters—unmarked even by bullets—nor the quick-footed lower-level ones who sensed danger and tried to flee could escape it.
Death was equal for all the monsters, and the leader of the Griffins watching the scene let out a roar like a scream.
—Kyaaaah!
*Whoom.* A heavy pressure pushed against my whole body.
I raised my head. The leader of the Griffins, already overhead, was shooting toward me.
Even within its massive shadow, which blocked the sunlight, the monster’s beak shone like the sun, packed with immense magical power.
If I met that attack head-on?
Even I wouldn’t come away unscathed.
At the fork in the road I’d faced a moment ago, I’d chosen not to fight it, but to break up the monster army’s formation.
But—
“I don’t have to be the one to do it. Right?”
At the Demon Realm language carried through the System, the flying beast’s pupils narrowed into vertical slits.
A moment’s hesitation at the very end.
And those who had been waiting for that moment didn’t let me down.
*Shwoop! Clang!*
The Griffin leader knocked aside something that flew up from the ground with a sharp crack, then staggered under the force of the blow.
*That’s...*
A spear made of bone.
As it fell to the ground, its job done, I thought of one person—or rather, one monster.
The Skeleton King.
That bastard never got tired, yet he was so much slower than me. He’d finally made it here.
But the person I’d really been counting on was someone else.
*Rumble.*
The air all around us shuddered. Everyone here, not just me, felt the battlefield’s atmosphere grow heavy.
I felt the wind die down in an instant, and the enormous mana rising from somewhere deep below press down on the battlefield.
—Screep?
The leader and around a hundred Griffins looked at one another in confusion.
They were no longer beating their wings.
No. Someone had bound them in midair.
“Rise, then crash back down.”
The voice that followed held none of its usual cheer. It was bleak and subdued.
“Reverse Gravity.”
And then—
*Whoooooom!*
Gravity within the area went wild.
Mana seized the remaining flying monsters with measured precision and slammed them into the ground.
—Screee!
As I listened to the Griffin leader cry out, a thought struck me.
What did you call the sight of around a hundred massive Griffins plummeting from hundreds of meters up like streaks of light?
A spectacular view? Or...
*Magic?*
At least one thing was certain.
The Grand Mage who’d staged this incredible end to the battle deserved to be called the world’s greatest War Mage.
*Rumble! Crack-crunch!*
The flames spread without end. Chaos took hold. Countless monsters were crushed beneath the Griffins’ huge bodies as they rained down like a meteor shower.
I looked over the monster army, its center utterly broken, and shouted with internal energy behind my voice.
“Formation! Change!”
This battle was already won.
“Kill every last one of those bastards!”
A mighty roar shook heaven and earth. A thousand spears and blades, still sharp, surged forward like a wave.

I saw opposite emotions appear in countless wide eyes.
There was joy in some.
In others, despair was slowly sinking into reality.
Humans and monsters.
Monsters and humans.
No one there needed to be told which side felt which.
*Fire Dragon Divine Spear.
This form.*
I drew in a breath.
My body descended slowly, keeping pace with time as I perceived it, while the flame-filled spearhead rose high, as if to pierce the sky.
*Fwoosh.*
At that moment, when the space around me warped under the extreme heat, a massive shadow that had been circling over the Hunters surrounded by monsters shot toward me.
—Screee!
A piercing cry rang in my ears.
I didn’t have to look to sense its approach.
Unlike the other monsters, it flew toward me like a streak of light.
The gale raised by a single flap of its wings carried immense magical power.
*The leader of the Griffins.*
Yeah.
It had to be.
As a flying monster that ranged through the sky as if it owned it, it was one of the most troublesome opponents in its own way.
But...
*It doesn’t matter.*
Ignoring the Griffins rushing at me with a gale of magical power, I brought the spearhead down.
Heavenly Strike.
*Whoooooom!*
Flames poured over the spearhead of White Flame, wiping out the gale of magical power rushing toward me and cleaving through space.
A fierce, razor-sharp slash like a dragon’s claw descended on the center of the tightly packed monster army.
*Fwoosh!*
The heat and flash were so intense they seemed capable of melting everything before they even touched it.
Hellfire engulfed hundreds—perhaps a thousand—monsters and exploded.
*BOOM!
Rumble-rumble!*
A rain of fire poured down.
Screams and death flowed like lava.
Neither the hides of the upper-level monsters—unmarked even by bullets—nor the quick-footed lower-level ones who sensed danger and tried to flee could escape it.
Death was equal for all the monsters, and the leader of the Griffins watching the scene let out a roar like a scream.
—Kyaaaah!
*Whoom.* A heavy pressure pushed against my whole body.
I raised my head.
The leader of the Griffins, already overhead, was shooting toward me.
Even within its massive shadow, which blocked the sunlight, the monster’s beak shone like the sun, packed with immense magical power.
If I met that attack head-on?
Even I wouldn’t come away unscathed.
At the fork in the road I’d faced a moment ago, I’d chosen not to fight it, but to break up the monster army’s formation.
But—
“I don’t have to be the one to do it.
Right?”
At the Demon Realm language carried through the System, the flying beast’s pupils narrowed into vertical slits.
A moment’s hesitation at the very end.
And those who had been waiting for that moment didn’t let me down.
*Shwoop!
Clang!*
The Griffin leader knocked aside something that flew up from the ground with a sharp crack, then staggered under the force of the blow.
*That’s...*
A spear made of bone.
As it fell to the ground, its job done, I thought of one person—or rather, one monster.
The Skeleton King.
That bastard never got tired, yet he was so much slower than me.
He’d finally made it here.
But the person I’d really been counting on was someone else.
*Rumble.*
The air all around us shuddered.
Everyone here, not just me, felt the battlefield’s atmosphere grow heavy.
I felt the wind die down in an instant, and the enormous mana rising from somewhere deep below press down on the battlefield.
—Screep?
The leader and around a hundred Griffins looked at one another in confusion.
They were no longer beating their wings.
No.
Someone had bound them in midair.
“Rise, then crash back down.”
The voice that followed held none of its usual cheer.
It was bleak and subdued.
“Reverse Gravity.”
And then—
*Whoooooom!*
Gravity within the area went wild.
Mana seized the remaining flying monsters with measured precision and slammed them into the ground.
—Screee!
As I listened to the Griffin leader cry out, a thought struck me.
What did you call the sight of around a hundred massive Griffins plummeting from hundreds of meters up like streaks of light?
A spectacular view?
Or...
*Magic?*
At least one thing was certain.
The Grand Mage who’d staged this incredible end to the battle deserved to be called the world’s greatest War Mage.
*Rumble!
Crack-crunch!*
The flames spread without end.
Chaos took hold.
Countless monsters were crushed beneath the Griffins’ huge bodies as they rained down like a meteor shower.
I looked over the monster army, its center utterly broken, and shouted with internal energy behind my voice.
“Formation!
Change!”
This battle was already won.
“Kill every last one of those bastards!”
A mighty roar shook heaven and earth.
A thousand spears and blades, still sharp, surged forward like a wave.

chapters.title: Chapter 808
paragraphs: The Great Cataclysm was a massive event that changed the course of human history.
Naturally, it became the subject of countless studies and analyses. Scholars around the world identified three decisive reasons humanity had won.
First: the existence of Cheon Taemin.
Second, the emergence of the Awakened, who would come to be known as Hunters.
And third:
*Human intelligence and will.*
They were right.
If Cheon Taemin’s existence and the emergence of the Awakened had been unexpected salvation, human intelligence and will were what allowed us to overcome any crisis.
They were the reason humanity had won—and the monsters had lost.
Decades ago.
And... at this very moment.
*CRRRRACK!*
With a tremendous roar, a thousand Hunters surged forward like a wave.

The healers’ blessings rained down on the tanks, who had exhausted every ounce of strength holding back the monsters pouring in from all sides. The towering Grand Mage dispelled the defensive magic that had enveloped the area and revealed his true power.
“Burn as much as you like. Cut straight through.”
Mana surged at his boiling command.

A spell on this scale would have taken an ordinary mage several minutes to prepare. Yet Magic Johnson swept his staff through the air, and the Magic Formation that appeared above him activated after only a short incantation.
“Fire Wall.”
*Fwoosh—WHOOOOSH!*
Flames carrying terrible heat raced in every direction. They burned through thick scales, melted flesh and bone, and split the monster army’s ranks down the middle.
—Kyaaaaaah!
Cries of pain rang out as an acrid stench rose all around us.
The wide-area spell had torn straight through their packed formation. Amid the chaos, a higher-level monster that seemed fairly intelligent hurried to pull the broken ranks back together.
Or tried to.
—Alu. Karsh...!
*CRUNCH!*
I dropped onto it from above and burst its hard skull with a punch packed with internal energy.
*Ding.*
**System** You have defeated the Lv. 101 Minotaur Warrior! You have gained a small amount of EXP!
*Stagger. Thud.*
With the System notification, its stumbling body fell like a rotten log.
I spat a wad of phlegm onto the corpse, adjusted my grip on White Flame, and muttered, “You piece of shit. Way to ruin the moment.”
The monsters around me blinked at the sight of me dropping out of the sky like a comet. They had the innocent eyes of herbivores gathered by a stream.
But I knew better.
Those eyes looked gentle only because the creatures behind them were so stupid. The instincts hidden beneath that look were more savage and cruel than those of any other living thing.
—Grrk?
“Nice meeting you. Goodbye.”
With that first and last greeting, I spun and swung my spearhead.
*CRRRACK!*
Bone separated from flesh, and a haze of blood filled the air. Dozens fell to the first strike. I stepped forward and swung again, clearing the space around me.
*Squish.*
As I approached, stepping through the blood-soaked sand, the air around me gave a sharp, tingling hum.
Scorching Yang Qi stirred up intense heat, but the monsters’ eyes had gone cold long ago.
One Against a Thousand.

My overwhelming martial prowess and aura radiated outward. **Intimidation**, so palpable I could almost reach out and touch it, tightened around their bodies. Fear wiped away their ferocity and swallowed their instincts.
The Hunters had waited patiently for this moment. They didn’t miss it.
*CRUNCH!*
“Charge! Wipe them all out!”
“Die, you bastards!”
*Clang-clang! Slice!*
With a tremendous roar, a shining wave of steel crashed into the monsters.
The battle had been relatively short, but these elites had held their ground against a force more than ten times their size without taking heavy losses.

After holding back for so long against the endless tide, the Hunters seized their chance. They drove into the ranks Magic Johnson’s spell had broken apart, stabbing and slashing at every monster in their path.
*Slice, thud-thud-thud!*
“God damn it! Motherfucker!”
—GRAAAAAH!
Curses and screams mingled as aura and magical power, light and darkness, clashed all around us.
And with every passing second, the balance tipped further toward the light.
“Team Three, watch two o’clock! Circle around and break through!”
“Ranged unit, ready! Fire!”
“Fire!”
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh—BOOM!*
Arrows whistled through the air in a sudden rain. The mages’ wide-area spells swept across the battlefield.
Each team moved like a living organism, their tactics disciplined and aimed at the enemy’s openings.

The monster army had grown stronger than before as the concentration of magical power rose. But if the superior bodies and magical power they were born with were enough to win every battle, the monsters would have conquered the world already.
“Come on, you bastards.”
My voice came out cold as I shot forward. The moment I chose a target, I was already closing the distance and moving on to my next attack.
*Slice, boom!*
I cut the throat of a goblin shaman preparing a spell, then smashed the chest of the Orc chieftain beside it.
The Orcs lost their leader in an instant. As they milled about in confusion, a rain of arrows fell on their heads.
*Whoosh, thud-thud-thud!*
Aura-coated arrowheads pierced their thick hides and passed through their heads and chests.
A particularly huge Troll hurried to retreat as I approached. Just then, two streaks of light curved out from behind it.
*Thud, slice!*
The first sword pierced its chest. The second cut off its head.
The movements were coordinated, without a hint of hesitation or wasted effort.
The swordsmen chopped the Troll, still twitching despite its fatal wounds, into dozens of pieces. Then they spotted me and smiled faintly.
*Xiao Shen. And Team Leader Choi.*
There was no need to exchange words amid the chaos of battle. Not when we understood each other without speaking.
They gave me a light nod, then charged toward another target. They were going after the higher-level monsters intelligent enough to control their respective groups.
*Good choice.*
Most people instinctively resist killing living things, especially other people.
I didn’t know whether that reluctance was an instinct ingrained over our long history or something we’d learned as civilized beings. Either way, it was real.
Monsters were different from the start. Born to struggle, they barely had a concept of their own kind.
*Take out the monsters giving orders to each group, and that’s when the real chaos begins.*
No. The chaos had already begun.

Four S-rank monsters, including the strongest of them, the Manticore Lord, had fallen. On my orders, Magic Johnson and the Hunters had stopped concentrating solely on defense. Now they were driving into the heart of the monster army and grinding it down.

The leaders of each group—lower-ranking commanders, in effect—were falling across the battlefield to A-rank Hunters led by Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen. Yamamoto Genji was making his own conspicuous contribution.
“Hup. Gale Slash!”
The name of the technique, barked in a low voice, was pure Japanese bravado. But the power behind that single sword strike was no bluff.
*Shwaa—slice!*
A flash streaked across the battlefield, and dozens of monsters fell, spraying blood.
Hunters rushed into the space he’d opened and cut down every monster in their path.
*CRUNCH! FWOOSH!*
The formation slowly collapsed. The front line gave ground.
But waiting for the monster army as it gave ground, step by step, were the Skeleton King and a thousand Skeletons, blocking off their rear.
“Surround them! If you’ve got no teeth, hold them with your bones!”
*Clack-clack-clack!*
—GRAAAAH!
*CRUNCH!*
A massive monster several meters tall swung its mace, smashing a dozen Skeletons to pieces.
At the same time, dozens more latched onto it or climbed its body, driving rusty swords and teeth into its enormous frame.
*Thud. Crack!*
—GRAAAAAH!
Its furious roar became a scream of pain. When the massive monster finally met a gruesome death, a cold blue light appeared in its eyes.
—Grr. Ah. Ah. Ah.
Reborn as an undead, the massive monster charged off, dragging its heavy body along.
The Hunters flinched at the sight. Then they spotted the Skeleton King and went right back to fighting as if nothing had happened.
“Hit them! They’re breaking!”
“Their formation’s falling apart! Don’t back down—keep pushing!”
Less than an hour had passed.
But victory was already tipping toward the humans.
Thousands of monsters had already been wiped out. The force that had initially outnumbered us ten to one was now down to five to one—and the gap was shrinking by the second.
*CRACK! THUD!*
An Ogre Warrior more than four meters tall collapsed without a scream.
Its chest blown open, it pitched forward. I planted a foot on its shoulder and leaped into the air, taking in the battlefield below during that brief instant.
*It’s over. Push a little longer, and we win.*
There was no trace of the momentum the monsters had shown at the start, when they’d surrounded the Hunters and attacked without letup.

They’d lost four S-rank monsters and the lesser leaders commanding their groups. Now they were in utter disarray. The Grand Mage’s wide-area spells from the front and the Skeleton King’s undead soldiers pressing them from behind only deepened the confusion.
*And the Hunters are fighting like hell.*
The monster army was nothing but a mass of beasts now. Victory was only a matter of time.
Not one of those countless monsters could stop us. Could stop me.
Except for the one being that still hadn’t shown itself.
*Where the hell are you?*
Thinking of The Prophet, a mystery from beginning to end, I dropped toward the ground.
*BOOM! Slice!*
White Flame’s spearhead plunged down with me and split open another monster’s skull. Its body split cleanly in two and fell to either side. Between the halves, I saw eyes filled with fear.
“Die.”
I charged like a beast of prey and rampaged like a predator.
The lower-level monsters froze as though gripped by **Fear**, staring at the death bearing down on them. The higher-level monsters fought back with the last of their strength.
They fell in different ways, but the result was the same.
Death.
*Thud!*
I twisted the spearhead lodged between a Lycanthrope’s eyes and pulled it free. Brain matter ran down White Flame’s transparent blade.
A tingling ache rose through my arms and legs. They hadn’t stopped moving.
*Damn it.*
How long had I been fighting? How many monsters had I killed?
I didn’t know. Better not to. The moment my brain registered it, my body would feel even more exhausted.
And if The Prophet was watching me now, all the more reason not to show him any weakness.
*Hoo. Hah.*
I steadied my breathing and adjusted my grip on White Flame.
As I turned to face the next monsters, I realized the balance of the battle had finally tipped all the way over.
*Rumble. Rrrumble!*
—GRAAAAAH!
—Krrk. GRAAAAH!
The desert shook. With terrified cries, wave after wave of monsters were retreating.
*They’re running. All those monsters.*
The thought that flashed through my mind was exactly what I was seeing.
Their advantage in numbers?
The monster army had lost its will to fight and was fleeing at full speed. None of them cared about that anymore.
The Hunters stared, blinking, then raised their tired spears and swords. With bloodshot eyes, they raced after the monsters.
“Kill every last one!”
The only thing left on the battlefield was slaughter.

chapters.title: Chapter 809
paragraphs: It was like watching a massive dam collapse.
*Boom. Boom. KABOOM!*
The most ferocious of the large monsters turned and fled.
Every time their several-meter-tall bodies took a step, the enormous weight crushed corpses and smaller monsters underfoot like tofu.
*Crunch! Crack-crunch!*
—Kiiiiie!
—Kyargh!
Painful death cries rang out all around us, but not one of them belonged to a Hunter. At least on this battlefield today, the weak weren’t human. They were monsters.
The strong devour the weak.
Monsters followed the instincts stamped into them from birth. But this wasn’t the ferocity that had driven them to destroy cities and slaughter humans. What drove them now was something more primal.
*Fear.*
The S-rank monsters—so powerful the others hadn’t dared meet their eyes—were dead. So were most of the leaders who’d commanded the groups behind them.
Their threadbare chain of command had collapsed, and the ten-to-one gap in numbers was closing fast.
Several thousand monsters remained, by a rough count. But a beast that had lost the will to fight was easier prey than a herbivore.
And after the grueling battle they’d fought, the Hunters had no intention of ending the hunt just yet.
“They’re running! Wipe them out!”
“Don’t let a single one get away!”
“Aaaah!”
Bloodshot eyes. Weapons slick with flesh and blood.

Soaked from head to toe, the Hunters looked like people made of blood as they chased their prey. They bound slipping sword hilts tight with leather straps. Arms trembling from drawing bowstrings again and again reached for quivers at their sides.
They were exhausted. They wanted to collapse on the sticky sand and sleep.
But they couldn’t stop.
“Because of you bastards, Benjamin—Benjamin... You motherfuckers!”
Some had lost friends.
“N-no! Emma!”
Some had lost a comrade who was also a lover.
“Motherfucker. Were you in San Francisco a month ago, too? What? Damn it. Quit spewing shit I can’t understand and go to hell.”
Others had a recent wrong to avenge.
They had to kill monsters, again and again, until their anger was spent.
*Shhk. Thud!*
Monstrous cries rang out as green blood sprayed in every direction. An arrow flew in from somewhere, pierced an Orc’s head, and drove through a Troll’s ankle.
—Krrk.
The Hunters surrounded the staggering Troll. Scraping together the last of their mana, they poured it into their weapons. Dozens of blades hacked the monster to pieces.
*Thump! Crack-crack-crack!*
We’d fought against overwhelming numbers. The Hunters had suffered heavy losses, and the blood they’d shed had to be repaid in monsters.
“Die! Die!”
Hoarse shouts rang out here and there, voices raw from exhaustion and excitement.
The Hunters spat on the Troll’s corpse, chopped as fine as ground meat, then moved on with bloodshot eyes to find their next prey.
*Boom! Boom-boom-boom!*
Attack spells rained down.
Even now, thousands of monsters trampled corpses and their own kind as they surged south like a wave. The Hunters stood in their path like an enormous reef.
And I was at its center.
*Whoosh!*
A single diagonal downward sweep.
A razor-sharp gust shot along the spearhead and swept past the fleeing monsters.
*Shraaaak.*
Blood burst out instead of a scream, soaking into the sand.
But those lucky enough to escape the attack’s reach put more distance between us and ran faster.

Monsters had never even thought of their own kind as kin. Survival mattered more than fighting now, and they fled for their lives. Countless others were already scattering in every direction, slipping out of the encirclement.
*I can’t let them get away. I have to take down as many as I can.*
The battle was over. What we’d achieved would be remembered for generations and recorded in history as a great victory.
But more than five thousand monsters remained.
We’d killed so many, yet there were still enough to be called an army. Letting them escape today would leave the seeds of another disaster.
*Still, we can’t chase them right now.*
Everyone was exhausted from a long and brutal battle. Right now, the only things driving the Hunters were their anger and desire for revenge against the monsters. Nothing more, nothing less.
And I wasn’t the only one thinking it.
“Human!”
“Jin!”
The Skeleton King, who’d been holding the rear, and Magic Johnson, who’d fought his way through the monsters to reach me, came up on either side.
“We need to regroup as quickly as we can, then pursue them,” Magic Johnson said, short of breath. “We should split our forces into separate units.”
The Skeleton King cut down an injured ogre that had fallen behind before answering.
“I agree. My magical power is nearly depleted, but we can’t let this chance pass. I’ve already turned several Griffins into undead. They’ll give us enough of a view.”
I started to answer, then caught my breath. I steadied my ragged breathing and managed only a nod. The Skeleton King frowned.
“Human, are you all right?”
“It’s... it’s nothing. Don’t worry about it.”
A lie.
My arms and legs felt as heavy as if they’d been soaked in water. The internal energy that had filled my dantian was running low.
More than anything, the dull ache I’d felt deep inside my body on and off throughout the battle was growing worse.
*Damn debuff.*

I kept my expression calm by force and recalled a System message I’d seen not long ago. It was among the notifications waiting for me when I’d woken from my long sleep after defeating Michael Silbert.

**System** All things come with a price. But you have once again ignored repeated warnings and used power that surpasses your limits. Information for the special debuff **Broken Body** has been updated. The special debuff **Shattered Body** has been newly applied. The existing stat penalties caused by debuffs remain unchanged, and the effects of the new debuff will also apply. **Muscles and Bones** have weakened. The chance of injury has increased considerably. **Internal energy** is consumed more rapidly. Your control over qi is no longer as free as before.
Shattered Body.
That was the price of ignoring the System’s warning.
One Annihilation’s unprecedented destructive power had eaten away at my body as well as my enemy’s life. It was damage no method could heal—not even leveling up.
*Should I have avoided using One Annihilation against Michael Silbert?*
The thought left a bitter taste in my mouth, but there was nothing I could do about it. Back then, I hadn’t had much choice beyond One Annihilation.
I pushed aside the potion Magic Johnson held out with a worried look.
“That won’t do it. If I use a potion now, I’ll only end up more exhausted.”
“But—”
“Pursuing them comes first. Especially...”
“Yes. The Prophet.”
The Skeleton King spoke quietly. He read the meaning in my eyes and clicked his tongue.
“We still haven’t found him. I was certain he was watching from somewhere, but it seems we were wrong.”
Magic Johnson added, “I haven’t found him either. Jin, maybe The Prophet was never here at all.”
“Never here? You mean this was a trap aimed at something else from the start?”
“I can’t be sure. But it’s possible.”
I thought for a moment, then shook my head.
Four S-rank monsters and an army of more than fifteen thousand monsters. That was far too much to use as bait for a mere trap.
*So why hasn’t he shown himself?*

The Prophet was an unpredictable powerhouse. He’d killed Siegfried Bassmann, a Grand Mage surrounded by all kinds of barriers, without leaving any obvious signs of a fight. He might be as powerful as Michael Silbert—or more so.
*If he’d joined the battle, who knows how it would have turned out?*
Even for me, fighting the Manticore Lord and the Lycanthrope Champion at once had been anything but easy. That would have been the perfect moment for The Prophet to show himself.
*But he never did.*
Even if the battle had been a trap and our main camp was his true target, it still made no sense.
Embarrassing as it was to say, I was the heart and head of the World Hunter Federation.
That left me with one conclusion.
“It’s not a trap.”
My thoughts had run long, but only a moment had passed. I looked at the Hunters still chasing the monsters like mad.
The Team Leaders—our lower-ranking commanders—were ordering them to stop, but the Hunters pursued their prey as though they couldn’t hear a word.
“I don’t know what The Prophet really wants, but... he planned for this situation, too.”
“What?”
“If we keep pursuing them without rest, the units will fall apart in no time. First, get the worked-up Hunters back under control as quickly as you can.”
“Jin.”
Magic Johnson fixed me with a grave look.
“I agree we need to regroup. But then why did The Prophet drive all those monsters into this desert?”
“One of two reasons. Either he thought they’d be enough to deal with us...”
I stopped, then forced out the rest.
“Or he’s already built a force so powerful he can afford to lose an army this size.”
The air around us went cold.
I looked at their rigid faces and kept one thought to myself.
One thing was certain. My instincts, pushed to their limit, had seized me with the force of a premonition.
*The Prophet wants to face me.*
The monsters’ cries receded into the distance. Only then, among the people collapsing one by one, did a wind begin to blow.
Heavy with the smell of blood, it spread through the cool night air.
One hundred and eighty-five.
That was how many people had fought more bravely than anyone else—and, because of that, had crossed a river they could never come back over.
But the survivors had to keep moving.
We hadn’t come here to win a battle. We’d come to kill The Prophet and uproot the disaster.
*There’s no time.*
The idea that the person running is more desperate than the one giving chase is complete bullshit. Especially when the person running has a bomb that could swallow the whole world.
“Everyone has finished regrouping.”
I opened my eyes at Team Leader Choi’s report.
I’d spent less than an hour circulating my energy, but my body felt much better. My mind had settled, too.
*What the hell is The Prophet?*
I’d been asking myself that for a long time.
The fifth Muninn. A being thought to be a monster, wielding magic that wasn’t human. The desert’s pope, leading countless fanatics.
The more I learned about him, the more I felt as if I were sinking into a swamp. What was he really? What did he want? And where was he now?
If the System had a physical form, I wanted to grab it by the collar and demand answers.
I’d take any debuff it gave me. Just give me one tiny clue.
*Damn it.*
I cursed under my breath and looked up at the darkening sky.
Daylight in the desert was brief, and the sky was gray, perhaps because of the distribution of magical power.
Just like Michael Silbert.
The monster who had been born human and died a monster.
And as my memories of him surfaced, one after another—
A question flashed through my mind like a bolt of light.

chapters.title: Chapter 810
paragraphs: Perhaps intuition was another name for wisdom.
The feeling of an instinct etched into every cell suddenly waking. Of countless thoughts tangled in your head coming together as one.
“Michael Silbert. Michael Silbert. Michael...”
The name should have stayed in Jin Taekyung’s mind. Instead, it slipped from his lips without him noticing.
A question filled his mind in an instant. New thoughts followed, one after another. Each time a question came back to him with an answer, he sent it out again carrying another question.
And each time, the same words came first.
*What if. Suppose. Maybe...*
He questioned and questioned without pause, until the thoughts tangling in his head took on something like a coherent shape.
He had no idea how much time passed.
And...
He was so deeply absorbed that he didn’t notice someone’s footsteps—whose, he couldn’t tell—drawing close.
*Crunch.*
Sand shifted underfoot. Jin’s senses snapped awake.
The hairs on his body stood on end, and instinct moved him before his brain could give the order.
*Whoosh.*
He spun, slashing downward with his spear.

He’d made that move thousands—tens of thousands—of times in training and combat. It was etched into him, terrifyingly fast and precise. Fast enough to make the intruder in the darkness think of death.
But the intruder was no pushover.
*Vwooom.*
A flash of light accompanied an invisible ripple of qi. The space around them brightened, and Jin’s eyes widened as he recognized who stood before him.
Recognition brought control. His strike, hurtling forward with tremendous speed and force, stopped as if someone had pressed pause.
The spearhead halted a hair’s breadth from a faintly glowing, translucent barrier. A fierce gust swept through.
*Fwoooosh!*
Sand that had somehow escaped the blood flew into the air. The intruder spat some of it out of his mouth.
“Do me a favor. If you’re going to kill me, tell me first. Give me a little time to prepare.”
Jin lowered his spear and hurriedly asked, “Damn it. I’m sorry, Johnson. Are you hurt anywhere?”
“...As you can see.”
Magic Johnson dispelled his defensive spell. He barely managed to get the words out. In those few moments, cold sweat had gathered on the back of his neck, glistening in the faint moonlight.
“I’m fine. Though I might’ve had a little accident.”
“What?”
“Before you get the wrong idea, everything about me is big. Just this once, it was only a little.”
Jin let out a relieved breath at the joke.
That had been truly dangerous. If he hadn’t stopped the spearhead at the last moment, there would definitely have been blood.
“I’m sorry again.”
“I said it’s fine. More importantly, Jin, what the hell was that?”
“What was what?”
“Why you mistook a wonderful friend and comrade-in-arms like me for an enemy. What were you thinking about just now?”
“Ah, well...”
Jin started to answer, then suddenly shut his mouth.
Johnson studied him for a moment and shrugged. “You don’t have to tell me. If our young boss can’t talk about it, I’m sure he has his reasons. But there’s one thing I do have to say.”
“If there’s something you have to say...”
“We finished regrouping nearly thirty minutes ago. Whatever’s troubling you, if we delay the pursuit any longer, we’ll lose them for good. That’s why I came.”
*What? Already?*
Only then did Jin belatedly check the time and bite his lip. Everything Magic Johnson had said was true.
*When did that much time pass?*
It felt like less than a minute had passed since Choi Minwoo stopped by, but the sky had grown darker in the meantime.
*I must’ve had a lot on my mind.*

No-self wasn’t a state that belonged only to martial arts. Jin had been so absorbed in one question after another that he hadn’t noticed time passing. Johnson had no way of guessing why he’d stayed rooted to the spot.

“I know their deaths are weighing on you. That’s why I gave you a little time. But Jin, if we lose them now or fail to find The Prophet... remember, the sacrifices made up to this point will have been for nothing.”
*Pat, pat.*
Magic Johnson patted Jin on the shoulder with his large hand, then turned away after leaving him with one last remark.
“Everyone’s waiting. We need you, Boss.”
That was all.
Jin watched the Grand Mage’s back slowly recede and wondered how much truth was in the questions he’d come up with. What, exactly, was a lie, and what was the truth?
He steadied his breathing.
“No. Either way, there’s only one path.”
He’d barely managed to grasp a single clue. With no other choice, there was no point in thinking it over any longer.
Jin took a heavy step into the darkness surrounding them.
The desert night was cold, dark, and vast.
No one complained. They walked in silence.
One hundred and eighty-five.

We’d fought shoulder to shoulder with them, even if only for a short time, and lost them. Some had been strangers; others must have been close. We’d buried their bodies in the dunes, then had to leave them behind.
In place of gravestones worthy of heroes, we planted their bloodied weapons in the sand. We swore we would return to these coordinates and bring them home to their families.
That promise was why the survivors kept moving. I led the way.
*Whooooosh!*
Countless figures sped across the desert.
Sand carried on the wind stung my face. But sand wasn’t all the wind carried.
*The stench of blood. And a foul odor.*
The smell was sickening, but familiar. Sticky liquid coated the plants and rocks we passed.
Blue-green blood. Monster blood.
*Where are you?*
I spread the energy coiled inside me over a wide area. At the same time, I sensed faint breaths and the traces of an unpleasant magical power.
“Shen.”
I stopped. Xiao Shen understood at once, drew his sword in a flash, and drove it deep into the ground beneath his feet.
*Squish!*
Blood spurted from the sand as it suddenly caved in. At the same time, the ground all around us rippled like waves.
*Shhhhh!*
Monsters appeared for an instant amid the flying sand. An urgent shout rang through the night.
“Ant Lion!”
Colloquially known as the antlion.
Even the smallest specimen was about the size of a midsize car, and these powerful monsters were classified as at least Grade B.
But the one that had just appeared had larger pincers and more powerful mana than any Ant Lion I’d ever seen.
*It’s one of the ones that fled the battle earlier.*
It was one of more than a hundred Grade A monsters that had saved their lives by retreating from the battlefield.
I moved as soon as I realized it.
*Tap.*
The twenty meters between us vanished. As the Ant Lion lunged to swallow the nearest Hunters, I brought my spear down.
*Shhk!*
One strike. Both pincers, harder than steel, sliced off like tofu.
Before its anguished scream could even ring out, I twisted the spear shaft in midair and slammed it into the monster’s body.
*Crack!*
Blood sprayed out with a nauseating stench. The blow wasn’t enough to kill it.
I pressed the spearhead against the spot I guessed was between its eyes and moved my lips.
The language of monsters.
“A few questions. Think carefully before you answer.”
Scholars who studied the Demon Realm language existed. Humans who could speak it fluently were rarer than Named Monsters.
The Ant Lion’s eyes, clouded with pain, flew open. It clearly hadn’t expected this.
“You. Human. How?”
I tightened my grip on White Flame instead of answering.
*Shhk.*
As the keen spearhead cut smoothly through skin as hard as armor, a panicked voice burst out.
“I answer! Anything! Ask!”
Judging from its clumsy Demon Realm language, it wasn’t very intelligent—but it was quick to catch on. I stopped the spearhead.
“Where are the others?”
“Gone. All. Sun falls that way.”
“West?”
“Yes! There. Many!”
I had no reason to doubt it. The Ant Lion was stupid enough that everything it said rang true.
*West.*
Some must have fallen behind or scattered along the way, but most of the monsters that had left the battlefield had undoubtedly headed west.
What I really wanted to know was something else.
“Then what about The Prophet?”
“The Prophet?”
“Yes. The Prophet.”
The Ant Lion blinked its round eyes.
“What is that? I don’t know.”

I clicked my tongue as I realized my mistake. The Prophet had revealed that name to the world himself. Unless the monster army had gathered somewhere in the desert to watch TV, this creature wouldn’t know it.
“Let me rephrase. Not The Prophet. Your leader—the commander leading you and the other monsters.”
“Commander? Leader? Leads us?”
It repeated my words haltingly, then looked up at me with fear and confusion in its eyes.
“Dead. You. You all killed them.”
“What?”
“One. Two. Three. Four. All dead. Me, everyone, scared. So ran.”
I looked into its eyes and confirmed once more that it wasn’t lying.
“Right. I see.”
“Me, me, believe! Didn’t lie!”
“I know.”
I pushed the spearhead deep between the Ant Lion’s eyes and added calmly, “I know how many people died because of you, too.”
*Crunch. Gurgle.*
The monster’s enormous body shuddered as blood bubbled from it.
A System notification announced another death. I shook the blood and bodily fluids from my spear.
Johnson came over once he saw the interrogation was finished. “What did it say?”
I answered in a dry voice. “No luck. It didn’t even know The Prophet existed.”
“...Damn it. Well, it’d be strange for a Grade A monster—not even Grade S—to know all that. Did you find out where the ones that ran off are headed?”
“Yes.”
“Where?”
I stared at Magic Johnson without answering. Then I replied as if it were nothing.
“East.”
Over his shoulder, the Skeleton King stared at me, eyes wide.
