The space around them brightened, and Jin’s eyes widened as he recognized who stood before him.
Recognition brought control.
His strike, hurtling forward with tremendous speed and force, stopped as if someone had pressed pause.
The spearhead halted a hair’s breadth from a faintly glowing, translucent barrier.
A fierce gust swept through.
*Fwoooosh!*
Sand that had somehow escaped the blood flew into the air.
The intruder spat some of it out of his mouth.
“Do me a favor.
If you’re going to kill me, tell me first.
Give me a little time to prepare.”
Jin lowered his spear and hurriedly asked, “Damn it.
I’m sorry, Johnson.
Are you hurt anywhere?”
“...As you can see.”
Magic Johnson dispelled his defensive spell.
He barely managed to get the words out.
In those few moments, cold sweat had gathered on the back of his neck, glistening in the faint moonlight.
“I’m fine.
Though I might’ve had a little accident.”
“What?”
“Before you get the wrong idea, everything about me is big.
Just this once, it was only a little.”
Jin let out a relieved breath at the joke.
That had been truly dangerous.
If he hadn’t stopped the spearhead at the last moment, there would definitely have been blood.
“I’m sorry again.”
“I said it’s fine.
More importantly, Jin, what the hell was that?”
“What was what?”
“Why you mistook a wonderful friend and comrade-in-arms like me for an enemy.
What were you thinking about just now?”
“Ah, well...”
Jin started to answer, then suddenly shut his mouth.
Johnson studied him for a moment and shrugged.
“You don’t have to tell me.
If our young boss can’t talk about it, I’m sure he has his reasons.
But there’s one thing I do have to say.”
“If there’s something you have to say...”
“We finished regrouping nearly thirty minutes ago.
Whatever’s troubling you, if we delay the pursuit any longer, we’ll lose them for good.
That’s why I came.”
*What?
Already?*
Only then did Jin belatedly check the time and bite his lip.
Everything Magic Johnson had said was true.
*When did that much time pass?*
It felt like less than a minute had passed since Choi Minwoo stopped by, but the sky had grown darker in the meantime.
*I must’ve had a lot on my mind.*
No-self wasn’t a state that belonged only to martial arts.
Jin had been so absorbed in one question after another that he hadn’t noticed time passing.
Johnson had no way of guessing why he’d stayed rooted to the spot.
“I know their deaths are weighing on you.
That’s why I gave you a little time.
But Jin, if we lose them now or fail to find The Prophet... remember, the sacrifices made up to this point will have been for nothing.”
*Pat, pat.*
Magic Johnson patted Jin on the shoulder with his large hand, then turned away after leaving him with one last remark.
“Everyone’s waiting.
We need you, Boss.”
That was all.
Jin watched the Grand Mage’s back slowly recede and wondered how much truth was in the questions he’d come up with.
What, exactly, was a lie, and what was the truth?
He steadied his breathing.
“No.
Either way, there’s only one path.”
He’d barely managed to grasp a single clue.
With no other choice, there was no point in thinking it over any longer.
Jin took a heavy step into the darkness surrounding them.
The desert night was cold, dark, and vast.
No one complained.
They walked in silence.
One hundred and eighty-five.
We’d fought shoulder to shoulder with them, even if only for a short time, and lost them.
Some had been strangers; others must have been close.
We’d buried their bodies in the dunes, then had to leave them behind.
In place of gravestones worthy of heroes, we planted their bloodied weapons in the sand.
We swore we would return to these coordinates and bring them home to their families.
That promise was why the survivors kept moving.
I led the way.
*Whooooosh!*
Countless figures sped across the desert.
Sand carried on the wind stung my face.
But sand wasn’t all the wind carried.
*The stench of blood.
And a foul odor.*
The smell was sickening, but familiar.
Sticky liquid coated the plants and rocks we passed.
Blue-green blood.
Monster blood.
*Where are you?*
I spread the energy coiled inside me over a wide area.
At the same time, I sensed faint breaths and the traces of an unpleasant magical power.
“Shen.”
I stopped.
Xiao Shen understood at once, drew his sword in a flash, and drove it deep into the ground beneath his feet.
*Squish!*
Blood spurted from the sand as it suddenly caved in.
At the same time, the ground all around us rippled like waves.
*Shhhhh!*
Monsters appeared for an instant amid the flying sand.
An urgent shout rang through the night.
“Ant Lion!”
Colloquially known as the antlion.
Even the smallest specimen was about the size of a midsize car, and these powerful monsters were classified as at least Grade B.
But the one that had just appeared had larger pincers and more powerful mana than any Ant Lion I’d ever seen.
*It’s one of the ones that fled the battle earlier.*
It was one of more than a hundred Grade A monsters that had saved their lives by retreating from the battlefield.
I moved as soon as I realized it.
*Tap.*
The twenty meters between us vanished.
As the Ant Lion lunged to swallow the nearest Hunters, I brought my spear down.
*Shhk!*
One strike.
Both pincers, harder than steel, sliced off like tofu.
Before its anguished scream could even ring out, I twisted the spear shaft in midair and slammed it into the monster’s body.
*Crack!*
Blood sprayed out with a nauseating stench.
The blow wasn’t enough to kill it.
I pressed the spearhead against the spot I guessed was between its eyes and moved my lips.
The language of monsters.
“A few questions.
Think carefully before you answer.”
Scholars who studied the Demon Realm language existed.
Humans who could speak it fluently were rarer than Named Monsters.
The Ant Lion’s eyes, clouded with pain, flew open.
It clearly hadn’t expected this.
“You.
Human.
How?”
I tightened my grip on White Flame instead of answering.
*Shhk.*
As the keen spearhead cut smoothly through skin as hard as armor, a panicked voice burst out.
“I answer!
Anything!
Ask!”
Judging from its clumsy Demon Realm language, it wasn’t very intelligent—but it was quick to catch on.
I stopped the spearhead.
“Where are the others?”
“Gone.
All.
Sun falls that way.”
“West?”
“Yes!
There.
Many!”
I had no reason to doubt it.
The Ant Lion was stupid enough that everything it said rang true.
*West.*
Some must have fallen behind or scattered along the way, but most of the monsters that had left the battlefield had undoubtedly headed west.
What I really wanted to know was something else.
“Then what about The Prophet?”
“The Prophet?”
“Yes.
The Prophet.”
The Ant Lion blinked its round eyes.
“What is that?
I don’t know.”
I clicked my tongue as I realized my mistake.
The Prophet had revealed that name to the world himself.
Unless the monster army had gathered somewhere in the desert to watch TV, this creature wouldn’t know it.
“Let me rephrase.
Not The Prophet.
Your leader—the commander leading you and the other monsters.”
“Commander?
Leader?
Leads us?”
It repeated my words haltingly, then looked up at me with fear and confusion in its eyes.
“Dead.
You.
You all killed them.”
“What?”
“One.
Two.
Three.
Four.
All dead.
Me, everyone, scared.
So ran.”
I looked into its eyes and confirmed once more that it wasn’t lying.
“Right.
I see.”
“Me, me, believe!
Didn’t lie!”
“I know.”
I pushed the spearhead deep between the Ant Lion’s eyes and added calmly, “I know how many people died because of you, too.”
*Crunch.
Gurgle.*
The monster’s enormous body shuddered as blood bubbled from it.
A System notification announced another death.
I shook the blood and bodily fluids from my spear.
Johnson came over once he saw the interrogation was finished.
“What did it say?”
I answered in a dry voice.
“No luck.
It didn’t even know The Prophet existed.”
“...Damn it.
Well, it’d be strange for a Grade A monster—not even Grade S—to know all that.
Did you find out where the ones that ran off are headed?”
“Yes.”
“Where?”
I stared at Magic Johnson without answering.
Then I replied as if it were nothing.
“East.”
Over his shoulder, the Skeleton King stared at me, eyes wide.

chapters.title: Chapter 811
paragraphs: “East. You mean east.”
Magic Johnson turned his head to check the direction. For the Skeleton King, that was unfortunate.
He had to fight to hide the shock on his face. The shock filling his mind was harder to shake.
*Why on earth?*
To the Skeleton King, a monster, the Demon Realm language was practically his mother tongue.
Unlike Magic Johnson, who had been watching the rear of the formation, he’d stayed beside Jin Taekyung at the front the whole time. He’d heard enough of the conversation to understand it perfectly.
*The Ant Lion said most of the monsters went west. I’m sure of it.*

His thoughts tangled together. Jin Taekyung’s expression hadn’t changed in the slightest, and for a moment the Skeleton King wondered if he’d misheard. But no. However many times he went over the exchange, his memory stayed the same.
*That vile human... lied.*
So what did Jin Taekyung’s lie, and this situation now, mean?
After a brief moment of thought, the Skeleton King found the answer himself. It was the answer he’d already suspected and had tried so hard to ignore.
*No way.*
His pupils trembled as he faced what he could scarcely believe. Just then, Magic Johnson looked away from the darkened east and turned toward him.
“Did you send your minions east to search—hey. Are you listening to me?”
“Hm? Oh. Of course.”
“What were you looking at?”

The Skeleton King had looked at Jin Taekyung without realizing it, but he couldn’t say so. The instant he heard Magic Johnson’s voice, his heart had lurched. He forced himself to settle down, then gestured with his chin toward the dead Ant Lion’s corpse.
“That one. I thought it might move well if I brought it back as an undead.”
“Hmm, not a bad idea. But it burrows deep into the sand, so humans like us couldn’t ride it. And aboveground, its size would make it too conspicuous.”
“Then I’ll give up on it. Come to think of it, controlling something like that would take a lot of magical power.”
Had he answered convincingly? Had Magic Johnson noticed anything strange about his behavior?
As Johnson slowly stroked his chin, the Skeleton King pushed down his anxiety and hurriedly continued.
“But what were you going to ask?”
“Oh, right. I was going to ask if you’d sent your minions to search the east.”
“The eagles and griffins?”
“Right. Didn’t they already go out and come back? If the monsters fled east, I’d have thought they would’ve spotted them.”
Magic Johnson was right. The Skeleton King had already sent his subordinates east.

While everyone else regrouped and rested, a dozen or so eagles and griffins had taken to the sky after the monster army fleeing frantically across the desert. His magical power had soon run low, ending the undead’s pursuit without results. But he knew, at least, that few monsters had gone east.
“Well...”
His voice trailed off. Beside Magic Johnson, Jin Taekyung watched him with a dark, steady gaze.
*Damn it.*
The Skeleton King didn’t know if the choice he was about to make was right.
Then he remembered something Jin Taekyung had once said—words that had calmed not only him, but everyone around him.
*If you can’t trust yourself, trust me.*
He recalled the words and repeated them to himself. In that instant, his hesitation ended.
“I lost sight of them quickly, but there’s a good chance most of the monster army fled east.”
The Skeleton King trusted Jin Taekyung’s judgment—no, his friend’s judgment.
Perhaps more than his own.
Even before we met the Ant Lion, I’d put the conflict lingering in the back of my mind aside.
Now all I had to do was tug on the thread I’d barely managed to grasp and find out what lay at the other end.
*But I can’t do that right away.*
I had to be meticulous. I couldn’t leave them an opening.
I sorted out my thoughts, then gathered a few of the people in command.
“We’ll split up our forces and move out.”
My abrupt announcement sent a ripple of unease through the group. Team Leader Choi was the first to object.
“Weren’t we all going east together?”
Most of the monsters had headed east. That was what everyone except the Skeleton King and me believed, so his question made sense.
Assuming what they believed was true.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“When did I say that?”
“I know what you mean.”
My voice came out dry, so unlike my usual voice that it sounded strange even to me. I looked at Team Leader Choi’s stiff face and went on.
“But we can’t act on the Ant Lion’s information as if we know it’s true. It’s too dangerous.”
“You mean it could be a deliberate trap?”
“Yes.”
It struck me again: I was pretty good at lying.
I also knew a truth I’d learned in both Murim and the modern world.
*Authority.*
A lie told by someone with authority is remarkably persuasive. People who trust that person are ready to believe it.
Just like now.
“They lost the battle and ran, but they still outnumber us by more than five to one.”
Five thousand.
An army that had numbered well over ten thousand had been cut to a third in a single battle. But we’d taken losses, too.
Even with an overwhelming kill ratio, the two hundred or so people we’d lost amounted to a fifth of our force.
If the monster army was a pie too big to finish in one sitting, we were a muffin someone could swallow whole.
“We need to be careful. We should split up and pursue them.”
Xiao Shen nodded.
“I agree with Sir Jin. If we act on false information, we could walk into a trap—or head the wrong way and lose the monsters.”
“Exactly. Splitting up would lower the risk.”
Team Leader Choi furrowed his brow.
“I understand why you want to split up, but... wouldn’t that leave the units vulnerable to being picked off one by one?”
Any commander would worry about that, but the chance of it happening was extremely low.
*The monsters fled west, not east.*
I swallowed the words on the tip of my tongue and answered without hesitation.
“We’ll keep the units close together. Even with communications disrupted by the high concentration of magical power, we should still be able to maintain a reliable connection.”
“Hmm. I agree with Jin,” Magic Johnson said. “By my rough calculation, a hundred kilometers or so between units should be close enough.”
I looked at him in silence, then answered with a heavy heart.
“That’s right. We’ll cover more ground, too.”
The Rub’ al Khali Desert was said to be the second-largest desert in the world. Its size was staggering.
Even Team Leader Choi seemed to realize anew how large it was. He reluctantly nodded.
“If we assign a hundred people to each pursuit unit... we could cover the southeast and northeast as well as the east. Understood. There’s no time to waste, so let’s move quickly.”
He was about to leave, but turned back before he’d taken a step.
“You’ve left one thing out,” I said.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, what do you mean—”
“West. I’m sending a pursuit unit west, too.”
“What?”
“But that’s the opposite direction.”
“That’s right.”
I looked around at everyone.
“But if we travel a few more hours west from here, we’ll reach the oil fields. The very place the message The Prophet left for me points to.”
“You heard the message yourself,” I said to Yamamoto Genji. “Tell them. Am I right?”
He’d looked miserable ever since I mentioned splitting up. Now everyone was watching him. He glanced around nervously and nodded.
“Uh, well. He said it was a land where black jewels were buried, so I think that’s probably right...”
“Good enough. We’re going west.”
“Wait. We are?”
“Yes. You, me, the Skeleton King, and Magic Johnson.”
Yamamoto Genji’s face went deathly pale.
“Jin Sama! How can you do this?”
“Right here.”
“That’s ridiculous... Leave me out of it! I want to stay with the others!”
“No. I won’t leave you out. I have no intention of leaving you out. Go back.”
After answering firmly, I continued speaking to the people who were blinking at this unexpected turn of events.

“We didn’t come here for the monster army. We came for The Prophet. We need to follow his message at least as far as the place it points to. We’ll be back soon. Until then, keep pursuing the remaining monsters, but avoid a clash.”
“No!”
Team Leader Choi, who’d been staring at me blankly, shouted in protest.
“If The Prophet was in the west all along, why would the monsters run the exact opposite way?”
“That’s true. But if most of them don’t know The Prophet exists, like the Ant Lion, they have every reason to run east.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung. Do you really believe The Prophet is there?”
“I don’t know. But even if he isn’t, you and the others will still be pursuing the monsters, so nothing will go wrong. And if he’s in the west... we’ll have enough strength to take him on.”
Three S-rank Hunters.
No, four, if we counted the Skeleton King. And with his abilities, he could bring undead soldiers into the fight.
Just as he parted his lips to say something, I delivered the final blow.
“This is an order.”
“Hurry. Before the monsters get any farther away.”
I turned away. Then I sent a Sound Transmission, as though in passing, to someone who’d stood there without a word all this time.
—From now on, don’t answer or react to anything I say. Just listen.
For a brief moment, the Skeleton King’s eyes, which had been trembling violently, settled into a deep stillness.
After that one-sided discussion, I spent a short while circulating my qi, then set out west.
I wasn’t alone. The Skeleton King, Magic Johnson, and Yamamoto Genji came with me.
There were only four of us, but we were a powerful force, and we moved at a speed that couldn’t compare to when we’d been traveling with the army.
*Whoosh!*
Amid the scenery flashing past, I spotted pools of thick, sticky blood. I didn’t have to stop and examine them to see how much had been shed, or how far the trail spread.
A few dozen monsters couldn’t have left all this behind. Everything the Ant Lion had said was true.
*Though that’s not the important part.*
I kept running, muttering to myself. We crossed rolling dunes and passed through an open stretch of wilderness.
After about thirty minutes, we reached a canyon between two facing cliffs. Only then did I begin to slow.
“Hah... Hah. C-could you slow down a little?”
Yamamoto Genji was panting. Magic Johnson wiped his sweat-soaked forehead and spoke to me.
“Jin. How about we rest here for a bit? I don’t see any monsters around.”
Instead of answering, I came to a complete stop and slowly looked around.
Cliffs stretching into the distance. A narrow passage. Good terrain.
Little room to move. A narrow escape route.
I looked up at the sky. In the distance, I saw a shadow flapping its wings against the faint moonlight over the desert.
*An eagle.*
Magic Johnson followed my gaze and frowned.
“Still birds out here? With this concentration of magical power, they should hardly be able to live here.”
“Not impossible, if they aren’t ordinary eagles.”
“What?”
Magic Johnson blinked, not understanding. I stepped in front of the canyon entrance and blocked the way.

I kept running, muttering to myself.
We crossed rolling dunes and passed through an open stretch of wilderness.
After about thirty minutes, we reached a canyon between two facing cliffs.
Only then did I begin to slow.
“Hah...
Hah.
C-could you slow down a little?”
Yamamoto Genji was panting.
Magic Johnson wiped his sweat-soaked forehead and spoke to me.
“Jin.
How about we rest here for a bit?
I don’t see any monsters around.”
Instead of answering, I came to a complete stop and slowly looked around.
Cliffs stretching into the distance.
A narrow passage.
Good terrain.
Little room to move.
A narrow escape route.
I looked up at the sky.
In the distance, I saw a shadow flapping its wings against the faint moonlight over the desert.
*An eagle.*
Magic Johnson followed my gaze and frowned.
“Still birds out here?
With this concentration of magical power, they should hardly be able to live here.”
“Not impossible, if they aren’t ordinary eagles.”
“What?”
Magic Johnson blinked, not understanding.
I stepped in front of the canyon entrance and blocked the way.

chapters.title: Chapter 812
paragraphs: *Step.*
Jin Taekyung felt the earth crumble beneath his foot and wondered why his footsteps sounded so loud. Was it the depth of the night? Or was it because every nerve in his body was on edge?
He didn’t know. Maybe it was both.
But one thing was certain. From this moment on, no one would leave this long, narrow canyon without his permission.
“Jin?”
Magic Johnson stared at him, apparently unable to understand why the air had suddenly grown so heavy. Then he turned his head.
Beneath the moonlight spilling down the towering cliffs, a figure stood blocking the exit, its golden eyes gleaming.
The Skeleton King.
Johnson’s lips silently formed the name. As he realized the position he was in, the Grand Mage’s gaze darkened.
“What does this mean?”
“Nothing in particular. I just have a few things I need to check.”
Jin’s tone was gentle, but his eyes were cold.
The eagle in the distance was already forgotten. Magic Johnson studied him.
“If it isn’t urgent, why not check later?”
“It’s urgent. I have to check now.”
“Caution is a leader’s virtue. But I don’t think now is the right time.”
“I can see why you’d think that. But isn’t judging the right time exactly what a leader does?”
Magic Johnson fell silent for a moment, then gave a quiet laugh.
“You’re right, Jin. I didn’t know you were so good with words.”
“I’ve noticed this now and then, but test scores and running your mouth are two different things.”
Jin smiled faintly along with him, then called out a name.
“Genji.”
“Y-yes?”
Yamamoto Genji, who had been watching from beside Magic Johnson, jumped at the sudden call.
He’d already realized something was wrong. As his eyes darted around, Jin jerked his chin at him.
“You look uncomfortable. Come over here. You’re getting on my nerves.”
“Y-yes, sir!”
Yamamoto glanced at Magic Johnson and took a step forward. When the hulking Grand Mage didn’t react, he hurried over to Jin’s side.
“U-um. Jin-sama. What exactly is going on...”
“Shut up.”
Jin answered calmly, then looked at Magic Johnson.
Johnson’s expression hadn’t changed despite the sudden turn of events. He was still sitting on the rough rock.
“Johnson. When did we first meet?”
The question came out of nowhere, but Magic Johnson answered readily.
“During the Arch Lich subjugation. It hasn’t even been a year.”
“It feels strange. It seems like it’s been ten years already.”
“A lot has happened. Things we thought would never happen again—things we couldn’t even imagine.”
“Yeah. I really didn’t think things would turn out like this.”
Jin smiled bitterly. Two years ago—no, even just a year ago—he’d been nothing more than an unusually talented F-rank Hunter.
He’d never escaped the confines fate had set for him when he awakened. He’d spent his days in a cramped, musty goshiwon room.
But everything had changed.
Last summer had been unusually hot. One day, without warning, he’d been told he was fired.
And then... there was the beat-up capsule waiting for him on the melting asphalt.
Every moment was still vivid.
That night, the beat-up capsule had tossed the fool who’d been reckless enough to crawl inside it for a nap into a new world. Jin had escaped his confines and changed his fate.
“Things we couldn’t even imagine. That’s probably the best way to put it. I know because I’ve lived through them. But you know what’s funny?”
Jin didn’t wait for an answer.
The faint smile had vanished from his lips. They were now as rough and hard as the rock Magic Johnson sat on.
“After going through so many things I couldn’t have imagined, my imagination still barely improves.”
A being called the Demon King had descended upon Earth. Countless monsters had burned cities and slaughtered people.
Humanity had won after five years of the Great War, then built an even more brilliant and vast civilization.
Impossible things. And yet, they’d happened to everyone just a few decades ago.
Jin hadn’t lived through that era, but he’d crossed dimensions, traveled between two worlds, and gained no shortage of experience.
“Sometimes I think common sense is terrifying. It keeps you thinking inside the same old box, and you end up going nowhere.”
Jin tapped his temple with a dagger he’d drawn at some point.
Magic Johnson had watched in silence. Now he spoke.
“So this time, you used your imagination a little more?”
“Yes. I went back over everything that’s happened so far. Slowly. From as objective a perspective as I could manage.”
“Jin, humans can’t be objective.”
Magic Johnson was right.
People’s judgments were always subjective. Ironically, humanity had become the master of the world because, more than any other creature on Earth, it was made up of thought and emotion.
But...
“I found I could at least try. Set aside what I know and how I feel about someone as much as possible.”
“Right. You can try to look at things objectively. That’s humanity’s greatest strength.”
“Hmm.”
Jin licked his lips.
“That’s a dangerous thing to say.”
“Which part?”
“I don’t know. You make it sound like you’re not human yourself.”
Jin’s reflection shone in Magic Johnson’s clear eyes. A short laugh slipped from Johnson’s lips, breaking the silence.
“So, Jin. Did you achieve what you wanted?”
“Probably.”
Magic Johnson already knew what Jin had gone to such lengths to work out.
“The Prophet.”
Johnson’s deep voice carried through the night air. Jin gave a small nod.
“I started with the person most closely connected to him.”
“Michael Silbert. Considering their connection, that would be the obvious place to start.”

“Huginn called The Prophet Muninn. The fifth Muninn, at that. One of the beings swapped out like spare parts to make Michael Silbert who he is today. And on top of that, The Prophet uses magic that isn’t human.”
“That’s why we suspected he was a monster.”
“Right. But isn’t something strange? Huginn only learned about the fifth Muninn three years ago, yet Michael Silbert had been handling magical power little by little since the Great Cataclysm.”
“What’s strange about that?”
“Of course it’s strange. A human made magical power and mana coexist. That’s insane. Even I can’t do it now. And that guy did it thirty years ago? No way.”
Then Jin added, “Unless a real monster helped him.”
Magic Johnson paused. Jin went on.
“But the timing didn’t add up. Three years ago and thirty years ago. There was too much time in between.”
“After thinking it over, I came up with one answer.”
Jin scratched his chin with the dagger. A week without shaving had left him with patchy stubble, and the sharp blade scraped it away.
“The Prophet isn’t the fifth Muninn.”
*Shhk.*
The instant a drop of blood rolled from the tip of his chin, where the blade had nicked him, a chilly voice pierced everyone’s ears.
“For more than thirty years, there has been only one Muninn.”
The air around them seemed to chill. Jin shook the blood from his dagger and continued.
“Once I thought of it that way, things finally started to add up. What the fuck, this isn’t a claw machine. I couldn’t understand how people that powerful and loyal kept popping up every few years.”
Yamamoto Genji, who had been listening with wide eyes, let his mouth fall open.
“Th-then...”
“Yeah. The Prophet taught Michael Silbert how to handle magical power, and they worked together toward their own goals. He must’ve been incredibly powerful even thirty years ago.”
The scattered pieces began to fall into place, one by one. Jin Taekyung’s voice became an unseen hand, feeling its way over countless pieces.
One. Two. Three. Ten.
Each piece filled a space that matched its shape. As they came together, the outline of someone began to emerge.
It was a portrait. It was also a puzzle.
But...
*Not enough. Not nearly enough.*
Too many questions remained unanswered for Jin to complete it.
Lose even one piece, and a puzzle could never be whole. This one had gaps everywhere. Filling them was nearly impossible.
At least, it was impossible for Jin to do alone.
“Johnson.”
Jin spoke without warning.
The Grand Mage had risen from the rock. His shadow loomed large, and the staff in his hand gleamed in the moonlight.
“Can I ask you one thing?”
“Anything, Jin.”
“Why have you helped me all this time?”
“Because we’re friends.”
“Like Siegfried Bassmann?”
Magic Johnson raised his staff as he answered.
“Yeah.”
“I hesitated until the end. Honestly, even now I’m not sure. It makes no sense for a monster to use mana and even potions.”
“Anyone would think that if they were human. But there’s nothing in this world that can’t happen.”
*Vwooom.*
The Magic Gem at the tip of the staff began to vibrate. It was an S-rank Magic Gem, obtained by killing a monster that had slaughtered an entire city on its own during the Great Cataclysm.
Feeling the enormous flow of mana surging with the wind, Jin Taekyung suddenly spoke.
“Do you remember what you said earlier?”
Magic Johnson gave a heavy nod.
“I remember. Humans can’t be objective.”
“You were right. I’m only human, so I couldn’t help thinking subjectively.”
“Everyone does. He’s a bit of an unusual case, but that friend is the same.”
Magic Johnson gestured with his chin behind him.
Beyond the Skeleton King, who wore a golden crown made of magical power, hundreds of pairs of eyes gleamed throughout the canyon.
“Then sending the other forces east was...”
“I didn’t want people who had nothing to do with this getting caught up in it.”
“Excellent. Was that your decision?”
“Yes, but...”
Jin Taekyung raised the dagger in his hand and continued.
“It wasn’t just a subjective judgment.”
And at that moment—
*Flash!*
A blinding light burst from Jin’s eyes.
Everyone who faced the sudden flash in the darkness froze for an instant. Everyone but Jin. He was the one who had called forth the light, the one who had wanted it.
*Crack! Stab!*
The dagger shot forward like a beam of light, smashing through armor and tearing through flesh and bone. Jin watched Yamamoto Genji stagger.
“What the hell are you?”
Yamamoto Genji’s eyes widened in disbelief.
Then he—no, The Prophet—grinned.

chapters.title: Chapter 813
paragraphs: *Fwoosh.*
Everything sharpened and slowed.
Dirt and sand flew up beneath his staggering feet. His eyes widened. Blood surged from his chest.
And then...
“What the fuck are you?”
As the words left my mouth, time returned to normal.
I could see Yamamoto Genji—or rather, the bastard wearing his face—grinning.
*The Prophet.*
A moment ago, his eyes had been wide with pain. Now they gleamed with joy and surprise I couldn’t understand.
*He’s happy? Now?*
I pushed the question aside and swung my dagger again.
The Prophet staggered, clutching his bleeding chest. The moment his hand closed around the hilt at his waist, a slash leaped from my dagger and flashed through the darkness ahead of him.
*Shhk.*
A faint line appeared across The Prophet’s wrist with a chilling cut.
His right hand, which had half-drawn the sword, lost its strength and fell away from his body.
*Thud. Splatter!*
Blood sprayed onto the ground. Red blood, no different from any human’s. That only made it harder to believe what I was seeing, even as I charged him.
*Whoosh. Crack!*
I brought my heel down on his leg with the force of a thousand geun. The flesh of his calf burst, and the bones beneath it shattered.
The Prophet dropped to one knee, his balance gone. He reached for me with his remaining hand, but this time I didn’t have to move.
“Stop.”
A deep voice rang out. The wind died, and the air trembled.
I couldn’t see the force that caught The Prophet’s wrist before his hand reached me, but I could feel the Grand Mage’s powerful mana surrounding us.
*Crack.*
His hand stopped dead in midair. Bones ground out of place, and his brow twisted. Then his body began to rise, as if an invisible giant had seized him and lifted him off the ground.
*Whistle—thud, thud, thud!*
Something pure white shot toward him like a beam of light and pierced his limbs.
The long, sharp bone shards sliced through flesh and bone like tofu, pinning his body—which had been floating in the air—deep into the cliff.
*Crunch!*
The solid rock, which might have stood there for hundreds or even thousands of years, held him fast.
Overpowered in an instant after my surprise attack, The Prophet coughed up a mouthful of blood.
“Cough. Heh heh.”
Pain was the same for everyone.
But The Prophet laughed, curling his bloodstained lips as if he couldn’t feel a thing.
“Good. First, I’ll give you credit. Very well done.”
*Wham!*
A blow to the face snapped his head back. His skull struck the cliff with a boom, and he shook his head.
“It’s been a while since I felt my head ring. Having fun is one thing, but let’s not overdo it.”
I stifled a groan.

I’d already cut off his hand and crushed his knee. My first strike had driven straight toward his heart, too. He’d pulled away at the last moment, but the tremendous Scorching Yang Qi carried by my dagger had been enough to ravage his insides.
*An ordinary human would be dead by now.*
But The Prophet wasn’t an ordinary human. That impossible vitality couldn’t belong to one.
And unlike Michael Silbert, who had been practically half-human and half-demon, then died in the form of a monster while bleeding monster’s blood, The Prophet was still shedding red human blood.
“What... what the hell is that thing?”
Magic Johnson and the Skeleton King stared at the incomprehensible being, their gazes trembling. The Prophet laughed, his voice thick with blood.
“No one can answer that. That’s the kind of being I am.”
No. He was wrong.
I steadied my ragged breathing. My eyes gave off a faint glow and burned as if they were on fire.
This was the price of briefly taking in a power beyond humanity. It was also a gift the System had given one foolish human—and the only key to this enormous puzzle.
*The Truthful Eye.*

I’d received the special Item as a Reward for completing **Unknown Death**, the Quest that began with Siegfried Bassmann’s death. I’d only glanced at its details before, but the moment I found a clue, I’d recalled them.

**System Item Window Truthful Eye Type:** Single-Use Item **Grade:** Special **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung **Description:** In the distant past, a god who would become part of myth offered up an eye to drink from the spring of wisdom. In exchange for one eye, he gained infinite wisdom, while the eye that sank to the bottom of the spring gained the power to pierce even the truths of other worlds. **Effect:** Can be applied to a single target only.
*Looking back, the System had always shown me the way.*
At first, I hadn’t known what the consumable Item called the Truthful Eye was for. I hadn’t known what the hologram only I could see was trying to tell me.
But now I did.
A few hours ago, I’d found my one clue. Before that, the System had already handed me the key to understanding it.
A key that could be used on only one target—and therefore had to be used with even greater care.
And now I held the power to see through every truth.
*Fwoooosh.*
Heat flooded my eyes. My vision turned white.
But the divine power within them pushed through the pain and reached out.
Toward Yamamoto Genji. Toward the pope of the fanatics who had built a temple in this desert.
Toward the unknown being who had spent more than thirty years sowing the seeds of catastrophe in this land under the name Muninn—and now meant to bring them to flower himself.
A thick veil hid him, one even Qi Sense couldn’t penetrate. But the eye of the old god called Odin saw through it all.
Pierced it. Revealed what lay beneath.
*Flash!*
The instant a distant, blinding light flooded my vision, countless bells thrashed inside my mind.
System notifications I’d never heard before and holographic windows I’d never seen raced in every direction, to the ends of the earth and above the clouds.
*Ding. Ding. Ding. Diiiiing!*
One sound swallowed another. The translucent holographic windows multiplied from one to five, from five to dozens, then to a hundred.
They were a wave. A mountain.
A gasp escaped me. Cold ran down my spine at the sight before me.
Hundreds. Perhaps thousands.
More holographic windows than I could count burst forth like fireworks. They all came from one being—the beginning and center of everything.
*The Prophet.*
I could hardly breathe. These weren’t merely pieces of information. They were the countless lives he had devoured, the gravestones they had left behind.
Gravestones bearing nothing but names and levels.
And the Truthful Eye within me saw through the identity of the gravedigger who had built this vast cemetery of the dead. It stripped away the thick veil around him and revealed the truth.
*Ding.*
One final bell rang in my ears. The last piece of the puzzle fell into place.
*This is...*
At last, I understood what The Prophet truly was. How this cursed monster had hidden his identity for more than thirty years while doing everything he’d done.
*Right. Now I get it.*
I stared at The Prophet, still smiling. Then, with the breath I’d been holding, I spat out a single word.
“Doppelganger.”
I saw his reaction clearly.
The corners of his mouth, which had been curved like a half-moon, stiffened. The holographic window hovering above his head shone with a particularly gloomy light.
**System Level 170 “The Final Abyss” Doppelganger**
Doppelganger.
A harbinger of ill fortune, a being spoken of like a superstition.

Countless monsters of old myth had torn through the pages of legend and leaped into reality. Yet a doppelganger had never once appeared. Humanity had come to believe there were none among the enemies they had defeated, or those they had yet to face.
Not even in the horrifying Demon Realm. A doppelganger was nothing but an illusion born of fear, a mere superstition.
They were wrong.
The doppelganger had been there from the beginning. Everyone had mistaken its failure to reveal itself for its absence.
At least Jin Taekyung knew that better than anyone. He even knew when this incomprehensible being, which had devoured countless lives, had first slipped into their world.
“Michael Silbert. The Great Battle of Paris.”
His voice came out abruptly, hard as the cliff rock on either side of them. The monster’s smile, frozen for a moment, eased back into place.
“That’s right. On the very day you humans call Christmas, I met him and became part of this world.”
December 25, 2020.
The great battle that made a page in history—and made the name Michael Silbert known to all humanity.
As one layer of that day’s truth peeled away, Jin Taekyung swallowed hard. The Skeleton King clenched his teeth, while Magic Johnson stared at The Prophet—or rather, the doppelganger—in disbelief.
“That can’t be. The one that attacked Paris at the time was definitely...”

“A Dragon. More precisely, a hatchling less than three hundred years old. It was born a Dragon, so arrogance was in its nature. And it let its guard down, as young ones do. Of course, it was unexpected that a human would kill it, even so.”
The doppelganger had cut Johnson off. He went on.
“In the end, they were simply unlucky. The young Dragon, and the humans who miraculously survived their encounter with it.”
The Grand Mage, who had lived through the Great Cataclysm firsthand, couldn’t hold back a groan.
“...It was a lie, then. Michael Silbert made all of it up.”
“Well, not all of it. A Dragon did attack Paris. And Michael did survive alone.”
The doppelganger grinned.

“I knew the moment I saw him. Unlike the others, Michael was quick to understand his position. Before I’d killed even half of them, he was on his knees, begging me to spare him. He said he’d do anything if I let him live.”
“An interesting offer. I accepted. Then he killed the remaining humans himself.”
Jin Taekyung suddenly remembered a line from the conversation he’d had with Michael Silbert just before the man met his end.
*I was struggling to survive, too!*
He’d sounded as though he were spitting blood.
He’d been telling the truth. Michael Silbert had struggled to survive. His desire to live was greater than anyone’s, and he still had ambitions to fulfill.
And so a human and a monster had joined forces.
But it wasn’t a shackle. It was a contract. Two monsters who differed in appearance but shared the same nature had made a deal to achieve their own goals.
But...
“What for?”
“What?”
“I asked what it was for. What was your real reason for wanting to live among people in this world?”
Jin Taekyung ground out the words. After a moment’s silence, the doppelganger smiled.
“Well, I don’t think now’s the time to wait for my answer.”
And at that moment—
*Rumble.*
A tremor swept through the canyon from far away.

sentences.text: *Fwoosh.*
Everything sharpened and slowed.
Dirt and sand flew up beneath his staggering feet.
His eyes widened.
Blood surged from his chest.
And then...
“What the fuck are you?”
As the words left my mouth, time returned to normal.
I could see Yamamoto Genji—or rather, the bastard wearing his face—grinning.
*The Prophet.*
A moment ago, his eyes had been wide with pain.
Now they gleamed with joy and surprise I couldn’t understand.
*He’s happy?
Now?*
I pushed the question aside and swung my dagger again.
The Prophet staggered, clutching his bleeding chest.
The moment his hand closed around the hilt at his waist, a slash leaped from my dagger and flashed through the darkness ahead of him.
*Shhk.*
A faint line appeared across The Prophet’s wrist with a chilling cut.
His right hand, which had half-drawn the sword, lost its strength and fell away from his body.
*Thud.
Splatter!*
Blood sprayed onto the ground.
Red blood, no different from any human’s.
That only made it harder to believe what I was seeing, even as I charged him.
*Whoosh.
Crack!*
I brought my heel down on his leg with the force of a thousand geun.
The flesh of his calf burst, and the bones beneath it shattered.
The Prophet dropped to one knee, his balance gone.
He reached for me with his remaining hand, but this time I didn’t have to move.
“Stop.”
A deep voice rang out.
The wind died, and the air trembled.
I couldn’t see the force that caught The Prophet’s wrist before his hand reached me, but I could feel the Grand Mage’s powerful mana surrounding us.
*Crack.*
His hand stopped dead in midair.
Bones ground out of place, and his brow twisted.
Then his body began to rise, as if an invisible giant had seized him and lifted him off the ground.
*Whistle—thud, thud, thud!*
Something pure white shot toward him like a beam of light and pierced his limbs.
The long, sharp bone shards sliced through flesh and bone like tofu, pinning his body—which had been floating in the air—deep into the cliff.
*Crunch!*
The solid rock, which might have stood there for hundreds or even thousands of years, held him fast.
Overpowered in an instant after my surprise attack, The Prophet coughed up a mouthful of blood.
“Cough.
Heh heh.”
Pain was the same for everyone.
But The Prophet laughed, curling his bloodstained lips as if he couldn’t feel a thing.
“Good.
First, I’ll give you credit.
Very well done.”
*Wham!*
A blow to the face snapped his head back.
His skull struck the cliff with a boom, and he shook his head.
“It’s been a while since I felt my head ring.
Having fun is one thing, but let’s not overdo it.”
I stifled a groan.
I’d already cut off his hand and crushed his knee.
My first strike had driven straight toward his heart, too.
He’d pulled away at the last moment, but the tremendous Scorching Yang Qi carried by my dagger had been enough to ravage his insides.
*An ordinary human would be dead by now.*
But The Prophet wasn’t an ordinary human.
That impossible vitality couldn’t belong to one.
And unlike Michael Silbert, who had been practically half-human and half-demon, then died in the form of a monster while bleeding monster’s blood, The Prophet was still shedding red human blood.
“What... what the hell is that thing?”
Magic Johnson and the Skeleton King stared at the incomprehensible being, their gazes trembling.
The Prophet laughed, his voice thick with blood.
“No one can answer that.
That’s the kind of being I am.”
No.
He was wrong.
I steadied my ragged breathing.
My eyes gave off a faint glow and burned as if they were on fire.
This was the price of briefly taking in a power beyond humanity.
It was also a gift the System had given one foolish human—and the only key to this enormous puzzle.
*The Truthful Eye.*
I’d received the special Item as a Reward for completing **Unknown Death**, the Quest that began with Siegfried Bassmann’s death.
I’d only glanced at its details before, but the moment I found a clue, I’d recalled them.

**System Item Window Truthful Eye Type:** Single-Use Item **Grade:** Special **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung **Description:** In the distant past, a god who would become part of myth offered up an eye to drink from the spring of wisdom.

In exchange for one eye, he gained infinite wisdom, while the eye that sank to the bottom of the spring gained the power to pierce even the truths of other worlds. **Effect:** Can be applied to a single target only.
*Looking back, the System had always shown me the way.*
At first, I hadn’t known what the consumable Item called the Truthful Eye was for.
I hadn’t known what the hologram only I could see was trying to tell me.
But now I did.
A few hours ago, I’d found my one clue.
Before that, the System had already handed me the key to understanding it.
A key that could be used on only one target—and therefore had to be used with even greater care.
And now I held the power to see through every truth.
*Fwoooosh.*
Heat flooded my eyes.
My vision turned white.
But the divine power within them pushed through the pain and reached out.
Toward Yamamoto Genji.
Toward the pope of the fanatics who had built a temple in this desert.
Toward the unknown being who had spent more than thirty years sowing the seeds of catastrophe in this land under the name Muninn—and now meant to bring them to flower himself.
A thick veil hid him, one even Qi Sense couldn’t penetrate.
But the eye of the old god called Odin saw through it all.
Pierced it.
Revealed what lay beneath.
*Flash!*
The instant a distant, blinding light flooded my vision, countless bells thrashed inside my mind.
System notifications I’d never heard before and holographic windows I’d never seen raced in every direction, to the ends of the earth and above the clouds.
*Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
Diiiiing!*
One sound swallowed another.
The translucent holographic windows multiplied from one to five, from five to dozens, then to a hundred.
They were a wave.
A mountain.
A gasp escaped me.
Cold ran down my spine at the sight before me.
Hundreds.
Perhaps thousands.
More holographic windows than I could count burst forth like fireworks.
They all came from one being—the beginning and center of everything.
*The Prophet.*
I could hardly breathe.
These weren’t merely pieces of information.
They were the countless lives he had devoured, the gravestones they had left behind.
Gravestones bearing nothing but names and levels.
And the Truthful Eye within me saw through the identity of the gravedigger who had built this vast cemetery of the dead.
It stripped away the thick veil around him and revealed the truth.
*Ding.*
One final bell rang in my ears.
The last piece of the puzzle fell into place.
*This is...*
At last, I understood what The Prophet truly was.
How this cursed monster had hidden his identity for more than thirty years while doing everything he’d done.
*Right.
Now I get it.*
I stared at The Prophet, still smiling.
Then, with the breath I’d been holding, I spat out a single word.
“Doppelganger.”
I saw his reaction clearly.
The corners of his mouth, which had been curved like a half-moon, stiffened.
The holographic window hovering above his head shone with a particularly gloomy light.

Not even in the horrifying Demon Realm.
A doppelganger was nothing but an illusion born of fear, a mere superstition.

paragraphs: *Crack. Rumble.*
The ground shook. Clods of dirt and fragments of rock broke away from the towering cliffs and rained down overhead, one after another.
“...Damn it.”
Magic Johnson muttered the words like a groan. The Skeleton King and hundreds of undead blocked the canyon’s exit, crouching low as they stared into the darkness.
More precisely, at the countless enemies approaching from beyond it.
*Fwoooosh.*
I steadied my breathing and heightened my Qi Sense, sharpening my senses to take in everything around me.
The depth and force of the tremors traveling through the ground. The wind blowing from the west, and the smell it carried. And the sounds.
They were too far away for me to judge their exact number or strength, but I was certain of one thing.
*They’re not monsters.*
That left only one possibility. The Doppelganger sensed my gaze and bared its bloodstained teeth in a grin.
“Humans are such strange creatures. They’ll throw their lives away for a being they’ve never even seen, calling it a god. All it takes is a few solemn words, and they’re weeping buckets.”
“Fanatics...”

“I liked this land from the start. It was a good place to make plans and cover them up. Most of all, it was crawling with people willing to give their very souls to religion. It was astonishingly easy to win the faith of fools like that.”
*Squirm. Crack.*
The cleanly severed stump of its wrist twitched. Through the gaps in its shattered armor, I could see fresh, pale flesh already growing over the dagger wound in its chest.
It wasn’t a potion. It wasn’t magic.
And yet, even now, its broken body was healing.
An unbelievable rate of recovery—obviously not human. The power of Regeneration, enough to make anyone suspicious.
But the fanatics who had been launching terrorist attacks around the world since before the Great Cataclysm would have seen it differently.
Perhaps they’d glimpsed the shadow of a god in the Doppelganger, who used mana and had the same red blood and flesh as they did.
“A miracle.”
Its voice rang out, brimming with excitement. The Doppelganger stared at me with blazing eyes and continued.
“To them, I am not a monster but a miracle itself—the Prophet who will lead them to the promised land.”
“They’ll fight until the very last one falls. For their god. And for me.”
I didn’t argue with the Doppelganger’s confident claim.
It was the truth.
No matter what we did, a clash was inevitable.
The Doppelganger had planted its followers in this desert far earlier than I’d expected. The wave of fanatics that began there had already shaken the world through terrorism.
So even if I told them the truth about the Doppelganger, nothing would change.
*If a few words were enough to make them see reason, they wouldn’t be fanatics.*
This was the work of a monster and a bunch of madmen. And right now, I was nothing but a heretic who had to be killed.
A heretic persecuting the great Prophet chosen by God.
“Then there’s only one thing left to do.”
I muttered evenly, staring at the Doppelganger. It understood what I meant, and the corners of its mouth curled upward.
“I’m looking forward to it.”
“Yeah?”
*Thud!*
As I spoke, I thrust my dagger forward, piercing its heart.
Its limbs were bound, so it couldn’t dodge. The Doppelganger merely frowned and sighed.
“Give it a rest. That hurts like hell.”
*Crack.*
The severed muscles and shattered bones returned to their proper places. Bright red blood filled the gaps, and smooth skin, like a child’s, grew over it.
It healed at a staggering speed, as if a video were playing in fast-forward.
Even the great shards of bone that had pierced its limbs and pinned it deep into the cliff shifted slightly, pushed by the flesh and bone growing around them.
The countless Level windows I’d seen with the **Truthful Eye**—and could still see now—meant far more than they appeared to.
*Other lives.*
They were fuel, but they were also the lives of the victims the Doppelganger had devoured.
Like an arcade game character that came back to life whenever you fed it a coin, the bastard could keep reviving.
*But it’s not truly immortal.*
I twisted the dagger still in my hand. Heat surged from my dantian, raced through my acupoints, and flowed into the blade.
*Thud—boom!*
Scorching Yang Qi poured through the dagger buried deep in its chest and exploded inside the Doppelganger.
Its heart had already been pierced once, yet it had recovered as if nothing could kill it. Now the heart was crushed completely, and the clear bell I’d been waiting for rang in my ear.
*Ding.*
**System** Defeated Lv. 120 Yamamoto Genji! Gained a significant amount of **EXP**!
One life faded, and a new one took its place.
The Doppelganger was still grinning. Behind its melting skin, another unfamiliar face was ready to emerge.
“Imagine that. Jin Taekyung killed Genji. Japan’s going to lose its mind when they hear about this.”
“Shut your mouth.”
A low nose bridge. Crooked teeth visible inside its mouth.
Judging by features distinctive even among East Asians, this had to be a Hunter from J1—one of the team thought to have been wiped out apart from Yamamoto Genji.
“Come to think of it, I forgot to introduce myself. Nice to meet you. I’m Hiroshi Inoue. I spent my childhood in Nagasaki, then moved to Tokyo...”
I grabbed it by the throat and twisted hard.
Its neck bones shattered under my grip, and its head bent at a grotesque angle.
*Ding.* Another bell rang, and the twisted head straightened. The face, smiling coyly, belonged to a woman I’d never seen before.
“Oh, did you know? This woman was the lover of the man you just killed. Looks like they were planning to get married this year.”
My hand stopped dead, as if someone had hit a pause button. The Doppelganger whistled, clearly enjoying itself.
“Wow. So passionate. Humans really are amazing when it comes to things like this. We could learn a thing or two.”
“Ah, sorry. I apologize if that made you uncomfortable. But what can I do? It’s my ability.”
I clenched my teeth.
The Doppelganger hadn’t just absorbed its victims’ appearances. It could reproduce their abilities exactly as they’d had them in life—and it had their memories, too.
Those memories, spilling from its mouth, dug into my chest like an awl and made me hesitate.
*Crack.*
Blood seeped between my clenched teeth.
Beyond the canyon, the tremors had grown stronger, and I could feel a fierce killing intent. In front of me, a monster that came back no matter how many times I killed it was smiling faintly.
“Jin!”
Magic Johnson’s urgent shout struck my eardrums. The smile on the Doppelganger’s face deepened.
“This is your last chance.”
“What?”
“Right now is your last chance to run and survive.”
*Whoosh.*
The cool desert wind brushed my face. It felt as if I’d been doused in cold water.
The Doppelganger shrugged at me as I stood frozen like a statue.
“I understand. It’d hurt your pride. You’d be embarrassed. But if you die here like the rest of those humans, would that be a pointless death—or a noble sacrifice by a hero?”
“You have to look at the bigger picture. You’re the World Hunter Federation’s Alliance Leader. The one and only light and hope who can save this world, like someone from the past. Aren’t you?”
Its gentle voice tickled my ear, like a snake coaxing me to steal and eat the forbidden apple.
The Doppelganger’s low whisper wound softly around my whole body.
“Run. And survive.”
*Rumble.*
The canyon shook. The footsteps of countless fanatics—and the hooves of the camels they rode—were approaching from the darkness beyond.
“Think of your family and friends. Can you even imagine how much sorrow and pain they’ll suffer because of your death?”
“...Sorrow and pain?”
“That’s right. You’ve been through it yourself.”
My lips moved without a sound.
Sorrow and pain over someone’s death. Yeah, I’d been through it. It had shaken me so badly I’d felt close to falling apart.
“No one will blame you. Even I respect everything you’ve done. So even now...”
The eyes of the nameless woman—or rather, the Doppelganger—sparkled.
“Run.”
“Allahu Akbar!”
The mighty roar of countless voices merging into one rang across the darkening desert.
Brilliant light shimmered around Magic Johnson, while hundreds of undead stared with dimly glowing eyes at the waves of fanatics surging toward them.
And I...
Let go of the Doppelganger’s neck.
*Step.*
I took a step back and saw it smiling at me. It spoke gently, as if to a child.
“Good. You made the right choice.”
I found myself muttering.
“Is this the best option?”
“It has to be.”
“Good. Then I’m glad.”
I nodded, then murmured under my breath.
“Open. Summon.”
“Hm?”
*Shhk!*
As it asked its empty question, the Doppelganger’s head flew into the air.
A new face rose onto its shoulders as if someone had turned a page, and blinked.
The heat blazing around **White Flame**’s spearhead cast a reddish glow in its eyes.
“What the fuck are you, some Ditto from a failed link trade? Quit trying to pull that crap on me.”
Only then did the Doppelganger understand what had happened. It sighed.
“You crazy bastard...”
“Got anything more original? I’ve heard that one so many times I’m sick of it.”
“Why are you doing this?”
“That’s what I want to ask you.”
“What?”

“You started spouting nonsense from the get-go, and I wondered what the hell was going on. But the more I listened, the more curious I got. You’re the first monster I’ve ever seen telling a human to run. For a second, I almost called you Mom, you son of a bitch.”
“What the hell are you? You’re trying so hard not to get caught, but you keep giving yourself away. So I know you’re stupid—but what do you actually want?”
A brief silence followed. The Doppelganger stared at me without a word, then furrowed its brow.
“Damn it. This has gone to shit. Why are you so reckless? You want to be remembered by history as a hero who made a noble sacrifice?”
“Quit talking out of your ass and answer me. My dream is to be the head of a longevity village.”
“Then why the hell...!”
*Scree!*
A cry rang out from the sky, swallowing the Doppelganger’s unfinished words.
It naturally looked up at the sky, and its eyes suddenly widened.
“...What’s that?”
I already knew what the Doppelganger was seeing.
Before the forces split up, I’d used Sound Transmission to give the Skeleton King direct orders.
“They’re a little late, but they made it just in time.”
*Screee!*
Dozens of eagles and griffins glided over the canyon with their wings spread wide.
On the backs of the enormous flying beasts, I could see the Hunters who should have gone east.

Those memories, spilling from its mouth, dug into my chest like an awl and made me hesitate.
*Crack.*
Blood seeped between my clenched teeth.
Beyond the canyon, the tremors had grown stronger, and I could feel a fierce killing intent.
In front of me, a monster that came back no matter how many times I killed it was smiling faintly.
“Jin!”
Magic Johnson’s urgent shout struck my eardrums.
The smile on the Doppelganger’s face deepened.
“This is your last chance.”
“What?”
“Right now is your last chance to run and survive.”
*Whoosh.*
The cool desert wind brushed my face.
It felt as if I’d been doused in cold water.
The Doppelganger shrugged at me as I stood frozen like a statue.
“I understand.
It’d hurt your pride.
You’d be embarrassed.
But if you die here like the rest of those humans, would that be a pointless death—or a noble sacrifice by a hero?”
“You have to look at the bigger picture.
You’re the World Hunter Federation’s Alliance Leader.
The one and only light and hope who can save this world, like someone from the past.
Aren’t you?”
Its gentle voice tickled my ear, like a snake coaxing me to steal and eat the forbidden apple.
The Doppelganger’s low whisper wound softly around my whole body.
“Run.
And survive.”
*Rumble.*
The canyon shook.
The footsteps of countless fanatics—and the hooves of the camels they rode—were approaching from the darkness beyond.
“Think of your family and friends.
Can you even imagine how much sorrow and pain they’ll suffer because of your death?”
“...Sorrow and pain?”
“That’s right.
You’ve been through it yourself.”
My lips moved without a sound.
Sorrow and pain over someone’s death.
Yeah, I’d been through it.
It had shaken me so badly I’d felt close to falling apart.
“No one will blame you.
Even I respect everything you’ve done.
So even now...”
The eyes of the nameless woman—or rather, the Doppelganger—sparkled.
“Run.”
“Allahu Akbar!”
The mighty roar of countless voices merging into one rang across the darkening desert.
Brilliant light shimmered around Magic Johnson, while hundreds of undead stared with dimly glowing eyes at the waves of fanatics surging toward them.
And I...
Let go of the Doppelganger’s neck.
*Step.*
I took a step back and saw it smiling at me.
It spoke gently, as if to a child.
“Good.
You made the right choice.”
I found myself muttering.
“Is this the best option?”
“It has to be.”
“Good.
Then I’m glad.”
I nodded, then murmured under my breath.
“Open.
Summon.”
“Hm?”
*Shhk!*
As it asked its empty question, the Doppelganger’s head flew into the air.
A new face rose onto its shoulders as if someone had turned a page, and blinked.
The heat blazing around **White Flame**’s spearhead cast a reddish glow in its eyes.
“What the fuck are you, some Ditto from a failed link trade?
Quit trying to pull that crap on me.”
Only then did the Doppelganger understand what had happened.
It sighed.
“You crazy bastard...”
“Got anything more original?
I’ve heard that one so many times I’m sick of it.”
“Why are you doing this?”
“That’s what I want to ask you.”
“What?”
“You started spouting nonsense from the get-go, and I wondered what the hell was going on.
But the more I listened, the more curious I got.
You’re the first monster I’ve ever seen telling a human to run.
For a second, I almost called you Mom, you son of a bitch.”
“What the hell are you?
You’re trying so hard not to get caught, but you keep giving yourself away.
So I know you’re stupid—but what do you actually want?”
A brief silence followed.
The Doppelganger stared at me without a word, then furrowed its brow.
“Damn it.
This has gone to shit.
Why are you so reckless?
You want to be remembered by history as a hero who made a noble sacrifice?”
“Quit talking out of your ass and answer me.
My dream is to be the head of a longevity village.”
“Then why the hell...!”
*Scree!*
A cry rang out from the sky, swallowing the Doppelganger’s unfinished words.
It naturally looked up at the sky, and its eyes suddenly widened.
“...What’s that?”
I already knew what the Doppelganger was seeing.
Before the forces split up, I’d used Sound Transmission to give the Skeleton King direct orders.
“They’re a little late, but they made it just in time.”
*Screee!*
Dozens of eagles and griffins glided over the canyon with their wings spread wide.
On the backs of the enormous flying beasts, I could see the Hunters who should have gone east.

chapters.title: Chapter 815
paragraphs: *Whoooosh.*
Cold night wind swept over Choi Minwoo. He brushed back his windblown hair and looked down at the canyon rushing closer.
*There it is.*
The spearhead’s cold gleam was unmistakable even in the deep darkness.
Choi had collected countless fine weapons and artifacts over the years, but the strength and sharpness of the spear named White Flame still amazed him.
*Though not as much as its owner.*
He thought of Jin Taekyung.
When they first met, Choi could never have imagined that the young man his age who’d joined a raid as a porter would stand above every Hunter in the world less than a year later.
But Jin Taekyung had made the unimaginable real.

He had prevented countless disasters and grown astonishingly through every ordeal. The boldness and courage he showed in a crisis kept surpassing even Choi’s expectations—and Choi had watched him more closely than anyone.
Just like today.
*I could tell something was different from usual...but Mr. Jin keeps getting another step ahead of us.*
When the Skeleton King’s undead relayed what was happening, Choi had felt surprised and a little hurt. Before long, though, those feelings had turned to joy.
Jin had solved a problem no one else could. That was proof he’d grown yet again.
*With him, we can win.*
Jin Taekyung was the commander in chief leading them all, the general directing the battle, and the vanguard who charged toward the enemy ahead of everyone else.
How could Choi not trust him? How could he not love him?
No matter how many obstacles and dangers lay along Jin’s path, that would never change.
*There are a lot of them.*
Choi gazed down calmly.
Hundreds of meters below, a black mass of enemies poured into the canyon like a wave.
Too many to count.
Their footsteps shook the earth, and their shouts rang out from every direction.
“Allahu Akbar!”
“Brothers and sisters, charge! To the promised land!”
“God’s salvation awaits us!”
The fanatics who’d hidden from the eyes of the world were crying out. Ironically, those calling for God’s salvation held weapons that brought blood and death.
*They’re not people like us. They’re just enemies we have to bring down.*
Choi repeated the thought to himself like a vow. No—every Hunter looking down at them felt the same way.
They’d already seen it. They’d learned it the hard way.
Humans could be more good—or more evil—than any other living creature. Monsters weren’t the only things that threatened this world.
Before Demon King Asmodeus descended, those who had brought about countless wars and deaths had been human, too. Humanity had suffered at their hands and learned a lesson it must never forget.
*There are monsters with red blood, too.*
And the Hunters gathered here existed for one reason. Their sole duty was to hunt those monsters.
*Shing.*
Blades appeared here and there, their edges glinting coldly.
The Hunters were visibly more exhausted than usual after their battle against the monster horde, but the determination in their eyes was stronger than ever.
*Fwoooosh!*
The wind grew fiercer. Hearts pounded faster.
Dozens of eagles and griffins angled their enormous wings and plunged toward the ground.
The fanatics’ shouts, distant as an echo a moment ago, now thundered in everyone’s ears.
“Fight to the last! Don’t fall back!”
Choi swallowed. The wind stung his skin. The fanatics surged into the canyon, radiating a madness that seemed almost tangible.
A towering Grand Mage and the Skeleton King, with hundreds of undead at his command, stood in their way. Not one of the fanatics was afraid.
To them, this was a holy war. Even if they died, they would stand beside God as holy martyrs.
These warriors of God had already experienced the miracle of awakening. They kicked off their camels and shot forward at blinding speed.
Three hundred meters. One hundred. Fifty.
The distance vanished.
And then...
Impact.
*Boom! Kaa-boooom!*
“Graaagh!”
Flames devoured the darkness.
The vanguard took a direct hit from Magic Johnson’s attack magic and went up in flames, screaming. Other fanatics instantly filled the gap left by the dead and charged the undead without hesitation.
*Crunch, craaack!*
The canyon wasn’t absurdly narrow, but it wasn’t wide, either. Yet the fanatics the Doppelganger had cultivated over many years broke through the undead battle line at once.
In their hearts and minds, they might already have been monsters. But they were fundamentally different from actual monsters.
They were as strong and clever as any Hunter. Above all, they had two excellent commanders.
“Fallen demons! Wipe them all out!”
“Inshallah.”
One man rampaged at the front, shouting roughly. An old man watched the battlefield with a composed expression from the rear.
The two stood out even amid the chaos. The moment Choi spotted them, he instinctively grasped how powerful they were.
*S-rank Hunters—or should I call them fanatics?*
They were beyond what he could handle now.
Strangely, he wasn’t afraid.
The next moment, the old man looked up, and their eyes met. Choi’s resolve didn’t waver.
*Shhk. Slice!*
The strike came like a flash of light.
A streak of aura shot from the old man’s waist and cleanly severed the neck of Choi’s griffin. The huge flying monster went limp and tipped to one side.
*Fwoosh. Rattle!*
The wind turned violent, and Choi was thrown about.
But he didn’t panic. Their dive had become a fall, yet for some reason, he found himself smiling.
The screams of the other Hunters clinging to the griffin’s spine didn’t matter. Neither did the way they stared at him as though he’d lost his mind.
*I don’t regret any of the choices I’ve made. I’ll just fight as hard as I can.*
His mind was calm. The sword in his hand felt as light as a feather. Today, he felt he could do anything.
The ground rushed closer, and the shout of a fanatic he didn’t know struck his ears.
“For the great God, for the Prophet!”
Choi laughed aloud. Then he spoke.
“For our Alliance Leader.”
His voice was low but powerful. It was the signal.
*Papat!*
Choi Minwoo—and all the Hunters—kicked off the body of the griffin plummeting straight toward the ground and soared away.
*Tap.*
Choi landed first. The sword in his hand blurred.
*Whoosh! Chaaash!*
A sharp wind rose from the blade, slicing through the limbs of fanatics rushing him from every side.
A streak of light shot between the bodies collapsing in sprays of blood.
*Whoosh—bang!*
Choi raised his sword in time to block it, but that was all he could do.
The force drove him back several steps. A low voice reached his ears.
“I thought I recognized that face. Now I know—you’re Sky’s blood.”
The Arab man approached with a sword wrapped in aura, his eyes full of menace.
Amid the chaos, Choi spoke in his heart to someone he couldn’t see.
*I don’t know how long I—or we—can hold out.*
But he knew one thing better than anyone.
He had to fight. He couldn’t fall before the enemy did.
Even if that enemy was far stronger than him.
*Swish.*
Choi pointed his sword at the man. The **Hero’s Sword**, imbued with brilliant aura, shone brightly.
The eight hundred or so Hunters who’d dropped from the sky gathered around its light as it spread through the darkness.
“Damn heretics. I’ll send you all to hell.”
The man vanished from sight, a vicious smile on his face. A sword strike flashed out at the same instant and grazed Choi’s neck as he instinctively ducked.
The Skeleton King, who’d been holding off the fanatics swarming from all sides, shot toward the man.
*Boom!*
Countless roars and screams swept through the canyon. The ground heaved, and the solid bedrock split apart.
The bloodshed and shock of a battle unlike any the canyon had seen in centuries reached the cliffs on either side—even the canyon’s center, dozens of meters beyond its entrance.
And those tiny cracks helped, if only a little, to free someone who should never have escaped.
*Thud-thud. Bang!*
A bone shard as long as a spear and thicker than one blasted outward. At the same time, new flesh and blood welled up from the severed ends of countless shattered limbs.
*Slide. Crack.*
Recovery so fast it was impossible to believe, even seeing it firsthand.
No—Regeneration.
The Doppelganger completed its one hundred and forty-fifth resurrection and grinned, baring bloodstained teeth.
“Oh. We’re only getting started, and you’re tired already?”
*Thwack!*
A streak of light pierced the space between its eyes instead of answering. The young man holding the spear moved his dry, cracked lips.
“No. I think I’ve got a little more in me now.”
And at that moment—
*Ding.*
A bell rang out clearly, audible to one person alone.
Right after reaching the Supreme Peak realm, I’d joined the ranks of the superhuman. No one could deny that.
But even superhumans were still human.
They felt pain when they were hurt, tensed up when they faced someone strong, and eventually grew tired if they kept moving.
I was one of them.
Except for one thing.
*Ding.*

**System** Lv. 78 Brody Woods defeated! Gained a tiny amount of EXP! Level Up! The effects of leveling up fill you with healing power! Special Debuff: Broken Body rejects the healing power! Status Effect: Fatigue removed! Status Effect: Muscle Pain removed! Status Effect: Internal Energy Depletion... ... ...
As System messages appeared one after another, my fading vision cleared.
I felt the fatigue melt away and my internal energy return. I muttered a name.
“Brody Woods. Brody Woods...”
A name I had to remember for the rest of my life. Brody was a hero who’d saved me when I was nearing my limit.
The same went for every one of those victims who’d died twice.
With that in mind...
“Die.”
*Slice.*
The Doppelganger was staggering to its feet when my spearhead swept through it. Its upper body slid away at an angle.
And at the same time, the sight I’d grown sick of seeing played out before my eyes once again.
*Slither.*
Blood and flesh welled up at a terrifying speed. The Doppelganger rose whole, looking more relaxed than ever.
“That’s enough. You must be close to your limit by now.”
“Nope. I’m doing fine.”
*Thrust!*
“You can’t have much left. No need to bluff.”
“I told you, I’m fine.”
*Thud, splatter!*
“This really is the last—”
“Hey.”
*Slice!*
Resurrected yet again, the Doppelganger muttered, “What kind of fucking bastard are you...?”
