chapters.title: Chapter 816
paragraphs: What the hell was going on?
The Doppelganger couldn’t help being baffled. Dying the moment it came back to life was one thing. It had even expected to put up little resistance.
Its limbs had been bound, and Jin Taekyung was stronger than any human it had ever seen.
But there was one thing it couldn’t understand.
*What is this?*
He wasn’t getting tired. He just wasn’t.
More precisely, whenever he seemed to be tiring, he was suddenly fine again. Even the Doppelganger, sick to death of experiencing death, was starting to curse.
“What kind of fucking bastard is this...?”
*Slice!*
Before it could finish, a flash of light. A spearhead, driven with precise force and speed, cut across its Adam’s apple.
One life faded, and another life and its memories—absorbed long ago—filled the empty space.
*What kind of bullshit is this?*
The Doppelganger came back to life after a brief moment of pain, its eyelids twitching. A spearhead was already flying toward it.
*Whoosh!*
A lightning-fast strike.
But this time, the Doppelganger had no intention of going down so easily.
A moment ago, it had been a middling B-rank Hunter. With this resurrection, it was a genuine A-rank Hunter.
One of the top twenty rankers in France, no less.
*Jean the Swift.*
Recalling the nickname from the memories it had absorbed, the Doppelganger stepped onto the ground with feet that felt unusually light.
*Swish.*
A breeze skimmed past its chest by a hair’s breadth.
Its form wavered like a heat haze, then appeared several meters back. A relaxed smile spread across its lips. It had dodged without difficulty.
“From here on, things won’t be so ea—”
*Shwhack! Thunk!*
A streak of Finger Qi pierced the space between its eyes. Having died without putting up a fight after all, the Doppelganger blinked as it came back to life.
*Huh? That’s not right.*
It hadn’t even seen what hit it. At least Jin Taekyung had stopped attacking for a moment, for some reason.
“Huh? What was that just now?”
At the sight of him asking in apparent surprise, the Doppelganger felt sure of itself.
*Of course. That last hit must’ve been pure luck.*
From its perspective, the conclusion was only natural.

The Hunter whose life it had just used had ranked among the best in his country. An assassin-type Hunter whose speed had earned him the name Jean the Swift. If he’d decided to dodge from the start, even Michael Silbert would have found him a nuisance.
*No matter how special Jin Taekyung is, he can’t be that far above Michael Silbert.*
But the Doppelganger had no idea what Jin Taekyung’s question had really meant.
*Jean Pierre? Who’s this guy, and why is he worth so much EXP?*
He’d never heard the name. The Hunter world might be small, but he couldn’t know every foreign Hunter by name unless they were famous worldwide.
*Anyway, thank you. Rest in peace.*
Jin Taekyung offered his thanks and condolences to the Hunter who’d been absorbed, then raised his lowered spearhead.
That was enough respect for the dead. What he needed to do next was already clear.
Before even more people were sacrificed, he had to copy the EXP—no, completely erase the Doppelganger.
“No time to waste. Let’s get one more death in.”
*Thrust! Crack!*
With a final cry, another flame of life went out.
The Doppelganger had died more than two hundred times in less than ten minutes. Unease began to show in its eyes.
*This can’t go on. I underestimated him.*
The Doppelganger had greedily devoured countless lives. For more than thirty years, it had absorbed human souls, memories, and powers across the world, becoming something close to immortal.
Its ability was unique even among the countless kinds of monsters in the Demon Realm.
But the Doppelganger knew exactly where its limits lay.
*I’m not completely immortal, and I can’t combine the powers I’ve absorbed into one.*
A fire dies when it runs out of wood. Thousands of different fragments could be joined together, but they could never become a single whole.
It was an extraordinary ability. But not when measured against the rare few born to wield absolute power.
Like the one who had sent it to this world.
*Until every part of the plan is complete, I must never come face-to-face with the target.*
*Whump!*
Its vision went black. Another death—how many now?—cut off the voice echoing in its mind.
*Cough.*
The Doppelganger came back to life in pain, regret passing over its face.
*I should never have gotten close to him.*
The reason for its failure was clear.
For more than thirty years, the Doppelganger had enjoyed a freedom it had never known before. After Cheon Taemin disappeared, it had manipulated the world from the shadows.
That freedom and power had gone to its head.
In the Demon Realm, it had been bound to someone else. Here, it was a king in all but name, able to accomplish anything it set its mind to.
The more arrogant the Doppelganger became, the less weight it gave to its orders—and the heavier its own complacency grew.
Michael Silbert?
Even he was only a servant and a tool. His obedience was commendable enough, but when the time came, he would be discarded like any piece that had served its purpose.
The plan had taken a long time to prepare. Now it was only one step from completion.
And yet...
*Damn it.*
*Slice.*
Something hot cut across its chest. Pain it still couldn’t get used to seized its whole body.
*Hoo.*
As death gave way to life again, the Doppelganger let out the breath that had been cut short.
The moment it opened its eyes, someone’s fist filled its vision.
*Thwack.*
Its vision swam. Only when it came to again did it realize its head had been smashed apart.
It took an involuntary step back and slipped on the brain matter it had spilled moments earlier.
“Internal energy’s wasted on a bastard like you.”
Jin Taekyung’s voice reached its ears. He sounded so calm it was chilling, and the chill stole the Doppelganger’s breath.
A foot slammed down on its chest with tremendous weight and took what little breath remained.
*Crack! Crunch! Splatter!*
Darkness. Light. Darkness again, without pause.
In fractions of a single second, the Doppelganger died and came back to life several times.
Even freed from its restraints, it fared no better. If anything, a wider variety of deaths and agonies awaited it.
*Why? Why the hell?!*
It screamed its anger and regret in silence.
Only now did it truly understand its master’s command not to meet the target before the plan was complete.
*This man... is different.*
He was unlike any human it had absorbed over the years, or any it had watched from afar, licking its lips while taking care not to draw attention.
No. He didn’t seem human at all.
Just like Cheon Taemin.
*Whoom! Boom!*
With a heavy rush of air, an open palm struck its chest. The force shattered its bones, and the heat within the blow burned its organs.
*Cough.*
The Doppelganger spat out dead blood and looked at Jin Taekyung through dimming eyes.
Jin’s face blurred as its vision darkened, but the powerful aura pouring from his body was clearer than anything else in the world.
“The C-Chosen One...”
The words slipped out like a groan. Its head drooped limply.
Jin Taekyung’s fist shot toward it like a mace to deliver another death—then touched its forehead as lightly as a blade of grass.
*Tap. Fwoosh!*
The wind swept around them, unable to keep up with the speed of his punch. Jin Taekyung’s cold gaze settled on the Doppelganger’s new face.
“What did you just say?”
The Doppelganger swallowed. It had let the words slip without meaning to. Its consciousness had grown hazy through the endless deaths and resurrections of those few moments.
“I didn’t say anything...”
“Really?”
*Grab. Crack!*
Before it could finish, its vision went black.
It had lost count of its deaths. Less than half the countless lives that had filled its body remained.
The Doppelganger opened its eyes amid bedrock shattered along with its skull. Regret had given way to fear.
Fear of death itself.
*At this rate... I’ll be erased.*
Its life was not infinite. To survive, it had absorbed the life force of others and burned it like firewood, just as its kin had once done.
*And they, too, were erased forever.*
There had been a time when the Doppelgangers held sway over the Demon Realm. But after long years and a brutal purge, it alone had survived out of hundreds of its kind.
That was why “Doppelganger” had become the name of a single being—and why it was called “The Final Abyss.”
*I can’t—I can’t be erased. I have to survive!*
The Doppelganger gritted its teeth and opened its eyes. New life force and mana filled its body, along with the abilities of the human it had absorbed.
*Vrrrrm.*
Mana gathered around its fist, coating it in a faint aura. The Doppelganger sprang to its feet and drove a punch toward Jin Taekyung’s face.
*Whoosh!*
The thunderous rush of air came a moment later. A hard, thick palm blocked its fist.
No—it squeezed it.
*Crack.*
Pain nearly wiped its mind blank.
Its fist had been crushed like tofu. And once again, there was no escaping death.
“Hey, what are you doing?”
*Whoom! Boom!*
The world turned upside down. Its consciousness returned with a crash loud enough to burst its eardrums.
The Doppelganger revived in the center of a small crater and immediately kicked off the ground.
Away from Jin Taekyung.
*I’ll survive. Somehow!*
It had long since forgotten shame. Jin Taekyung was the “Chosen One” its master had spoken of.
The Doppelganger drew out every bit of power this new life had given it and launched itself away.
*Pop!*
Its blurred form shot through the air.
Or tried to.
As it took its second step, a streak of light flashed toward it.
*Slice!*
Its headless body slammed into the ground. Several meters away, the Doppelganger came back to life, only for a lightning-fast strike to cleave down over its head.
*Fwoosh!*
A fountain of blood burst from its body, split in two.
Jin Taekyung didn’t stop. His heated spearhead cut through the air again and again.
*Shh-shh-shhk!*
A flash of light cut across its tilting body. Its limbs, chopped into dozens of pieces, hit the ground—and immediately began to grow back at a terrifying speed.
“Gyaaaah!”
The Doppelganger roared as it revived amid that gruesome death. Pain still lingered, gnawing at its senses like insects.
If Jin Taekyung had just used up a considerable amount of internal energy with that last strike, the Doppelganger had to sacrifice a dozen or more lives.
Now it understood. To escape Jin Taekyung, it would have to spend even the lives it had been saving.
*Fwooooo.*
Vast mana poured over both its hands. Looking at a face he seemed to recognize, Jin Taekyung muttered like a groan:
“Siegfried Bassmann?”

chapters.title: Chapter 817
paragraphs: The Doppelganger’s new face was all too familiar to Jin Taekyung.
He’d seen it in person only once, shriveled like a mummy. But while investigating Michael Silbert, he’d seen that same face in photographs so many times he was sick of it.
And then there was...
*Whoooosh.*
That immense magical power, so palpable he could almost reach out and touch it.
He didn’t need to check the Level window to know the answer.
“Siegfried Bassmann?”
At Jin Taekyung’s muttered question, the Doppelganger snapped its fingers instead of answering.
*Crackle.*
White light flashed.
The faint current running along its finger became dozens of lightning bolts and came crashing down. It took only an instant.
*Zzap!*
Blinding light filled Jin Taekyung’s vision.
His eyes closed before he knew it, but he could still feel the tremendous current through the rock surrounding him, the air, and the ground. Through everything.
*Boom!*
The hard rock and earth beneath him split in a spiderweb of cracks.
Jin Taekyung kicked off the ground and shot upward, thrusting out a palm. The heat of Flame Divine Palm burned through the lightning as it surged forward.
*KABOOOOOM!*
A tremendous blast shook the canyon.
But Jin Taekyung sharpened his sight and caught everything that happened in that brief moment.
The rising flames. The acrid smoke.
And the Doppelganger vanishing like a ghost just before it all erupted.
*Blink.*
Teleport and Warp were spells for crossing long distances. Blink was short-range movement: disappearing for an instant, just as its name suggested.
Its range was limited. Jin Taekyung’s senses and vision, on the other hand, covered the entire canyon.
*There.*
He couldn’t see it. But he could feel it.
Jin Taekyung drew a breath. He trusted his senses and his abilities.
Channeling internal energy through his toes, he stepped on empty air and shot toward the Doppelganger beyond the drifting embers and acrid smoke.
*Whoosh! Boom!*
The air burst around him, unable to withstand his speed. Smoke and embers scattered as if blown apart, and his vision cleared.
At the end of his path, having become a streak of flame, he found the Doppelganger fleeing toward the followers who could help it.
A chill prickled down its back. The Doppelganger turned instinctively, its eyes widening.
In a world that seemed to slow around it, Jin Taekyung was already right in front of it, filling its vision.
*How the hell?*
Less than a second had passed.
Yet Jin Taekyung had found where Blink had taken it and crossed the dozen or so meters between them.
*You’ve got to be fucking kidding me...!*
The Doppelganger swallowed the curse rising to its lips.
No. It hadn’t even had time to curse.
Waste a moment, and it could lose the Grand Mage’s power forever—an asset far more precious than all the other lives it had discarded.
*Shwaa!*
A reddish-hot spearhead tore through the wind. The killing intent that accompanied it was cold enough to freeze the Doppelganger in place.
But the mana and abilities it possessed at that moment belonged to one of only three Grand Mages in the world.
*Blin—k!*
*Fwoosh, boom!*
Flames erupted along the spearhead and devoured the empty air.
The Doppelganger appeared a dozen or so meters away and felt a chill run down its spine.
Because it had barely escaped?
No.
Because a pair of eyes was staring straight at it.
*Jin Taekyung.*
Their gazes had only met, but its heart sank. An instinct honed over centuries of struggle whispered to it.
Run.
If it didn’t want that beast to tear out the back of its neck, it couldn’t let its guard down for a moment.
The Doppelganger cast Blink again without pausing. In the next instant, it knew its instinct had been right.
*Whoosh! Slice!*
It opened its eyes in a new space and let out the breath it had been holding.
The back of its armor, long since stripped of its original shape and purpose, was hot from the heat that had grazed it.
*He cut me. He’s fast enough to keep up with Blink.*
It had escaped by a hair.
A shiver ran through it. Of all the humans it had absorbed or encountered in passing, none had been a monster like this.
Except for the one person it feared—and had deliberately avoided for that reason.
*Cheon Taemin.*
The savior of humanity.
The only Adversary to face the Demon King Asmodeus with the body and mind of a frail human. A divine man.
The Doppelganger neither denied its fear of Cheon Taemin nor felt ashamed of it.
He was no being it could call “a mere human.”
That was why, even after absorbing Siegfried Bassmann years ago and learning of Cheon Taemin’s condition, it had never dared to go after him.
But the Doppelganger had never imagined it could feel this much fear of any human other than Cheon Taemin.
*Blink, Blink, Blink!*
Hesitate, and it might face permanent Erasure.
Desperate, the Doppelganger leaped through space again and again.
Each time its form vanished as if rubbed away by an eraser, it drew closer to the canyon exit, where a fierce battle was underway.
The hunter pursuing it drew closer, too.
*Whsssh!*
A sharp whistle cut through the air.
A dozen or so daggers flashed toward the Doppelganger’s entire body. The attack had been timed and aimed so precisely that it had no chance to cast Blink.
With no other choice, the Doppelganger gritted its teeth and spread both hands.
*Vrrrrm, crack!*
Its mana shield shattered before it had fully formed. The daggers ricocheted away and buried themselves in the cliffs and ground on either side.
But in the brief time it took to block them, Jin Taekyung had reached it.
“Got you.”
*Crack!*
The Doppelganger had no time to react.
Its mouth fell open as tremendous pain shot through its wrist.
Siegfried Bassmann had been a great Grand Mage in life, but Jin Taekyung’s terrifying strength couldn’t be stopped by any magic in his memories.
*Crreeeak!*
“Gyaaaah!”
The scream tore from the Doppelganger’s lips.
Jin Taekyung’s grip alone crushed flesh and muscle and splintered bone.
Its vision went white. The sky and ground tilted.
*I’m being flipped over. No—I’m going to die.*
The Doppelganger knew it instinctively.
After this terrifying feeling of weightlessness would come the impact. Its whole body would be crushed against the ground.
*No!*
Siegfried Bassmann was the most precious of all the lives it had absorbed.
Hunting a publicly known S-rank Hunter was difficult enough. A Grand Mage was an especially valuable prize, granting it the versatile power of magic.
*If I lose magic, I’m finished. I’d rather...!*
Fear sent its thoughts racing. Its decision was immediate.
*Whoooom!*
As it hurtled toward the ground, the Doppelganger drew up mana with all its strength.
*Blink!*
*Flash.*
The world slowed.
Space warped by mana swallowed its body. But this time, the amount of mana was different—and so was the spell’s stability.
The Doppelganger fixed its gaze on the battlefield hundreds of meters away, far beyond Blink’s normal range.
*I have to make it.*
This crossed a forbidden limit of spatial magic.
But it was better than dying here. The fanatics who worshiped it like a god were there, followers it had spent decades cultivating.
*Crreeeak!*
Bone and flesh twisted along with space.
The pain felt as though an invisible hand were squeezing its heart until it burst. None of that mattered.
Jin Taekyung.
If it could get out of this monstrous human’s grasp...
If it could escape under its followers’ protection and carry out the plan it had prepared for so long...
*Goodbye. See you next time.*
The Doppelganger grinned, baring blood-soaked teeth.
*Grrk, whoooosh!*
Mana whipped around it like a storm, and warped space swallowed it whole.
Its vision went black. Then new light, noise, and faces washed over it in waves.
*Boom! KABOOOOOM!*
*Shing! Krrrrk!*
“Gah!”
“Warriors of God, do not fear death!”
“Go fuck yourselves, you insane fanatics!”
Blasts and screams erupted on every side. Shouts from both sides battered its ruptured eardrums.
But all that mattered to the Doppelganger was that the faces in its blurred vision belonged to its followers.
“W-wait!”
“Prophet!”
Fanatics in turbans spotted it and gathered around. The Doppelganger spat up blood mixed with bits of its entrails, then laughed aloud.
“Cough. Heh-heh...”
Pain?
That was fine. It would recover soon.
Bones throughout its body were shattered, and the left arm Jin Taekyung had grabbed had been torn off at the shoulder. What mattered was that Blink had worked beyond its limits.
*An ordinary human would have died.*
It had been lucky.
The spell had succeeded because Siegfried Bassmann was a Grand Mage. It had survived the injuries because it was a Doppelganger.
*Slide. Crack.*
Pale flesh, soft as a child’s, slowly grew from the stump of its severed arm. Torn muscles joined, and white bone grew back.
Its recovery was incomparably slower than before. The Doppelganger clicked its tongue bitterly.
*Damn it.*
The countless lives it had absorbed were running low.
By the time it escaped this place entirely, it might have only a handful left.
*But that doesn’t matter. I have others willing to die for me.*
A sea of fanatics surrounded it.
Smiling to itself, the Doppelganger staggered to its feet.
Fierce fighting raged around the canyon exit, but the rear position it had reached with Blink was peaceful. Plenty of troops remained there.
Including the core force it had taken such care to raise.
“Amir.”
At the Doppelganger’s low voice, the surrounding fanatics stepped aside.
An old man carrying a staff approached and knelt before it.
“I have been waiting for you, great Prophet.”
Wonder filled his face and voice.
The Doppelganger looked down at him with all the authority befitting a prophet.
“God has led me elsewhere, so I must leave ahead of you. Hold back Jin Taekyung and the other heretics with all your strength.”
God and Prophet were names that commanded absolute obedience.
But Amir asked again, looking bewildered.
“Jin Taekyung?”
“Why? Are you afraid of him?”
“No. But... hadn’t you already subdued him, Prophet?”
The Doppelganger frowned.
“What do you mean? You couldn’t have seen what happened.”
“Yes. But you personally subdued him and brought him here.”
“What?”
The Doppelganger blinked, unable to make sense of it.
Behind it, Jin Taekyung lay facedown as if dead. His eyes slowly opened.
“Uh, fuck. Where the hell am I now?”

*Whoooosh.*
That immense magical power, so palpable he could almost reach out and touch it.
He didn’t need to check the Level window to know the answer.
“Siegfried Bassmann?”
At Jin Taekyung’s muttered question, the Doppelganger snapped its fingers instead of answering.
*Crackle.*
White light flashed.
The faint current running along its finger became dozens of lightning bolts and came crashing down.
It took only an instant.
*Zzap!*
Blinding light filled Jin Taekyung’s vision.
His eyes closed before he knew it, but he could still feel the tremendous current through the rock surrounding him, the air, and the ground.
Through everything.
*Boom!*
The hard rock and earth beneath him split in a spiderweb of cracks.
Jin Taekyung kicked off the ground and shot upward, thrusting out a palm.
The heat of Flame Divine Palm burned through the lightning as it surged forward.
*KABOOOOOM!*
A tremendous blast shook the canyon.
But Jin Taekyung sharpened his sight and caught everything that happened in that brief moment.
The rising flames.
The acrid smoke.
And the Doppelganger vanishing like a ghost just before it all erupted.
*Blink.*
Teleport and Warp were spells for crossing long distances.
Blink was short-range movement: disappearing for an instant, just as its name suggested.
Its range was limited.
Jin Taekyung’s senses and vision, on the other hand, covered the entire canyon.
*There.*
He couldn’t see it.
But he could feel it.
Jin Taekyung drew a breath.
He trusted his senses and his abilities.
Channeling internal energy through his toes, he stepped on empty air and shot toward the Doppelganger beyond the drifting embers and acrid smoke.
*Whoosh!
Boom!*
The air burst around him, unable to withstand his speed.
Smoke and embers scattered as if blown apart, and his vision cleared.
At the end of his path, having become a streak of flame, he found the Doppelganger fleeing toward the followers who could help it.
A chill prickled down its back.
The Doppelganger turned instinctively, its eyes widening.
In a world that seemed to slow around it, Jin Taekyung was already right in front of it, filling its vision.
*How the hell?*
Less than a second had passed.
Yet Jin Taekyung had found where Blink had taken it and crossed the dozen or so meters between them.
*You’ve got to be fucking kidding me...!*
The Doppelganger swallowed the curse rising to its lips.
No.
It hadn’t even had time to curse.
Waste a moment, and it could lose the Grand Mage’s power forever—an asset far more precious than all the other lives it had discarded.
*Shwaa!*
A reddish-hot spearhead tore through the wind.
The killing intent that accompanied it was cold enough to freeze the Doppelganger in place.
But the mana and abilities it possessed at that moment belonged to one of only three Grand Mages in the world.
*Blin—k!*
*Fwoosh, boom!*
Flames erupted along the spearhead and devoured the empty air.
The Doppelganger appeared a dozen or so meters away and felt a chill run down its spine.
Because it had barely escaped?
No.
Because a pair of eyes was staring straight at it.
*Jin Taekyung.*
Their gazes had only met, but its heart sank.
An instinct honed over centuries of struggle whispered to it.
Run.
If it didn’t want that beast to tear out the back of its neck, it couldn’t let its guard down for a moment.
The Doppelganger cast Blink again without pausing.
In the next instant, it knew its instinct had been right.
*Whoosh!
Slice!*
It opened its eyes in a new space and let out the breath it had been holding.
The back of its armor, long since stripped of its original shape and purpose, was hot from the heat that had grazed it.
*He cut me.
He’s fast enough to keep up with Blink.*
It had escaped by a hair.
A shiver ran through it.
Of all the humans it had absorbed or encountered in passing, none had been a monster like this.
Except for the one person it feared—and had deliberately avoided for that reason.
*Cheon Taemin.*
The savior of humanity.
The only Adversary to face the Demon King Asmodeus with the body and mind of a frail human.
A divine man.
The Doppelganger neither denied its fear of Cheon Taemin nor felt ashamed of it.
He was no being it could call “a mere human.”
That was why, even after absorbing Siegfried Bassmann years ago and learning of Cheon Taemin’s condition, it had never dared to go after him.
But the Doppelganger had never imagined it could feel this much fear of any human other than Cheon Taemin.
*Blink, Blink, Blink!*
Hesitate, and it might face permanent Erasure.
Desperate, the Doppelganger leaped through space again and again.
Each time its form vanished as if rubbed away by an eraser, it drew closer to the canyon exit, where a fierce battle was underway.
The hunter pursuing it drew closer, too.
*Whsssh!*
A sharp whistle cut through the air.
A dozen or so daggers flashed toward the Doppelganger’s entire body.
The attack had been timed and aimed so precisely that it had no chance to cast Blink.
With no other choice, the Doppelganger gritted its teeth and spread both hands.
*Vrrrrm, crack!*
Its mana shield shattered before it had fully formed.
The daggers ricocheted away and buried themselves in the cliffs and ground on either side.
But in the brief time it took to block them, Jin Taekyung had reached it.
“Got you.”
*Crack!*
The Doppelganger had no time to react.
Its mouth fell open as tremendous pain shot through its wrist.
Siegfried Bassmann had been a great Grand Mage in life, but Jin Taekyung’s terrifying strength couldn’t be stopped by any magic in his memories.
*Crreeeak!*
“Gyaaaah!”
The scream tore from the Doppelganger’s lips.
Jin Taekyung’s grip alone crushed flesh and muscle and splintered bone.
Its vision went white.
The sky and ground tilted.
*I’m being flipped over.
No—I’m going to die.*
The Doppelganger knew it instinctively.
After this terrifying feeling of weightlessness would come the impact.
Its whole body would be crushed against the ground.
*No!*
Siegfried Bassmann was the most precious of all the lives it had absorbed.
Hunting a publicly known S-rank Hunter was difficult enough.
A Grand Mage was an especially valuable prize, granting it the versatile power of magic.
*If I lose magic, I’m finished.
I’d rather...!*
Fear sent its thoughts racing.
Its decision was immediate.
*Whoooom!*
As it hurtled toward the ground, the Doppelganger drew up mana with all its strength.
*Blink!*
*Flash.*
The world slowed.
Space warped by mana swallowed its body.
But this time, the amount of mana was different—and so was the spell’s stability.
The Doppelganger fixed its gaze on the battlefield hundreds of meters away, far beyond Blink’s normal range.
*I have to make it.*
This crossed a forbidden limit of spatial magic.
But it was better than dying here.
The fanatics who worshiped it like a god were there, followers it had spent decades cultivating.
*Crreeeak!*
Bone and flesh twisted along with space.
The pain felt as though an invisible hand were squeezing its heart until it burst.
None of that mattered.
Jin Taekyung.
If it could get out of this monstrous human’s grasp...
If it could escape under its followers’ protection and carry out the plan it had prepared for so long...
*Goodbye.
See you next time.*
The Doppelganger grinned, baring blood-soaked teeth.
*Grrk, whoooosh!*
Mana whipped around it like a storm, and warped space swallowed it whole.
Its vision went black.
Then new light, noise, and faces washed over it in waves.
*Boom!
KABOOOOOM!*
*Shing!
Krrrrk!*
“Gah!”
“Warriors of God, do not fear death!”
“Go fuck yourselves, you insane fanatics!”
Blasts and screams erupted on every side.
Shouts from both sides battered its ruptured eardrums.
But all that mattered to the Doppelganger was that the faces in its blurred vision belonged to its followers.
“W-wait!”
“Prophet!”
Fanatics in turbans spotted it and gathered around.
The Doppelganger spat up blood mixed with bits of its entrails, then laughed aloud.
“Cough.
Heh-heh...”
Pain?
That was fine.
It would recover soon.
Bones throughout its body were shattered, and the left arm Jin Taekyung had grabbed had been torn off at the shoulder.
What mattered was that Blink had worked beyond its limits.
*An ordinary human would have died.*
It had been lucky.
The spell had succeeded because Siegfried Bassmann was a Grand Mage.
It had survived the injuries because it was a Doppelganger.
*Slide.
Crack.*
Pale flesh, soft as a child’s, slowly grew from the stump of its severed arm.
Torn muscles joined, and white bone grew back.
Its recovery was incomparably slower than before.
The Doppelganger clicked its tongue bitterly.
*Damn it.*
The countless lives it had absorbed were running low.
By the time it escaped this place entirely, it might have only a handful left.
*But that doesn’t matter.
I have others willing to die for me.*
A sea of fanatics surrounded it.
Smiling to itself, the Doppelganger staggered to its feet.
Fierce fighting raged around the canyon exit, but the rear position it had reached with Blink was peaceful.
Plenty of troops remained there.
Including the core force it had taken such care to raise.
“Amir.”
At the Doppelganger’s low voice, the surrounding fanatics stepped aside.
An old man carrying a staff approached and knelt before it.
“I have been waiting for you, great Prophet.”
Wonder filled his face and voice.
The Doppelganger looked down at him with all the authority befitting a prophet.
“God has led me elsewhere, so I must leave ahead of you.
Hold back Jin Taekyung and the other heretics with all your strength.”
God and Prophet were names that commanded absolute obedience.
But Amir asked again, looking bewildered.
“Jin Taekyung?”
“Why?
Are you afraid of him?”
“No.
But... hadn’t you already subdued him, Prophet?”
The Doppelganger frowned.
“What do you mean?
You couldn’t have seen what happened.”
“Yes.
But you personally subdued him and brought him here.”
“What?”
The Doppelganger blinked, unable to make sense of it.
Behind it, Jin Taekyung lay facedown as if dead.
His eyes slowly opened.
“Uh, fuck.
Where the hell am I now?”

chapters.title: Chapter 818
paragraphs: “Uh, shit. Where the hell am I now?”
The moment Jin Taekyung’s voice reached its ears, the Doppelganger froze like a statue. Two questions sprang to mind.
*Why is he here?*
Magic manifested according to the caster’s will alone.
And the Doppelganger had, of course, cast Blink on itself alone.

Even a full-blown psychopath with a mind that had spun around thirty-five times wouldn’t do something insane like cast a dangerous movement spell alongside Jin Taekyung—a man who could break the Doppelganger’s neck thirty-six times in the blink of an eye.
There was only one answer.
*He interfered with my Blink spell... against my will.*
Mana interference.
A theory the scholarly Grand Mage Siegfried Bassmann had developed after years of research surfaced among the memories the Doppelganger had absorbed.
The Doppelganger felt a chill sweep through its entire body. As it watched Jin Taekyung stagger to his feet, a second unanswered question lingered in its eyes.
*How? How did he survive?*
It could set the mana interference aside. The man was a monster, after all.
Absurd as it was—utterly absurd—perhaps a close-combat Hunter really did possess mana control surpassing even a Grand Mage’s.

But that Blink had been an outrageously dangerous attempt. The Doppelganger itself had nearly been torn apart for breaking the taboo and had sacrificed dozens of lives to heal. What more was there to say?
And yet...
“Ugh, my body’s all numb.”
Hearing Jin Taekyung mumble, the Doppelganger’s mind went hazy for a moment.
*Numb? He’s numb?*
It was impossible. The Doppelganger felt betrayed. Even if Jin Taekyung were an ogre, shouldn’t he at least have lost an arm or a leg or two, out of basic decency?
*His body isn’t made of steel. So how?*

The Doppelganger had no idea that Jin Taekyung’s physique—once called the Heavenly Martial Physique in Murim—had long since surpassed its limits, enough to withstand even a Blink spell that broke the taboo.
But it could grasp one truth without knowing why.
*Jin Taekyung is weaker now than he’s ever been.*
The shock set off a long, tangled train of thought. In reality, only a few seconds passed.
And at the end of the suffocating silence pressing down on everything came the Doppelganger’s shout, ringing out like a scream.
“Stop him!”

The silence shattered. At the same time, the world that had momentarily stopped began moving again. The fanatics, who had been staring blankly back and forth between Jin Taekyung and their great Prophet in that slowed-down moment, sprang into action.
“Inshallah!”
“God is great!”
*Whoosh! Fwoooooosh!*
Shouts and the whistle of weapons rang out on every side. Looking at the countless flashes hurtling toward him, Jin Taekyung suddenly opened his mouth.
No—he let it all out.
“Ugh. Bwaaaaaagh!”
Vomit sprayed into the air before a drop of blood did.
The price of hitching a ride on Blink was a hellish bout of motion sickness.
I’d tried to hold it in. I’d thought I could.
But life doesn’t always go the way you want.
“Bwaaaagh!”
Fuck. I’d been about to say something cool.
Vomit came pouring out instead. Bent over like a grub, I hurriedly rolled across the ground.
*Slice! Spurt!*
A chill ran through me. I felt a sharp blade cut away a handful of my hair.
As the auras flying in from all sides grazed my body, stinging pain flared across my skin.
*After coming all this way, I’m rolling around like a lazy donkey?*
Tears blurred my vision. The one small mercy was that the fanatics hadn’t expected this either.
*...It’d be weirder if they had.*
What kind of lunatic lands in the middle of his enemies and starts vomiting? I fought down the churn in my stomach and swung the thing in my hand.
*Thwack!*
Flesh and blood flew with a dull impact.
The Prophet’s arm, torn off in the aftermath of the Blink spell, made an excellent club.
“Oh, power attack.”
“You bastard! How dare you profane His sacred flesh—”
“Then let me rephrase. Holy attack.”
*Wham! Wham! Wham!*
The three nearest fanatics fell like dominoes.
I hurled the ruined arm like an axe, then stamped my foot in the middle of the enemies packed around me.
*Thud!*

A shock wave rumbled outward. The ground sank for several meters in every direction, and the fanatics staggered as they lost their footing. Their weapons veered off course with them and swept past my body.
*Whoosh! Spurt!*
The aura and wind pressure carried by the blades left fine cuts in my skin.
That alone told me how skilled they were.
*More than half are B-rank or higher.*

And I’d counted hundreds of them. The followers the Doppelganger had raised somewhere in a desolate desert no one could find were a match for the World Hunter Federation’s elite, locked in battle barely a hundred meters away.
*Crazy bastard. No—crazy bastards.*
The Doppelganger and its disgusting followers were all shit from the same cesspit.
I swallowed the curses rising in my throat and thrust out both hands.
Fanatics who looked like tanks raised round, enchanted shields across my path. They weren’t enough to stop the ten streaks of Finger Qi I’d fired a step ahead of them.
*Fwoosh! Thud-thud-thud!*
The wind blew, and ten fanatics fell like reed leaves.
Through the gap that opened for an instant, I caught a glimpse of someone’s back. I’d lost sight of him for a moment.
*There you are.*
The glimpse was brief, but I’d seen enough. The bastard was leaving the battlefield.
He was using the countless followers he’d raised as bait, treading across their blood like a carpet as he fled beyond my reach.
Just as he always had. And...
*He’ll keep doing it.*
Too many people had already died.
I still didn’t know what plan the bastard had spent more than thirty years building. But I had to bring it down here, today, with my own hands.
If I didn’t, my world—and the people in it—would fall apart.
“You won’t get past—!”
*Crack. Thud-thud!*
I broke the neck of the fanatic blocking my way and used his body to shield myself from an arrow flying in from ahead.
Its mana-infused head punched through the corpse, grazed my cheek, then lodged in the eye of another fanatic nearby.
“Gyaaaaaah!”
Blood sprayed as he screamed in pain. Moments later, a cold slicing sound cut the scream short.
*Slice.*
A red line crossed the fanatic’s neck. A heavy voice, announcing his death, rang out.
“Hassan. Brave warrior of God. We shall meet again in the Kingdom of Heaven, far in the future.”
*Thud.*
The screaming stopped. His head fell.
His body crumpled like a scarecrow and never moved again. Only then did faint beads of blood begin to gather on the cut surface of his neck.
*This is...*
Even after facing countless powerful fighters, I couldn’t help being astonished by the skill. I stopped and looked at the speaker, eyes wide.
Among the fanatics surrounding me stood a sturdy old man, tall as an iron tower, looking straight at me.
“This is the first time we’ve met face to face, Jin Taekyung, king of the wicked heretics.”
His turban was wrapped so carefully that not a strand of hair escaped it. His back was straight, his gaze deep and still.
I’d sensed it from the moment I opened my eyes here: the old man was immensely powerful.
Not merely as one of the Awakened known as Hunters in the modern world, but as a martial artist in his own right.
And I knew instinctively that if the Doppelganger was the untouchable symbol the fanatics revered, this old man was their real commander-in-chief and the heart of their fighting force.
“Yahya Muhammad Ahmad Bedouin... Did I get that right? That’s one hell of a long name.”
As I read aloud the information in the holographic window floating above his head, the old man’s eyes widened in surprise.
“How do you know my name?”
“God told me, you crazy old bastard.”
“Nonsense. God would never tell such a thing to the king of the wicked heretics.”
“You’re the one talking nonsense. I’m an atheist, so I’m not a heretic—and I’m definitely not a king.”
“Do not deny the existence of the great God with your vile tongue, demon.”
“Come on, sir. It’s time to take your pills.”
*Slide. Thump.*
His robe slipped from his shoulder and spread over the ground.
Holding a crooked staff in one hand and a scimitar—what Murim would call a curved saber—in the other, the old man stepped forward. The air grew cold, and the ring around me tightened.
*Step. Sssssss.*
Killing intent from every direction made my whole body prickle.
It wasn’t just the old man in front of me. I could see more than thirty men in black, wrapped head to toe in black robes and turbans, scattered among the fanatics.
*Those are the real deal.*
Every one of them was skilled enough to hold their own anywhere in the world. And unlike Hunters who weren’t used to killing other people, they showed no hesitation at all.
*Seasoned killers.*
Perhaps it wasn’t my imagination that I saw the martial artists of Dark Heaven superimposed on them.
They were alike in their blind loyalty and faith in one being, and even more so in their willingness to do any terrible thing for that being.
And...
*I’ve killed countless people like them.*
There were too many people in the world who needed killing. That was all.
Deep down, I had a vague sense that an absolute being called God might exist in this world. But I didn’t believe in him or pledge my loyalty to him.
In the end, people were the ones who accomplished things through hardship. Like countless others, I’d survived that way.

But if that god was the one who’d slipped a beat-up capsule to someone who’d suddenly lost his job a year ago—to a young man climbing a steep alley, worried about how he’d get through this month... Well, in that case, I might be willing to believe in him a little.
“Then your deaths at my hands will be God’s will, too.”
I muttered the words and closed my hand around empty air. Where there had been nothing but air and dust, my fingers caught a spear that had been away from my side for a while.
The old man saw something even magic couldn’t explain, and a stubborn crease formed between his brows.
“Demon. You truly are a demon.”

I wanted to tell the old man in front of me, and the fanatics all around us, that the real demon was running away and leaving them behind. That the monster they called a prophet was racing toward a new catastrophe.
Instead, I stepped forward. The wind burst, space vanished, and I charged.
*Whoosh.*
A scorching wind swept away the darkness. White Flame’s spearhead traced a path no one could block.
*Slice—KRRRUNCH!*
A thick mist of blood settled over everything.

“Do not deny the existence of the great God with your vile tongue, demon.”
“Come on, sir.
It’s time to take your pills.”
*Slide.
Thump.*
His robe slipped from his shoulder and spread over the ground.
Holding a crooked staff in one hand and a scimitar—what Murim would call a curved saber—in the other, the old man stepped forward.
The air grew cold, and the ring around me tightened.
*Step.
Sssssss.*
Killing intent from every direction made my whole body prickle.
It wasn’t just the old man in front of me.
I could see more than thirty men in black, wrapped head to toe in black robes and turbans, scattered among the fanatics.
*Those are the real deal.*
Every one of them was skilled enough to hold their own anywhere in the world.
And unlike Hunters who weren’t used to killing other people, they showed no hesitation at all.
*Seasoned killers.*
Perhaps it wasn’t my imagination that I saw the martial artists of Dark Heaven superimposed on them.
They were alike in their blind loyalty and faith in one being, and even more so in their willingness to do any terrible thing for that being.
And...
*I’ve killed countless people like them.*
There were too many people in the world who needed killing.
That was all.
Deep down, I had a vague sense that an absolute being called God might exist in this world.
But I didn’t believe in him or pledge my loyalty to him.
In the end, people were the ones who accomplished things through hardship.
Like countless others, I’d survived that way.
But if that god was the one who’d slipped a beat-up capsule to someone who’d suddenly lost his job a year ago—to a young man climbing a steep alley, worried about how he’d get through this month...
Well, in that case, I might be willing to believe in him a little.
“Then your deaths at my hands will be God’s will, too.”
I muttered the words and closed my hand around empty air.
Where there had been nothing but air and dust, my fingers caught a spear that had been away from my side for a while.
The old man saw something even magic couldn’t explain, and a stubborn crease formed between his brows.
“Demon.
You truly are a demon.”
I wanted to tell the old man in front of me, and the fanatics all around us, that the real demon was running away and leaving them behind.
That the monster they called a prophet was racing toward a new catastrophe.
Instead, I stepped forward.
The wind burst, space vanished, and I charged.
*Whoosh.*
A scorching wind swept away the darkness.
White Flame’s spearhead traced a path no one could block.
*Slice—KRRRUNCH!*
A thick mist of blood settled over everything.

chapters.title: Chapter 819
paragraphs: Fanatics and Hunters.
The battle between two forces, waged around the canyon, could be summed up in four characters:
Advance and retreat.
The fighting was that fierce, and everyone on both sides had put their lives on the line.
Some fought for a faith they had held all their lives, one they could not even imagine was false. Others fought for convictions just as firm.
And so they fought.
It was a clash of faith and conviction, and at the same time, a holy war.
But amid so much blood and death, whether anyone was religious no longer mattered.
*Demons.*
They were human beings with the same appearance, but each held a different standard for good and evil. Their eyes met between the blades lunging toward one another, burning with murderous intent.
“Die!”
*Clang!*
Sword met saber. Blue sparks flew with a sharp screech. Blood spurted amid ragged shouts, impossible to tell who had cried out.
*Slice—shaaak!*
No scream followed. The fanatic, his throat cut, glared at the Hunter before him with venom in his eyes, then collapsed.
Blue light flashed above the fallen body.
“Watch out!”
*Whoosh! Boom!*
A warning shout mingled with the roar of impact. A tank stared at the arrowhead protruding halfway through his enormous tower shield, inches from his face, and swallowed.
If he’d raised his shield just a fraction later, he would have died.
But Hunters lived closer to death than anyone. Everyone here had survived countless brushes with it.
The tank grabbed the arrow and snapped it in two, then shouted in a hoarse voice.
“They’re coming! Hold formation!”
*Rumble!*
Countless flashes rained down. Sharp blades and heavy clubs struck, and even fanatics on the verge of death forced themselves upright and charged.
The impacts hammered the shields so hard that even veteran tanks, hardened by years of combat, thought they might die.
“Arrrgh!”
*Grit.*
They shouted to wring out the last of their strength and clenched their teeth until they felt ready to break. Their feet slid backward under the pressure, carving deep furrows in the ground.
“Hold the line! If we break, it’s over!”
Even the commanders’ shouts seemed distant.
The enemy had an overwhelming advantage in numbers.
Less than three hours had passed since the battle against the monster army. That fight had drained them in body and mind, and the fanatics were the worst opponents they could have faced now.
Ten thousand of them.
They kept charging even after their chests were cut open or their limbs were severed.
Decades ago, the Doppelganger had raised these fanatics somewhere in this barren desert, hidden from the world, under the name of the Prophet. They were monsters of another kind.
*Thrust!*
A sword bearing a faint aura pierced a fanatic’s chest and emerged from his back.
It was a grievous wound. Even if he used a potion right away, there was no telling whether he’d live or die. Yet the fanatic whose chest had been pierced bared his blood-soaked teeth and smiled.
“I-Inshallah...”
The madness in that fading voice made the Hunter freeze.
A chill swept over him. By the time he came to his senses, it was too late.
*Whoosh!*
A sharp whistle cut past his ear. At the same instant, his vision went dark.
*Slump. Thud.*
“Hans! Hans!”
The Hunter who caught his falling comrade bit his lip.
But the man who had saved his life time and again—and whose life he had saved in turn—did not answer.
The dagger lodged squarely between Hans’s eyes had taken his voice and his life.
*Goddammit.*
The Hunter laid down the body, his gaze darkening.
The canyon was an ideal battlefield for facing a larger force, but no matter how efficiently they fought, casualties were unavoidable.
Especially against madmen who saw death as martyrdom.
It was just as their ranks were about to crumble before the wave of fanatics charging without regard for their lives—
*Fwoosh.*
A fierce heat washed over everyone’s heads.
Before anyone could look up, fire came pouring down like a meteor shower with a fierce whistle.
*Whoooooosh!*
Dozens of fireballs appeared above the Hunters and fell toward the battlefield, toward the fanatics who charged without end.
As everyone stared, mouths open, one name flashed through their minds.
*Magic Johnson.*
The Grand Mage said to have been blessed by mana. The world’s greatest War Mage, whose power had been proven during the Great Cataclysm, was finally showing what he could do.
A powerful area spell that could turn the tide of battle.
*That’s it. With that...*
Every Hunter thought the same thing. No—they were certain.
With Jin Taekyung nowhere to be seen, Magic Johnson was their surest bet to lead them to victory.
At least, they were certain until blue waves surged up from parched land that held nothing but sand and stone in every direction.
“Aqua Storm!”
“Aqua Storm!”
“Aqua Storm!”
*Fwoooooosh!*
Dozens of voices rang as one. Spheres of water piled upon spheres of water and rose into an enormous tidal wave.
And then...
*BOOM!*
A roar like the sky splitting apart shook the air.
Water and fire. Fire and water.
The opposing forces met and mingled. Then they collided.
With a shockwave that shook everything within a radius of hundreds of meters, they exploded above the heads of the Hunters and fanatics.
*Fwoosh! Boom-boom!*
“Gyaaaah!”
“M-My God!”
Someone screamed from beyond the steam that swept through the area on the wind.
The thick steam blinded everyone to what had happened. But Magic Johnson, who had cast the spell, knew better than anyone.
His magic had been canceled out.
*Blocked. Almost completely.*
Only almost because part of his Fire Storm had engulfed some fanatics. Even so, he could tell the damage was far less than he had expected.
*They were ready for it.*
Magic Johnson had seen them clearly: thirty mages emerging under heavy guard.
Their turbans were pulled low. Every last one was A-rank and, like him, a War Mage specialized in combat.
*The Doppelganger...*
Magic Johnson swallowed a groan.
He didn’t need to wonder who had built the force before him.
The Great Cataclysm had been a time of immense chaos. Thirty years was long enough for nature itself to change, and the desert must have been the perfect place to hide something.
How the Doppelganger had gathered and trained them was not what Magic Johnson wanted to know.
His question went to the beginning and end of it all.
*What do you want badly enough to have prepared all this?*
But his question reached no one. Even if the Doppelganger had known what he was thinking, it would not have answered.
No—it would not even have had time.
At that very moment, the Doppelganger was leaving the battlefield with a small escort.
*I have to chase it. I can’t let it get away.*
But despite his determination, Magic Johnson couldn’t move easily.
Unlike monsters, the fanatics were thoroughly trained. They knew what mattered most in this battle.
They had more than ten times the Hunters’ numbers and used them to attack in rotating waves.
And...
“Stop them! Those two must not get through!”
“Open fire!”
Magic Johnson and the Skeleton King.
The fanatics concentrated their attacks on the two strongest members of the Hunters’ force—the two who could also be called its commanders.
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!*
*Boom-boom!*
Arrows and magic rained down. Even a Grand Mage like Magic Johnson could not afford to ignore the attacks coming without pause from every direction.
He had already spent a great deal of his stamina and mana. The fanatics, by contrast, kept drawing on their strength as they cried out for a holy war.
The Skeleton King was in much the same position.
*Slice. Slice. Slice!*
His Bone Sword swept in smooth arcs.
But before the bodies crumpling in sprays of blood could hit the ground, dazzling flashes cut through them and shot toward him.
“This is insane...!”
The Skeleton King was aghast. Since coming into this world, he had never encountered people this crazy.
Much less ten thousand of them.
*They’re insane. Completely insane.*
He wielded the power of death, yet the endless wave of fanatics was nearly enough to overwhelm even him.
Every human feared death. Even he, an Undead Monster, feared Erasure. That fear seemed as inevitable as being born.
So why weren’t these humans afraid to die?
No—what had made them this way?
*They’re the real monsters...*
*Thrust-thrust-thrust!*
Swallowing a groan, he swung his Bone Sword and cut through a human body.
When he took one down, three more came. When he took down three, ten came. And when he felled those, fanatics rushed in from every direction, swinging their weapons.
“Die, demon!”
*Crunch!*
A blade cut through him with a chilling sound. Naturally, he felt no pain.
The Skeleton King sighed at the sword piercing his chest.
“Who are you calling a demon?”
*Whoosh—thrust!*
He turned his wrist. A bone shard shot out and pierced his attacker’s throat.
With a gurgling sound, the fanatic fell. The Skeleton King kicked him hard, clearing some space. At that moment—
*Whoom.*
A dark shape came flying toward him with a heavy whistle. He caught it in a hurry.
It coughed up blood. A human, still alive.
And one he knew.
*Goddammit. This guy...*
There was no mistaking him, even covered head to toe in blood.
The Skeleton King raised an Undead Monster with what little magical power he had left, then tapped the man’s cheek.
“Hey. Human with a fine-looking build. Can you hear me?”
*Cough.* Choi Minwoo spat up blood again, then answered in a voice on the verge of fading.
“Yes. Very clearly.”
“Good. We’re short on time, so listen carefully. You’re not going to die, so don’t worry. And even if you do, I’ll bring you back as an undead, so don’t—dammit. He passed out.”
The Skeleton King clicked his tongue and stood. Then he added, almost as an afterthought, “Still, he held out remarkably well, all things considered. Don’t you think?”
*Whoooosh! Slice!*
An aura swept past the Skeleton King’s head in place of an answer.
He watched blond hair flutter through the air, muttered a string of curses, then faced forward. Through the thick steam, he saw a man.
“Not at all. That bastard is trash.”
His hair was disheveled, and a wound crossed his cheek.
The Skeleton King gave a quiet laugh at the fury in the man’s eyes.
“No matter how I look at it, he fought well. When he wakes up, I’ll have to praise him myself.”
“Shut your filthy mouth, cursed demon.”
“When you die, you’ll find out which of us was the demon.”
The Skeleton King pulled the hilt of the sword from Choi Minwoo’s hand. Sacred light spread along the blade of the [Hero’s Sword].
“Get in here, quick. Before someone scarier than me shows up.”

chapters.title: Chapter 820
paragraphs: Everything alive is born into a struggle.
Humans, monsters, animals in the wild or behind fences, even green plants—all of them.
Even when survival itself wasn’t the reason to struggle, you had to fight and take what you wanted.
And under this absolute law, I was no exception.
*Crunch!*
Minimum force. Minimum speed.
That was enough. I twisted aside, leaving behind a fanatic who collapsed with his brains spilling out.
*Whoosh!*
The air split. A flash dropped from empty space and skimmed past me by half a handspan.
Between the pitch-black robe and turban that covered him completely, I saw his eyes widen. The White Flame’s spearhead was reflected in them.
*Thump. Splurt!*
His head flew up. More enemies and their auras surged through the spraying blood.
As blades came at me from every direction, I tightened my grip on the blood-slick spear shaft.
*Hoo.*
I breathed out. The world slowed. My muscles loosened, and the flames coiling around my spearhead flickered.
Like a tail fluttering in the wind.
*Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.*
Flames surged. The enemies’ auras flashing from every direction drove away the darkness racing toward the dim dawn.
I turned, my whole body moving in one smooth motion.
*Shiiiiing!*
Blue-white flames swept across the space between us. They were faster than any aura bearing down on me, their edge too sharp for anyone to stop.
*Slice.*
With a clean, cold sound, a sword tilted in its wielder’s hand.
No—faint lines had already appeared across the bodies of dozens of fanatics, frozen in place.
“Ghk. Ghrk...”
Trembling pupils. A fading voice.
But no words or actions could stop death from bearing down without mercy.
*Fwoooooosh!*
Flames raced along the faint lines, devouring their lives.
Thick sprays of blood mist blanketed the steam hanging low over the battlefield.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
Blood rained down on my head.
At the same time, flesh, bones, and organs—torn apart by a single horizontal strike—tumbled across the ground. Hundreds of fanatics had already fallen the same way.
Someone’s voice reached my ears. Of course, it belonged to one of the fanatics, someone whose face and name I didn’t know—and an enemy I had to kill.
*Pfft!*
I thrust out a hand without looking. Finger Qi shot from it, and a familiar bell rang.
*Ding.*
Another notification of death.
The fanatics surrounding me stopped moving.
Most of them probably couldn’t understand even a quarter of what they’d just seen.
How their comrades had died. Why they couldn’t wound me, even with so many fighters.
They would die with those questions unanswered.
All except one.
*Whoom. Boom!*
My spearhead struck the crescent curve of a saber.
The impact made my ears ring. I’d blocked the attack before I heard it coming. Now I stared past the white scimitar’s blade at the old man holding it.
“You lousy old bastard. Finally crawled out, did you?”
“I was waiting for my prey to tire.”
The old man with the long name, Yahya Muhammad Ahmad Bedouin, twisted his scimitar as he answered.
*Ka-ga-gak!*
Auras of different colors collided, sparking like lightning. A small explosion waited at their tips.
*Boom!*
The impact roared like cannon fire and traveled down my spear.
Its force drove me backward. The old man hadn’t moved an inch, and the sight made me realize something.
“Don’t tell me...”
“You’ve finally understood, King of the heathens.”
A smile formed on his wrinkled lips.
Two entirely different energies, neither of which he’d revealed until now, coexisted along the scimitar’s blade pointed at me.
*Mana. And magical power.*
As those two words crossed my mind, the old man continued.
“I, Yahya Muhammad Ahmad Bedouin, am a warrior chosen by God.”
“Huh.”
A hollow laugh escaped me.
The Doppelganger hadn’t raised only Michael Silbert. It had chosen its most loyal, most insane fanatic and taught him to wield magical power.
If more fanatics had been capable of accepting those two opposing energies, the Doppelganger would’ve churned out half-human, half-demon monsters like they were coming off an assembly line.
“I knew you were out of your mind from the start...but you’re no ordinary crazy old bastard.”
“If that is what you wish to believe, then believe it.”
The old man shook his head and looked at me with gray eyes.
“You know nothing. Dozens, hundreds died trying to be chosen by God. But I alone survived.”
“So being ‘chosen by God’ just means mixing a human and a monster half and half? Does that make a half-and-half order of black-bean noodles and spicy seafood noodles a warrior of God too?”
“The great Prophet said that monsters, too, are God’s creations—calamities sent to punish the fallen humans of this world.”
“Bullshit. Anyone listening would think you lived in some other world, not this one. By your logic, you’re one of those fallen humans too, you crazy old bastard.”
“Though fallen, I was given a chance at salvation. I inherited two powers that can never coexist. That is who I am: a warrior and a punisher chosen by God.”
The madness in his faith came through with every word.
But a madman doesn’t know he’s talking crazy.
Even if the Doppelganger gathered every fanatic in one place and made a public apology to the entire nation, they wouldn’t believe it.
Their faith was their whole life, their reason for living. It was even bound up with what they believed awaited them after death.
In the end, there was only one thing I could say to fanatics like them.
“You fucking lunatics. Talking to you is a waste of time.”
“Remember one thing.”
*Step.*
The old man came toward me. The fanatics who had faltered found their fighting spirit again.
“Your steps will never reach the Prophet.”
“Fuck off.”
*Whoosh.*
I shot forward like the wind as I answered.
Our brief exchange had given my body time to recover from the strain of battle. It had also given me time to assess the situation.
*It’s even. Fierce, but we’re holding our own.*
The Hunters’ shouts, which had been distant, were drawing closer.
But to overcome odds of more than ten to one and win, we had to cut off the head.
It was the best thing I could do before chasing the Doppelganger, which was still fleeing.
*Thwack! Crunch!*
My spear drove through three fanatics and came free.
Without hesitation, the old man threw his subordinates in as bait and swung his scimitar at my neck.
*Whoosh! Slice!*
I bent at the waist. The slash missed me and cut apart the fanatics charging from behind.
The old man sprang back, ready for my counterattack, and shouted in a cold voice.
“That demon means to harm the great Prophet! Give your lives to stop him!”
Damn old bastard.
He might’ve been the most fanatical of the fanatics, but the experience he’d gained over the years was no joke.
He knew exactly what his job was, and he kept his head even in the heat of battle.
*If this drags on any longer...I’ll really lose him for good.*
As I cut down the fanatics rushing in from every direction like moths to a flame, I thought. No—I calculated.
How much strength I could muster right now.
How to end this fight as quickly as possible.
And how much I’d have left when I could finally chase the Doppelganger again.
Then, amid the unending blood and screams, I realized I’d been thinking about something stupid.
*Fuck. When did I start calculating every little thing?*
When had it started? Every moment had become a struggle.
Each time, I’d had to forget the past and put the future out of my mind.
That was how you survived. Only by betting everything on the present could you think about the past and move toward the future.
*Slice!*
Hot pain ran down my back. My exhausted body felt as heavy as waterlogged cotton. Weapons came at me like gears turning together, large and small, opening wounds all over me.
But because of that, my hesitant body and mind woke up completely.
*Grit.*
I clenched my teeth against the pain and hurled the spear I held in a reverse grip at the fanatics charging straight at me.
The space was too tight for a proper throw, but one step was all I needed.
*Cr-r-runch!*
Flesh and blood were crushed. They screamed with pain enough to make them forget their faith.
The old man’s command rang out through their cries.
“Now!”
Now? Now what?
Oh. My weapon?
“So what?”
I spat out the blood running between my lips and reached out. The Flame Divine Palm I’d held back for the sake of an efficient fight erupted.
The fanatics packed around me went down in flames.
At the sight of their comrades writhing in agony, the others faltered.
*One more.*
*Fwoosh—BOOM!*
Blue-white flames lit the darkness. They burned flesh and turned the blood and bones within it to ash.
“Aaaaaagh!”
That was when it happened.
One fanatic, who had unconsciously stepped backward before that cruel, dazzling sight of a mass execution by fire, suddenly had his head fly into the air.
*Slice!*
The sound of the cut came a moment later. The old man, who had slipped out of my sight, gave a cold command.
“Fire.”
*Whooooosh!*
Dozens of arrows whistled through the air, one after another.
By the time I spotted the archers and their dark bows through the thinning ranks of fanatics, it was too late.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
“Guh!”
“Ghk.”
The arrows rained down without regard for friend or foe.
The fanatics hesitating around me fell like straw. Mana-laden arrows pierced their bodies and kept coming toward me.
*Whoosh.*
The whistle of their flight seemed to stretch on and on.
Dark arrowheads wrapped in blood and mana.
As the world slowed, one thought came to me with absolute certainty.
*I can’t dodge this.*
Of course, I could knock aside half of them. Of the rest, I could somehow twist my body to evade half.
But the Fire Dragon Armor hadn’t finished repairing itself. I would still have to take some damage.
But why?
A strange feeling came over me.
My instincts seemed to reject the judgment my mind had made.
A strange sense of déjà vu ran through me, as though every part of me were taking another step into an unknown realm.
*I can do this.*
A strange certainty, like a conviction, took over my body and mind. An inexplicable tickling sensation began around the center of my chest and spread through my entire body.
*Right now.*
I reached out as if in a trance, toward the dozens of arrows almost at my face.
No—not just the arrows. Everything around them.
*Shhhhaaa.*
Time began to move again, but no one spoke.
I stared silently at the arrows stopped in midair, then snapped my fingers.
*Swish.*
The arrows pointed toward the enemy. And once again, the power of my newly advanced Middle Dantian pressed down on the space around us.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
As the clear chimes pierced my ears, I smiled at the old man, frozen like a statue.
“Whoa. It worked?”
“T-This is—!”
“Refund, you fucking bastard.”
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!*
The arrows’ powerful whistle swallowed the words he was about to say.

sentences.text: Everything alive is born into a struggle.

His head flew up.

I breathed out.
The world slowed.
My muscles loosened, and the flames coiling around my spearhead flickered.

Flames surged.
The enemies’ auras flashing from every direction drove away the darkness racing toward the dim dawn.

Blood rained down on my head.

Someone’s voice reached my ears.

I thrust out a hand without looking.
Finger Qi shot from it, and a familiar bell rang.
*Ding.*
Another notification of death.
The fanatics surrounding me stopped moving.

How their comrades had died.
Why they couldn’t wound me, even with so many fighters.

“I was waiting for my prey to tire.”

Auras of different colors collided, sparking like lightning.
A small explosion waited at their tips.
*Boom!*

A smile formed on his wrinkled lips.
Two entirely different energies, neither of which he’d revealed until now, coexisted along the scimitar’s blade pointed at me.
*Mana.
And magical power.*
As those two words crossed my mind, the old man continued.
“I, Yahya Muhammad Ahmad Bedouin, am a warrior chosen by God.”
“Huh.”

The Doppelganger hadn’t raised only Michael Silbert.
It had chosen its most loyal, most insane fanatic and taught him to wield magical power.
If more fanatics had been capable of accepting those two opposing energies, the Doppelganger would’ve churned out half-human, half-demon monsters like they were coming off an assembly line.

chapters.title: Chapter 821
paragraphs: The moment dozens of arrows stopped in midair, the old man doubted his own eyes.
*Magic?*
No. That couldn’t be.
Mages and warriors shared the same root—mana—but their trunks and branches grew in entirely different directions.
That was why a Spellblade was considered as impossible as the coexistence of mana and magical power. Perhaps even more so.
*But if it isn’t magic, how...?*
The old man had long since reached the realm of the superhuman.

In his youth, he had ranged across battlefields amid the turbulent politics of the Middle East, protecting his tribe. Then, as the Great Cataclysm began in his middle age, he awakened to a power he had never known existed.
Even without accepting magical power, he would have been strong enough to stand shoulder to shoulder with the heroes of the Great Cataclysm.
That made what he was seeing all the harder to believe.
There was a clear, undeniable limit to what a warrior like him could move using mana.
*And those are arrows. Dozens of them, fired from close range.*
The unit waiting in the rear was made up of elite troops he had personally trained—swords and shields he had saved for the most crucial moment.
Yet the arrows those very troops had loosed had been stopped.
No—they were under control.
Dozens of arrows, shot with tremendous force and filled with mana, controlled by a single gesture.
*Whoooosh.*
The air stopped. The wind, thick with the stench of blood, vanished.
In that space where everything else seemed to have disappeared like a desert mirage, the wave of steel pouring toward one man turned.
*Swish.*
Dozens of arrowheads glinted in the darkness, their mana still intact. They pointed toward the men who had shot them. And...
“Wow. It actually worked.”
They were ready to obey the will of their new master.
*Jin Taekyung.*
The old man stared at the young man smiling beneath a coating of blood and clenched his teeth without meaning to.
A groan slipped through his bloodless lips.
“Th-This is...!”
*What is this? What have you done?*
He wanted to ask, but the young man did not wait for an old fool blinded by false faith to find his words.
“Refund, you fucking bastard.”
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!*
A fierce whistle of air shattered the silence. Hundreds of fanatics surrounding them watched the unbelievable sight with vacant eyes.
As if an invisible giant had drawn a bowstring, dozens of steel arrows came raining down, faster and harder than before.
All aimed at one man.
The old commander-in-chief who led the fanatics.
“Block—!”
*Boom!*
The unfinished shout vanished beneath a small explosion.
A sword swung to knock the arrows aside flew into the air, along with its wielder’s arm.
“Gaaah!”
The scream came a moment later. Then dozens of streaks of light swept in, cutting through and smashing everything in their path.
*Grit.*
The metallic taste of blood filled the old man’s mouth.
He had bitten his lip hard enough to draw blood without noticing. He brought down his scimitar, unleashing a murky force of mingled magical power and mana.
*Whoooooom!*
The immense wind pressure rushing off the blade pushed back the arrows flying in from the front.
Jin Taekyung had been surrounded, forced to face arrows coming from every direction. The old man, by contrast, had fanatics around him willing to die to stop the arrows.
Perhaps that was why he stepped forward at once, turning to the offensive. Why he trusted the dozens of followers surrounding him like shields.
The next moment, that trust vanished.
*Whish.*
At the faint whistle of air, the old man’s eyes widened.
Arrows were flying toward him, weaving around the fanatics as though they were alive.
*This is impossible...!*
A cry like a scream rose to his tongue, then disappeared. No—he wasn’t even given time to let it out.
He sucked in a breath and swung his scimitar. As streaks of light filled the air around him, he knew.
*Damn it.*
Unlike Jin Taekyung, he could not escape this attack.
*Crack!*
Arrows caught in the scimitar’s path bent and broke.
But even the old man, who had reached the superhuman realm, could not deflect or dodge them all.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
“Guh!”
Blood spilled through his clenched teeth. His vision blurred, and pain struck all through his body.
Ribs. Legs. Chest. Back.
He felt arrowheads pierce armor and flesh and shatter bone. The heat they carried seeped deep into his organs.
“Cough.”
His once-sturdy legs trembled. As the old man staggered, more than ten arrows buried deep in his body, the fanatics supporting him shouted like they were screaming in despair.
“No!”
“Amir! Amir! Please, stay with us!”
“What are you waiting for? Get him somewhere safe!”
The fanatics, finally grasping what had happened, were more shaken than ever.
If the Doppelganger, calling itself the Prophet, was their spiritual pillar, the old man was the warrior chief favored by God—the general who led them.
A voice pierced their ears like a spike.
“Who said you could?”
The shock hit like a bucket of cold water.
Heavy footsteps advanced.
“I asked you. Who said you could move?”
The voice was low. The face above it was worn with fatigue.
But the fanatics stepping backward without realizing it saw none of that. In their wide eyes, there was only one thing:
The flames flickering in his gaze.
“Did all you bastards eat a load of dates together? Not one of you can answer me.”
His blood-crusted lips twitched. Jin Taekyung smiled and reached out, and an immense, invisible force pressed down on the space around them.
No—it ruled it.
*Hssssss.*
The air stopped. The wind scattered.
Jin Taekyung felt an intangible force welling up from his chest, from his Middle Dantian.
Everything within a radius of dozens of meters already belonged to him. The hundreds of fanatics staring at him in shock were invaders. Demons defiling not just this land, but the entire world.
*No. To you, I’m the demon.*
Jin Taekyung looked down at the frozen fanatics with disgust.
He did not want to kill them. He only wanted peace.
He was no Killing Ghost, forever thirsting for blood. Whenever another Hunter who had united with the others under one banner for the sake of the world fell, he felt pain and sorrow.
But...
In the end, this too was a struggle for each side’s purpose.
To gain peace, they had to wage war. And in that war, rivers of blood and death would flow.
There was no other choice.
“It’s too late to turn back now. For me and for you.”
As Jin Taekyung’s quiet voice rang out—
*Rooooom.*
The still air and wind stirred again.
At that same moment, the old man got back to his feet. Magical power had given him a recovery beyond anything human, but waiting for him was a mass of steel filling the air.
“This is...”
He could not finish. No one could have.
All they could do was stare.
Spears. Sabers. Swords. Axes. Countless arrows and fragments of broken blades.
The wave of steel had left its dead former owners behind and taken a new master. It surged through the air, cold edges glinting as each weapon turned toward its target.
At the center of it all stood Jin Taekyung.
“Any last words?”
The old man sighed at the impossible sight. A murky force, neither monster nor human, overflowed from the scimitar in his hand.
“Inshallah.”
*May it be God’s will.*
With that prayer ringing in his heart, the old man stepped forward alone.
He left behind his followers, paralyzed with fear and waiting for death. He went forward with the duty and pride of a warrior chosen by God.
And yet, why?
*Is this—is this really what God wanted?*
For the first time, the old man who had believed in God and the Prophet more than anyone felt doubt.
But even now, as he charged like a streak of light and watched the rain of steel pour from the sky, brimming with lava-hot mana, he couldn’t find an answer.
*Answer me. Is this truly the promised land you spoke of?*
But the old man’s god did not answer.
It never had, from the distant past until now. And it seemed it never would.
Only a faint voice reached his ears. He could not tell whether it belonged to a god or a demon.
“Die, old man.”
*Fwoooosh!*
A gale swept through. A wave of steel, falling in place of damp rain, swallowed him.
As his body and power—part monster, part human—were smashed to pieces, the old man heard a terrible scream echoing faintly.
“Gaaah!”
His vision darkened. His consciousness scattered. The warriors of God met their brutal end.
*Ah.*
At last, he knew the answer to his question.
This was not the promised land. It was the land of death.
*Thud.*
His lifeless body crumpled to the ground.
Though he had found the answer in his final moment, the old man’s face was twisted with anger and disbelief.
It happened in an instant.
Weapons swinging at one another stopped in midair. Shouts forced from hoarse throats cut off.
Every head turned in the same direction.
*Fwaaaash!*
It was a roar and a scream at once.
A scream of steel raining through the air. And a scream of terror from people who sensed their own deaths.
*Kwaaaang!*
Dust billowed upward. Through sand surging like a whirlwind, streams of blood spurted like fountains.
*Splash—splat!*
Dozens of meters away, fanatics stared blankly at the sight and blinked.
Blood rained onto their heads and ran down in sticky streams, along with something hard and something soft.
It did not take long to realize what had fallen on them: human bone and flesh.
Their hands and feet trembled. The clatter of teeth spread among the fanatics like an epidemic.
They all knew that carefully chosen elite troops had been waiting in the far rear with the commander-in-chief, ready to join the fight.
Now that was a fact of the past.
Annihilation.
Everyone on the battlefield understood instinctively.
No one could survive the storm of steel raging there.
No—there was one person who could.
*Jin Taekyung.*
As the name surfaced in every mind—
*Kwaaaaa.*
The whirlwind slowly settled. Within it, someone’s silhouette wavered like heat haze.
