At the faint whistle of air, the old man’s eyes widened.
Arrows were flying toward him, weaving around the fanatics as though they were alive.
*This is impossible...!*
A cry like a scream rose to his tongue, then disappeared.
No—he wasn’t even given time to let it out.
He sucked in a breath and swung his scimitar.
As streaks of light filled the air around him, he knew.
*Damn it.*
Unlike Jin Taekyung, he could not escape this attack.
*Crack!*
Arrows caught in the scimitar’s path bent and broke.
But even the old man, who had reached the superhuman realm, could not deflect or dodge them all.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
“Guh!”
Blood spilled through his clenched teeth.
His vision blurred, and pain struck all through his body.
Ribs.
Legs.
Chest.
Back.
He felt arrowheads pierce armor and flesh and shatter bone.
The heat they carried seeped deep into his organs.
“Cough.”
His once-sturdy legs trembled.
As the old man staggered, more than ten arrows buried deep in his body, the fanatics supporting him shouted like they were screaming in despair.
“No!”
“Amir!
Amir!
Please, stay with us!”
“What are you waiting for?
Get him somewhere safe!”
The fanatics, finally grasping what had happened, were more shaken than ever.
If the Doppelganger, calling itself the Prophet, was their spiritual pillar, the old man was the warrior chief favored by God—the general who led them.
A voice pierced their ears like a spike.
“Who said you could?”
The shock hit like a bucket of cold water.
Heavy footsteps advanced.
“I asked you.
Who said you could move?”
The voice was low.
The face above it was worn with fatigue.
But the fanatics stepping backward without realizing it saw none of that.
In their wide eyes, there was only one thing:
The flames flickering in his gaze.
“Did all you bastards eat a load of dates together?
Not one of you can answer me.”
His blood-crusted lips twitched.
Jin Taekyung smiled and reached out, and an immense, invisible force pressed down on the space around them.
No—it ruled it.
*Hssssss.*
The air stopped.
The wind scattered.
Jin Taekyung felt an intangible force welling up from his chest, from his Middle Dantian.
Everything within a radius of dozens of meters already belonged to him.
The hundreds of fanatics staring at him in shock were invaders.
Demons defiling not just this land, but the entire world.
*No.
To you, I’m the demon.*
Jin Taekyung looked down at the frozen fanatics with disgust.
He did not want to kill them.
He only wanted peace.
He was no Killing Ghost, forever thirsting for blood.
Whenever another Hunter who had united with the others under one banner for the sake of the world fell, he felt pain and sorrow.
But...
In the end, this too was a struggle for each side’s purpose.
To gain peace, they had to wage war.
And in that war, rivers of blood and death would flow.
There was no other choice.
“It’s too late to turn back now.
For me and for you.”
As Jin Taekyung’s quiet voice rang out—
*Rooooom.*
The still air and wind stirred again.
At that same moment, the old man got back to his feet.
Magical power had given him a recovery beyond anything human, but waiting for him was a mass of steel filling the air.
“This is...”
He could not finish.
No one could have.
All they could do was stare.
Spears.
Sabers.
Swords.
Axes.
Countless arrows and fragments of broken blades.
The wave of steel had left its dead former owners behind and taken a new master.
It surged through the air, cold edges glinting as each weapon turned toward its target.
At the center of it all stood Jin Taekyung.
“Any last words?”
The old man sighed at the impossible sight.
A murky force, neither monster nor human, overflowed from the scimitar in his hand.
“Inshallah.”
*May it be God’s will.*
With that prayer ringing in his heart, the old man stepped forward alone.
He left behind his followers, paralyzed with fear and waiting for death.
He went forward with the duty and pride of a warrior chosen by God.
And yet, why?
*Is this—is this really what God wanted?*
For the first time, the old man who had believed in God and the Prophet more than anyone felt doubt.
But even now, as he charged like a streak of light and watched the rain of steel pour from the sky, brimming with lava-hot mana, he couldn’t find an answer.
*Answer me.
Is this truly the promised land you spoke of?*
But the old man’s god did not answer.
It never had, from the distant past until now.
And it seemed it never would.
Only a faint voice reached his ears.
He could not tell whether it belonged to a god or a demon.
“Die, old man.”
*Fwoooosh!*
A gale swept through.
A wave of steel, falling in place of damp rain, swallowed him.
As his body and power—part monster, part human—were smashed to pieces, the old man heard a terrible scream echoing faintly.
“Gaaah!”
His vision darkened.
His consciousness scattered.
The warriors of God met their brutal end.
*Ah.*
At last, he knew the answer to his question.
This was not the promised land.
It was the land of death.
*Thud.*
His lifeless body crumpled to the ground.
Though he had found the answer in his final moment, the old man’s face was twisted with anger and disbelief.
It happened in an instant.
Weapons swinging at one another stopped in midair.
Shouts forced from hoarse throats cut off.
Every head turned in the same direction.
*Fwaaaash!*
It was a roar and a scream at once.
A scream of steel raining through the air.
And a scream of terror from people who sensed their own deaths.
*Kwaaaang!*
Dust billowed upward.
Through sand surging like a whirlwind, streams of blood spurted like fountains.
*Splash—splat!*
Dozens of meters away, fanatics stared blankly at the sight and blinked.
Blood rained onto their heads and ran down in sticky streams, along with something hard and something soft.
It did not take long to realize what had fallen on them: human bone and flesh.
Their hands and feet trembled.
The clatter of teeth spread among the fanatics like an epidemic.
They all knew that carefully chosen elite troops had been waiting in the far rear with the commander-in-chief, ready to join the fight.
Now that was a fact of the past.
Annihilation.
Everyone on the battlefield understood instinctively.
No one could survive the storm of steel raging there.
No—there was one person who could.
*Jin Taekyung.*
As the name surfaced in every mind—
*Kwaaaaa.*
The whirlwind slowly settled.
Within it, someone’s silhouette wavered like heat haze.

chapters.title: Chapter 822
paragraphs: In the wake of the Great Cataclysm, the boundary between what humanity considered common sense and nonsense crumbled like a sandcastle.
Awakened people, monsters, magic, Gates.
Things that had existed only in novels and movies became reality.
Calamity became a neighbor, and the word *death* came cheap.
But humans are adaptable creatures.
They quickly accepted the unbelievable reality before them and made the impossible their new normal.
They thought nothing like it would ever happen again in human history.
No—they hoped it wouldn’t. Please.
But at this very moment, in an unnamed canyon in the Rub’ al Khali Desert, those who had been piling up blood and bodies without end had no choice but to admit it.
The common sense they had accepted had crumbled once more.
*Rooooar.*
The rain of steel lashing through the darkness stopped. The whirlwind that had seemed ready to swallow the entire desert slowly died away.
Amid the silence and shock that gripped them all, thousands of eyes settled on the figure who had emerged.
“Oh my God.”
“What the hell did I just see?”
The Hunters stared in awe and elation.
“He’s a demon. He has to be.”
“Inshallah. God...”
The fanatics trembled with fear and hatred.
And among all the people gathered there, the one being who wasn’t human spat out the one word they had all wanted to say.
“Monster.”
The Skeleton King’s mouth curled as he looked at the man before him.
“I told you, didn’t I? Let’s finish this before someone scarier than me shows up.”
The man’s eyes widened. His hair was disheveled, and wounds large and small covered his body.
He had already been struggling against the Skeleton King, but now his injuries were the last thing on his mind.
“How... How can anyone do that?”
The man muttered in a dazed voice.
His bulging eyes stared past the whirlwind, at the blood and corpses it had left behind.
A thousand.
There had been a thousand warriors waiting in the rear.
The finest of the elite, held in reserve for the final blow. And with them, Amir—their greatest warrior and commander.
No. He *had* been with them.
Until that enormous whirlwind of steel swept them away.
*They’re all dead? Killed by one man?*
It was impossible to believe. Impossible to understand.
The man’s hand trembled around his sword hilt. A groan escaped through his clenched teeth.
“Th-That’s impossi—”
“Possible.”
His wavering voice cut off.
The Skeleton King had severed his words like a guillotine blade. He went on evenly.
“Jin Taekyung can do it.”
“Shut your mouth!”
The man’s furious roar split the desert. He glared at the Skeleton King, his eyes blazing.
*Shhhhh.*
Immense killing intent and aura rose from him, swallowing the space around him.
An ordinary Hunter would have struggled even to breathe beneath that pressure. The Skeleton King didn’t so much as blink.
To the undead, killing intent was more familiar than anything else.
Simply by existing, he was already in contact with death.
The man’s aura was no different.
*Half as strong as that guy, if I’m generous.*
Thinking of *that guy*, shimmering in the distance like a mirage, the Skeleton King let out a quiet snort.
The world called beings like him monsters. But the real monster was someone else.
“Why did you have to do something like this? If you’d stayed quietly tucked away in some corner of the desert, you wouldn’t have made that guy angry.”
“...God, God chose us. The great God Himself sent the Prophet to lead His warriors to the promised land!”
“The promised land?”
The Skeleton King glanced around as he echoed the words.
Corpses lay in every direction.
Blood flowed like a river, rising to their ankles. Limbs and chunks of flesh—no one knew whose—bloomed across the desert like flowers.
“Surely this isn’t the promised land you’ve been blathering on about.”
“Unless you promised God you’d all die here together. In that case, I’ll give you that one.”
The man’s eyes wavered. So did those of every fanatic around him.
The Skeleton King’s voice, infused with magical power, carried far enough to reach Hunter and fanatic alike.
Each word poured cold water on the flames of fanaticism that had seemed as though they would burn forever. And each word made the Hunters take up their weapons again.
“There was a human. No, there were humans. Frail creatures compared to me, born with death as their fate.”
The Skeleton King remembered.
Countless faces he had encountered since coming into the world flashed before his eyes.
“They fought countless battles and kept dying. But they didn’t fight only for the god they believed in.”
They had families and friends. People they loved. Values worth protecting.
“I couldn’t understand those stupid humans. I couldn’t even accept that there were different kinds of death.”
But not anymore.
The Skeleton King had watched humans more closely than any other monster had.
He had stood beside them.
And at last, he understood.
The countless deaths he had witnessed could not all be called simply deaths.
“They were sacrifices.”
Some people killed for money and power. They abandoned their parents and children, betrayed their lovers and friends.
But there were others who burned like torches and died away like wildfires.
People who went forward prepared to die.
People who stood their ground and fought for others, for a better world, even in the face of death.
The world called them heroes.
It called their deaths sacrifices.
“But what should I call you? What should I call your deaths?”
“If you have a mouth, then answer me. You foolish people who brought calamity upon the world after being deceived by an illusion.”
*Kiiiiing.*
The man swallowed a breath as the fading golden crown above the Skeleton King’s brow began to shine.
His wandering gaze passed over the countless faces surrounding him.
Hatred and contempt.
Resentment and confusion.
And not just from the Hunters.
Even the fanatics under his command were wavering.
Some of them looked at him with eyes clouded by resentment and confusion, then turned away. The sight struck the man as though something solid inside him had suddenly collapsed.
He wanted to speak.
He wanted to shout at the people wavering before him.
Tell them not to be taken in by a demon’s silver tongue.
Tell them not to dare question the great God and His Prophet.
But his tongue wouldn’t move. The hand gripping his sword seemed to be losing its strength.
In his mind, gone blank, the demon’s words from a moment ago repeated without end.
*But what should I call you? What should I call your deaths?*
The man clenched his teeth without realizing it. Pain shot through a broken molar, but even that felt distant, like a dream.
The corpses of his followers filling every direction.
So did the sticky pool of blood at his feet.
*Is this really...*
Was this the promised land, meant to be green and beautiful?
Was it the heaven Almighty God and His Prophet had prepared for His people?
The question he had barely managed to keep from speaking echoed through his mind.
And through his dreamlike haze, a dazzling shaft of light brightened the darkness.
*Whoooooom.*
Golden radiance rose along the many-colored blade.
The light felt so warm. So sacred.
The man even forgot that the Skeleton King was holding the sword.
Looking at the demon who stood before him with the Hero’s Sword in hand, shining with a brilliance reserved for the chosen, he found himself asking:
“Are you... really a demon?”
It was at that very moment.
*Step.*
In a world where everything had stopped, a single person’s footfall rang out.
At the same time, a calm voice reached the man’s ears.
“You see what you want to believe. Just like you called a monster the Prophet and worshiped it.”
The wind held its breath.
Everyone turned in the same direction.
And at the end of all those gazes stood Jin Taekyung.
“Hamid Shah Masoud.”
The man stared blankly at Jin Taekyung.
Apart from Amir, no one knew that name. There was no way the man before him could know it.
“How could you know?”
“If I said God told me, would you believe me?”
“You’re an easy bunch to read. You saw what you wanted to believe, and believed what you wanted to see. All the while telling yourselves this was God’s will.”
*Splash.*
He strode forward.
Blood splashed in every direction from a pool with pieces of flesh floating in it. The young man, already drenched in blood, paid it no mind.
“Tens of thousands are dead because of idiots like you. No—hundreds of thousands.”
Cities had burned. A massive tidal wave had swept through a harbor.
Countless people had died in sudden disasters. Happy families had vanished, and children who lost their parents had been sent to orphanages.
And none of it had been a natural disaster.
People had caused it.
“There is no God. And even if there is, He wouldn’t be an idiot who watches over trash like you.”
Jin Taekyung spat out each word as he looked across the countless fanatics.
Some staggered in shock. Others wept, belatedly realizing what they had done.
But if a few short words could have changed their hearts, those disasters would never have happened.
“How dare you, you wicked heretic!”
“God is great!”
*Papapat!*
At those sharp cries, figures rushed him from all sides like streaks of light.
A cold smile touched Jin Taekyung’s lips as he met their hate-filled gazes.
“Yeah. That’s more like it.”
At that moment—
*Shwoosh!*
Silver flashes shot up from every direction, splitting the wind.
They tore through space, piercing and slicing the blades and bodies hurtling toward him.
*Whoooosh! Slice!*
*Thud-thud-thud-thud!*
Only then did the survivors understand.
What the earlier whirlwind had been.
And how those caught within its reach had died.
*Krrrunch!*
An eerie noise filled the space for more than ten meters around him.
Blood poured down like rain. Arrows and daggers shot through the air, then flew back the way they had come, taking their owners’ lives.
They were lucky if they managed a dying gasp.
Of the hundred or so fanatics who had charged at once, half were torn to pieces beyond recognition.
*Thud, thud, thud.*
Flesh, blood, and bone fragments filled the empty spaces where screams had been.
Hamid Shah Masoud could only stare, eyes wide, as his sword hilt slipped from his hand.
*Clang.*
No one spoke.
Not the Hunters. Not the fanatics.
Not the Skeleton King, the Hero’s Sword hanging at his side, or Magic Johnson, standing upright in midair.
At this moment, only one person could speak.
He alone could pass judgment or grant forgiveness.
So Hamid Shah Masoud pleaded for mercy in a trembling voice. To survive, he had no choice but to beg for his one and only life.
He let go of his sword and fell to his knees.
He threw his faith, shattered beyond recognition, into the trash.
“P-Please spare me.”
A desperate plea.
Jin Taekyung looked down at him without a flicker in his eyes. Then he reached out.
A searing heat gathered at the tips of his bloodstained fingers.
*Thwip. Thud.*
A single blast of hot wind.
That was all. The man fell quietly and never got up again.
*At last.*
Jin Taekyung let out the breath he had been holding and lifted his head.
*Clang. Thud-thud.*
Countless still-sharp weapons fell, and knees sank into the blood-soaked sand.
Victory had come in the dim light of dawn. The battle was over.
But Jin Taekyung was looking west, where darkness still held.

*Jin Taekyung.*
The defeated did not dare raise their heads before him. The victors gazed at their young Alliance Leader with wonder in their eyes.
They had been outnumbered more than ten to one, facing fanatics who charged without fear of death.
The Hunters had been afraid.
Afraid they would never see their families again. Afraid that if they fell in this nameless canyon, an even greater calamity would swallow those who remained.
But their brief fear had been rendered meaningless. Jin Taekyung had ended this massive battle in an instant.
He had been overwhelming—and, in a way, divine.
Everyone who survived knew it.
Jin Taekyung hadn’t just cut through the enemy’s flesh and bone. He had broken the fanatics’ spirits and made them lay down their weapons of their own accord.
Like a scene from a myth.
*If miracles exist... this must be what one looks like.*
Magic Johnson suddenly felt something stir in his chest. The Grand Mage’s gaze, fixed on Jin Taekyung, trembled like ripples on a pond.
*He reminds me of him. Astonishingly so.*
Old memories rose like heat haze before his eyes.
Memories from more than thirty years ago. Yet every moment he had spent with *him* remained vivid.
The miracle Magic Johnson had witnessed with his own eyes—that great achievement—would be remembered as long as humanity endured.
And so would the young hero standing alone at the center of the now-quiet battlefield.
But Magic Johnson knew something else.
To gain anything in this world—even a miracle—one had to pay its price.
*Equivalent exchange is the one unchanging law.*
His gaze on Jin Taekyung deepened. Then dazzling light streamed from the tip of the staff he slowly raised.
*Fwoooosh.*
A flash heralding the end of the fierce battle drove back the darkness and lit the dawn.
The Hunters touched by its gentle warmth finally grasped what had seemed impossible to believe.
They had won.
Today, they had written a new line in history.
*Clang-clang-clang!*
Blades smeared with blood and flesh thrust toward the sky.
“Waaaaaaah!”
A tremendous roar shook the canyon.
It was joy at victory, mourning for fallen comrades, and reverence offered wholly to one man.
But most of them neither knew nor saw it.

The young hero’s eyes twitched as he stood amid the cheers pouring in from every direction. His fingers had turned white, gripping with all their strength the spear shaft that kept slipping from his hand.
*...Fuck.*
Jin Taekyung swallowed the curse and forced down the hot surge rising from deep in his chest.
His vision kept blurring. In his ringing ears, the Hunters’ cheers and the System notifications crowded together in a jumble.

**System You have defeated Lv. 140 Hamid Shah Masoud! - You have gained a substantial amount of EXP and Fame! - Level Up! - All status ailments have been removed as a Level Up effect! - Some wounds have been healed as a Level Up effect! - Special debuff Broken Body rejects the healing effect! - Status ailment Mental Strength Depleted rejects the healing effect! - Middle Dantian has reached its limit! Rest as soon as possible to recover your mental strength!
Jin Taekyung’s condition was exactly as the System had described.
His physical wounds and fatigue had recovered, but his Middle Dantian was beyond the System’s power to heal. The catastrophic force he had unleashed earlier could never have come cheaply.
*Throb.*
He had already wrung himself out to his limit—and beyond it. Even standing was a struggle.
Pain around his heart and mental exhaustion gnawed at him without pause, whispering:
*The battle is over.*
*Your part is done. Rest now.*
“Yeah. I’ve done enough.”
The hollow words fell from his lips.
Through his blurred vision, Jin Taekyung looked at the cheering Hunters.
He recognized faces from the battles they had fought together. There were gaps here and there, but he could tell that not many Hunters had died in this one.
If he hadn’t pushed his Middle Dantian beyond its limits, more than half the Hunters who had survived would probably be lying across the battlefield by now, growing cold.
That was no exaggeration.
He had brought a grueling battle to a swift victory and stopped more blood from being spilled.
He had brought a battle that would go down in history to an end, all on his own.
But...
*It’s not over yet.*
Jin Taekyung tightened his grip on the spear shaft. He forced his eyes open against their growing weight and looked west, where desert and wilderness stretched into the distance.
*There’s still something I have to do.*
The light had not gone out of his eyes as he stared at the endless horizon.
His gaze was already following someone who had vanished from sight.
*The Doppelganger.*
Even now, as dawn arrived, the western land where the Doppelganger had disappeared remained shrouded in darkness.
As though its shadow had fallen over it. As though it foretold the great war to come.
*I have to go.*
The thought was more than resolve. It was almost a duty.
He had to keep moving. He couldn’t stop here.
He had to pursue the Doppelganger far to the west and stop the calamity that would strike before long.
*Step.*
He moved forward as if entranced.
But his mental strength was spent. His body would no longer obey.
He staggered.
*Walk forward.*
His legs failed to receive that simple command in time and gave way. A wrenching pain gripped his chest, hampering body and mind alike.
*Damn it.*
He’d hit a wall on his second step.
As his vision slowly tilted, Jin Taekyung stifled a hollow laugh. Then, just as everything seemed to go dark—
*Slide. Tap.*
His forehead, pitching forward, touched something solid.
A hand reached out from behind and hauled his collapsing body upright. Two voices broke through the ringing in his ears.
“You did good, Jin.”
“Pull yourself together, human.”
Jin Taekyung blinked.
Now he knew whose hand was holding him up, and what the solid wall in front of him was.
*Magic Johnson. And the Skeleton King.*
They had come.
A human and a monster. No—his friends had come.
To help him.
*Crack.*
Through the distant pain, his blurred vision cleared again. Jin Taekyung swallowed the blood on his tongue and raised his head. Two welcome faces were waiting for him.
“Ha.”
At the laugh that escaped him, the Skeleton King turned to Magic Johnson with a stiff expression.
“Why’s that ugly bastard grinning like that? Has he finally lost his mind?”
“Quit saying stupid things and shut your mouth. Hey, Jin. Can you hear me?”
“Human. How many fingers am I holding up?”
Jin Taekyung answered weakly.
“I can hear you fine. And I can see your finger.”
“Tell me how many, you ugly, dim-witted bastard.”
“One. But if you don’t want me to break it, quit waving it around and lower it.”
The Skeleton King, who had been waggling his middle finger in front of Jin’s face, nodded.
“Good. You’re still sane.”
Jin Taekyung snorted, then broke into a cough.
“Team Leader Choi... *cough*, how is he?”
“He’s fine. A little injured, but fine.”
“Really? You’re sure?”
“Trust me. I’m not lying.”
Jin Taekyung let out a relieved sigh and straightened his back with effort.
He was still short of breath, his senses still dull. But he couldn’t stop here.
“Johnson.”
Sometimes a small gesture or a single word said everything.
Magic Johnson sensed what lay behind that brief call.
“No.”
“I have to go. You know that.”
“I do.”
Magic Johnson’s expression hardened.
“And I know you need to rest.”
The Grand Mage could see Jin Taekyung’s condition clearly. He was already at his limit, staying conscious through sheer force of will.
But recklessness belonged to the young.
It always had with the young man before him.
“Use Teleport magic.”
“Damn it, Jin. Are you crazy?”
“This isn’t a request.”
“Then as of this moment, I’m leaving the World Hunter Federation.”
“Then leave.”
Looking up at Magic Johnson, who was a head taller than him, Jin Taekyung continued:
“But until I accept your resignation, you’ll have to follow my orders.”
“Come on, Johnson.”
Magic Johnson found himself at a loss for words.

The talk of resignations and orders was nothing more than a clumsy play on words. But there was nothing false about the resolve in Jin Taekyung’s eyes, or the sense of duty keeping his fading consciousness intact.
*Damn it.*
He couldn’t bring himself to meet those eyes. He was ashamed of himself for having to make this choice.
He squeezed his eyes shut, then opened them and gritted his teeth.
“...This is insane. Teleporting with the magical power concentration this high is practically suicide.”
Jin Taekyung gave a faint smile.
“That takes me back.”
“What?”
“Sichuan, China. You said the same thing there. And we pulled it off just fine.”
“Send me to the place the Prophet—no, the Doppelganger—told us about at the beginning.”
Magic Johnson’s pupils trembled as he looked at Jin Taekyung.
He had to stop him. He absolutely had to stop him.
But his damned Grand Mage’s mind was already calculating, already drawing a reasonable conclusion.
*There’s a good chance it’ll work.*
They had tried Teleport magic once before under a magical power concentration like this, during the battle against the Arch Lich.
It had been possible because Magic Johnson was among the finest mages alive—and because the person he was transporting was Jin Taekyung.
*If it isn’t Teleport magic, if it isn’t Jin... no one else can stop the Doppelganger.*
Jin Taekyung’s proposal was reckless, but the reality behind it could not be ignored.
A considerable amount of time had passed since the Doppelganger fled the battlefield. Catching up to it was almost impossible.
But if they used Teleport magic—
And if there was someone who could endure Teleport magic this dangerous, things would be different.
How cruel.
“Fuck.”
Magic Johnson muttered a curse weakly. Jin Taekyung was standing on his own now, without anyone’s help, looking straight at him.
And beside Jin stood someone who had volunteered to share the danger.
“I’m going with him. You stay and protect this place.”
The Skeleton King. Lord of the undead, who had overcome even death.
The moment Magic Johnson saw him, he knew he had nowhere left to retreat.
“Promise me one thing.”
*Whummm.*
The staff, filled with mana, trembled. Beyond the dazzling flash, his voice rang out faintly.
“Come back alive. No matter what.”
*Fwoooosh.*
An overwhelming flash of light swallowed the space around them.

chapters.title: Chapter 824
paragraphs: When dawn comes, the darkness retreats.
It was as natural as water flowing downhill. But to those fleeing a pursuer, daylight was hardly welcome.
Especially when that pursuer was a monster they could scarcely believe was human.
*Already?*
The Doppelganger bit its lip as it watched the sky slowly brighten.
Dawn had come too soon. No—it had taken longer than expected.
*Everything should have been over before daybreak at the latest.*
The Doppelganger knew that no amount of regret would change what had happened. Its carefully laid plans had gone awry long ago, and at the center of it all, from the very beginning, was that bastard.
*Jin Taekyung.*
A throb ran through its body. Just thinking of his name brought stabbing pain to one place after another.
The Doppelganger had died at Jin Taekyung’s hands hundreds of times. It shuddered at the memory of his terrifying power.
*I should never have approached him.*
It had been a mistake. Greed.
After absorbing Yamamoto Genji, it should have hurried away—or never revealed itself in the first place.
*I only needed a little more. Just a little.*
The other humans had been its targets from the start: the many Hunters left in the rear. If it had absorbed their mana and life force, it could have achieved its goal.
*Damn it.*
But Jin Taekyung hadn’t let the Doppelganger go. He had treated it like a slave, never allowing it out of his sight.
That was the Doppelganger’s misfortune—and every other Hunter’s good fortune.

If it had escaped Jin Taekyung’s grasp, put on Yamamoto Genji’s skin, and gone to the main force in the rear... it would have led countless monsters and fanatics into the desert and stained it red with blood.
Instead, the opposite had happened.
The monster army had been crushed, and the fanatics it had spent so much effort raising had become a shield for its escape.
*I can’t believe I got beaten this badly.*
A bitter taste filled the Doppelganger’s mouth.
It had lost a force tens of thousands strong. Their might aside, what it regretted most was losing a private army that obeyed its every command.
*Still, I confirmed he’s the Chosen One... Master will be pleased.*
The Doppelganger shook its head at the thought of its master, whose intentions and true nature it could never fathom.
For decades, it had manipulated the world in secret from behind an unseen curtain. Yet before its master, even it was nothing more than a lowly servant.
Just like the foolish humans following it now.
“Are we still far?”
At the question, delivered with deliberate gravity, the man in black carrying it answered. Black cloth and a turban covered him from head to toe.
“We will arrive shortly, O great Prophet.”
“You’re too slow. At this rate, we may be caught. Go faster.”
“Caught?”
“Yes. He’s more of a monster than I thought. There’s no telling what he might do.”
At the Doppelganger’s words, laced with an unusual mixture of impatience and fear, the dozens of men in black running around it like an escort exchanged glances.
They’d been running at full speed for nearly an hour. And now it wanted them to go even faster?
The man carrying the Doppelganger to conserve its strength glanced back at it before speaking carefully.
“I’m sorry to say this, but... we cannot go any faster.”
“What?”
“Forgive our shortcomings, O Prophet.”
His feet kept moving even as he spoke.
The Doppelganger stared at the back of the fanatic’s head. Then it spoke.
“I see. This is my fault. I urged you on without considering how hard you’re already pushing yourselves.”
“We are unworthy of such words. Please, take them back.”
“No. How could I fail to understand your hearts? It cannot have been easy to leave the battlefield while the brothers and sisters you grew up with remained behind.”
“That...”
“And you must have struggled to accept why we had to flee like this, pursued by those evil heretics. Am I right?”
The eyes visible beneath the men’s turbans wavered.
Every word struck home, as though the Doppelganger could see straight into their hearts.

Amir, their leader, had raised them to serve as the Prophet’s personal guard. But the Promised Land they had all longed for had proved to be a barren canyon. Instead of green life and hope, heretics had awaited them there.
Then came the fierce battle, and their brothers and sisters fell, their blood spraying across the ground.
Even so, they had not faltered. They believed they were fighting a holy war to uphold God’s will. They believed their brothers’ and sisters’ deaths were holy martyrdom.
At least, they had believed it until the Prophet they revered appeared in a wretched state and left the battlefield.
*Was this really the right choice?*
Escorting him west across desert and wilderness, they had passed oases without stopping. As they ran, a question that had flickered through their minds grew harder to ignore.
God was omniscient and omnipotent. The Prophet was a great seer.
Then why were they running? Why had they abandoned the battlefield like cowards to flee a force of heretics less than a tenth their size?
They tried to suppress their doubts with the faith they had built over a lifetime. But the questions they could not quite bury kept rising.
At last, they became words.
“To be honest, I don’t understand.”
The Prophet on the man’s back gave no answer.
Taking his silence as permission, the man continued cautiously. Their destination had finally come into view in the distance.
“If we stood and fought, we could win. Haven’t you always told us God is with us? That victory and glory would always be ours?”
*Whoooosh.*
Wind roared around the figures racing forward. Other men in black joined in.
“We abandoned our brothers and sisters and ran.”
“We’re afraid God will abandon us.”
“O Prophet, may we ask what the Almighty told you?”
That was when the Prophet—no, the Doppelganger, which had listened in silence—spoke.
“Stop.”
The men in black halted for the first time since they had set out.
Its strength restored while it rode on the man’s back, the Doppelganger set its feet on the ground and murmured, “We’ve finally arrived.”
The place was desolate.
No trace remained of what had once been said to be the world’s second-largest oil field. Bones of unknown origin lay scattered across ground where not a blade of grass grew.
*A land of death.*
The thought came to the men in black as they took in the sight. One found the courage to ask, “Where are we?”
The others wanted to know just as badly. Mere servants, they had followed orders without daring to guess the great Prophet’s purpose.
At his answer, their eyes flew wide.
“During the time of tribulation known as the Great Cataclysm, He stayed upon this land for a while.”
“My master. The master of all creation. He told me, ‘Go to the humans. Wait there until the time comes.’”
For a moment, the air seemed to stand still.
The men in black stared around them, dazed. Then they dropped to their knees as one and cried out.
“Ooh, oooooh...!”
“Inshallah!”
“God is great!”
Their reaction was only natural.
The Prophet served only one person, and this was the land where that person had once descended. It was worthy of being called the Sacred Land.
They prostrated themselves, crying out for God’s blessing. Above their heads, the Prophet’s voice continued.
“You said you feared God would abandon you.”
His tone was gentle, as though soothing a fretful child.
“You wanted to hear what He told me.”
His hand brushed the hair of the worshipers bowing upon the Sacred Land. His touch was warm, like a hand tending the painful wound of a groaning patient.
“Then I’ll tell you.”
But the gaze he turned on them was neither gentle nor warm.
The change was as stark as desert sunlight turning to a freezing northern blizzard. His voice had gone cold.
“How utterly worthless you are.”
At that moment—
*Boom! Thud-thud.*
The men in black blinked, still overcome with emotion.
When they raised their heads from the ground, red blood and pieces of flesh were scattered all around them.
A dazed sound escaped someone’s lips.
It was a pure question—and a reality they couldn’t accept.
Before they could find an answer, deep darkness fell over them.
*Whoooosh.*
A chill ran down their spines. Their hands and feet stiffened like stone, beyond their control.
Bodies honed through a lifetime of training, mana, the swords at their waists—none of it was any use now.
Ah.
A single groan.
Seized by a terror and shock unlike anything they had ever known, the men in black stared at the darkness bearing down on them.
The darkness was as smooth as a mirror, and their faces were reflected in it, clear as day.
*This is...*
Their voices failed them. Their bodies would not move.
Unable even to scream, they shifted their eyes. Above the darkness enveloping them, they saw a face.
The great Prophet who would lead them all to the Promised Land.
No. The *thing* they had believed was the Prophet looked down at them and smiled.
It was leading them not to death, or anything else, but into a bottomless pit within a dreadful abyss.
“Listen, you fools. You weak, worthless humans.”
*Fwoooosh.*
The darkness drained away their living vitality. Dozens of pale souls flowed into it, drawn toward the being within as if entranced.
“There is only one king in this world.”
The darkness swallowed the blood spilling from the seven openings in their faces. Taut skin shriveled. Bones crumbled.

Or so it thought.

sentences.text: When dawn comes, the darkness retreats.
It was as natural as water flowing downhill.
But to those fleeing a pursuer, daylight was hardly welcome.
Especially when that pursuer was a monster they could scarcely believe was human.
*Already?*
The Doppelganger bit its lip as it watched the sky slowly brighten.
Dawn had come too soon.
No—it had taken longer than expected.
*Everything should have been over before daybreak at the latest.*
The Doppelganger knew that no amount of regret would change what had happened.
Its carefully laid plans had gone awry long ago, and at the center of it all, from the very beginning, was that bastard.
*Jin Taekyung.*
A throb ran through its body.
Just thinking of his name brought stabbing pain to one place after another.
The Doppelganger had died at Jin Taekyung’s hands hundreds of times.
It shuddered at the memory of his terrifying power.
*I should never have approached him.*
It had been a mistake.
Greed.
After absorbing Yamamoto Genji, it should have hurried away—or never revealed itself in the first place.
*I only needed a little more.
Just a little.*
The other humans had been its targets from the start: the many Hunters left in the rear.
If it had absorbed their mana and life force, it could have achieved its goal.
*Damn it.*
But Jin Taekyung hadn’t let the Doppelganger go.
He had treated it like a slave, never allowing it out of his sight.
That was the Doppelganger’s misfortune—and every other Hunter’s good fortune.

If it had escaped Jin Taekyung’s grasp, put on Yamamoto Genji’s skin, and gone to the main force in the rear... it would have led countless monsters and fanatics into the desert and stained it red with blood.
Instead, the opposite had happened.
The monster army had been crushed, and the fanatics it had spent so much effort raising had become a shield for its escape.
*I can’t believe I got beaten this badly.*
A bitter taste filled the Doppelganger’s mouth.
It had lost a force tens of thousands strong.
Their might aside, what it regretted most was losing a private army that obeyed its every command.
*Still, I confirmed he’s the Chosen One...
Master will be pleased.*
The Doppelganger shook its head at the thought of its master, whose intentions and true nature it could never fathom.
For decades, it had manipulated the world in secret from behind an unseen curtain.
Yet before its master, even it was nothing more than a lowly servant.
Just like the foolish humans following it now.
“Are we still far?”
At the question, delivered with deliberate gravity, the man in black carrying it answered.
Black cloth and a turban covered him from head to toe.
“We will arrive shortly, O great Prophet.”
“You’re too slow.
At this rate, we may be caught.
Go faster.”
“Caught?”
“Yes.
He’s more of a monster than I thought.
There’s no telling what he might do.”
At the Doppelganger’s words, laced with an unusual mixture of impatience and fear, the dozens of men in black running around it like an escort exchanged glances.
They’d been running at full speed for nearly an hour.
And now it wanted them to go even faster?
The man carrying the Doppelganger to conserve its strength glanced back at it before speaking carefully.
“I’m sorry to say this, but... we cannot go any faster.”
“What?”
“Forgive our shortcomings, O Prophet.”
His feet kept moving even as he spoke.
The Doppelganger stared at the back of the fanatic’s head.
Then it spoke.
“I see.
This is my fault.
I urged you on without considering how hard you’re already pushing yourselves.”
“We are unworthy of such words.
Please, take them back.”
“No.
How could I fail to understand your hearts?
It cannot have been easy to leave the battlefield while the brothers and sisters you grew up with remained behind.”
“That...”
“And you must have struggled to accept why we had to flee like this, pursued by those evil heretics.
Am I right?”
The eyes visible beneath the men’s turbans wavered.
Every word struck home, as though the Doppelganger could see straight into their hearts.
Amir, their leader, had raised them to serve as the Prophet’s personal guard.
But the Promised Land they had all longed for had proved to be a barren canyon.
Instead of green life and hope, heretics had awaited them there.
Then came the fierce battle, and their brothers and sisters fell, their blood spraying across the ground.
Even so, they had not faltered.
They believed they were fighting a holy war to uphold God’s will.
They believed their brothers’ and sisters’ deaths were holy martyrdom.
At least, they had believed it until the Prophet they revered appeared in a wretched state and left the battlefield.
*Was this really the right choice?*
Escorting him west across desert and wilderness, they had passed oases without stopping.
As they ran, a question that had flickered through their minds grew harder to ignore.
God was omniscient and omnipotent.
The Prophet was a great seer.
Then why were they running?
Why had they abandoned the battlefield like cowards to flee a force of heretics less than a tenth their size?
They tried to suppress their doubts with the faith they had built over a lifetime.
But the questions they could not quite bury kept rising.
At last, they became words.
“To be honest, I don’t understand.”
The Prophet on the man’s back gave no answer.
Taking his silence as permission, the man continued cautiously.
Their destination had finally come into view in the distance.
“If we stood and fought, we could win.
Haven’t you always told us God is with us?
That victory and glory would always be ours?”
*Whoooosh.*
Wind roared around the figures racing forward.
Other men in black joined in.
“We abandoned our brothers and sisters and ran.”
“We’re afraid God will abandon us.”
“O Prophet, may we ask what the Almighty told you?”
That was when the Prophet—no, the Doppelganger, which had listened in silence—spoke.
“Stop.”
The men in black halted for the first time since they had set out.
Its strength restored while it rode on the man’s back, the Doppelganger set its feet on the ground and murmured, “We’ve finally arrived.”
The place was desolate.
No trace remained of what had once been said to be the world’s second-largest oil field.
Bones of unknown origin lay scattered across ground where not a blade of grass grew.
*A land of death.*
The thought came to the men in black as they took in the sight.
One found the courage to ask, “Where are we?”
The others wanted to know just as badly.
Mere servants, they had followed orders without daring to guess the great Prophet’s purpose.
At his answer, their eyes flew wide.
“During the time of tribulation known as the Great Cataclysm, He stayed upon this land for a while.”
“My master.
The master of all creation.
He told me, ‘Go to the humans.
Wait there until the time comes.’”
For a moment, the air seemed to stand still.
The men in black stared around them, dazed.
Then they dropped to their knees as one and cried out.
“Ooh, oooooh...!”
“Inshallah!”
“God is great!”
Their reaction was only natural.
The Prophet served only one person, and this was the land where that person had once descended.
It was worthy of being called the Sacred Land.
They prostrated themselves, crying out for God’s blessing.
Above their heads, the Prophet’s voice continued.
“You said you feared God would abandon you.”
His tone was gentle, as though soothing a fretful child.
“You wanted to hear what He told me.”
His hand brushed the hair of the worshipers bowing upon the Sacred Land.
His touch was warm, like a hand tending the painful wound of a groaning patient.
“Then I’ll tell you.”
But the gaze he turned on them was neither gentle nor warm.
The change was as stark as desert sunlight turning to a freezing northern blizzard.
His voice had gone cold.
“How utterly worthless you are.”
At that moment—
*Boom!
Thud-thud.*
The men in black blinked, still overcome with emotion.
When they raised their heads from the ground, red blood and pieces of flesh were scattered all around them.
A dazed sound escaped someone’s lips.
It was a pure question—and a reality they couldn’t accept.
Before they could find an answer, deep darkness fell over them.
*Whoooosh.*
A chill ran down their spines.
Their hands and feet stiffened like stone, beyond their control.
Bodies honed through a lifetime of training, mana, the swords at their waists—none of it was any use now.
Ah.
A single groan.
Seized by a terror and shock unlike anything they had ever known, the men in black stared at the darkness bearing down on them.
The darkness was as smooth as a mirror, and their faces were reflected in it, clear as day.
*This is...*
Their voices failed them.
Their bodies would not move.
Unable even to scream, they shifted their eyes.
Above the darkness enveloping them, they saw a face.
The great Prophet who would lead them all to the Promised Land.
No.
The *thing* they had believed was the Prophet looked down at them and smiled.
It was leading them not to death, or anything else, but into a bottomless pit within a dreadful abyss.
“Listen, you fools.
You weak, worthless humans.”
*Fwoooosh.*
The darkness drained away their living vitality.
Dozens of pale souls flowed into it, drawn toward the being within as if entranced.
“There is only one king in this world.”
The darkness swallowed the blood spilling from the seven openings in their faces.
Taut skin shriveled.
Bones crumbled.
Death drew near.

chapters.title: Chapter 825
paragraphs: A blinding flash erupted with the Teleport spell.
That was how it began.
The space around me warped. A terrible pressure unlike anything I’d ever felt seized my heart, and my joints and muscles screamed as they were pulled into a third void.
*Hngh.*
I couldn’t breathe. It hurt.
Those few seconds felt like days.
But I clung to the thread of consciousness that was about to snap.
*Crack.*
I had to endure. I had to hold on.
I clenched my teeth around that single thought. Through the dazzling light flooding my vision, the ground and sky flipped past without end.
A vast wilderness. A desert leading toward hills curved like a crescent moon.
Hundreds of kilometers vanished in an instant, and the violently churning light began to fade.
At last, deep darkness settled over us.
*Fwoosh.*
Space split open. Through the gap seeped a new light, different from the flash moments ago.
And the light wasn’t the only thing that had changed.
*This is...*
I could see it. Feel it.
Dim light, neither dark nor bright. The damp air of early morning.
Grains of sand carried on the wind. And beneath it all, the sticky, unpleasant sensation that belonged only to magical power.
*We did it.*
I knew it instinctively.
The dangerous attempt had succeeded. The Grand Mage’s Teleport spell had pushed through the interference of magical power and brought us to the chosen coordinates.
And beyond the unfamiliar space we’d finally reached was the being we’d searched for so desperately.
The Doppelganger.
Our eyes met in midair. Both of us stared wide-eyed.
I looked at the Doppelganger, and the Doppelganger looked at me.
Time slowed as if the world had stopped.
But my body already knew what it had to do. It moved, defying time and space.
*Whoosh.*
Wind split around the spearhead and brushed past my ears.
I drew back White Flame’s shaft, clenched tight in my hand. Bones shifted out of place with a crack, and unexpected pain surged through me.
*Crack.*
An aftereffect of the unstable Teleport spell.
The Doppelganger’s Blink spell had carried it only a few hundred meters. This attempt had taken us hundreds of kilometers, and my body had to pay the price.
*Fuck.*
My breath caught. My fingertips trembled. The Scorching Yang Qi racing along the spearhead faltered, as if it too sensed something wrong with my body.
But I had nothing to worry about.
I wasn’t alone.
*Thump.*
A firm hand pressed against my back with tremendous force. The Skeleton King’s clear voice reached my ear.
“Go.”
In that instant—
*Whoom!*
I shot forward.
I tore through the gap opened by the Teleport spell and plunged down like lightning. The Scorching Yang Qi surged back to life like wildfire, coiling around the spearhead.
*Fwoosh.*
Heat spread outward. Ten-odd meters vanished in an instant.
And at the end of it stood the Doppelganger, eyes wide at this unexpected turn of events.
What had it been trying to say? What had it wanted to say so badly?
No one—not even the Doppelganger itself—would hear the rest.
It couldn’t finish.
*KWA-BOOM!*
Blue-white flames erupted like a wave, swallowing its body and its unfinished cry.
The Doppelganger writhed.
Of all the countless deaths it had suffered, this was among the most agonizing. This was a true inferno.
*Shhk. Fwoosh.*
The spearhead had slashed diagonally across its upper body. In its wake, a lava-like force seeped into every part of it and raged there.
It kept devouring the life force that replaced each life lost to death.
It vaporized blood and melted flesh and bone.
“GRAAAAH!”
The Doppelganger screamed in agony.
The flames inside its body had already burned through more than ten lives. If its flesh and bones hadn’t kept regenerating to smother them, it would still be dying at that very moment.
“Grrr...”
Burst blood vessels stained its eyes red.
The Doppelganger groaned and straightened up.
*Whizz—thunk!*
Before it could steady itself, something flew in and pierced its forehead.
It revived before its falling body could hit the ground, then hurled itself to the side.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
White objects narrowly grazed its body and drove into the ground.
The Doppelganger recognized them as pieces of bone and looked up.
Something was rushing toward it, bearing a power at once utterly familiar and strangely alien.
*That thing...!*
The Skeleton King.
His sword flashed, imbued with power far beyond what a mere undead monster should possess—and far too great to ignore.
*Shhk!*
A sharp slicing sound.
Dazzling magical power, utterly at odds with the name **Hero’s Sword**, cut through the Doppelganger’s wrist.
It recoiled from the pain and snarled.
“How dare an undead like you...!”
Even in the Demon Realm, with its countless monsters, undead occupied the very bottom.
Unless they were like Liches, who chose to become undead only after reaching the highest realms, they were nothing but foot soldiers.
At least, that was how it was supposed to be.
*Crack—splash!*
Blood sprayed through a blinding flash of sword light.
The Doppelganger died again in an instant and clenched its teeth.
*Damn it.*
The exchange had been brief, but it could no longer deny the truth. The Skeleton King was no easy opponent.
The aberration before it had broken past the limits of ordinary undead and reached a higher level of existence.
But...
*It’s still no match for that monster.*
The Doppelganger leapt back from the Skeleton King, its gaze shifting quickly.
Its sunken eyes found Jin Taekyung breathing hard, leaning on his spear like a cane.
*He’s different from the last time I saw him. He must have pushed himself beyond his limits, too.*
The Doppelganger was no fool.
It was far more cunning than most humans or monsters. It had manipulated the world for decades from behind its puppet, Michael Silbert.
And when Jin Taekyung had appeared without warning and struck, it had swapped Siegfried Bassmann’s soul for another.
*Take hold.*
*KWA-AAH.*
A fierce wind whipped around the Doppelganger. Sensing the ominous aura, the Skeleton King kicked off the ground and thrust out his hand.
*Whoosh!*
Pieces of his arm bone cut through the air with a sharp whistle. The white fragments flew like hidden weapons and lodged throughout the Doppelganger’s body.
Or so the Skeleton King thought.
The figure that should have fallen in a spray of blood vanished as though it had never been there.
*Pop.*
Gone. In the blink of an eye.
That meant one thing.
Magic.
*Blink?*
Realization struck, and the Skeleton King twisted instinctively.
But the Doppelganger had already slipped from his sight and prepared its next move.
*Grrrrk.*
Mana surged through the slowing world.
At its center was the monster that had greedily swallowed everything the Grand Mage had possessed in life, absorbing it all for itself.
*Air Slash.*
And then—
*Whoooosh!*

Blades of wind rained down on the Skeleton King. Watching them, the Doppelganger was certain that even if the spell could not erase the aberration outright, it would put him out of the fight for a while.
That would be enough to end this wretched battle.
But it was wrong.
Just as the Skeleton King had lost sight of the Doppelganger for an instant, the Doppelganger had forgotten someone else.
*Fwoosh.*
Floating more than ten meters above the ground, it suddenly felt heat rising toward it.
Only then did it remember the man who, moments earlier, could barely keep his own body upright.
*You’ve got to be fucking kidding me...!*
The Doppelganger sucked in a startled breath and hurriedly drew back its mana.
*Whoosh.*
The gale descending on the Skeleton King dissolved into a gentle breeze. At the same time, layer upon layer of translucent barriers covered the Doppelganger’s body.
Then, just as a dazzling flash shot across the space and finally struck the surface of the shields—
*Crack!*
The Doppelganger heard it. Saw it.
A single streak of flame bored through dozens of layers of Shield magic, shattering the barriers of mana.
*KWA-BOOM!*
Ignition. Shattering. Explosion.
All three happened at once. Blue-white flames filled the air, and a massive shock wave lashed out in every direction.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
The Skeleton King felt the impact reach the ground. For an instant, he wondered if that strike had cost the Doppelganger one of its most precious souls.
But Jin Taekyung knew better.
Exhausted as he was, he had scraped together every last bit of strength for that strike. He knew better than anyone why the clear, familiar chime had not sounded.
*Not yet. Not yet.*
The bastard still had the Grand Mage’s power and soul.
But his legs, which should already have driven him off the ground, would not move.

His depleted mental strength kept dragging his consciousness toward a bottomless pit. The dozens of movements and attack routes flashing through his mind were no more than things he could imagine doing.
All he had was a friend who could read his intent from a glance.
*Bang!*
Their eyes met for an instant across the open air.
That was enough. The Skeleton King read the look in Jin Taekyung’s eyes and launched himself off the ground without hesitation.
Through the acrid smoke filling the air.
Toward the Doppelganger at the center of the explosion.
*Tssssss!*
Golden magical power surged along his blade.
The force was less than half of what it would normally have been, thanks to the aftermath of the reckless Teleport spell. But the dazzling sword light cut through the sky without hesitation.
It sliced through the thick smoke and shot toward the enemy beyond.
*Shing!*
A single streak of light.
At the end of that keen strike—
*Shhk!*
Crimson blood burst forth like a fountain.
My vision was slowly blurring, but I saw it clearly.
The Skeleton King’s strike cutting through the air. And someone’s arm shooting up through the blood.
*He cut it off.*
No doubt about it. That slender white arm belonged to the Doppelganger—or, more precisely, to the Grand Mage it had absorbed three years ago.
But no head fell. No scream came.
If I hadn’t spotted where the Doppelganger had gone after vanishing from sight again, I might have shouted in frustration.
Instead, I swallowed my anger.
My voice came out exhausted and unfamiliar, as though it belonged to someone else.
“Are you a fucking lizard or something, you son of a bitch?”
I turned slowly. The Doppelganger stood in the middle of the ruins, blood pouring from its cleanly severed shoulder.
“Let’s go for your head this time. Not an arm or a leg—your head. How’s that?”
“I’m afraid that won’t be possible.”
Its face twisted like a Fiend’s, the Doppelganger continued.
“I’ll need the Grand Mage’s soul for what comes next.”
*What?*
Just as I was about to blurt out a question—
*Vwoom.*
An immense power pulsed around it.
No—the entire ruin shuddered like a living creature.

A single streak of flame bored through dozens of layers of Shield magic, shattering the barriers of mana.
*KWA-BOOM!*
Ignition.
Shattering.
Explosion.
All three happened at once.
Blue-white flames filled the air, and a massive shock wave lashed out in every direction.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
The Skeleton King felt the impact reach the ground.
For an instant, he wondered if that strike had cost the Doppelganger one of its most precious souls.
But Jin Taekyung knew better.
Exhausted as he was, he had scraped together every last bit of strength for that strike.
He knew better than anyone why the clear, familiar chime had not sounded.
*Not yet.
Not yet.*
The bastard still had the Grand Mage’s power and soul.
But his legs, which should already have driven him off the ground, would not move.
His depleted mental strength kept dragging his consciousness toward a bottomless pit.
The dozens of movements and attack routes flashing through his mind were no more than things he could imagine doing.
All he had was a friend who could read his intent from a glance.
*Bang!*
Their eyes met for an instant across the open air.
That was enough.
The Skeleton King read the look in Jin Taekyung’s eyes and launched himself off the ground without hesitation.
Through the acrid smoke filling the air.
Toward the Doppelganger at the center of the explosion.
*Tssssss!*
Golden magical power surged along his blade.
The force was less than half of what it would normally have been, thanks to the aftermath of the reckless Teleport spell.
But the dazzling sword light cut through the sky without hesitation.
It sliced through the thick smoke and shot toward the enemy beyond.
*Shing!*
A single streak of light.
At the end of that keen strike—
*Shhk!*
Crimson blood burst forth like a fountain.
My vision was slowly blurring, but I saw it clearly.
The Skeleton King’s strike cutting through the air.
And someone’s arm shooting up through the blood.
*He cut it off.*
No doubt about it.
That slender white arm belonged to the Doppelganger—or, more precisely, to the Grand Mage it had absorbed three years ago.
But no head fell.
No scream came.
If I hadn’t spotted where the Doppelganger had gone after vanishing from sight again, I might have shouted in frustration.
Instead, I swallowed my anger.
My voice came out exhausted and unfamiliar, as though it belonged to someone else.
“Are you a fucking lizard or something, you son of a bitch?”
I turned slowly.
The Doppelganger stood in the middle of the ruins, blood pouring from its cleanly severed shoulder.
“Let’s go for your head this time.
Not an arm or a leg—your head.
How’s that?”
“I’m afraid that won’t be possible.”
Its face twisted like a Fiend’s, the Doppelganger continued.
“I’ll need the Grand Mage’s soul for what comes next.”
*What?*
Just as I was about to blurt out a question—
*Vwoom.*
An immense power pulsed around it.
No—the entire ruin shuddered like a living creature.

chapters.title: Chapter 826
paragraphs: That’s how humans are.

There are billions of us, and each of us sees the world through our own standards, our own idea of what makes sense. Only when we witness something those standards can’t account for do we feel true shock.
I’m no exception.
One day, I suddenly began traveling between two worlds. The unbelievable power of the System brought me this far. None of that changed how I reacted to the impossible.
I’d always been honest about my feelings. Sometimes I got so caught up in them that I forgot what I was supposed to do.
Like right now.
*What... is that?*
The question brought every thought in my head to a halt.
I stared at the sight unfolding before me, stunned.
And I wasn’t alone.
“What the hell...”
Even the Skeleton King, who’d been about to charge the Doppelganger again, muttered in a daze. The golden magical power that had blazed along the Hero’s Sword had already faded.
We felt a tremendous force flowing out from the Doppelganger. At the same time, a rumble rose from deep beneath the ruins at our feet.
*Rumble. Rumble-rumble.*
*This is...*
The sensation was familiar. But the rumble wasn’t merely loud. There was something deeper, more fundamental to it.
If I had to put a word to it...
*Resonance.*
The thought sounded crazy even to me.
In Murim, a First Rate swordsman could make a sword ring in response to him. But this was earth. A barren wasteland where not a tree or weed grew. A ruin no one visited anymore.
And now this dead land—the ruins in every direction—was trembling as if it were responding to something.
It sounded just as crazy the second time I thought it.
If an idea hadn’t flashed through my mind, I might have stood there wrestling with the question for a long time. But as usual, the answer was closer than I’d expected.
“Magic.”
The word came out almost as a groan.
*Boom!*
The ruins, which had been pulsing with a deep, heartbeat-like rumble, rippled. At the same instant, a dazzling mass of light burst forth and washed over everything.
*Fwoooosh!*
The flash was blinding. The Teleport spell I’d experienced earlier couldn’t compare.
I shut my eyes without hesitation and bent sideways. The spear shaft trembled in my tightening grip.
*It’s coming. It has to be.*
An instinct carved into my bones long ago forced my exhausted body to move. I was ready to evade the Doppelganger’s attack and counter its ambush.
My body and mind felt as heavy as waterlogged cotton.
But even if I died in the clash, I was certain the Doppelganger wouldn’t come out of it unscathed.
*One Strike.*
Whoever fell, the fight would be decided in a single move.
I couldn’t see the Skeleton King, but he was probably waiting for the Doppelganger with the same resolve.
*Come on.*
I steadied my breathing and sharpened my senses as far as I could.
My eyes stayed shut. I felt the air quiver and smelled the earth of the dead ruins. I could even sense the dazzling light slipping through my eyelids, brushing my retinas—then gradually fading.
*The light... is fading?*
Of course, my first question was *why*.
The flash had given the Doppelganger a perfect opening. But there wasn’t even a hint of the ambush I’d expected. All that reached me was a voice I’d grown used to hearing.
“You’re more timid than you look, Chosen One.”
I bit my lip.
Was it trying to lure me into a trap, or had it simply let its guard down?
I had only an instant to wonder. My choice was clear.
I slowly opened my eyes. The Doppelganger stood before me, staring straight at me.
No—it wasn’t just the Doppelganger. Everything around it had changed.
Over its shoulder, I saw the Skeleton King’s eyes widen. Mine might have looked the same.
I had never imagined a sight like this.
*This is...*
“What do you think? Impressive, isn’t it?”
The Doppelganger cut off the Skeleton King and swept both arms out with a flourish.
A ball of light floated up in the wake of its fingertips, illuminating the ruins—or rather, the space that had been ruins only moments ago.
“Consider it an honor. You’re the first guests in this marvelous temple.”
Its words were half truth, half lie.
The place certainly had everything it needed to be called a temple. But *grotesque* fit it far better than *marvelous*.
Naturally.

Everything I could see was grand and immense, as though modeled on a temple from mythology. Yet rotten plant roots wrapped around the towering pillars, and the ceiling shut out every last ray of sunlight.
The temple reminded me of the Doppelganger. It had copied the outer trappings of myth convincingly enough, but everything inside was rotten and dead.
The only things that looked as though they belonged in a myth were the enormous stone statues of monsters packed into the vast space, which measured hundreds of meters across.
“A masterpiece, wouldn’t you say?”
I gave the Doppelganger no answer. I just watched it.
Its attitude had changed unmistakably. And the instinct I’d developed through countless fights told me its ease wasn’t carelessness.
*Composure.*
It had regained the composure it had briefly lost.
But that wasn’t merely because a new arm had grown from its empty shoulder, or because a temple full of monster statues had risen around us.
*It came here for a reason.*
I quietly extended my senses.
An unseen force stirred on every side. At the same time, something Magic Johnson had once mentioned in passing about Siegfried Bassmann came back to me.
“Bassmann was an excellent Grand Mage. He wasn’t the War Mage I am, but no one was more eager to study, and he was especially good at using Magic Formations.”
I already knew that much. I was also certain the Doppelganger, after spending so long absorbing souls and accumulating experience, had grown even stronger than the Grand Mage had been in life.
*Three years.*
A long time, depending on how you looked at it. Or a short one.
Either way, it was enough time for the Doppelganger to make preparations after taking the Grand Mage’s power and soul.
“Hey.”
The Doppelganger clicked its tongue as it watched me.
“When someone asks you a question, you should answer.”
*Vwoom.*
A low hum resonated with its forceful words.
I exchanged a quick glance with the Skeleton King, then opened my mouth.
“Are you an idiot? I’m not answering because the thing asking isn’t a person.”
“Hmm. No respect for your elders. Siegfried Bassmann is quite a respected hero in this world, isn’t he?”
“Sure. The Grand Mage I know is. But...”
I lowered my spearhead.
“A monster like you doesn’t count, you bastard.”
I didn’t know what Siegfried Bassmann had been like in life. I’d never seen him or met him. All I knew came from textbooks and what other people had told me.
But listening to a bastard wearing someone else’s shell mock me still left me disgusted.
Of course, I had another reason to show my hostility so openly: the Doppelganger would consider it a natural reaction.
*Just a little longer. Just a little.*
I’d lowered the spearhead I’d aimed at it, but another spear remained pointed at it in my mind.
Slowly, I drew in the qi around me. Quietly. Subtly enough that the Doppelganger wouldn’t notice.
It was one of the things I’d learned when I discovered what my Middle Dantian could do.
*I spent too much strength before I’d recovered from the Teleport spell. I need a little time.*

The Skeleton King did, too. But being already dead put him in better shape than me. He was gradually absorbing the magical power scattered through the air, ready to take the Doppelganger’s head the moment I gave the signal.
Meanwhile, the bastard kept talking.
“Monster. Right, that’s what I am. I’ve spent so many decades among humans that I sometimes forget.”
The Doppelganger scratched its chin.
“But there’s one thing I never forgot, no matter what happened. This place. The command my master gave me here.”
I stopped short despite myself.
The Doppelganger’s master.
The being who had planted it in this world, just as the Doppelganger had put Michael Silbert forward as its puppet.
“Don’t tell me...”
My voice trailed off. The question rising in my mind made my stomach churn.
As if it had seen right through me, the Doppelganger smiled gently.
“Shall I guess who you’re thinking of?”
Why did that smile make my heart sink?
I struggled to keep my voice even.
“Shut your mouth.”
“Why? Weren’t you curious?”
“I don’t care who it is. Even if...”
My mouth felt as though I’d swallowed a handful of sand. I steadied my breathing and forced out the rest in a hoarse voice.
“Even if your master is the Demon King Asmodeus.”
The air trembled. I could feel the Skeleton King’s agitation from where I stood.
The Demon King.
Ruler of the monsters and master of the Demon Realm, that land of death no human had ever reached.

To humanity, the Demon King Asmodeus was the cause of calamity—and calamity itself. His arrival had changed human history, overturned civilization, and robbed countless people of those they held dear.
People like me.
*Father.*
A beloved face flashed before my eyes. The misfortune that struck my family had lasted only an instant, but the sorrow and longing lasted forever.
Maybe that was why something hot was boiling deep in my chest when I needed to be calmer than ever.
Why I wanted to rip the mouth off the bastard smiling in front of me—and, at the same time, wanted him to answer.
*Crack.*
My grip had tightened until my hand turned white.
I glared at the Doppelganger and spoke. No, I muttered the words like a promise to myself.
“He—the Demon King—is already dead.”
And at that moment, I saw it clearly.
The Doppelganger’s smile deepened. Then came the question, carrying a truth I couldn’t accept.
“Do you really think so?”
