chapters.title: Chapter 827
paragraphs: For a moment, it was as if the world had stopped.
I stared blankly at the Doppelganger’s silent smile. In my frozen mind, the voice I’d heard moments ago played over and over.
*Do you really think so?*
I couldn’t breathe.
I already understood what that question meant. But a deep, instinctive refusal surged up from my chest, and before I knew it, I was speaking.
“Don’t spout that bullshit.”
There was no way.
I knew it. Everyone in the world knew it.
The Demon King—Asmodeus—was already dead.

Near the end of the Great Cataclysm, on what would later be called Victory Day, humanity’s hero fought the Demon King and finally brought down the calamity that had turned the whole world into a blazing inferno.
And a few hours later, a small life was born in a country on a peninsula surrounded by the sea on three sides.
That life stood here now.
“The Demon King died the day I was born. On Victory Day.”
The hoarse voice escaping my lips sounded like someone else’s. I pressed on, putting force into the words as if making a vow to myself.
“He was erased, and we won. That’s all there is to it. That’s the truth.”
I was only standing there. Only moving my lips to speak. Yet I was short of breath, and every breath I let out tasted bitter, as if it carried poison.
Like the voice now burrowing into my ears.
“Yes. That, too, is true, Jin Taekyung. Chosen One.”
The abyss-like Doppelganger looked at me and curled its lips. On the Grand Mage’s stolen face, the smile was as sly and wicked as a serpent’s.
“That is all you know. And to you, it is the truth.”
*Step.*
It took a slow step toward me. Its footfall echoed through the vast, grotesque temple, mingling with its voice.
“But look at me.”
Its eyes, dark and deep, swirled like the abyss as they fixed on me.
“Look at me, who merely watched while countless humans died, and while you wept for joy at your victory. I was there among you, carrying out the Great King’s command.”
“Do you still not understand? My existence is proof. Proof that the truth you believe is a lie, and that another truth exists beyond your knowledge.”
My vision blurred in an instant.
The massive pillars supporting the temple vanished from sight, along with the grotesque statues and the Skeleton King, whose lips were moving as if he were trying to say something.
There was only one presence.
The Doppelganger filled my vision, its image etched sharply into my eyes.
*The Great Battle of Paris.*
My mind reeled. Small puzzle pieces surfaced one by one, filling the empty spaces.
*Long before the Demon King Asmodeus fell, the Doppelganger had already infiltrated this world.*
Michael Silbert hadn’t chosen the Doppelganger from the start.
The Doppelganger had chosen him.
The monster from another world had recognized a monster in this one. It had read the immense ambition curled up inside a human body of flesh and bone.
*Why had the Doppelganger chosen Michael Silbert, of all people?*
I already knew the answer.
*Because merely existing in this world wasn’t all it wanted.*

The Doppelganger possessed a gift unlike any other. It could absorb not only a person’s appearance and abilities, but even their memories, making them its own. Living out its life as a single human would have been easy.
But now I understood. Its infiltration of humanity hadn’t been an act of betrayal or defection.
It had received an order.
An order from the master it served with its life: the Demon King Asmodeus.
What happened after that must have been just as I knew it.
The Doppelganger put Michael Silbert forward and used him to move the world.

The puppet that had made a name for itself at the Great Battle of Paris quietly grew in the shadow of Cheon Taemin, the sky above it. And the shadow controlling the puppet fed on someone’s soul, out of sight.
For more than thirty years, the Doppelganger climbed the stairs, keeping the order it had received in mind.
Until the endless staircase came to an end.
Until the moment it had waited for arrived, and a tightly shut door appeared.
“Judging by your face, you’re finally starting to understand.”
The Doppelganger laughed and raised a hand.
*Whoosh.*
A lone sphere of light drifted through the sunless darkness and stopped at the far end of the vast temple.
Its hazy glow lit the enormous space—and the single throne beneath it.
*That’s...*
The moment I saw the empty throne, I knew instinctively who this temple and that seat had been built for.
And what the seventy-two bizarre, hideous stone statues represented.
“The seventy-two commanders of the Demon Realm...”
The Skeleton King’s words came out like a groan. The Doppelganger spread both arms toward the throne, its face alight with rapture.
“The Great King will surely return. Before long, He will come with the countless armies that follow Him.”
Every hair on my body stood on end. A chill crawled up my spine like a snake.
I didn’t believe the Doppelganger. It was made of lies, through and through. For now, I couldn’t be sure whether what it had told me was true or just another lie meant to shake me.
But...
*If every word it said was true.*
Then I already knew what I had to do.
Dynamite with a severed fuse won’t explode. A locked door won’t open without a key.
And in that sense, the Doppelganger was both the fuse and the key: the signal for a vast calamity about to unfold.
This was the only chance to stop the return of a being who would be a nightmare for humanity.
*I’ll kill it.*
The clouds in my mind cleared. With that single thought, as inescapable as a duty, qi surged through my body.
*Fwoooosh.*
My vision went hazy. My body, still bearing the full strain of the reckless Teleport spell, cried out in pain.
But I didn’t hesitate. I drew Scorching Yang Qi from my Lower Dantian and sent it flooding through my limbs and acupoints, dulling the pain, forcing life back into my torn muscles—
Then I unleashed it.
*BOOM!*
Flamefire Path.
Blue-white flames burst from my toes and devoured the darkness.
In an instant split into ever smaller pieces, I erased the space between us and thrust my spear. It was a motion I’d repeated thousands, tens of thousands of times.
Toward a single being.
*SHWAAA!*
True to its name, White Flame cut through the darkness, its spearhead dazzling as a white flame.
As if nothing could stop it.
As if it would turn everything to ash.
At least, that was how it looked until the Doppelganger gestured and something invisible barred its path.
*BOOM!*
A deafening impact left my ears ringing. The force of the collision drove back against me.
*Hngh.*
I tightened my grip on the vibrating spear shaft.
Only ten paces away, the Doppelganger’s smiling face wavered behind a transparent barrier.
“Do you understand now why I came all the way here?”
Shield magic?
No. This wasn’t ordinary Shield magic.
Even as a Grand Mage, the Doppelganger could hardly have conjured a shield strong enough to stop my strike so easily in an instant.
Unless—
*A Magic Formation.*
Siegfried Bassmann.
One of only three Grand Mages in the world, and considered the finest master of Magic Formations among them.
The Doppelganger had absorbed his soul. And it had been given three years.
“You son of a...”
“You humans take out insurance. Think of this as something similar.”
Confidence showed in its curled lips. It hadn’t smiled like that while fleeing from me, dying again and again.
“Don’t waste your effort. I’m the master here.”
*Vwoom.*
An unprecedented force resonated from every direction.
Magic Formations blazed into view all around us, and the enormous statues depicting the seventy-two commanders of the Demon Realm began to tremble.
“As the Great King’s representative, I command you: awaken from your slumber.”
*Crackle.*
Stone fragments fell on every side as the Doppelganger’s command rang out.
The statues, which had seemed destined to stand motionless forever, began to move.
No—they opened their eyes.
*Flash.*
Monsters, ranging from a few meters to dozens of meters tall, gazed down at the distant ground with glowing red eyes.
The Skeleton King, whose earlier attack had been stopped by a translucent barrier just like mine, stared at them.
Then he shouted like a bolt of lightning.
“Dodge!”
At that moment—
*WHOOOOM!*
Arms, legs, and claws of stone filled my vision as they came crashing down.
The world slowed, and my breath stretched out.
*No. I can’t dodge.*
Not because the statues’ attacks were too powerful or too fast.
Because every step I took away from them would take me farther from the Doppelganger.
*Now’s the time to go.*
The statues under its control were powerful. But it had copied only the forms of the Demon Realm’s seventy-two commanders. Not one of them had the strength of an S-rank monster.
In that case—
*I’ll cut them down.*
My body moved with the thought.
No. My body wasn’t the only thing that moved.
*Vwoooooom.*
With a powerful hum, my closed Middle Dantian opened.
A space pitifully small beside the vast temple—but large enough for what I needed—fell under my control.
*Hngh.*
A headache so sharp it nearly blacked out my vision.
I endured it. I had to.
I clenched my teeth until my lips were ragged, then let go of White Flame’s shaft.
*Fwoosh.*
Hot. Blinding.
The spear blazed blue-white with Scorching Yang Qi drawn from my Lower Dantian. The will of my Middle Dantian moved it.
No—it sent it whirling.
*SHWAAAA!*
I heard no roar. In a world filled only with the sound of air being torn apart, a streak of light-flames cut through everything around it.
*SHWAK!*
Through space.
*SHHK!*
Through the soulless Golems, as if it had only grazed them.
Again and again. Perhaps dozens of times.
At last, after tearing through everything on every side, the spear returned to its master. I caught it.
*KWA-AAAA!*
Everything came crashing down.
All seventy-two colossal statues. The pillars as thick as the World Tree.
And the countless Magic Formations that had filled every corner of the temple.
*KWA-CRASH!*
Maybe my body had been pushed past its limit.
My vision turned white. I couldn’t see a thing.
But I could hear. I could feel.
The mana and magical power breaking apart. And beyond them, one presence struck with shock.
“Say that again.”
The words came out in a voice that sounded ready to give out. I drew on the last of my strength and stepped forward.
*Step.*
“Who exactly is the master here?”
At that moment, instead of an answer, a dazzling radiance filled the temple.

sentences.text: For a moment, it was as if the world had stopped.
I stared blankly at the Doppelganger’s silent smile.
In my frozen mind, the voice I’d heard moments ago played over and over.
*Do you really think so?*
I couldn’t breathe.
I already understood what that question meant.
But a deep, instinctive refusal surged up from my chest, and before I knew it, I was speaking.
“Don’t spout that bullshit.”
There was no way.
I knew it.
Everyone in the world knew it.
The Demon King—Asmodeus—was already dead.

Near the end of the Great Cataclysm, on what would later be called Victory Day, humanity’s hero fought the Demon King and finally brought down the calamity that had turned the whole world into a blazing inferno.
And a few hours later, a small life was born in a country on a peninsula surrounded by the sea on three sides.
That life stood here now.
“The Demon King died the day I was born.
On Victory Day.”
The hoarse voice escaping my lips sounded like someone else’s.
I pressed on, putting force into the words as if making a vow to myself.
“He was erased, and we won.
That’s all there is to it.
That’s the truth.”
I was only standing there.
Only moving my lips to speak.
Yet I was short of breath, and every breath I let out tasted bitter, as if it carried poison.
Like the voice now burrowing into my ears.
“Yes.
That, too, is true, Jin Taekyung.
Chosen One.”
The abyss-like Doppelganger looked at me and curled its lips.
On the Grand Mage’s stolen face, the smile was as sly and wicked as a serpent’s.
“That is all you know.
And to you, it is the truth.”
*Step.*
It took a slow step toward me.
Its footfall echoed through the vast, grotesque temple, mingling with its voice.
“But look at me.”
Its eyes, dark and deep, swirled like the abyss as they fixed on me.
“Look at me, who merely watched while countless humans died, and while you wept for joy at your victory.
I was there among you, carrying out the Great King’s command.”
“Do you still not understand?
My existence is proof.
Proof that the truth you believe is a lie, and that another truth exists beyond your knowledge.”
My vision blurred in an instant.
The massive pillars supporting the temple vanished from sight, along with the grotesque statues and the Skeleton King, whose lips were moving as if he were trying to say something.
There was only one presence.
The Doppelganger filled my vision, its image etched sharply into my eyes.
*The Great Battle of Paris.*
My mind reeled.
Small puzzle pieces surfaced one by one, filling the empty spaces.
*Long before the Demon King Asmodeus fell, the Doppelganger had already infiltrated this world.*
Michael Silbert hadn’t chosen the Doppelganger from the start.
The Doppelganger had chosen him.
The monster from another world had recognized a monster in this one.
It had read the immense ambition curled up inside a human body of flesh and bone.
*Why had the Doppelganger chosen Michael Silbert, of all people?*
I already knew the answer.
*Because merely existing in this world wasn’t all it wanted.*
The Doppelganger possessed a gift unlike any other.
It could absorb not only a person’s appearance and abilities, but even their memories, making them its own.
Living out its life as a single human would have been easy.
But now I understood.
Its infiltration of humanity hadn’t been an act of betrayal or defection.
It had received an order.
An order from the master it served with its life: the Demon King Asmodeus.
What happened after that must have been just as I knew it.
The Doppelganger put Michael Silbert forward and used him to move the world.
The puppet that had made a name for itself at the Great Battle of Paris quietly grew in the shadow of Cheon Taemin, the sky above it.
And the shadow controlling the puppet fed on someone’s soul, out of sight.
For more than thirty years, the Doppelganger climbed the stairs, keeping the order it had received in mind.
Until the endless staircase came to an end.
Until the moment it had waited for arrived, and a tightly shut door appeared.
“Judging by your face, you’re finally starting to understand.”
The Doppelganger laughed and raised a hand.
*Whoosh.*
A lone sphere of light drifted through the sunless darkness and stopped at the far end of the vast temple.
Its hazy glow lit the enormous space—and the single throne beneath it.
*That’s...*
The moment I saw the empty throne, I knew instinctively who this temple and that seat had been built for.
And what the seventy-two bizarre, hideous stone statues represented.
“The seventy-two commanders of the Demon Realm...”
The Skeleton King’s words came out like a groan.
The Doppelganger spread both arms toward the throne, its face alight with rapture.
“The Great King will surely return.
Before long, He will come with the countless armies that follow Him.”
Every hair on my body stood on end.
A chill crawled up my spine like a snake.
I didn’t believe the Doppelganger.
It was made of lies, through and through.
For now, I couldn’t be sure whether what it had told me was true or just another lie meant to shake me.
But...
*If every word it said was true.*
Then I already knew what I had to do.
Dynamite with a severed fuse won’t explode.
A locked door won’t open without a key.
And in that sense, the Doppelganger was both the fuse and the key: the signal for a vast calamity about to unfold.
This was the only chance to stop the return of a being who would be a nightmare for humanity.
*I’ll kill it.*
The clouds in my mind cleared.
With that single thought, as inescapable as a duty, qi surged through my body.
*Fwoooosh.*
My vision went hazy.
My body, still bearing the full strain of the reckless Teleport spell, cried out in pain.
But I didn’t hesitate.
I drew Scorching Yang Qi from my Lower Dantian and sent it flooding through my limbs and acupoints, dulling the pain, forcing life back into my torn muscles—
Then I unleashed it.
*BOOM!*
Flamefire Path.
Blue-white flames burst from my toes and devoured the darkness.
In an instant split into ever smaller pieces, I erased the space between us and thrust my spear.
It was a motion I’d repeated thousands, tens of thousands of times.
Toward a single being.
*SHWAAA!*

As if nothing could stop it.
As if it would turn everything to ash.

chapters.title: Chapter 828
paragraphs: Fear comes in different kinds and degrees.
Some people spend their whole lives afraid of water because they fell into a valley stream as children. Those who’ve lived through an earthquake carry trauma like a brand.
But the greatest, deepest fear is fear of the unknown.
A realm no one has ever seen—or even imagined.
That is the unknown.
The universe. The deep sea. Places even humanity, which built a brilliant civilization through science and magic, has yet to fully reach.
And now, in this very moment, a single streak of fire tearing everything around it to shreds.
*BOOOOM!*
It was like a storm.
A storm of fire, so sharp it made your skin crawl, turning everything it touched to ash.
The Doppelganger stared, stunned.
Blue-white flames poured out suffocating heat, tinting its pupils red.
*SHWAAK!*
Tear. Cleave. Cut.
The wind shrieked. The Golems it had spent three years painstakingly shaping burst apart like fireworks.
Limbs made of massive, solid rock were no use. Neither were weapons brought down hard enough to split the earth.
*Fwoosh. KRRRACK!*
They melted. They broke apart.
In an instant, all seventy-two Golems became heaps of rubble—before the Doppelganger could order them to retreat.
No. It hadn’t even had time to give the order.
The flames tearing through everything hadn’t destroyed only the Golems.
*CRASH!*
An immense force shook the air.
The magic circles, scattering dazzling halos of light, exploded one after another.
The Doppelganger watched in horror as the translucent barrier around it melted like candle wax.
“What the...”
Before it could finish, something hot surged up from deep inside its body and spilled through its throat into its mouth.
*Hack.*
The Doppelganger coughed up a clump of dark red blood. Its pupils trembled.
Knowledge from Siegfried Bassmann’s memories struck its empty mind.
Mana backlash.
Its connection to countless magic circles had been forcibly severed, sending the energy throughout its body into turmoil.
If it had cast the magic directly instead of preparing the circles through various conduits and spells, the backlash would have been severe enough to kill it several times over.
*How? How is this possible?*
The Doppelganger raised its head, gasping for breath.
No trace of composure remained in its shocked eyes. Reflected in them was a human who seemed as unknowable as the unknown itself.
*Jin Taekyung.*
There he stood, gripping a silver spear that shone white as the Golems’ remains rained down over his head.
Through the lingering light of the magic circles melted by the flames, the Doppelganger saw him staring back.
A predator.
“Say that again.”
His voice sounded ready to give out, yet it seethed like lava as it reached the Doppelganger’s ears.
He staggered toward it as if he might collapse at any moment.
*Step.*
It was strange.
The whole place was filled with thunderous noise. The temple, stripped of its pillars, was slowly collapsing, and the rocks that had once been Golems were scattering in every direction...
*Step.*
Yet that small human’s footsteps sounded like thunder. His next words made every hair on the Doppelganger’s body stand on end.
“Who exactly is the master here?”
The Doppelganger swallowed a scream before it could escape its lips.
Fear showed plainly in its eyes as it stared at Jin Taekyung.
A monster. That human was a monster.
One who exceeded every expectation, every limit, by an impossible margin.

After dying countless times on the battlefield, the Doppelganger had abandoned its contempt for Jin Taekyung. It had set everything else aside and judged the situation coldly. This time, it had been certain.
Once it reached its destination, everything would go smoothly.
Jin Taekyung would never catch it.
But it had been wrong.
The Doppelganger, which had left the battlefield before anyone else, hadn’t known Jin Taekyung had reached an even higher realm in that brief time.
Now that it understood, it was too late.
*If I waste even a little more time here... I’m finished.*
Erasure. Forever.
Cold fear crawled up its spine. What it did next came from instinct rather than reason.

The Doppelganger burned through the souls it had left without hesitation. It healed the body mangled by mana backlash, then gathered the energy that had once again filled it to the brim into both hands and unleashed it.
At the inhuman monster approaching it.
At Jin Taekyung.
*FWOOSH!*
The instant a blinding flash burst forth—
“No!”
A step ahead of Jin Taekyung, the Skeleton King had been charging toward the Doppelganger. He twisted sharply and threw himself in front of the flash.
*POP!*
The Skeleton King in his usual state wouldn’t even have snorted at it.
For all his bluster, he acknowledged that Jin Taekyung was stronger than he was.
But...
*Right now, I’m the only one who can protect that devious human.*
He would protect him, even if it put him in danger.
At some point, that had become the most natural thing in the world to the Skeleton King.
Why?
He’d stopped asking himself. Friends didn’t need a reason.
*SHWAA!*
The Skeleton King brought down the Hero’s Sword.
Golden magical power, bright as sunlight and strangely unlike magic, split the flash.
No.
Just as he thought he’d cut through it, the flash passed through the blade like mist and swelled like a balloon.
*WHUM.*
*What the—*
Before he could finish the thought, a light far brighter than the first filled his vision.
*FWOOSH!*
The whole world turned white.
In that blinding flash, which would have instantly robbed an ordinary human of their sight, the Skeleton King belatedly remembered the answer to his question.
*Damn it.*
There was no doubt.
This was Light magic, a spell even lower- and mid-level mages could cast with ease.
A simple convenience spell. Its light was faint and it had little killing power, so it was almost never used in combat.
At least, that was what the Skeleton King knew. It was accepted as fact among Hunters, too.

If he’d known that Siegfried Bassmann, a scholarly Grand Mage, had shut himself away in his hideout to study countless spells—and had improved Light magic’s power and usefulness by several levels—he could have dealt with it.
But it was too late. The mistake made the Skeleton King’s heart sink.
*I can’t see. Anything.*
He hadn’t lost his sight completely.
The Skeleton King was undead. His vitality far exceeded that of a human made of flesh and blood.
But even a moment without sight was a mistake he couldn’t take back when he was fighting an enemy as dangerous as the Doppelganger and trying to protect someone else.
*It planned this from the start. It knew I’d step in...*
In the blank white world, the Skeleton King raised his sword. With his sight gone, his hearing took in everything around him.
The roar of rubble crashing down a moment later.
An unfamiliar cracking sound from high above.
And then...
A low voice no one else could hear reached his ear.
—Don’t let it get away.
At Jin Taekyung’s Sound Transmission, the Skeleton King understood.
Why no magic had come flying at him, even though this was the perfect chance to knock him down.
And what the energy moving stealthily through the air was.
*Teleport!*
The Skeleton King’s guess was right.
The Doppelganger was pouring all its strength into drawing a Teleport magic circle.
It felt both relief and regret that it had taken the soul of such an accomplished Grand Mage.
*You piece of shit...!*
The Doppelganger’s nature might be that of a monster familiar with magical power, but right now it was in the body of an ordinary human.
If it tried to cast Teleport without a magic circle to get as far as possible from that inhuman monster, Jin Taekyung, it would crumble to dust without even a chance to resurrect.
*Fwoosh.*
Mana flowed from the Doppelganger’s hand as it swept through the air, slowly wrapping around its body.
The magic circle would take a little time to complete, but it would reduce the danger by more than half.
Instead of disintegrating without a trace, it might manage to save its upper body.
That was enough for the Doppelganger to survive. The ancient monster of the abyss had no intention of letting anyone interfere with a matter on which its continued existence depended.
*Whoosh. CLANG!*
It happened in an instant.
A bone fragment shot in with a sharp whistle and was deflected by the defensive magic the Doppelganger hurriedly cast.
*SH-SH-SH-SH! CLANG!*
With the magic circle nearly complete, the Doppelganger grimaced at the Skeleton King, who kept firing bone fragments without pause.
*What? The effect should last much longer.*
According to the Grand Mage’s memories, the spell had been perfect. It had struck precisely at a weakness and robbed the Skeleton King of his sight.
Losing your sight in battle was like losing the use of both legs.
That was why the Doppelganger hadn’t tried to disable him any further. The Skeleton King was a formidable opponent, and getting far away from Jin Taekyung—who might do anything next—was more urgent.
But right now, the Skeleton King’s movements were far beyond anything the Doppelganger had expected.
*CRASH!*
Fired with great speed and force, and aimed with extraordinary precision, the bone fragments finally shattered its defensive magic.
The Doppelganger escaped through the opening with a Blink spell, confusion filling its eyes.
*How the hell...*
It could tell from every move the Skeleton King made. Those attacks required certainty.
Even though the Skeleton King had taken the full force of the Light magic, he continued his attacks without the slightest hesitation.
*POP.*
His hazy form shot across the space. At the same time, the golden magical power coating his sword traced a graceful arc.
As its wielder intended.
And as the voice at his ear directed.
—One step left.
At that moment—
*SHWAAK!*
The Skeleton King’s unhesitating charge wavered.
An ice spear shot past between his streaming golden locks and slammed into a pile of rubble.
*BOOM! CRACK-CRACK!*
The air turned cold. The Skeleton King moved by his own senses and the Sound Transmissions reaching his ear.
—Three steps right. A horizontal slash.
*SHHK!*
Binding magic summoned vines to restrain its target. Stems as thick and tough as chains were severed in a single stroke.
—Duck.
Dozens of Magic Missiles tore through empty air.
—Ten steps forward. Run it through.
*BOOM-BOOM-BOOM!*
As expected of spells cast with a Grand Mage’s power, they struck hard and exploded spectacularly.
But not a single spell touched the Skeleton King. The Doppelganger swallowed a startled breath as he closed to within ten steps.
*Already...!*
It felt as though a ghost had bewitched it.
The Skeleton King kept firing bone fragments to disrupt the magic circle. He dodged or cut through every attack spell it cast.
*Was that mutant always this strong?*
But the question disappeared without a trace the moment the Doppelganger saw the Skeleton King’s unfocused eyes.
A shock like a bucket of cold water took its place.
*It was him. From the start.*
What had Jin Taekyung done?
How could he be barely standing, as if he were about to collapse at any moment, and still render the Doppelganger this helpless?
Confusion and fear gripped it as it gathered its mana.
Blink magic.
That instant flicker put distance between it and the Skeleton King once more.
Or so it thought.
It would have, if a voice hadn’t reached the Skeleton King before the spell took effect—before several meters of space vanished.
—Five o’clock. Advance and...
Before the Doppelganger’s form could blur, the Skeleton King changed direction and charged, lifting his sword.
*Fwooooosh.*
In a world gone slow, brilliant golden magical power rose like a wave.
The voice came again, and the sword cut through space.
—From the sky to the ends of the earth. Bring it down.
*SHWAAK!*
A golden flash split the monster of the abyss where, a moment earlier, there had been nothing but empty air.
*SHHK. FWOOSH!*
A red line ran from the crown of its head to its crotch.
Blood burst out. Then a Sound Transmission reached the Skeleton King’s ear, sounding almost like a groan.
—Ah, shit. Right. My EXP.

Jin Taekyung would never catch it.
But it had been wrong.
The Doppelganger, which had left the battlefield before anyone else, hadn’t known Jin Taekyung had reached an even higher realm in that brief time.
Now that it understood, it was too late.
*If I waste even a little more time here...
I’m finished.*
Erasure.
Forever.
Cold fear crawled up its spine.
What it did next came from instinct rather than reason.
The Doppelganger burned through the souls it had left without hesitation.
It healed the body mangled by mana backlash, then gathered the energy that had once again filled it to the brim into both hands and unleashed it.
At the inhuman monster approaching it.
At Jin Taekyung.
*FWOOSH!*
The instant a blinding flash burst forth—
“No!”
A step ahead of Jin Taekyung, the Skeleton King had been charging toward the Doppelganger.
He twisted sharply and threw himself in front of the flash.
*POP!*
The Skeleton King in his usual state wouldn’t even have snorted at it.
For all his bluster, he acknowledged that Jin Taekyung was stronger than he was.
But...
*Right now, I’m the only one who can protect that devious human.*
He would protect him, even if it put him in danger.
At some point, that had become the most natural thing in the world to the Skeleton King.
Why?
He’d stopped asking himself.
Friends didn’t need a reason.
*SHWAA!*
The Skeleton King brought down the Hero’s Sword.
Golden magical power, bright as sunlight and strangely unlike magic, split the flash.
No.
Just as he thought he’d cut through it, the flash passed through the blade like mist and swelled like a balloon.
*WHUM.*
*What the—*
Before he could finish the thought, a light far brighter than the first filled his vision.
*FWOOSH!*
The whole world turned white.
In that blinding flash, which would have instantly robbed an ordinary human of their sight, the Skeleton King belatedly remembered the answer to his question.
*Damn it.*
There was no doubt.
This was Light magic, a spell even lower- and mid-level mages could cast with ease.
A simple convenience spell.
Its light was faint and it had little killing power, so it was almost never used in combat.
At least, that was what the Skeleton King knew.
It was accepted as fact among Hunters, too.

If he’d known that Siegfried Bassmann, a scholarly Grand Mage, had shut himself away in his hideout to study countless spells—and had improved Light magic’s power and usefulness by several levels—he could have dealt with it.
But it was too late.
The mistake made the Skeleton King’s heart sink.
*I can’t see.
Anything.*
He hadn’t lost his sight completely.
The Skeleton King was undead.
His vitality far exceeded that of a human made of flesh and blood.
But even a moment without sight was a mistake he couldn’t take back when he was fighting an enemy as dangerous as the Doppelganger and trying to protect someone else.
*It planned this from the start.
It knew I’d step in...*
In the blank white world, the Skeleton King raised his sword.
With his sight gone, his hearing took in everything around him.
The roar of rubble crashing down a moment later.
An unfamiliar cracking sound from high above.
And then...
A low voice no one else could hear reached his ear.
—Don’t let it get away.
At Jin Taekyung’s Sound Transmission, the Skeleton King understood.
Why no magic had come flying at him, even though this was the perfect chance to knock him down.
And what the energy moving stealthily through the air was.
*Teleport!*
The Skeleton King’s guess was right.
The Doppelganger was pouring all its strength into drawing a Teleport magic circle.
It felt both relief and regret that it had taken the soul of such an accomplished Grand Mage.
*You piece of shit...!*
The Doppelganger’s nature might be that of a monster familiar with magical power, but right now it was in the body of an ordinary human.
If it tried to cast Teleport without a magic circle to get as far as possible from that inhuman monster, Jin Taekyung, it would crumble to dust without even a chance to resurrect.
*Fwoosh.*
Mana flowed from the Doppelganger’s hand as it swept through the air, slowly wrapping around its body.
The magic circle would take a little time to complete, but it would reduce the danger by more than half.
Instead of disintegrating without a trace, it might manage to save its upper body.
That was enough for the Doppelganger to survive.
The ancient monster of the abyss had no intention of letting anyone interfere with a matter on which its continued existence depended.
*Whoosh.
CLANG!*
It happened in an instant.
A bone fragment shot in with a sharp whistle and was deflected by the defensive magic the Doppelganger hurriedly cast.
*SH-SH-SH-SH!
CLANG!*
With the magic circle nearly complete, the Doppelganger grimaced at the Skeleton King, who kept firing bone fragments without pause.
*What?
The effect should last much longer.*
According to the Grand Mage’s memories, the spell had been perfect.
It had struck precisely at a weakness and robbed the Skeleton King of his sight.
Losing your sight in battle was like losing the use of both legs.
That was why the Doppelganger hadn’t tried to disable him any further.
The Skeleton King was a formidable opponent, and getting far away from Jin Taekyung—who might do anything next—was more urgent.
But right now, the Skeleton King’s movements were far beyond anything the Doppelganger had expected.
*CRASH!*
Fired with great speed and force, and aimed with extraordinary precision, the bone fragments finally shattered its defensive magic.
The Doppelganger escaped through the opening with a Blink spell, confusion filling its eyes.
*How the hell...*
It could tell from every move the Skeleton King made.
Those attacks required certainty.
Even though the Skeleton King had taken the full force of the Light magic, he continued his attacks without the slightest hesitation.
*POP.*
His hazy form shot across the space.
At the same time, the golden magical power coating his sword traced a graceful arc.
As its wielder intended.
And as the voice at his ear directed.
—One step left.
At that moment—
*SHWAAK!*
The Skeleton King’s unhesitating charge wavered.
An ice spear shot past between his streaming golden locks and slammed into a pile of rubble.
*BOOM!
CRACK-CRACK!*
The air turned cold.
The Skeleton King moved by his own senses and the Sound Transmissions reaching his ear.
—Three steps right.
A horizontal slash.
*SHHK!*
Binding magic summoned vines to restrain its target.
Stems as thick and tough as chains were severed in a single stroke.
—Duck.
Dozens of Magic Missiles tore through empty air.
—Ten steps forward.
Run it through.
*BOOM-BOOM-BOOM!*
As expected of spells cast with a Grand Mage’s power, they struck hard and exploded spectacularly.
But not a single spell touched the Skeleton King.
The Doppelganger swallowed a startled breath as he closed to within ten steps.
*Already...!*
It felt as though a ghost had bewitched it.
The Skeleton King kept firing bone fragments to disrupt the magic circle.
He dodged or cut through every attack spell it cast.
*Was that mutant always this strong?*
But the question disappeared without a trace the moment the Doppelganger saw the Skeleton King’s unfocused eyes.
A shock like a bucket of cold water took its place.
*It was him.
From the start.*
What had Jin Taekyung done?
How could he be barely standing, as if he were about to collapse at any moment, and still render the Doppelganger this helpless?
Confusion and fear gripped it as it gathered its mana.
Blink magic.
That instant flicker put distance between it and the Skeleton King once more.
Or so it thought.
It would have, if a voice hadn’t reached the Skeleton King before the spell took effect—before several meters of space vanished.
—Five o’clock.
Advance and...
Before the Doppelganger’s form could blur, the Skeleton King changed direction and charged, lifting his sword.
*Fwooooosh.*
In a world gone slow, brilliant golden magical power rose like a wave.
The voice came again, and the sword cut through space.
—From the sky to the ends of the earth.
Bring it down.
*SHWAAK!*
A golden flash split the monster of the abyss where, a moment earlier, there had been nothing but empty air.
*SHHK.
FWOOSH!*
A red line ran from the crown of its head to its crotch.
Blood burst out.
Then a Sound Transmission reached the Skeleton King’s ear, sounding almost like a groan.
—Ah, shit.
Right.
My EXP.

chapters.title: Chapter 829
paragraphs: The Doppelganger.
The Final Abyss, which had existed for hundreds of years, saw and felt everything as time slowed.
The Skeleton King charging toward it.
Blink magic to put distance between them.
And then...
*SHWAK.*
A soft rush of air reached its ears, and golden swordlight filled its vision.
It all happened—and ended—in an instant.
So quickly that the monster of the abyss, born in the deepest reaches of the Demon Realm, couldn’t even react.
*Slice.*
Hot.
The strike it could neither block nor dodge split the crown of its head. It carved through flesh and bone, devoured its organs and mana, and raced down to its crotch.
Like a bolt of lightning.
*Ah.*
The Doppelganger staggered backward with a silent sigh.
No—at the moment it felt itself take a step, it crumpled, spraying a fountain of blood.
*SPURT!*
Its blood-red view tilted slowly.
As the Doppelganger realized it had died, the bond that had held a soul tightly captive for three years was torn away.
*Siegfried Bassmann.*
The Doppelganger could feel it clearly.
The mana, memories, and carefully hoarded vitality of the Grand Mage once hailed as a hero were draining away like the tide.
The ticket for the last flight out of here had just sold out.
*Splash.*
Its body, split cleanly in two, fell into a pool of blood.
A death no one could deny.
And a resurrection that defied the natural order.
*Pop!*
Reborn with a new life and a new body, the Doppelganger threw itself forward without hesitation.
It had failed to escape with Teleport magic, but there was still a way out.
*Get as far away as possible. Even if it costs every life I have left!*
It had lived for hundreds of years.
Throughout that long life, it had survived by prostrating itself at the king’s feet. It had been promised certain rewards when the coming day arrived.
The commanders of the Demon Realm’s seventy-two legions? Even those arrogant, mighty beings could never hope to share in its glory.
Besides, many of them were already dead.
How it had laughed when it learned that Leviathan, one of those commanders, had been killed by Jin Taekyung.
But it couldn’t die like a dog here. Not when it was destined to stand at the Great King’s right hand.
*I have to survive. I can’t die here.*
The Doppelganger ran with all its strength.
Toward an exit from the temple it had hidden in case of emergency.
Toward the countless glories waiting for it in the near future.
Only then did it realize.
At this very moment, only its lower half was running for its life.
*Slice—*
The delayed sound of the cut reached its ears.
The Doppelganger’s already-severed upper half tilted in midair.
Its eyes grew distant as it watched its lower half run on, still moving with its original force, unaware that the body had been split apart.
“You son of a—”
*SH-SH-SH-SH!*
The rush of air swallowed its unfinished words.
As its upper half scattered into dozens of pieces, the Skeleton King’s sword moved again.
*Thrust!*
“Ghk.”
A stifled groan.
The Doppelganger writhed, reborn from one of those tiny pieces with a new body. It was hard to believe it had died so gruesomely only moments ago.
Even with its chest pierced, its bloodshot eyes remained fixed on the exit.
*Damn it. Damn it!*
The Doppelganger cursed soundlessly and regretted what it had done.
How many souls had it stolen from humans over the past thirty years? How many of those humans had been considered strong?
It didn’t know. Even the Doppelganger couldn’t count them all.
They had been little more than a harvest. Like a farmer gathering the eggs his hens laid each morning, the Doppelganger collected human souls and spent most of them without a second thought.
It hadn’t mattered.
No matter how many it used up, it could simply replenish them. Even if it didn’t, it had enough.
No—it had had more than enough.
Until today, when it met a monster wearing human skin.
*Swish.*
A cold breeze brushed its nape. A sharp blade cut through its neck, and death and rebirth arrived together.
No. They came again and again, like a record stuck on repeat.
*Slice! Thrust! SH-SH-SH!*
It was cut, stabbed, and broken into dozens of pieces that scattered through the air.
Each time, the Doppelganger died and came back as a man, a woman, or an old person. Drawing on the powers and memories it had stolen from them, it edged closer to the exit.
A hundred meters became dozens.
Dozens of meters became a few.
It threw away its lives one by one—lives that were no longer expendable, each one precious now.
*I can’t... I can’t lose any more.*
Fear rose with the word *Erasure*.
The lives that had once numbered around a thousand were gone.
Feeling its vitality dwindle until it could count what remained on both hands, the Doppelganger summoned every ounce of strength and stood up again.
*Slide. WHOOSH!*
Its body regenerated in an instant, like the beanstalk in an old fairy tale. Reborn in a grotesque way words couldn’t explain, the Doppelganger hurriedly rolled aside.
*Slash!*
Pain like a burn raked down its back.
But its desire to survive was stronger than the pain that lingered. As the Doppelganger threw itself forward, heedless of its life, the Skeleton King reached out without hesitation.
*Thud-thud-thud!*
The Doppelganger staggered and swallowed a surge of blood.
Something white jutted from the middle of its chest. Another bone fragment had pierced its calf and lodged deep in the ground.
“Where do you think you’re going?”
The Skeleton King’s low voice came from behind it, followed by a rush of wind.
Feeling him close in, the Doppelganger gritted its teeth. The bone fragment pinning its calf to the ground held as firmly as a stake.
*Crack!*
Though far weaker than the Skeleton King, its new body was still easily strong enough to belong to an A-rank Hunter.
The Doppelganger tore off its leg below the knee and moved the one leg it had left.
It summoned all its strength and kicked off the ground.
*BOOM!*
A deafening impact rang out, and a fierce wind swept over its body.
Its eyes burned with longing at the sight of the temple entrance, now right in front of it.
*If I can just get out of here.*
*If I can somehow avoid Erasure...*
*I swear I’ll turn the world you tried to protect into ashes.*
It reached toward the secret door that would open only for it.
*SHWEEEE!*
From somewhere far away—
*CRUNCH!*
A streak of light tore through space and swallowed the Doppelganger whole, ripping and smashing its body apart.
As its vision went black, a voice pierced its ears.
“You fucking bastard. You invite a guest over and then try to leave?”
How cold that voice sounded.
And how hot the flames bursting from the spearhead buried in its body.
*Fwoosh.*
*ROOOAR!*
The Doppelganger writhed in blue-white flames, its vision dyed blue and white, unable even to scream.
Until the body that had once belonged to someone else, and all the vitality within it, burned to ash.
Until every lie it had built up burned away, leaving a single truth behind.
*Step. Step.*
*Whoosh.*
Wind followed unsteady footsteps, scattering the ash.
A black, gray-white shadow stirred amid the thick layer that had settled on the ground.
“...So that’s it.”
Supported by the Skeleton King, Jin Taekyung stood before it. A faint light shone in his eyes as he looked down at the shadow.
He saw through to the one truth of a being made entirely of lies. To its pathetic essence.
**System Level 10 Doppelganger**
“So this is all you were.”
The shadow—no, the Doppelganger—trembled.
Just standing there left me short of breath.
My senses were fading and my vision was blurring, but my racing heartbeat sounded as loud as thunder.
*Thump. Thump-thump.*
Was this the price of pouring all my strength into that final strike?
My whole body trembled. If the Skeleton King hadn’t been supporting me, I would’ve collapsed already.
But I didn’t fall.
I pushed back the sleep demon pressing in from every direction, pulled away from the Skeleton King, and stood on my own two feet.
Then I looked down.
At a shadow as small as a child, made of an evil purer than any child could ever be.
At the hideous being that was now nothing more than a shadow.
“Yeah. This was all you were.”
I repeated the words I’d said earlier, almost to myself.
The Doppelganger trembled as if it were afraid. Looking at it, then at the Level window floating over its head, I nearly let out a hollow laugh.
**System Level 10 Doppelganger**
Level 10.
That was all. Nothing more, nothing less.
For a Hunter, that was the very bottom of F-rank. For a Murim martial artist, it was a Third Rate swordsman who’d only just begun to sense internal energy.
That was the Doppelganger’s essence, revealed by the *Truthful Eye*. Its origin. Its one and only truth.
*All this, because of a thing like this...*
I swallowed the rest and clenched my teeth.
When I closed my eyes, flames flickered in the darkness.
A city in ruins.
Bodies lay scattered among the smoke rising everywhere. The screams of those still alive rang in my ears.
How many people had died because of the Doppelganger’s terrorist attacks and the monsters?
How many had lost their homes and had to say goodbye to their precious family and friends?
Hundreds of thousands? Millions?
I didn’t know.
More than thirty years had passed since the Doppelganger slipped into this world. I couldn’t even begin to guess what it had done behind the scenes.
*Grind.*
My fists tightened.
Blood seeped from the skin where my nails had dug deep. I opened my eyes, but none of it went away.
Not the ruined city. Not the emptiness in the dead people’s eyes or the cries of those still alive.
I remembered it all. It was branded into my eyes and ears, impossible to erase.
And of all those things, only one was here before me.
*Crush.*
“Ghk. Guhh...”
My foot, charged with internal energy, pressed down on the shadow.
The Doppelganger, writhing and groaning, begged me for mercy. It could feel pain, even in this cursed form.
“S-save me...”
“Save you?”
“Y-yes. Anything. I’ll do anything! I will!”
For a moment, I just stared down at it. Then I gathered the internal energy I had left and sent it surging toward the tip of my foot.
*Crack. Crunch!*
“AAAGH!”
I watched the Doppelganger scream.
Then the Skeleton King placed a hand on my shoulder.
“Human.”
“What?”
I’d only asked a question, but when the Skeleton King saw my face, his lips moved quietly.
“...Nothing.”
What kind of face was I making? Did I look exhausted? Or was it twisted with a rage he’d never seen before?
Probably the latter.
The Doppelganger had stopped screaming the moment it saw my expression.
It spoke in a voice full of fear.
“I-I didn’t want to do it! Have you forgotten? It was all on the king’s orders!”
The king.
Demon King Asmodeus.
At the name that came to mind with its cry, the anger gripping my body and mind wavered.

Not the emptiness in the dead people’s eyes or the cries of those still alive.
I remembered it all.
It was branded into my eyes and ears, impossible to erase.
And of all those things, only one was here before me.
*Crush.*
“Ghk.
Guhh...”
My foot, charged with internal energy, pressed down on the shadow.
The Doppelganger, writhing and groaning, begged me for mercy.
It could feel pain, even in this cursed form.
“S-save me...”
“Save you?”
“Y-yes.
Anything.
I’ll do anything!
I will!”
For a moment, I just stared down at it.
Then I gathered the internal energy I had left and sent it surging toward the tip of my foot.
*Crack.
Crunch!*
“AAAGH!”
I watched the Doppelganger scream.
Then the Skeleton King placed a hand on my shoulder.
“Human.”
“What?”
I’d only asked a question, but when the Skeleton King saw my face, his lips moved quietly.
“...Nothing.”
What kind of face was I making?
Did I look exhausted?
Or was it twisted with a rage he’d never seen before?
Probably the latter.
The Doppelganger had stopped screaming the moment it saw my expression.
It spoke in a voice full of fear.
“I-I didn’t want to do it!
Have you forgotten?
It was all on the king’s orders!”
The king.
Demon King Asmodeus.
At the name that came to mind with its cry, the anger gripping my body and mind wavered.

chapters.title: Chapter 830
paragraphs: Master of the Demon Realm. Lord of the monsters.
Demon King Asmodeus.
How could I forget that name? The demon who was the beginning and the source of every catastrophe.
“I-I didn’t do it because I wanted to! Have you forgotten? The king ordered all of it!”
I looked down at the Doppelganger as it cried out in desperation. After a brief struggle with myself, I drew back the internal energy I’d been channeling into my foot.
“Cough—hack.”
The pressure on its chest lifted, and it broke into a fit of coughing.
The Doppelganger let out the breath it had been holding, then glared at me with eyes full of pain and fury. But deep inside them, fear lurked—fear it hadn’t quite managed to hide.
It looked so helpless that it was hard to believe it had been a Named Monster at Level 170.
Yet the little shadow before me was the Doppelganger’s essence. Its one and only truth.
*It must have stolen countless lives to become so powerful.*
It had taken whatever it could, absorbed it, digested it.
Those lives had fed it and served as steps on its climb to power.
But today, the feast it had enjoyed for so long was over.
The fanatics who worshiped it like a god were gone. So was its army of monsters. With no one at its side, only one path remained open to it.
“Spit it all out.”
*Crick.*
The thousand-geun pressure I’d lifted a moment ago bore down through the tip of my foot once more. I watched the Doppelganger stifle a groan, then continued quietly.
“What you know. And what’s about to happen.”
Demon King Asmodeus.
Evil itself. The source of it.
What I wanted from the Doppelganger was information about that accursed being—and about the future of this world.
“What you said just now.”
The hoarse voice that came from my mouth sounded like someone else’s.
My mouth felt as though I’d swallowed a handful of sand. Exhaustion and thirst weren’t the only reasons.
“He—the Demon King...”
Each syllable was a struggle. I didn’t dare say it aloud, or even imagine it.
But I knew.
I knew what became of people who turned away from reality. I knew what lurked beyond the reality they tried so hard not to face.
To escape a forest fire, you first have to know it’s there.
You have to see the rising smoke and the red flames, feel the heat that threatens to burn you alive.
Just as I was doing now.
“Is he still alive?”
In the suffocating silence, the patter of small stones falling from overhead sounded unusually loud.
I said nothing. Neither did the Skeleton King or the Doppelganger.
For a moment, none of us spoke.
Until I heard the whisper of a shadow, something not of this world.
“Is he still alive?”
*Stir.*
The darkness rippled. Its pitch-black face, its features barely discernible, split into a long grin.
“You know nothing, Chosen One. Foolish mortal. One day, time will break you, and you will crumble into dust.”
The Doppelganger was laughing.
It had forgotten its anger, pain, and fear of me.
Or perhaps it had covered them all with the presence of its absent master.
“Our Great King overcame the curse of the gods. He may waver, but he will not break. Even if he perishes, he will rise again. And at last, he will make all the earth and water in this world his own.”
“That is the only truth. A truth you cannot stop, even now that you know it. Before long, it will become reality.”
I stared blankly at the Doppelganger as it laughed aloud.
The moment I met its eyes, darkness swirling within them, my vision swam.
*This is...*
No sound came out. The dust and rubble around us vanished. So did the Skeleton King and the Doppelganger.
No. It felt as though my entire consciousness was being pulled somewhere.
At the same time, sights unlike anything I’d ever seen poured before my eyes like a meteor shower.
*SHWAAAA...*
A brilliant sun rose in the east, painting the world with light. Clouds raced across the blue sky. Sunset came, then the moon rose and darkness fell.
One day. Then another.
Time sped past like a scene from a nature documentary I’d once watched. But there was nothing beautiful about it.
*BOOM!*
A tremendous blaze erupted with a thunderous roar.
Wild animals scattered across the vast wilderness, all bolting at once as if on cue. Behind them, monsters advanced across the horizon with flames the color of sunset at their backs.
*Rumble...*
Hundreds of thousands. Millions.
Perhaps even more.
An army of monsters beyond counting poured in from every direction. They shook the earth and blotted out the sky.
*Kyaaaaargh!*
A terrible roar rang out from above the clouds.
Huge wings swept through them, blocking the sunlight. Then the shadow they cast fell over me.
*Whoosh.*
My view flipped. Sky and earth turned upside down.
In that inverted landscape, I saw a city burning.
*BOOM!*
Hundreds of cannons fired at once. Giants as tall as skyscrapers staggered, engulfed in flames, while figures shot like streaks of light through the ruined streets and charged at them.
Their weapons blazed with radiance. They shouted their resolve as if coughing up blood.
“Never retreat! Stand and fight!”
“For humanity!”
They were Hunters.
Humanity’s sword and shield against those accursed beings.
Warriors given a sacred mission by someone unseen.
I couldn’t move a finger. From high above, I watched their magnificent charge.
They fought monsters that outnumbered them dozens of times over. True to their cries, they never retreated. They shed their blood for humanity and fell.
Until the sun went down and the moon rose.
Until the last of them was gone.
All I could do was watch.
As if someone were controlling me, I saw Niagara Falls turn red with blood. I saw hundreds crushed to death beneath the shattered Leaning Tower of Pisa.
I was a consciousness without a body. Nothing more than a spectator.
There was nothing I could do.
As the scene changed without pause, my only right—and my curse—was to watch civilization burn to ash and hear the screams of the dying.
Death beyond counting. Destruction.
Corpses covered the streets. A broken church cross lay plunged into a pool of blood.

A child, unaware of what had happened to their parents, could no longer bear the hunger and crawled out of a small box. When the child saw a pack of goblins in the alley, the doll in their hand fell to the ground.
Catastrophe.
A word for an unexpected, unfortunate disaster.
But even that word, a symbol of the Great Cataclysm, could not begin to describe the horrors I had seen.
In place of the voice that wouldn’t come, one word suddenly occurred to me.
*The end.*
Yes. This was the end.
The civilization humanity had built over countless years lay in ruins, and not a scrap of hope remained in anyone’s heart.
More precisely, their hope was already dead.
One person at a time. Slowly.
Torn into hundreds or thousands of pieces, they disappeared into the bellies of hungry monsters.
“To Magic Johnson.”
A quiet voice carried across a vast plaza lit by countless flickering candles.
A face both familiar and unfamiliar.
Team Leader Choi, his face covered in scars and one arm gone, drained his glass.
Xiao Shen lifted a bottle with tearful eyes and filled the empty glass.
“To ‘Uncle Chuck’ Hagel and our friend Stone-King, who became eternal stars one year ago today.”
As I heard the names called out with every glass filled and drained, I understood.
This was a memorial for the fallen.
A send-off before battle, one last remembrance of the heroes who had gone ahead—the people who had been humanity’s hope.
And...
“To the bravest man of all.”
“To the light of humanity, who stood against the darkness and always lit the way for everyone.”
I was nowhere to be seen.
“To Jin Taekyung...”
The trembling voice fell silent. Team Leader Choi drained yet another glass and clenched his fist.
*Crack.*
Blood ran from his hand, mingling with the shards of the shattered glass and dripping onto the ground. The candles went out all at once, and silence fell over the entire plaza.
At the same time, light swelled at Team Leader Choi’s waist.
*Fwoosh.*
The Hero’s Sword.
Cracked and broken though it was, its blade still held a keen edge. Brilliant light welled up along it, spreading across the candleless plaza and faintly illuminating the deep darkness.
*Flap.*
A powerful wind swept in from afar and whipped dozens of flags, large and small.
A crossed sword and shield. The design was crudely drawn, but I recognized it: the flag of the World Hunter Federation.
“There’s nowhere left to retreat.”
*Thud. Thud-thud.*
Thousands—perhaps tens of thousands—of feet stamped the ground. The light gathered on the Hero’s Sword picked out their faces one by one.
“And we must not retreat.”
*Clang! Clang-clang!*
Blades clashed in the air, spitting sparks. The tanks slammed and pounded their massive Tower Shields like mad.
They moved with a single purpose, like the pulse of one enormous heart.
For those who had gone before them, and as they waited for the battle ahead, they looked to their new Alliance Leader.
They waited for his final words.
“Today, we fight until the very last person.”
*Clang-clang-clang!*
“WAAAAH!”
Countless auras surged upward at once, as if on cue. Their distant cry rose as one voice and drove back the darkness.
The candles that had lit the plaza were long since out, but humanity’s flame still burned.
At least until they fell here today.
Until the darkness came to extinguish that final flame.
*SHWAAAA...*
At that moment, the wind stopped.
The air trembled.
The plaza, heated to a fever pitch, went cold. Countless eyes turned in the same direction.
There stood a being cloaked in darkness.
A moan escaped someone’s lips and reached my ears.
My senses, floating as if submerged in water, came back to me. The hairs all over my body stood on end.
*The Demon King.*
Instinctive fear and wariness rose in me. Unlike before, I turned my head of my own will. Following everyone’s gaze, I looked at him.
Demon King Asmodeus.
The accursed king who had driven humanity into the flames in the past—and would do so in a future that had yet to begin.
And the moment I stared into the writhing darkness in the distance—
*Crack...*
The world around me collapsed. Every illusion shattered.

chapters.title: Chapter 831
paragraphs: I could’ve sworn I heard something like that.
*CRASH.*
The sound of a window shattering.
It was the signal that it was time to leave the illusion around me and return to reality. An alarm waking my mind from its deep slumber.
*Fwoosh.*
The scenery around me melted away like ice cream. The shouts that had sounded so clear now seemed distant, like echoes.
“Chaaaarge!”
The last battle of the Great War. Perhaps the final battle, with humanity’s fate hanging in the balance.
Team Leader Choi strode forward, the Hero’s Sword held high, and countless Hunters followed him like a surging wave.
Toward somewhere the moonlight couldn’t reach.
Toward a being standing alone, cloaked in darkness.
*No.*
Not yet. Not yet.
I reached out with all my strength. Through my blurring vision, I moved the body that had become entirely my own and took a step toward him.
Demon King Asmodeus.
I could see the back of that calamity. He wasn’t enormous or grotesque.
Even if all of this was an illusion that would never come to pass, I wanted to see his true form with my own eyes—the form no one had ever told me about.
I wanted to catch even a glimpse of him buried in the deep darkness, to feel the power coiled within him, if only for a moment.
*More. Just a little more!*
I didn’t know.
Maybe my desperate cry had echoed in my heart and reached him. Or maybe everything I was seeing and feeling wasn’t an illusion after all, but something else.
There was only one thing I could be sure of: something had reacted to my soundless cry.
*Rustle.*
A figure slowly turning around. Darkness rippling.
My heart lurched. An icy chill ran down my spine.
It made no sense. It was impossible.
But the Demon King was definitely turning toward me—and that was the last thing I saw.
*Flash.*
Everything around me disappeared. Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen, the countless Hunters. Even Demon King Asmodeus.
But the darkness did not disappear.
No—an abyss-like presence was closing in, pressing in on me from every direction.
*What the hell is this...*
I was confused. I couldn’t tell what was happening.
Was what I was seeing another illusion? Or had I finally reached my limit, lost consciousness, and started dreaming?
And just as those questions gripped me—
*Ding.*

**System** You are the Chosen One. The Master of the Ark. The System automatically activates its firewall. The System blocks a newly detected virus. Abyssal Swamp has been dispelled. Power of the Abyss dissipates. Level 10 “The Final Abyss” Doppelganger has been blocked.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
Clear chimes reached my ears and rang out in every direction.
At the same time, the darkness that had writhed toward me like a living snake rapidly scattered.
It shuddered violently, as if it had encountered something it feared.
And then I realized what this abyss was.
I knew what had brought all those illusions crashing down on me, too.
*Doppelganger.*
A line I’d read somewhere suddenly came to mind.
When you look into the abyss, the abyss looks back at you.
The line meant something else, but it described what had happened to me.
I looked at the Doppelganger, and the Doppelganger looked at me. That was how I’d been dragged into the abyss it had created.
No—that was what had happened.
But now I knew.
This was another illusion within reality. The Doppelganger’s power itself.
And I knew what I had to do.
*Fwoosh.*
Heat surged from my empty hands. Darkness writhed against the dazzling blue-white flames.
As if I’d made up my mind to do this long ago, I reached out with hands blazing with Scorching Yang Qi and seized the darkness.
*CRUNCH.*
And the instant I tore it apart—
*SHRAAAK!*
I saw it.
The darkness crumbled away, reduced to ash by the flames. Beyond it, the world I remembered came into view.
*Huff.*
Dusty air flowed through my nose and mouth.
The chunks of stone that had hung in midair began to fall again. The Skeleton King came into view, staring at me with wide eyes.
*It all happened in an instant.*
Had even a second passed in reality?
But I’d experienced at least several hours—years’ worth of illusions—and returned.
There probably wasn’t a single survivor among those who’d gone through what I had. They must all have been absorbed by the Doppelganger.
“What the...”
I couldn’t explain it in a few words, and there was no time to try.
Instead of answering the confused Skeleton King, I shook my head.
Then I left him behind and faced the Doppelganger, which was staring up at me in a daze.
“You—you... What are you...?”
*Rustle.*
Its shadowy body wavered and kept scattering, bit by bit.
What I’d torn apart with my flame-wreathed hands wasn’t just an illusion. It was the Doppelganger’s body, its very life.
“I got a good look at your last-ditch effort.”
“Yeah. I figured there had to be some reason that dog barking its head off this whole time was cooperating so easily.”
At my offhand remark, the Doppelganger shuddered.
Darkness welled up from it like blood, then scattered like ash. Each time, the shadow that served as its body grew smaller.
“Honestly, it wasn’t a bad attempt. If I’d been in my usual shape, you wouldn’t have stood a chance. But I didn’t expect some fucker to cut in without using his turn signal.”
“This can’t... This can’t be happening.”
“If a bastard like you can exist, why can’t a bastard like me?”
The Doppelganger muttered as if groaning.
“The Chosen One...”
The Chosen One. The Master of the Ark.
I didn’t know why the Doppelganger and the System called me that.
I didn’t know who had chosen me, or what the Ark was. I couldn’t know that right now.
But if those two words referring to me weren’t just nonsense, then I knew at least this much: stopping that fucked-up scene the Doppelganger had shown me must be the mission I’d been given.
“Brace yourself. Everything you saw will soon become the future—and reality.”
“Are you sure? I may be a genius, but I’m not exactly planning to die young.”
The Doppelganger laughed out loud at my reply. Its helplessness and madness were impossible to hide now that it had accepted its complete Erasure.
“If the King returns, will you still be able to say that?”
I thought of the deep darkness I’d seen in the illusion.
I thought of that last glimpse of Demon King Asmodeus, whose appearance I’d never managed to make out clearly. I thought of the overwhelming strength I’d felt from him, even from a distance.
*If I fought him, could I really win?*
An empty question.
I already knew the answer.
Demon King Asmodeus was strong. No—there was no point even talking about how strong he was.
If that had been reality, and the power I’d felt was real, just meeting his gaze would’ve frozen my hands and feet.
But sometimes a question has more than one answer.
Especially when I’m the one solving it.
“If I fought him as I am now, I’d definitely die. Miserably, without even managing to hurt him properly.”
At my answer, the Doppelganger’s laughter grew louder. It didn’t seem to care that more than half its body had already disappeared.
“Yes. That is the truth. Accepting the death our King has decreed is all you can do...”
“You’re leaving out a premise.”
“What?”
I looked at the Doppelganger as it fell silent and continued slowly.
“If it were me right now. That’s the most important premise.”
At some point, I’d changed. I’d had no choice but to change in order to survive, in order to protect what mattered.
I’d thrown away the caution I’d held on to as an F-rank Hunter. Sometimes I’d faced my enemies boldly—and with even greater recklessness.
And every time I risked my life in a fight, I’d reaped the rewards of that risk.
*That’s how it’s been so far, and that’s how it’ll keep being.*
The man I am now and the man I’ll be in the future are different.
So the future has to change, too. Whatever risks I have to take—even if it costs me my life—I’ll change it with my own power.
That’s all I can do. And it must be why someone I don’t know chose me.
“An illusion is just an illusion. We’ll have to wait and see how the future changes... but some bastard who’s about to drop dead won’t be around to find out, so it’s none of his business.”
The Middle Dantian is moved by mental strength, and mental strength comes from a steadfast heart.
I won’t be shaken by some horrible illusion or a few words from the Doppelganger.
“And you seem to have forgotten something important.”
I was tired. I felt like I could collapse at any moment.
But as I looked down at the Doppelganger, which had stiffened, I wanted to make sure I said this.
“The future’s already changed.”
I pulled at the corner of my mouth, stiff with dried blood. Fighting off the sleep that threatened to overwhelm me, I went on.
“I put an end to your plan. With my own hands.”
I didn’t know exactly what the Doppelganger had planned to do or what it had hoped to achieve.
I’d wanted to hear it directly from the thing itself, but it would be completely gone in a few seconds. There was no point asking now.
I could find everything out.
Even if I had to scour the whole world, I’d track down every trace of the Doppelganger and pull up the roots it had left behind. Then the illusion would remain an illusion.
Peace would settle over the future that had been filled with calamity.
*I can do it.*
This wasn’t just a wish. I was certain.
At last, the world had come together. I’d sounded the alarm for those who’d grown complacent in times of peace and thrown cold water in the faces of the powerful who’d refused to confront reality.
And I’d brought those known as humanity’s sword and shield—the countless Hunters—together under one flag.
The World Hunter Federation.
An organization that transcended gender, race, age, and national borders.
I was the Alliance Leader at the head of that vast federation.
Everyone had chosen me. Everyone trusted and followed me. So there was no room in my heart for the word *impossible*.
My voice trailed off, growing weak.
My vision slowly tilted against my will. Without a word, the Skeleton King suddenly came up beside me and reached out to support me.
He helped me finish what I hadn’t yet managed to say.
“Quit your bullshit and go link arms with your friend who went ahead of you. You can watch from there.”
*Whoosh.*
My toe came down hard, with a heavy rush of air.
And in that moment, something inexplicable caught my eye through my hazy vision.
*Was it... smiling?*
I couldn’t possibly know.
Was the smile an illusion brought on by exhaustion? Or was it a reality I couldn’t understand?

Before I could even think back over that fleeting question, the toe, still wreathed in a faint flame, had already stamped down on the shadow. It led a monster that had lived through ages beyond imagining to Erasure.
*BOOM!*
The shadow shattered and scattered with a deafening crash. Through it rang the clear chime announcing the Doppelganger’s Erasure.
*Ding.*
It was over. At last.
At least in that moment, I was sure it was.
Until an unpleasant noise pierced my ears.
*Beep.*
**System** Main Quest Cataclysm has failed!
*...What?*

sentences.text: I could’ve sworn I heard something like that.
*CRASH.*
The sound of a window shattering.
It was the signal that it was time to leave the illusion around me and return to reality.
An alarm waking my mind from its deep slumber.
*Fwoosh.*
The scenery around me melted away like ice cream.
The shouts that had sounded so clear now seemed distant, like echoes.
“Chaaaarge!”
The last battle of the Great War.
Perhaps the final battle, with humanity’s fate hanging in the balance.
Team Leader Choi strode forward, the Hero’s Sword held high, and countless Hunters followed him like a surging wave.
Toward somewhere the moonlight couldn’t reach.
Toward a being standing alone, cloaked in darkness.
*No.*
Not yet.
Not yet.
I reached out with all my strength.
Through my blurring vision, I moved the body that had become entirely my own and took a step toward him.
Demon King Asmodeus.
I could see the back of that calamity.
He wasn’t enormous or grotesque.
Even if all of this was an illusion that would never come to pass, I wanted to see his true form with my own eyes—the form no one had ever told me about.
I wanted to catch even a glimpse of him buried in the deep darkness, to feel the power coiled within him, if only for a moment.
*More.
Just a little more!*
I didn’t know.
Maybe my desperate cry had echoed in my heart and reached him.
Or maybe everything I was seeing and feeling wasn’t an illusion after all, but something else.
There was only one thing I could be sure of: something had reacted to my soundless cry.
*Rustle.*
A figure slowly turning around.
Darkness rippling.
My heart lurched.
An icy chill ran down my spine.
It made no sense.
It was impossible.
But the Demon King was definitely turning toward me—and that was the last thing I saw.
*Flash.*
Everything around me disappeared.
Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen, the countless Hunters.
Even Demon King Asmodeus.
But the darkness did not disappear.
No—an abyss-like presence was closing in, pressing in on me from every direction.
*What the hell is this...*
I was confused.
I couldn’t tell what was happening.
Was what I was seeing another illusion?
Or had I finally reached my limit, lost consciousness, and started dreaming?
And just as those questions gripped me—
*Ding.*
**System** You are the Chosen One.
The Master of the Ark.
The System automatically activates its firewall.
The System blocks a newly detected virus.
Abyssal Swamp has been dispelled.
Power of the Abyss dissipates.
Level 10 “The Final Abyss” Doppelganger has been blocked.
*Ding.
Ding.
Ding.*
Clear chimes reached my ears and rang out in every direction.
At the same time, the darkness that had writhed toward me like a living snake rapidly scattered.
It shuddered violently, as if it had encountered something it feared.
And then I realized what this abyss was.
I knew what had brought all those illusions crashing down on me, too.
*Doppelganger.*
A line I’d read somewhere suddenly came to mind.
When you look into the abyss, the abyss looks back at you.
The line meant something else, but it described what had happened to me.
I looked at the Doppelganger, and the Doppelganger looked at me.
That was how I’d been dragged into the abyss it had created.
No—that was what had happened.
But now I knew.
This was another illusion within reality.
The Doppelganger’s power itself.
And I knew what I had to do.
*Fwoosh.*
Heat surged from my empty hands.
Darkness writhed against the dazzling blue-white flames.
As if I’d made up my mind to do this long ago, I reached out with hands blazing with Scorching Yang Qi and seized the darkness.
*CRUNCH.*
And the instant I tore it apart—
*SHRAAAK!*
I saw it.
The darkness crumbled away, reduced to ash by the flames.
Beyond it, the world I remembered came into view.
*Huff.*
Dusty air flowed through my nose and mouth.
The chunks of stone that had hung in midair began to fall again.
The Skeleton King came into view, staring at me with wide eyes.
*It all happened in an instant.*
Had even a second passed in reality?
But I’d experienced at least several hours—years’ worth of illusions—and returned.
There probably wasn’t a single survivor among those who’d gone through what I had.
They must all have been absorbed by the Doppelganger.
“What the...”
I couldn’t explain it in a few words, and there was no time to try.
Instead of answering the confused Skeleton King, I shook my head.
Then I left him behind and faced the Doppelganger, which was staring up at me in a daze.
“You—you...
What are you...?”
*Rustle.*
Its shadowy body wavered and kept scattering, bit by bit.
What I’d torn apart with my flame-wreathed hands wasn’t just an illusion.
It was the Doppelganger’s body, its very life.
“I got a good look at your last-ditch effort.”
“Yeah.
I figured there had to be some reason that dog barking its head off this whole time was cooperating so easily.”
At my offhand remark, the Doppelganger shuddered.
Darkness welled up from it like blood, then scattered like ash.
Each time, the shadow that served as its body grew smaller.
“Honestly, it wasn’t a bad attempt.
If I’d been in my usual shape, you wouldn’t have stood a chance.
But I didn’t expect some fucker to cut in without using his turn signal.”
“This can’t...
This can’t be happening.”
“If a bastard like you can exist, why can’t a bastard like me?”
The Doppelganger muttered as if groaning.
“The Chosen One...”
The Chosen One.
The Master of the Ark.
I didn’t know why the Doppelganger and the System called me that.
I didn’t know who had chosen me, or what the Ark was.
I couldn’t know that right now.
But if those two words referring to me weren’t just nonsense, then I knew at least this much: stopping that fucked-up scene the Doppelganger had shown me must be the mission I’d been given.
“Brace yourself.
Everything you saw will soon become the future—and reality.”
“Are you sure?
