chapters.title: Chapter 842
paragraphs: The young man woke with a start and blinked.
An unfamiliar ceiling. A strange smell lingering at his nose. And before he could make sense of either, something loomed into view.
“Ugh!”
*Wham!*
It happened in an instant.
He sat up on instinct, collided with something hard, and fell straight back down.
*What was that?*
He had no idea.
Not that he cared. It hurt too damn much.
“Urrgh...”
Was this what it felt like to have your face smashed with a rock?
As the young man curled up and groaned, something big and thick flew through his vision, bleached white with pain, and slapped him across the cheek.
*Smack.*
“Hyukmu. Wake up.”
*Smack. Smack.*
“Hyukmu. Hyukmu.”
The voice reached him as though from a dream. The young man—Hyuk Mujin—realized who it belonged to.
He also realized that the hard thing he’d struck when he sat up had been that person’s face.
*Taishan, you son of a bitch...*
No doubt about it. That familiar voice. That inhumanly solid body.
There were plenty of monsters around Hyuk Mujin, but only one who was a monster in the purest sense of the word.
*Smack. Smack. Smack.*
“Hyukmu, are you all right?”
*I’m not all right because of you, you bastard.*
Mujin wanted to cry. He’d only blacked out for a moment after the collision, but the lunatic kept slapping him so relentlessly that he couldn’t get up.
“P-please stop...”
“Hyukmuu! Open your eyes!”
*Whack!*
That one landed squarely. Mujin had barely managed to open his mouth when the blow made him bite his tongue. His body went limp.
As his vision faded, his life flashed before his eyes.
*Mother, Father. I’m sorry. You were right.*
He should’ve just taken over the family business like a good son from the start.

By now, he could have been the heir to the Hyuk Family Textile Shop, addressed as Young Master and scattering silver nyang in the streets. Instead, mouthing off to Jin Taekyung whenever he got the chance and getting punched until his nose bled had become his daily routine.
*And now that bastard Taishan is going to beat me to death.*
As his vision dimmed, Mujin wondered whether dying like this would count as an accident or a death in battle.
Just as he thought it was all over, he heard a voice like a bell ringing out his salvation.
“Good heavens, Young Hero Taishan! Stop right now!”
The clear voice rang out suddenly. The hand slapping his cheek stopped at once.
“Huh? Uh...”
Taishan blinked his calf-like eyes at Ju Hwaran, who had appeared out of nowhere.
“Taishan waking Hyukmu. Not doing anything bad.”
“Not Hyukmu. Hyuk. Hyuk is his surname. And what you were doing looked more like putting him to sleep than waking him.”
“That’s unfair. Taishan only wanted to help Hyukmu.”
“I’m sure you did. If Hyuk Mujin regretted his life and asked you to kill him.”
Hwaran sighed quietly and checked Mujin’s condition.
Jin Taekyung had once beaten his face until it swelled to twice its size. Now it was three times its size.
“Young Hero Hyuk. Young Hero Hyuk. Can you hear me... Are you crying?”
Realizing he was going to live, Mujin answered through streaming tears.
“No, Young Lady Ju. A real man doesn’t cry. Sniff...”
“Should I call you Young Lady Hyuk from now on, then?”
“No, I’d rather you didn’t.”
“You sound fine, at least. The physician the Tang Family sent earlier must have treated you well.”
Song Ilseom, standing beside Hwaran as usual, watched them and muttered, “We may need to call that physician back.”
“It’s all right. The ointment he left should be enough. He’ll recover soon.”
Mujin wiped at his tears. “Young Lady Ju, I’m sorry to say this, but I’m not all right.”
“Finish wiping your tears first. Now, where’s that ointment? Young Hero Taishan, did you see the jar beside the bed?”
“Taishan knows. The one in the little porcelain jar?”
“That’s right. Where is it?”
“Taishan ate it. It was pretty tasty.”
“Young Lady Ju, please call the physician. I think I’m going to die.”
Hwaran tried to decide who was worse: the man who’d eaten the ointment or the man sniveling and making a fuss. Unable to settle on an answer, she opted to get more ointment.
“Captain Song, I’m sorry, but could you bring me some?”
“No need to apologize. It’s just that this falls outside my duties, so there’ll be an additional fee...”
Song Ilseom noticed Ju Hwaran fiddling with the scabbard at her waist. His face stiffened as he continued.
“...but this doesn’t seem like the time for jokes.”
“Was that a joke?”
“Probably. No, definitely.”
“You’re still here.”
“I’ll be right back.”
Song hurried out. He returned with the ointment before more than a few moments had passed, accompanied by two people who hadn’t been there earlier.
“I brought extra in case that idiot eats it again. Is this enough?”
“I heard Taishan caused more trouble while I was gone. I apologize.”
After Song Ilseom, who was judging the amount of ointment, came Sama Pyo, apologizing. Then Namho asked with an expectant look:
“Just asking, but does the Fire Dragon Pavilion have a rule for offenses like this? Dismemberment into five pieces, perhaps...”
As all three said whatever was on their minds, Hwaran reached for her scabbard again. It had become a habit.
It had started after the Chief Escort she’d trusted like family nearly let the Zhongnan Sect take the Yongbong Escort Bureau, and after everything she’d endured in Nanman.
*Hold it together, Hwaran. Just a little longer.*
She wanted to draw her sword and go on a mad rampage. Instead, she took a deep breath, gathered the last of her patience, and answered them in turn.

“That’s plenty of ointment. Young Hero Sama, don’t leave in the first place. Taishan would probably cause some other trouble even with you here, but at least he wouldn’t eat the ointment or knock Hyuk Mujin unconscious again. And Old Master Namho.”
“Yes?”
“If you want to deal with Taishan so badly, do it yourself. We’re at the Sichuan Tang Clan. See if you can find some poison.”
“What? Does anyone else have something to say?”
Her icy voice made everyone in the room shut their mouths and shake their heads.
Even Taishan, one of the most oblivious men alive, and Mujin, who had been moaning in pain, fell silent. They traded glances with the others.
*Young Lady Ju has changed a lot. She’s had a hard time lately, but I didn’t think it was this bad. That man’s supposed to be her escort. Doesn’t he know anything?*
*Why is that unorthodox bastard staring at me? Does he want a real fight this time?*
*Good heavens. I thought I’d gained a sweet little granddaughter in my old age. How did she turn out like this? Then again, dismemberment was a bit much. I should look for poison, as she suggested.*
*Taishan wants more ointment. It was a nice little treat.*
*These damn people don’t care that I’m hurt at all. And what does she mean, the Sichuan Tang Clan? What the hell happened?*
Not a single thought got through to anyone else, but everyone except Hwaran reached the same unspoken agreement: they would keep their mouths shut until she calmed down.
It wasn’t until Ju Hwaran’s stiff face softened that Hyuk Mujin, who’d been furtively checking the others’ expressions while applying ointment himself, was able to hear what had happened.
“What? It’s been two days?”
Hwaran nodded. “Exactly two days.”
“Then this really is...”
“As I told you, we’re at the Sichuan Tang Clan. More precisely, in the Medical Hall of its Outer Court.”
Mujin could only blink.
He’d closed his eyes for what felt like a short, deep sleep. Now two days had passed, and he’d woken in the Sichuan Tang Clan’s Medical Hall.
“What on earth happened?”
“Young Hero Hyuk, you don’t remember?”
“No. I only remember what the Captain and the Huang tribe member were saying at the river landing. After that, there was a flash before my eyes.”
Song Ilseom, leaning against the wall with his arms crossed, muttered, “You remember it exactly.”
“What? That’s it?”
“Yes. None of us got a clear look at what happened.”
Sama Pyo nodded without thinking, then added, “The punch was unbelievably fast. I’ve never seen one like it. Something blurred, there was a sound like a drum bursting, and you fell. That was all.”
“Lord is wrong. That’s not all. Taishan saw everything. From start to finish.”
Taishan cut in, shuddering.
“Pavilion Master beat Hyukmu. Beat him a lot. Beat the fucking hell out of him.”
“Hyukmu was already down. Pavilion Master stomped on him. Stomped and stomped, like mincing meat. Ah, Taishan wants meat.”
“Oh, Pavilion Master tried to stomp on his pepper too, but people stopped him. Taishan helped stop him. No one should do that. Ah, Taishan wants Sichuan-style five-spice pork with lots of pepper.”
From a corner of the Medical Hall, where he sat puffing on his long-stemmed tobacco pipe, Namho groaned.
“Fuck’s sake. I told you we should dismember him into five pieces.”
“Taishan doesn’t know what that means. Namho know?”
“Of course I do. You tie bastards like a certain someone to oxen or horses, then pull their arms and legs right off—”
“Oh! Taishan gets the leg meat!”
*Crack.*
Namho snapped his pipe and charged at Taishan with a roar like a wild beast. Sama Pyo caught him and held him back as he struggled.
Hwaran sighed. “Anyway, that’s what happened. That part of you is safe, so you don’t need to check it now.”
Mujin had seized on the commotion to make a frantic check of his most important parts. He answered weakly, “That’s a relief. Where’s the Captain?”
“With Great Hero Jeok.”
“What? For the whole two days?”
“Yes. They seem to have a lot to talk about. I don’t know exactly what.”
“But they were together not long ago. What could take two days to talk about?”
“They haven’t told us, so we can only guess. I heard the Divine Physician is making a pill for the Pavilion Master. Perhaps it isn’t just talk. They may be preparing to help him recover.”
Hwaran’s guess sounded reasonable enough. Mujin nodded.
“True. It’s not as if he’s come back from some faraway land. How much could they possibly have to talk about? Don’t you all agree?”
When you come back from a faraway land, you have plenty to talk about.
Especially when all sorts of unimaginable things have been happening there.
After I’d told Jeok Cheongang my endless story, he stayed silent for a long while. Then he summed up his thoughts in a single, short, blunt remark.
“We’re fucked.”

Mujin had barely managed to open his mouth when the blow made him bite his tongue.
His body went limp.
As his vision faded, his life flashed before his eyes.
*Mother, Father.
I’m sorry.
You were right.*
He should’ve just taken over the family business like a good son from the start.
By now, he could have been the heir to the Hyuk Family Textile Shop, addressed as Young Master and scattering silver nyang in the streets.
Instead, mouthing off to Jin Taekyung whenever he got the chance and getting punched until his nose bled had become his daily routine.
*And now that bastard Taishan is going to beat me to death.*
As his vision dimmed, Mujin wondered whether dying like this would count as an accident or a death in battle.
Just as he thought it was all over, he heard a voice like a bell ringing out his salvation.
“Good heavens, Young Hero Taishan!
Stop right now!”
The clear voice rang out suddenly.
The hand slapping his cheek stopped at once.
“Huh?
Taishan blinked his calf-like eyes at Ju Hwaran, who had appeared out of nowhere.
“Taishan waking Hyukmu.
Not doing anything bad.”
“Not Hyukmu.
Hyuk.
Hyuk is his surname.
And what you were doing looked more like putting him to sleep than waking him.”
“That’s unfair.
Taishan only wanted to help Hyukmu.”
“I’m sure you did.
If Hyuk Mujin regretted his life and asked you to kill him.”
Hwaran sighed quietly and checked Mujin’s condition.
Jin Taekyung had once beaten his face until it swelled to twice its size.
Now it was three times its size.
“Young Hero Hyuk.
Young Hero Hyuk.
Can you hear me...
Are you crying?”
Realizing he was going to live, Mujin answered through streaming tears.
“No, Young Lady Ju.
A real man doesn’t cry.
Sniff...”
“Should I call you Young Lady Hyuk from now on, then?”
“No, I’d rather you didn’t.”
“You sound fine, at least.
The physician the Tang Family sent earlier must have treated you well.”
Song Ilseom, standing beside Hwaran as usual, watched them and muttered, “We may need to call that physician back.”
“It’s all right.
The ointment he left should be enough.
He’ll recover soon.”
Mujin wiped at his tears.
“Young Lady Ju, I’m sorry to say this, but I’m not all right.”
“Finish wiping your tears first.
Now, where’s that ointment?
Young Hero Taishan, did you see the jar beside the bed?”
“Taishan knows.
The one in the little porcelain jar?”
“That’s right.
Where is it?”
“Taishan ate it.
It was pretty tasty.”
“Young Lady Ju, please call the physician.
I think I’m going to die.”
Hwaran tried to decide who was worse: the man who’d eaten the ointment or the man sniveling and making a fuss.
Unable to settle on an answer, she opted to get more ointment.
“Captain Song, I’m sorry, but could you bring me some?”
“No need to apologize.
It’s just that this falls outside my duties, so there’ll be an additional fee...”
Song Ilseom noticed Ju Hwaran fiddling with the scabbard at her waist.
His face stiffened as he continued.
“...but this doesn’t seem like the time for jokes.”
“Was that a joke?”
“Probably.
No, definitely.”
“You’re still here.”
“I’ll be right back.”
Song hurried out.
He returned with the ointment before more than a few moments had passed, accompanied by two people who hadn’t been there earlier.
“I brought extra in case that idiot eats it again.
Is this enough?”
“I heard Taishan caused more trouble while I was gone.
I apologize.”
After Song Ilseom, who was judging the amount of ointment, came Sama Pyo, apologizing.
Then Namho asked with an expectant look:
“Just asking, but does the Fire Dragon Pavilion have a rule for offenses like this?
Dismemberment into five pieces, perhaps...”
As all three said whatever was on their minds, Hwaran reached for her scabbard again.
It had become a habit.
It had started after the Chief Escort she’d trusted like family nearly let the Zhongnan Sect take the Yongbong Escort Bureau, and after everything she’d endured in Nanman.
*Hold it together, Hwaran.
Just a little longer.*
She wanted to draw her sword and go on a mad rampage.
Instead, she took a deep breath, gathered the last of her patience, and answered them in turn.
“That’s plenty of ointment.
Young Hero Sama, don’t leave in the first place.
Taishan would probably cause some other trouble even with you here, but at least he wouldn’t eat the ointment or knock Hyuk Mujin unconscious again.
And Old Master Namho.”
“Yes?”
“If you want to deal with Taishan so badly, do it yourself.
We’re at the Sichuan Tang Clan.
See if you can find some poison.”
“What?
Does anyone else have something to say?”
Her icy voice made everyone in the room shut their mouths and shake their heads.
Even Taishan, one of the most oblivious men alive, and Mujin, who had been moaning in pain, fell silent.
They traded glances with the others.
*Young Lady Ju has changed a lot.
She’s had a hard time lately, but I didn’t think it was this bad.
That man’s supposed to be her escort.
Doesn’t he know anything?*
*Why is that unorthodox bastard staring at me?
Does he want a real fight this time?*
*Good heavens.
I thought I’d gained a sweet little granddaughter in my old age.
How did she turn out like this?
Then again, dismemberment was a bit much.
I should look for poison, as she suggested.*
*Taishan wants more ointment.
It was a nice little treat.*
*These damn people don’t care that I’m hurt at all.
And what does she mean, the Sichuan Tang Clan?
What the hell happened?*
Not a single thought got through to anyone else, but everyone except Hwaran reached the same unspoken agreement: they would keep their mouths shut until she calmed down.
It wasn’t until Ju Hwaran’s stiff face softened that Hyuk Mujin, who’d been furtively checking the others’ expressions while applying ointment himself, was able to hear what had happened.
“What?
It’s been two days?”
Hwaran nodded.
“Exactly two days.”
“Then this really is...”
“As I told you, we’re at the Sichuan Tang Clan.
More precisely, in the Medical Hall of its Outer Court.”
Mujin could only blink.
He’d closed his eyes for what felt like a short, deep sleep.
Now two days had passed, and he’d woken in the Sichuan Tang Clan’s Medical Hall.
“What on earth happened?”
“Young Hero Hyuk, you don’t remember?”
“No.
I only remember what the Captain and the Huang tribe member were saying at the river landing.
After that, there was a flash before my eyes.”
Song Ilseom, leaning against the wall with his arms crossed, muttered, “You remember it exactly.”
“What?
That’s it?”
“Yes.
None of us got a clear look at what happened.”
Sama Pyo nodded without thinking, then added, “The punch was unbelievably fast.
I’ve never seen one like it.
Something blurred, there was a sound like a drum bursting, and you fell.
That was all.”
“Lord is wrong.
That’s not all.
Taishan saw everything.
From start to finish.”
Taishan cut in, shuddering.
“Pavilion Master beat Hyukmu.
Beat him a lot.
Beat the fucking hell out of him.”
“Hyukmu was already down.
Pavilion Master stomped on him.
Stomped and stomped, like mincing meat.
Ah, Taishan wants meat.”
“Oh, Pavilion Master tried to stomp on his pepper too, but people stopped him.
Taishan helped stop him.
No one should do that.
Ah, Taishan wants Sichuan-style five-spice pork with lots of pepper.”
From a corner of the Medical Hall, where he sat puffing on his long-stemmed tobacco pipe, Namho groaned.
“Fuck’s sake.
I told you we should dismember him into five pieces.”
“Taishan doesn’t know what that means.
Namho know?”
“Of course I do.
You tie bastards like a certain someone to oxen or horses, then pull their arms and legs right off—”
“Oh!
Taishan gets the leg meat!”
*Crack.*
Namho snapped his pipe and charged at Taishan with a roar like a wild beast.
Sama Pyo caught him and held him back as he struggled.
Hwaran sighed.
“Anyway, that’s what happened.
That part of you is safe, so you don’t need to check it now.”
Mujin had seized on the commotion to make a frantic check of his most important parts.
He answered weakly, “That’s a relief.
Where’s the Captain?”
“With Great Hero Jeok.”
“What?
For the whole two days?”
“Yes.
They seem to have a lot to talk about.
I don’t know exactly what.”
“But they were together not long ago.
What could take two days to talk about?”
“They haven’t told us, so we can only guess.
I heard the Divine Physician is making a pill for the Pavilion Master.
Perhaps it isn’t just talk.
They may be preparing to help him recover.”
Hwaran’s guess sounded reasonable enough.
Mujin nodded.
“True.
It’s not as if he’s come back from some faraway land.
How much could they possibly have to talk about?
Don’t you all agree?”
When you come back from a faraway land, you have plenty to talk about.
Especially when all sorts of unimaginable things have been happening there.
After I’d told Jeok Cheongang my endless story, he stayed silent for a long while.
Then he summed up his thoughts in a single, short, blunt remark.
“We’re fucked.”

paragraphs: Jeok Cheongang was a giant who had left his footprints in the vast sandpit of Murim.
He might not admit it himself, but everyone who had ever set foot in Murim thought so.
He was the Fire King, a great martial artist who had survived countless wars and crises over more than a hundred years.
The strong inspired awe. Old veterans earned respect. Jeok Cheongang was one of the few who commanded both.
His martial prowess placed him among the ten strongest people in the world, and no one could guess the depths of his experience and knowledge.
But even Jeok Cheongang didn’t know everything about the world he’d lived in for more than a hundred years.
Much less a world that wasn’t *this* one.
“We’re fucked.”
After a long silence, Jeok Cheongang spat out those words, certain that if everything he’d heard was true, there was no better way to put it.
The young man sitting across from him nodded.
“Yes. You’ve got it exactly right, Old Master.”
Jin Taekyung clicked his tongue bitterly.
*We’re fucked.* Nothing else quite captured how bad things were in the modern world.
One disaster after another had erupted without pause.
Looking back, Lee Jungryong seemed like a fairy. Michael Silbert and the Doppelganger had spent more than thirty years working together to bring the whole world to the brink of chaos.
No—the chaos had already begun in earnest.
“So, what was it called?”
“Monsters.”
“Right. Mosu-tuh. Those Demonic Cult-like bastards are coming in force to the realm of immortals where you live, is that it?”
“Yes. Just like they did thirty years ago.”
This wasn’t the first time Jeok Cheongang had heard about it.
Taekyung had told him once, right after they left the Nanman Beast Palace, and again over the past two days.
But even with a far more detailed explanation this time, Jeok Cheongang struggled to understand what he’d heard. Another twenty explanations wouldn’t have helped.
*How could such a place exist?*
A distant world no one could reach, no matter how many decades or centuries they walked. An unknown land they would never see, even after crossing mountains and seas.
And that wasn’t all.
People there could talk face-to-face from tens of thousands of li apart, while enormous birds made of steel flew above the clouds.
Jeok Cheongang had spent his life walking through a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords. No wonder every new detail filled him with amazement and disbelief.
If anyone else had told him all this, he’d have slapped them across the face and burned them to a crisp with Flame Divine Palm.
Even if it had been the Martial God or the Son of Heaven.
But...
*That brat’s the one telling me. I have to believe him.*
Believe him. Jin Taekyung.
At some point, that had become the most natural thing in the world. The old man trusted the young man, and the young man trusted the old man.
Jeok Cheongang didn’t know when it had happened, but they had become the kind of people who would take even the most unbelievable nonsense from each other as fact.
“If the Dharma King, that damned monk, were alive and here with us, he’d have fainted dead away. He spent every day staring up at the stars, but do you think he ever imagined anything like this?”
Thinking of his departed friend, Jeok Cheongang looked at Taekyung.
“The more I hear, the less I understand that world. And yet, in a way, it’s much like this one. Don’t you think?”
Taekyung nodded.
At first, everything around him had felt unfamiliar and different. But not anymore.
The modern world and Murim. Murim and the modern world.
The two worlds were astonishingly alike—not in their civilizations, but in the currents of change running through them.
“If Murim has Dark Heaven, then the world I lived in has monsters. And both are headed in a bad direction.”
“Not so long ago, each world went through its own Great Faction War, too.”
“That’s right.”
“Then you...”
Jeok Cheongang trailed off. When he continued, his voice was grave.
*Do you think all of this is just a coincidence?*
A short silence fell.
As Jin Taekyung gazed at the oil lamp flickering in the darkness, his eyes began to glow red.
It was late enough that even the stars had fallen asleep.
I left Jeok Cheongang behind, stepped out of the pavilion, and wandered alone through the Inner Court. I had no destination in mind. All I carried was the question he’d just asked.
*Do you think all of this is just a coincidence?*
If Jeok Cheongang had asked me anything more specific, I would’ve hesitated to answer.
There was so much even I still didn’t know. So many secrets remained hidden in both worlds.
But I was certain of my answer to that question.
*Not at all.*
It wasn’t a coincidence.
That was what I’d told him after a short silence. It had taken me a long time to become sure of it.
I’d been thinking about it ever since I first opened my eyes in Murim. And after all that time, I’d reached one conclusion.
*There’s a connection. A definite connection.*
At first, everything that happened to me had felt like a terrible run of bad luck.
All I’d done was fall asleep in a damn old capsule. Then I’d had to fight one danger after another in a world where I couldn’t even tell whether it was a game or reality.
But as my circumstances changed, so did my thinking.
I’d gone from an F-rank Hunter who lost his job overnight to a celebrity, gripping power and wealth in both hands that I never could’ve imagined before.
And I’d gained them in both worlds—the modern world and Murim.
*My bad luck turned into good luck.*
The days when I’d lamented, *How can I be this unlucky?* quickly faded into the past.
What I’d thought was bad luck turned out to be good fortune sent down from the heavens. Maybe it was even more than that—a stroke of heavenly fortune.
Until, one day, I began to feel a strange sense of déjà vu.
*From Shanxi Province to Henan. Across Sichuan and all the way to Hubei.*
Beneath the dark clouds of Dark Heaven, blood-soaked flames had risen.

The Head Elder of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, who had long harbored a desire for revenge, drew the sword he’d kept hidden for years. A revered monk, respected for his extraordinary martial prowess and wisdom, met his death. And the flames that swept through Shaolin Temple spread to Sichuan and Hubei.
*And finally, they reached distant Nanman.*
The one saving grace was that those flames hadn’t reduced everything in their path to ash.
Though countless people had died, even more had escaped the fire. And I’d found many traces left behind where that terrible disaster had swept through.
The Water God Dragon, driven mad and stripped of reason.
Fishermen and fish transformed into grotesque creatures that looked like monsters.
Dark Heaven’s Moving Formation, so much like modern Teleport Magic that I couldn’t dismiss it as mere dark arts or a formation.
And finally...
*The rift that opened in Nanman.*
I remembered it clearly. No—I couldn’t forget it.
That darkness writhing like a living creature. The familiarity I’d sensed time and again in what Murim’s martial artists called demonic qi.
*It was magical power. I’m sure of it.*
At first, I couldn’t accept that.
It shouldn’t exist. It couldn’t exist.
But as time passed, the picture grew clearer, forcing me to face reality.
*It isn’t just a difference in names.*
Mana and internal energy were identical at their core. Both were qi.
Something everywhere and nowhere at once. An intangible force present in blue seas and forests, and in smog-filled canyons of skyscrapers, though most people couldn’t sense it.
Magical power was different.
That evil energy, steeped in death, had flowed in from another world.
If mana and internal energy were natives, present from the beginning, then magical power was a stranger—an invader that had crossed over from beyond along with the monsters.
And now that very magical power had appeared.
Not in the modern world, but here in Murim.
*How am I supposed to make sense of that?*
Ha.
A hollow laugh escaped me.
How was I supposed to make sense of it? I could try to deny it all I wanted, but I couldn’t ignore what was right in front of me. I already knew the answer.
*Dark Heaven.*
There was no doubt.
Dark Heaven was the true link between the modern world and Murim.
Everything I’d personally witnessed since becoming entangled with them was evidence—and served as both prosecutor and judge.
*But how?*
How had they set foot in this world—in Murim?
The Great Faction War had been a major event, but in the end, it was a war over supremacy in Murim.
If anything like the Great Cataclysm had happened, I would’ve known. Or at least Jeok Cheongang and the others who’d lived through that time would have.
Rumors of hideous monsters sweeping across the land would’ve reached even the most remote villages.
*But all anyone knows is that Dark Heaven succeeded the Demonic Cult and uses strange dark arts.*
The implication was clear.
*Something that shouldn’t exist appeared in Murim during the chaos of the Great Faction War—or shortly afterward.*
If so, the timing lined up exactly. That was when Dark Heaven first approached the Head Elder.
But I still didn’t know the underlying cause. The biggest question remained unanswered.
*The Lord of Heaven.*
Dark Heaven’s master.
No, an absolute being they might as well worship as a god.
How he could exist in Murim wasn’t what puzzled me. The Great Cataclysm thirty-odd years ago had begun much the same way.
The problem was...
*Who the Lord of Heaven really is.*
Step.
I stopped walking.
Darkness lay heavy over the world, and torches burned red throughout the Inner Court.
As I stared blankly into their flames, lost in thought, I suddenly felt a shock as if something had pierced through the top of my head.
“Could it be...?”
The words escaped me like a groan and faded into the darkness.
Just then—
Swish.
The shadow cast by a wavering torch touched the tips of my feet.
Like that cursed being who no longer existed. Like the one who had smiled even as he met his eternal Erasure.
And at the same time, a conversation buried in the depths of my memories rang in my ears like an illusion.
*The great king has overcome a god’s curse. He may waver, but he will not break. Even if he falls, he will rise again. And at last, he will make all the earth and water in this world his own.*
*What?*
*That alone is the truth. A truth you cannot stop even knowing it—a truth that will become reality before long.*
I froze like a statue, as though I were back in that moment when I’d faced the Doppelganger.

The shadow cast by a wavering torch touched the tips of my feet.
Like that cursed being who no longer existed.
Like the one who had smiled even as he met his eternal Erasure.
And at the same time, a conversation buried in the depths of my memories rang in my ears like an illusion.
*The great king has overcome a god’s curse.
He may waver, but he will not break.
Even if he falls, he will rise again.
And at last, he will make all the earth and water in this world his own.*
*What?*
*That alone is the truth.
A truth you cannot stop even knowing it—a truth that will become reality before long.*
I froze like a statue, as though I were back in that moment when I’d faced the Doppelganger.

chapters.title: Chapter 844
paragraphs: “Is that it?”
The man who spoke looked to be around thirty at most. His face was ordinary—the kind you might see several times in a day at the marketplace.
Yet no one would dare look at him and think he was ordinary.
He wasn’t standing in a marketplace. He was standing in a pool of dark-red blood.
“It’s certainly improved, but it’s still nowhere near what I expected...”
Crunch.
He stepped on an arm half-submerged in the blood and continued.
“Did you call me here just to show me this?”
The owner of the arm? He didn’t know. He had no need to know.
It belonged to one of countless test subjects, one of the dozens he had killed here today.
The problem was that he wasn’t particularly pleased with the experiment’s results.
“You’ve all got mouths. Say something, will you?”
The black-robed men lined up before him swallowed dryly in the icy silence.
They knew the man all too well. Whenever his temper soured, blood was sure to follow. Some of their own comrades had died that way.
After witnessing it countless times, who would dare open their mouth?
Their silence was a lesson learned through repetition. But for all the man’s brutality, he wasn’t stupid.
“Hah. Look at you lot. I call you sorcerers and treat you like people, and this is what I get...”
He gave a short laugh. The next instant, his figure blurred.
Thud.
Flesh and brain matter flew in every direction. One of the black-robed men—or rather, one of the sorcerers—crumpled like a rotten tree, his head smashed to pieces.
Boom.
The thunderous sound told the sorcerers what they had to do.
Thump.
They dropped to their knees without hesitation.
Silence wasn’t the only lesson they’d learned. They also knew that however cruel the man was, he preferred not to spill more of *their* blood than necessary.
“P-please, calm your anger.”
“Blood Lord...!”
The man—the Blood Lord—looked down at the sorcerers as they cried out and knocked their heads against the stone floor. A faint bloody light glowed in his eyes.
*Vermin.*
He wanted to tear their limbs off right then and there, but he forced down the urge to kill them.
*Western Heaven is dead, and now Southern Heaven too. We need to preserve every bit of strength we can if we’re to accomplish the great cause.*
Sorcerers were precious. Few in Dark Heaven could wield supernatural powers, and the research they’d pursued for years was bearing considerable fruit.
Today’s results simply hadn’t pleased him.
Once they produced something close to a finished result, its impact would be more than enough to swallow the world.
“Not enough. Still not enough.”
At the words he seemed to have spoken to himself, the sorcerers bowed their heads even lower.
If it wasn’t enough, they would have to make up the difference somehow. They didn’t want to end up like their comrades who had died before them.
“Blood Lord, if you could tell us which part you found lacking...”
“Every part of it.”
The Blood Lord turned slowly and gestured toward the bodies scattered around them.
“They were all too weak. And the duration still hasn’t improved.”
“We’re looking for ways to improve them, but we’re nowhere near able to increase the potency of both effects at once. Obtaining enough Peak masters is just as difficult.”
The Blood Lord frowned at what sounded like an excuse, but this time he had to accept it.
Peak masters couldn’t be made overnight.
Even at the great sects of the Central Plains, which accepted only exceptional talent, reaching the Peak realm took more than ten years of grueling training.
The time varied with talent and effort, but that was all. Even demonic, heterodox martial arts, which could be mastered far faster than those of the orthodox faction, were no exception.
Nothing came easily. Those martial arts lacked purity and depth, and countless practitioners faltered before the wall of the Peak realm.
*Those two were the exceptions.*
The Blood Lord bit his lip. He couldn’t bring himself to say it aloud.
As he recalled the not-so-distant past, a bloody gleam flickered in his eyes.
*Jin Taekyung. Cheongpung.*
At first, he’d thought they were earthworms. Creatures that would pop with a little pressure from his foot.
But at some point, those two earth dragons had become heavenly dragons. They’d risen from a mud pit full of filth and flown into the blue sky.
*No. At least one of them was never an earthworm to begin with.*
Even the Blood Lord had to admit that comparing Cheongpung to an earthworm might have been too harsh.
The youngest Disciple Sword Saint Mae Jonghak had accepted in his later years. A martial talent bestowed by the heavens.
Cheongpung was a genius whose equal was hard to find in Murim’s history, born with the destiny of a dragon.
But...
*What the hell is Jin Taekyung?*
The Blood Lord had been the power behind Jin Yangbaek, Head Elder of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. He remembered all too clearly the day he’d first received a report on Jin Taekyung, long ago.
He remembered the first thing he’d said to the subordinate who delivered it, too.
“Investigate him again.”
“Pardon?”
“How can anyone be that fucking useless? There must be something he’s hiding.”
It was only natural.
Jin Taekyung’s martial arts were worse than a Third Rate street thug’s, and he even made a schedule for his rounds of the pleasure houses.

If the eldest son, struggling to restore the family’s fortunes, and the second, training day and night, were the pillars of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, Jin Taekyung was gnawing at what remained of them from the roots up.
An earthworm.
No. A bug.
But one day, Jin Taekyung changed.
Unlike Cheongpung, Jin Taekyung had been born a bug. Then he became an earthworm, then a venomous centipede, then an imugi, and finally a dragon.
When the Blood Lord pieced together the entire transformation, he was stunned.
*That bastard has gone far beyond anything that makes sense.*
Cheongpung was born with the destiny of a dragon. There was nothing strange about calling him one now.
Jin Taekyung had been granted no such destiny by the heavens.
He was nothing but a bug, an earthworm. All he could do when stepped on was writhe.
That should have been all.
Throb.
A sudden pain made the Blood Lord clench his teeth.
He looked down at his arms. Both were whole and attached. Someone’s purplish Force had once severed them, but they had grown back stronger than before. Now they trembled faintly.
From fear? No. This was anger.
And pain and humiliation etched into his soul.
*If Jin Taekyung hadn’t gotten in my way...*
The Blood Lord ground his teeth as he recalled that day: Jin Taekyung, drenched in blood, clinging to his ankle and refusing to let go—and the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s Force sweeping across his arm.
Worse than the pain had been the ridicule of the others.
Though two of them were lonely spirits now.
*Western Heaven. Southern Heaven. Watch closely from wherever you are. I’ll accomplish what you two failed to do.*
The Western Heaven Demon Lord and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had been too powerful for even the prideful Blood Lord to dismiss.
Their deaths were an enormous loss to Dark Heaven, but they had taught him two lessons.
First, he must never let his guard down against Jin Taekyung.
Second, helping the Lord of Heaven accomplish the great cause would require greater strength and effort than ever before.
“Spread them.”
“What?”
The Blood Lord looked at the sorcerers who had questioned him without thinking. The bloody gleam that had been in his eyes moments ago had settled into a cold stare.
“Now that the Great War has begun, we need to gather every bit of strength we can. We can’t keep using Peak masters in experiments like these forever.”
“You mean...”
“You’ve already planted seeds throughout the Central Plains. Am I wrong?”
The head of the sorcerers bowed deeply.
“No. Some of the seeds have already blossomed.”
It was true.
With vast wealth and years of research, Dark Heaven had created the “seeds” and scattered some of them throughout the land long ago.
Some had gone to Henan and Shaanxi, at the heart of orthodox Murim. Others had gone to border regions such as Guangxi and Guangdong.
And some... to the northern plateau bordering Shanxi Province.
The seeds were both an experiment and a means of sowing chaos across Central Plains Murim. Barely a month ago, one had nearly shaken an entire city.
Nearly.
“You failed spectacularly in Guangxi Province.”
“That was...”
“I know. If the Fire King—that old man—hadn’t happened to show up pretending to be a monk, it might have worked.”
The unorthodox faction’s uprising in Guangxi Province had been no coincidence.
A man carrying a “seed” had gathered followers and seized control of half of Guangxi.
At least until Jeok Cheongang, hiding his identity under the sobriquet Blood Monk, had smashed his head.
“But those were failures made before we improved the effects. If the ones we have now fall into the wrong hands...”
“It doesn’t matter.”
The Blood Lord cut off the sorcerer’s warning that the blade might turn against them.
“Select men fit to become seeds and bury them deep. Make sure they can be spread whenever the time comes.”
The sorcerers could see that further objections were useless.
They had two choices: obey or die.
And the Blood Lord wasn’t wrong. They chose to obey.
“As you command.”
The Blood Lord’s eyes flashed as he looked down at their bowed heads.
He could still recall every word of his conversation with the Lord of Heaven, who had awakened without warning from his long slumber just ten days ago.
“The time has come.”
“Lord of Heaven, what do you mean?”
“The world is twisting. Now... bring down the heavens.”
The Blood Lord drew a long breath.
After issuing that one command, the Lord of Heaven had fallen asleep again. He had given his faithful servant an unbelievable opportunity: the chance to draw the bowstring in his name.
And now the Blood Lord knew by instinct.
It was time to release it.
“Send out missives.”
That day, dozens of black-feathered hawks took to the sky.

chapters.title: Chapter 845
paragraphs: “Chew it thoroughly before you swallow.”
“Chew it?”
“Yes. Don’t swallow it whole, and don’t spit it out halfway through. Understood?”
The Divine Physician had arrived at first light with that stern warning. I gave a faint laugh and accepted the pill he held out.
“Of course. I’m not a child, and you made it for my sake.”
The pill was dark and about the size of a marble.

The Appraisal System was still inaccessible, so I couldn’t tell exactly what was in it or what it would do. But the Divine Physician must have spent several sleepless nights making it. The exhaustion around his eyes was proof enough.
*He must have had plenty of other patients to care for, too.*

The best physician in the world had sacrificed his own time and health to make this pill for me. Even if it was hard as a rock, I planned to chew it until the sweetness came out. It was the least I could do.
And the moment I chewed the pill with heartfelt gratitude—
Crunch.
I realized that being a decent human being could go to hell. This wasn’t something a human being could eat.
Ptooey.
The pill I spat out on instinct stuck fast to the Divine Physician’s pristine white robe.
He gazed mournfully at the pill he’d spent days making. “I told you not to spit it out...”
Still retching and struggling to keep my senses, I spoke from the heart.
“Sorry, but are you out of your mind?”
“I am, and I understand exactly how you feel.”
“Have you tried eating it yourself?”
“I haven’t.”
“Then you have no idea how I feel. None.”
“Medicine that’s good for you is supposed to taste bitter. It always is.”
“This wasn’t just bitter. Did you put poison in it or something?”
“Enough!”
Jeok Cheongang, who’d watched the whole thing, bellowed and glared at me.
“He may not be particularly trustworthy and may seem a bit of a quack, but he made that medicine with care for your sake. Poison? Where did you get the nerve to say such blasphemous nonsense?”
“Sorry.”
“Don’t apologize to me. Apologize to that quack!”
“Sorry, elder. I misspoke.”
The Divine Physician, who was apparently neither particularly trustworthy nor entirely unlike a quack, looked silently between us.
I could almost feel how badly he wanted to stab one of us with a large acupuncture needle. Fortunately, his martial arts weren’t up to the task. His sobriquet was Divine Physician, not Divine Needle.
He drew a deep breath, as if suppressing the urge to kill, and spoke calmly.
“It’s all right. I’ve devoted the rest of my life to medicine. A physician must put up with unfair and filthy treatment while caring for a patient, mustn’t he?”

“Sometimes I do wonder what my Master would think if he were here, but it’s all right. I’m a physician, after all. I should expect a pill I spent several sleepless nights making to be chewed up and spat out. Ha ha ha.”
He did not look all right.
His words didn’t merely have a barb in them. They had an acupuncture needle the size of an awl hidden inside.
Jeok Cheongang and I watched his face and quietly exchanged Sound Transmission.
—This is all your fault.
—If you hadn’t butted in, it wouldn’t have come to this.
—You asked a physician who’d brought you medicine whether he put poison in it. Is that any way for a human being to talk?
—Is calling him a quack any better?
—Why wouldn’t it be?
—He’s the Divine Physician. He might take offense.
—I’m the Fire King.
—I’m the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
—How dare a little fucking nobody like you compare yourself to me?
—Anyway, shut up and eat it. It’s all for your sake.
A little fucking nobody? That hurt.
Jeok Cheongang shot me a fierce glare, then made an effort to soften his voice as he addressed the Divine Physician.
“Don’t take it to heart. I’ll give the boy a proper scolding.”
“Then who’s going to scold Sir Jeok...?”
“Hm? What was that?”
“Nothing. I misspoke.”
Lying through his teeth, the Divine Physician peeled the pill off his robe. He stared mournfully at the clear tooth marks I’d left in it and sighed.
“Some of its medicinal properties have leaked out, but it’s not too late. This time, chew it well and swallow it.”
One thing was certain: its medicinal properties weren’t the only thing leaking out.
Jeok Cheongang caught a whiff of the hideous stench escaping from the crushed pill and instinctively stepped back.
“Could this be Formless Ultimate Poison...!”
“I’m done treating him. I’ll throw this pill in the latrine. Find another physician.”
“W-wait!”
The Fire King caught the Divine Physician’s robe as he turned away and spoke through his nose. His other hand had already flashed up to pinch it shut.
“Ah, I didn’t mean to do that. Sorry. But this stench... What in the world did you put in this pill?”
“If I told you, would you understand?”
“It’s a secret method my Master taught me. Stop asking and let it go. And don’t worry—it isn’t poison.”
The Jeok Cheongang I knew would have answered with a spectacular string of curses and a blazing Flame Divine Palm. But for now, the Divine Physician held all the cards.
As patient and guardian, we kept our mouths shut and nodded. Jeok Cheongang urged me on, looking equal parts worried and curious.
“Do as he says. I’m here, so don’t worry about what happens afterward.”
Put like that, it really did sound as if I was about to swallow Formless Ultimate Poison.
I gave him a resentful look, then squeezed my eyes shut. Blocking out my senses as best I could, I tossed the pill into my mouth.
Crunch, crunch, crunch.
My jaw worked without pause. I curled my tongue as tightly as I could to avoid tasting anything. Then I added a spoonful of desperate effort to keep from retching.
*Hnnngh.*
I felt like I was going to die. No, I wouldn’t have been surprised if I was already dead.

A hideous stench burst through my mouth with every chew. As some unidentified, thick juice trickled down my throat, my esophagus started doing the Zero Two and my guts launched into the cocaine dance.
*Urgh, shit...!*
I swear, I’d never encountered a stench or anything so revolting in my life.

Not even when I was a rookie Hunter and fell nose-first into a goblin’s armpit inside a Gate. Not even when I screamed and flailed so wildly that I accidentally burst the creature’s balls with my bare hand.
“Urk! Uuugh!”
Reason deserted me. My body moved on instinct.
Bent over like a shrimp, I tried to vomit up something hot surging from deep in my stomach.
Tried to.
If someone hadn’t clamped a hand over my mouth and nose at that very moment—
Crack.
My breath caught. I struggled on reflex, but the grip holding me fast stuck like glue.
And there was only one person here who could restrain me so completely.
*Old Master?*
I forced open the eyes I’d squeezed shut and saw Jeok Cheongang’s eyes glowing red with Scorching Yang Qi.
Then a powerful blow struck my Adam’s apple.
Thwack!
With his hand sealed over my mouth and nose, I couldn’t even scream.
As my newly brightened vision went black, I thought, *At this point, that’s closer to poison than medicine.*
That was it.
I felt the finely crushed pill mix with my saliva and flow deep into my body. Then I lost consciousness.
Whoosh.
Along with a heat I knew better than anything.
Jeok Cheongang neither panicked nor hesitated.

He had lived for a hundred and several dozen years. The age of fifty, when a man came to understand Heaven’s will and the natural order, lay far behind him. He knew better than anyone what he had to do.
*Now.*
Scorching Yang Qi seethed through his body, but his mind was as cold as year-round snow.
All trace of his earlier banter gone, he reached toward the unconscious Jin Taekyung, his face grave.
Swish. Tap. Dudududuk!
His movements were as swift as a flash of light, his hands terrifyingly calm.
Every time they blurred, Jin Taekyung’s body jerked. Scorching Yang Qi seeped in with each Pressure-Point Strike, melting the pill and spreading its medicinal effects throughout Jin’s body.
*Don’t rush. Stay calm.*
Jeok Cheongang repeated the words to himself as if making a vow.
He couldn’t afford the slightest mistake. Humans weren’t so easy to kill, but their bodies were astonishingly sensitive. All the more so when that body held several jiazi of internal energy.
Rumble.
Tremendous heat surged around them. The solid wooden floor of the pavilion charred black, and the two men were surrounded by a shimmer like a desert mirage.
Hssssss.
An ordinary physician witnessing the scene would have rubbed his eyes or screamed and fled.
But the Divine Physician was the one physician who did neither.

He had spent decades following his Master and treating countless patients, and his Master’s excellent teaching had given him experience beyond even that. It mattered, too, that the Master in question was the Slaughter Saint.
*It’s going as smoothly as it possibly could. Hard to believe, considering the treatment he’s performing.*
The Divine Physician watched Jeok Cheongang in wonder.

Working the channels and pressure points was no easy undertaking. The practitioner had to sweep, strike, press, and tap hundreds of points across the body, opening blocked flows of qi and blood and loosening knotted muscles.
That alone consumed enormous concentration and internal energy. A single mistake could seriously injure the practitioner, too.
*And this time, he has to spread the pill’s energy to every corner of the body.*
It wasn’t merely difficult. It was extraordinarily difficult.
Under normal circumstances, even the Divine Physician wouldn’t have dared treat someone this way.

With the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, it was different. Of the ten Supreme Peak masters known as kings throughout the world, he alone could be compared to the Three Saints. He was also a Master willing to risk anything for his only Disciple.
Just like the Divine Physician’s own Master.
*You’re doing well somewhere, aren’t you? Aren’t you?*
The Divine Physician had just thought of the Master he’d parted from four months earlier, almost as if he’d been forced to leave, and smiled faintly when—
Whoosh.
The heat and haze slowly dispersed. Through them, Jeok Cheongang came into view, rising to his feet, his face a little pale.
“Sir Jeok. Are you all right?”
“Don’t make a fuss. This much won’t hurt me.”
“Even so, you should at least—”
“I’m fine. See to that reckless brat first.”

sentences.text: “Chew it thoroughly before you swallow.”
“Chew it?”
“Yes.
Don’t swallow it whole, and don’t spit it out halfway through.
Understood?”
The Divine Physician had arrived at first light with that stern warning.
I gave a faint laugh and accepted the pill he held out.
“Of course.
I’m not a child, and you made it for my sake.”
The pill was dark and about the size of a marble.
The Appraisal System was still inaccessible, so I couldn’t tell exactly what was in it or what it would do.
But the Divine Physician must have spent several sleepless nights making it.
The exhaustion around his eyes was proof enough.
*He must have had plenty of other patients to care for, too.*
The best physician in the world had sacrificed his own time and health to make this pill for me.
Even if it was hard as a rock, I planned to chew it until the sweetness came out.
It was the least I could do.
And the moment I chewed the pill with heartfelt gratitude—
Crunch.
I realized that being a decent human being could go to hell.
This wasn’t something a human being could eat.
Ptooey.
The pill I spat out on instinct stuck fast to the Divine Physician’s pristine white robe.
He gazed mournfully at the pill he’d spent days making.
“I told you not to spit it out...”
Still retching and struggling to keep my senses, I spoke from the heart.
“Sorry, but are you out of your mind?”
“I am, and I understand exactly how you feel.”
“Have you tried eating it yourself?”
“I haven’t.”
“Then you have no idea how I feel.
None.”
“Medicine that’s good for you is supposed to taste bitter.
It always is.”
“This wasn’t just bitter.
Did you put poison in it or something?”
“Enough!”
Jeok Cheongang, who’d watched the whole thing, bellowed and glared at me.
“He may not be particularly trustworthy and may seem a bit of a quack, but he made that medicine with care for your sake.
Poison?
Where did you get the nerve to say such blasphemous nonsense?”
“Sorry.”
“Don’t apologize to me.
Apologize to that quack!”
“Sorry, elder.
I misspoke.”
The Divine Physician, who was apparently neither particularly trustworthy nor entirely unlike a quack, looked silently between us.
I could almost feel how badly he wanted to stab one of us with a large acupuncture needle.
Fortunately, his martial arts weren’t up to the task.
His sobriquet was Divine Physician, not Divine Needle.
He drew a deep breath, as if suppressing the urge to kill, and spoke calmly.
“It’s all right.
I’ve devoted the rest of my life to medicine.
A physician must put up with unfair and filthy treatment while caring for a patient, mustn’t he?”
“Sometimes I do wonder what my Master would think if he were here, but it’s all right.
I’m a physician, after all.
I should expect a pill I spent several sleepless nights making to be chewed up and spat out.
Ha ha ha.”
He did not look all right.
His words didn’t merely have a barb in them.
They had an acupuncture needle the size of an awl hidden inside.
Jeok Cheongang and I watched his face and quietly exchanged Sound Transmission.
—This is all your fault.
—If you hadn’t butted in, it wouldn’t have come to this.
—You asked a physician who’d brought you medicine whether he put poison in it.
Is that any way for a human being to talk?
—Is calling him a quack any better?
—Why wouldn’t it be?
—He’s the Divine Physician.
He might take offense.
—I’m the Fire King.
—I’m the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
—How dare a little fucking nobody like you compare yourself to me?
—Anyway, shut up and eat it.
It’s all for your sake.
A little fucking nobody?
That hurt.
Jeok Cheongang shot me a fierce glare, then made an effort to soften his voice as he addressed the Divine Physician.
“Don’t take it to heart.
I’ll give the boy a proper scolding.”
“Then who’s going to scold Sir Jeok...?”
“Hm?
What was that?”
“Nothing.
I misspoke.”
Lying through his teeth, the Divine Physician peeled the pill off his robe.
He stared mournfully at the clear tooth marks I’d left in it and sighed.
“Some of its medicinal properties have leaked out, but it’s not too late.
This time, chew it well and swallow it.”
One thing was certain: its medicinal properties weren’t the only thing leaking out.
Jeok Cheongang caught a whiff of the hideous stench escaping from the crushed pill and instinctively stepped back.
“Could this be Formless Ultimate Poison...!”
“I’m done treating him.
I’ll throw this pill in the latrine.
Find another physician.”
“W-wait!”
The Fire King caught the Divine Physician’s robe as he turned away and spoke through his nose.
His other hand had already flashed up to pinch it shut.
“Ah, I didn’t mean to do that.
Sorry.
But this stench...
What in the world did you put in this pill?”
“If I told you, would you understand?”
“It’s a secret method my Master taught me.
Stop asking and let it go.
And don’t worry—it isn’t poison.”
The Jeok Cheongang I knew would have answered with a spectacular string of curses and a blazing Flame Divine Palm.
But for now, the Divine Physician held all the cards.
As patient and guardian, we kept our mouths shut and nodded.
Jeok Cheongang urged me on, looking equal parts worried and curious.
“Do as he says.
I’m here, so don’t worry about what happens afterward.”
Put like that, it really did sound as if I was about to swallow Formless Ultimate Poison.
I gave him a resentful look, then squeezed my eyes shut.
Blocking out my senses as best I could, I tossed the pill into my mouth.
Crunch, crunch, crunch.
My jaw worked without pause.
I curled my tongue as tightly as I could to avoid tasting anything.
Then I added a spoonful of desperate effort to keep from retching.
*Hnnngh.*
I felt like I was going to die.
No, I wouldn’t have been surprised if I was already dead.
A hideous stench burst through my mouth with every chew.
As some unidentified, thick juice trickled down my throat, my esophagus started doing the Zero Two and my guts launched into the cocaine dance.
*Urgh, shit...!*
I swear, I’d never encountered a stench or anything so revolting in my life.
Not even when I was a rookie Hunter and fell nose-first into a goblin’s armpit inside a Gate.
Not even when I screamed and flailed so wildly that I accidentally burst the creature’s balls with my bare hand.
“Urk!
Uuugh!”
Reason deserted me.
My body moved on instinct.
Bent over like a shrimp, I tried to vomit up something hot surging from deep in my stomach.
Tried to.
If someone hadn’t clamped a hand over my mouth and nose at that very moment—
Crack.
My breath caught.
I struggled on reflex, but the grip holding me fast stuck like glue.
And there was only one person here who could restrain me so completely.
*Old Master?*
I forced open the eyes I’d squeezed shut and saw Jeok Cheongang’s eyes glowing red with Scorching Yang Qi.
Then a powerful blow struck my Adam’s apple.
Thwack!
With his hand sealed over my mouth and nose, I couldn’t even scream.
As my newly brightened vision went black, I thought, *At this point, that’s closer to poison than medicine.*
That was it.
I felt the finely crushed pill mix with my saliva and flow deep into my body.
Then I lost consciousness.
Whoosh.
Along with a heat I knew better than anything.

He had lived for a hundred and several dozen years.
The age of fifty, when a man came to understand Heaven’s will and the natural order, lay far behind him.
He knew better than anyone what he had to do.

chapters.title: Chapter 846
paragraphs: Dududududu!

Some twenty horsemen galloped without slowing. The faces beneath their low-pulled helmets were tense, and white foam had dried around the mouths of their panting horses. Not one rider eased the reins.
Not until they reached their destination, enclosed by stone walls like a fortress.
The first thing to greet them was a wary shout.
“Stop!”
It happened in an instant. At the shout from atop the stone wall, a dozen or so arrows flashed through the air and pierced the plumes on the horsemen’s helmets.
Shaaak! Thunk, thunk, thunk!
The accuracy was almost supernatural, the force tremendous. The horsemen stared at the arrows quivering where they’d struck the ground.
A mistake?
No. A warning.
If they ignored the warning and came any closer, the next arrows would pierce their throats instead of their helmet plumes.
“Gasp...!”
Sighs erupted from all around.
The more than twenty horsemen stopped where they stood as if on cue. They couldn’t hide their fear, but the man at their center was different.
*As expected. The reputation is well deserved.*
He looked up at the wall, admiration and tension mingling in his eyes. A group of archers stood there with bows drawn, backlit by the early morning sun.
Above their green martial robes fluttered a banner bearing four characters written in a single flowing stroke.
Sichuan Tang Clan.
The Nine Sects and One Gang. The Five Great Families. Fifteen pillars supporting Murim as it stood today.
And among them, none had a reputation for being more closed-off or cunning.
But...
*He’s here. Right here.*
The man steeled himself and stepped forward alone. Rather than a sturdy shield against the arrows that might fly at any moment, he held high a silver token drawn from his robes.
“Don’t attack! I’ve come from Seongju Prefecture!”
“Who did you say you were?”
“Huang. I’m the City Lord’s Captain of the Guards.”
“The City Lord? Ah, that fellow who’s been wasting away?”
“...I don’t know who you are, but you’d do well to watch your tongue.”
“If you don’t know who I am, you’re the one who should watch his tongue. You look like you’ve spent a fair bit of time in Murim. How have you not figured out something that simple?”
The Captain of the Guards swallowed before he realized he was doing it.
The man had plainly been picking a fight, yet somehow the captain didn’t feel offended. No—the man’s bearing made it seem only natural that he should speak that way.
*Who is he?*
For a moment, the Captain of the Guards forgot his mission and studied the man in front of him.
He wasn’t quite a giant, but he had a sturdy, well-proportioned build and a face that looked around forty. So far, he could have been any martial artist in Murim.
But his gaze was so piercing it bordered on menacing. Even the Captain of the Guards, who’d seen all sorts of people since his days as a wandering martial artist, flinched.
*And he’s bald.*
The Captain of the Guards saw the middle-aged man’s scalp gleaming in the sunlight and sensed danger.
In his experience, most martial artists were missing something important. Why would anyone who was carefree and happy throw himself into the brutal, turbulent martial world?
The bald ones he remembered were especially unpredictable. They were missing something inside, just like the others—but, unfairly, they were missing their hair as well.
“Hey.”
“Yes?”
The captain jumped and answered on reflex. He’d slipped from polite speech into outright deference so naturally that he hadn’t noticed it himself.
“You know me?”
“N-no.”
“Then why are you staring at my head like that? It’s making me uncomfortable.”

It was hard to say which was ruder: calling someone “you” and “that bastard” the moment you met, or staring at his head. But for the Captain of the Guards, who’d already sensed danger, there was only one option left.
“I-I’m sorry.”
“Some stray mutt barges in out of nowhere, raising hell... At least you know when to back down.”
The captain felt wronged. He didn’t know who this middle-aged man was. He’d ridden hard since early morning to meet someone else.
*How did things end up like this? Was the information wrong from the start?*

Tang Sadok, Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan, had approved the meeting. Yet the person the captain had come to see was nowhere in sight. Instead, a menacing bald man stood across from him, staring as if he meant to eat him alive.
That last part, however, was all in the captain’s head.
The middle-aged man—Jeok Cheongang—snorted. His gaze settled on the captain as he sank into thought.

Uninvited guests, barging in during broad daylight. Ordinarily, he’d have kicked them out on their asses. Officials were another matter, especially the Captain of the Guards, one of the City Lord’s closest men.
*I can guess why they’re here.*

Jeok Cheongang had eyes and ears. However little interest he took in the world around him, rumors still reached him. He’d heard that the City Lord had been confined to his sickbed for a couple of months.
“You came to see the Divine Physician?”

The captain, already on edge, stared at him. Two things startled him: the Divine Physician, whom even the imperial court had failed to find, really was staying with the Sichuan Tang Clan—and Jeok Cheongang had mentioned the renowned physician as casually as if he were Jang Sam from next door.
“I wasn’t sure whether to believe it. Is he really here?”
“What an ill-mannered bastard. Answer what I asked.”
“Y-yes.”
“Because the City Lord is ill?”
“Yes. I don’t know if you’ve already heard, but... We’re here to treat the City Lord’s illness.”
“Surely you have plenty of physicians.”
“That...”
The Captain of the Guards hesitated for a moment, but not for long.

He didn’t know who the man before him was, but he was clearly someone of considerable standing in Murim. He’d inserted himself into a meeting arranged by the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan as though it were nothing. However badly the clan had been struck, challenging the authority of Tang Sadok, the Myriad-Poison Asura, took more than nerve. It took madness.
And then Jeok Cheongang spoke one sentence, enough to make the Captain of the Guards the most honest man in the world.
“You don’t have to force yourself to talk. Once you’ve been beaten senseless, you’ll start remembering things you’d forgotten.”
“I must be seeing things. Your mouth still looks shut.”
Deeply grateful that his subordinates weren’t here, the Captain of the Guards hurriedly opened his mouth.
“The City Lord’s condition is that serious.”
“Five.”
“Pardon?”
“That answer was worth five hits. I’ll take one off for every proper answer you give from now on.”
*Is he insane?*

Jeok Cheongang hadn’t so much as blinked while making the threat. The captain’s knees went weak. He’d been a master of some renown among wandering martial artists, yet he felt he wouldn’t stand a chance against this man, who looked about his age.
“Go on, then. Spit it out properly.”
Jeok Cheongang spread the fingers of one hand. The captain forced out his answer.
“It’s quite different from what people say. Even the renowned physicians nearby have given up.”
“So you need the Divine Physician?”
“Yes. After everything we’ve tried, there should have been at least some improvement. Instead, his condition keeps getting worse.”
“Then it must be a race against time.”
“It is. But...”
The captain licked his dry lips before continuing.
“The City Lord’s illness is a little—no, very strange.”
“Strange...”
Jeok Cheongang murmured and folded one finger.
“Four. Go on.”
“Sometimes he’s conscious and can move about, but at other times he thrashes around like someone who’s gone mad.”
“Rather than *like* a madman, hasn’t he simply gone mad?”
“I thought so at first. The unmistakable symptoms started right after he returned from the Imperial Capital.”
“The Imperial Capital?”
“Yes. He was summoned to court over the Blood Tragedy that happened four months ago.”

The Sichuan Blood Tragedy had caused an enormous upheaval, even to an outsider with no ties to Murim. The authorities and Murim might have kept out of each other’s affairs, but an event of that scale was bound to have repercussions.

More than ten thousand martial artists had fought in Sichuan, territory of the Great Nation. Countless people died or were wounded, and smoke from the cremation of the dead lingered for more than three days.
“Word spread quickly. It happened not far from Chengdu, and there were too many witnesses for it not to. But the biggest problem was...”
Jeok Cheongang, who’d been listening quietly, tossed out a single word.
“Dark Heaven.”
“Yes. The court learned that members of Dark Heaven had disguised themselves as government soldiers.”
“The higher-ups must have been furious.”
“I spent years in Murim myself, but authority and saving face matter everywhere, don’t they?”
Whether a man made his living by the sword or by the pen, he was still human. And the dignity and authority of the unified dynasty—founded after an age of warring powers—were not to be challenged.
Dark Heaven had done just that. Disguised as government soldiers, they’d walked the streets in broad daylight and gone on to carry out a horrific massacre.
*Which means...*
Jeok Cheongang sorted through his tangled thoughts and spoke.
“This is more interesting than I expected. Fine. Three. Keep going.”
“After returning from the Imperial Capital, the City Lord took to his bed. Strictly speaking, it began on his way back to Sichuan.”
“The higher-ups must have given him a thorough dressing-down.”
“The court’s reprimand was part of it, but he also fell ill because he lost what he cherished most in the Imperial Capital.”
“What he cherished most?”
“Yes.”
The captain gave that brief answer, then fixed his gaze on Jeok Cheongang’s three raised fingers.
“...You crafty bastard.”
“The City Lord doesn’t favor me for nothing.”
“Fine. Two.”
“Be a little more generous. One.”
“Do you want to spend the rest of your life with one eye?”
“Fine. One.”
The Captain of the Guards stared at the last finger still raised and swallowed hard before speaking.
“His favored concubine.”
“His favored concubine?”
“Yes. Her name was Aehyang. He couldn’t live without her.”
“If he took her all the way to the Imperial Capital in the middle of that mess, I get the idea. So what, did he lose her in the street?”
“No. To be precise, a high-ranking person in the Imperial Capital took her from him.”
“Important enough to take the City Lord’s concubine. Who?”
“Well...”
Jeok Cheongang folded his last finger at the captain’s hesitation. Then he heard the answer and his eyes widened.
“The Son of Heaven.”

*I can guess why they’re here.*
Jeok Cheongang had eyes and ears.
However little interest he took in the world around him, rumors still reached him.
He’d heard that the City Lord had been confined to his sickbed for a couple of months.
“You came to see the Divine Physician?”
The captain, already on edge, stared at him.

Two things startled him: the Divine Physician, whom even the imperial court had failed to find, really was staying with the Sichuan Tang Clan—and Jeok Cheongang had mentioned the renowned physician as casually as if he were Jang Sam from next door.
“I wasn’t sure whether to believe it.
Is he really here?”
“What an ill-mannered bastard.
Answer what I asked.”
“Y-yes.”
“Because the City Lord is ill?”
“Yes.
I don’t know if you’ve already heard, but...
We’re here to treat the City Lord’s illness.”
“Surely you have plenty of physicians.”
“That...”
The Captain of the Guards hesitated for a moment, but not for long.
He didn’t know who the man before him was, but he was clearly someone of considerable standing in Murim.
He’d inserted himself into a meeting arranged by the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan as though it were nothing.
However badly the clan had been struck, challenging the authority of Tang Sadok, the Myriad-Poison Asura, took more than nerve.
It took madness.
And then Jeok Cheongang spoke one sentence, enough to make the Captain of the Guards the most honest man in the world.
“You don’t have to force yourself to talk.
Once you’ve been beaten senseless, you’ll start remembering things you’d forgotten.”
“I must be seeing things.
Your mouth still looks shut.”
Deeply grateful that his subordinates weren’t here, the Captain of the Guards hurriedly opened his mouth.
“The City Lord’s condition is that serious.”
“Five.”
“Pardon?”
“That answer was worth five hits.
I’ll take one off for every proper answer you give from now on.”
*Is he insane?*
Jeok Cheongang hadn’t so much as blinked while making the threat.
The captain’s knees went weak.
He’d been a master of some renown among wandering martial artists, yet he felt he wouldn’t stand a chance against this man, who looked about his age.
“Go on, then.
Spit it out properly.”
Jeok Cheongang spread the fingers of one hand.
The captain forced out his answer.
“It’s quite different from what people say.
Even the renowned physicians nearby have given up.”
“So you need the Divine Physician?”
“Yes.
After everything we’ve tried, there should have been at least some improvement.
Instead, his condition keeps getting worse.”
“Then it must be a race against time.”
“It is.
But...”
The captain licked his dry lips before continuing.
“The City Lord’s illness is a little—no, very strange.”
“Strange...”
Jeok Cheongang murmured and folded one finger.
“Four.
Go on.”
“Sometimes he’s conscious and can move about, but at other times he thrashes around like someone who’s gone mad.”
“Rather than *like* a madman, hasn’t he simply gone mad?”
“I thought so at first.
The unmistakable symptoms started right after he returned from the Imperial Capital.”
“The Imperial Capital?”
“Yes.
He was summoned to court over the Blood Tragedy that happened four months ago.”
The Sichuan Blood Tragedy had caused an enormous upheaval, even to an outsider with no ties to Murim.
The authorities and Murim might have kept out of each other’s affairs, but an event of that scale was bound to have repercussions.
More than ten thousand martial artists had fought in Sichuan, territory of the Great Nation.
Countless people died or were wounded, and smoke from the cremation of the dead lingered for more than three days.
“Word spread quickly.
It happened not far from Chengdu, and there were too many witnesses for it not to.
But the biggest problem was...”
Jeok Cheongang, who’d been listening quietly, tossed out a single word.
“Dark Heaven.”
“Yes.
The court learned that members of Dark Heaven had disguised themselves as government soldiers.”
“The higher-ups must have been furious.”
“I spent years in Murim myself, but authority and saving face matter everywhere, don’t they?”
Whether a man made his living by the sword or by the pen, he was still human.
And the dignity and authority of the unified dynasty—founded after an age of warring powers—were not to be challenged.
Dark Heaven had done just that.
Disguised as government soldiers, they’d walked the streets in broad daylight and gone on to carry out a horrific massacre.
*Which means...*
Jeok Cheongang sorted through his tangled thoughts and spoke.
“This is more interesting than I expected.
Fine.
Three.
Keep going.”
“After returning from the Imperial Capital, the City Lord took to his bed.
Strictly speaking, it began on his way back to Sichuan.”
“The higher-ups must have given him a thorough dressing-down.”
“The court’s reprimand was part of it, but he also fell ill because he lost what he cherished most in the Imperial Capital.”
“What he cherished most?”
“Yes.”
The captain gave that brief answer, then fixed his gaze on Jeok Cheongang’s three raised fingers.
“...You crafty bastard.”
“The City Lord doesn’t favor me for nothing.”
“Fine.
Two.”
“Be a little more generous.
One.”
“Do you want to spend the rest of your life with one eye?”
“Fine.
One.”
The Captain of the Guards stared at the last finger still raised and swallowed hard before speaking.
“His favored concubine.”
“His favored concubine?”
“Yes.
Her name was Aehyang.
He couldn’t live without her.”
“If he took her all the way to the Imperial Capital in the middle of that mess, I get the idea.
So what, did he lose her in the street?”
“No.
To be precise, a high-ranking person in the Imperial Capital took her from him.”
“Important enough to take the City Lord’s concubine.
Who?”
“Well...”
Jeok Cheongang folded his last finger at the captain’s hesitation.
Then he heard the answer and his eyes widened.
“The Son of Heaven.”
